qs.q: The witness provided a candid account of what transpired during the robbery.
qs.e: 'Candid' means truthful and straightforward, synonymous with 'frank'.

qs.q: His fastidious nature made it difficult for him to find a suitable roommate.
qs.e: 'Fastidious' means very attentive to and concerned about accuracy and detail; fussy.

qs.q: The hostility between the two neighboring communities has finally subsided.
qs.e: 'Hostility' means unfriendliness or opposition; its opposite is 'friendliness' or amity.

qs.q: The newly installed security system provides genuine protection against cyberattacks.
qs.e: 'Genuine' means authentic and real; its antonym is 'spurious' or fake.

qs.q: The author's explanation of the complex economic theory was remarkably lucid.
qs.e: 'Lucid' means expressed clearly or easy to understand; its antonym is 'obscure' or vague.

qs.q: The government launched a campaign to pacify the aggrieved citizens.
qs.e: 'Pacify' means bring peace or calm to; its opposite is 'incite' or provoke.

qs.q: The team of auditors _____ examining the company's financial ledgers since yesterday morning.
qs.e: 'Team' treated as a single entity takes the singular verb 'has been'.

qs.q: Either the chief accountant or the cashiers _____ responsible for the discrepancy.
qs.e: With 'either... or', the verb agrees with the closer plural subject ('cashiers' -> 'are').

qs.q: Ten thousand naira _____ the total price charged for the textbook.
qs.e: Sums of money take a singular verb when considered as a single total amount ('is').

qs.q: Bread and butter _____ the traditional breakfast served in many hotels.
qs.e: 'Bread and butter' forming a single combined dish or concept takes a singular verb ('is').

qs.q: Not only the manager but also his workers _____ commended for their diligence.
qs.e: With 'not only... but also', the verb agrees with the closer subject ('workers' -> 'were').

qs.q: Had I known that the venue had changed, I _____ there so early.
qs.e: Inverted third conditional 'Had I known...' requires 'would not have + past participle' in the main clause.

qs.q: It is recommended that the bank manager _____ the loan application promptly.
qs.e: The subjunctive after verbs of recommendation requires the base verb form ('review').

qs.q: When we arrived at the terminal, the express train _____ already departed.
qs.e: Past perfect 'had departed' indicates an event completed prior to another past event ('arrived').

qs.q: The research scholar _____ on this manuscript for over five years.
qs.e: Present perfect continuous 'has been working' expresses an action originating in the past and continuing into the present.

qs.q: The phrase 'as brave as a lion' is an example of _____.
qs.e: Comparison using 'as' or 'like' is a simile.

qs.q: When someone is described as a 'dark horse', it implies that they _____.
o: have a dark complexion and rides horses
possess hidden abilities or win unexpectedly
are dishonest and untrustworthy in business
refuse to participate in athletic competitions
qs.e: 'Dark horse' refers to a candidate or competitor about whom little is known but who unexpectedly succeeds.

qs.q: The statement 'Her voice is music to my ears' is an example of _____.
qs.e: Direct comparison without using 'like' or 'as' is a metaphor.

qs.q: In commercial banking, an asset pledged as security for repayment of a loan is called _____.
qs.e: Collateral is something pledged as security for repayment of a loan, to be forfeited in the event of a default.

qs.q: A sum of money paid regularly by a company to its shareholders out of its profits is a _____.
qs.e: A dividend is a distribution of profits by a corporation to its shareholders.

qs.q: In business, a state of financial ruin in which a firm cannot pay its debts is termed _____.
qs.e: Bankruptcy is the legal status of a person or organization that cannot repay debts to creditors.

qs.q: A legal agreement by which a bank lends money at interest in exchange for taking title of the debtor's property is a _____.
qs.e: A mortgage is a legal agreement by which a bank or creditor lends money at interest in exchange for property security.

qs.q: The gradual reduction of the recorded cost of an intangible asset over time is known as _____.
qs.e: Amortization is the accounting practice of spreading the cost of an intangible asset over its useful life.

qs.q: The committee chairman urged the members to _____ the matter thoroughly before voting.
qs.e: 'Look into' means to investigate or examine a matter.

qs.q: She decided to _____ smoking after attending a health awareness seminar.
qs.e: 'Give up' means to stop doing or consuming something.

qs.q: The meeting was _____ until next week due to the lack of a quorum.
qs.e: 'Put off' means to postpone or delay an event.

qs.q: While running through the park, he unexpectedly _____ his primary school teacher.
qs.e: 'Run into' means to meet someone unexpectedly.

qs.q: The manager insisted _____ seeing the original receipts before authorizing the refund.
qs.e: The verb 'insist' collocates with the preposition 'on'.

qs.q: He is immune _____ the tropical fever because he was vaccinated prior to travel.
qs.e: 'Immune' can take 'to' or 'from' ('immune to disease').

qs.q: The suspect's statement was not consistent _____ the physical evidence gathered at the scene.
qs.e: 'Consistent' takes the preposition 'with'.

qs.q: Which of the following words contains the vowel sound /iː/ as in 'key'?
qs.e: 'Quay' (/kiː/) contains the long vowel sound /iː/.

qs.q: Identify the word that features the central long vowel sound /ɜː/ as in 'turn'.
qs.e: 'Earth' (/ɜːθ/) features the central long vowel sound /ɜː/.

qs.q: Which word contains the diphthong /aʊ/ as in 'house'?
qs.e: 'Towel' (/taʊəl/) contains the diphthong /aʊ/.

qs.q: Which word features the short vowel sound /ʊ/ as in 'put'?
qs.e: 'Wolf' (/wʊlf/) contains the short near-close rounded vowel sound /ʊ/.

qs.q: In which word is the consonant sound /ð/ present as in 'then'?
qs.e: 'Clothe' (/kləʊð/) contains the voiced dental fricative /ð/, whereas 'cloth', 'growth', and 'faith' have /θ/.

qs.q: Which word contains the voiceless velar plosive /k/?
qs.e: 'Character' (/ˈkær.ək.tər/) begins with the sound /k/.

qs.q: Identify the word containing the voiced postalveolar fricative /ʒ/.
qs.e: 'Measure' (/ˈmeʒ.ər/) contains the voiced postalveolar fricative /ʒ/.

qs.q: Which word features a silent letter 'l'?
qs.e: The letter 'l' in 'salmon' (/ˈsæm.ən/) is silent.

qs.q: In which word is the letter 'b' silent?
qs.e: The letter 'b' in 'tomb' (/tuːm/) is silent.

qs.q: Select the word with primary stress on the first syllable.
qs.e: 'DEM-o-crat' has primary stress on the first syllable.

qs.q: Which word has primary stress on its penultimate (second-to-last) syllable?
qs.e: Words ending in '-ic' like 'eco-NOM-ic' have primary stress on the penultimate syllable.

qs.q: Identify the sentence that matches emphatic stress on 'MONDAY': 'John traveled to Lagos on Monday.'
o: Did John return from Lagos on Monday?
Did Peter travel to Lagos on Monday?
Did John travel to Ibadan on Monday?
Did John travel to Lagos on Tuesday?
qs.e: Emphatic stress on 'MONDAY' contrasts the day of travel.

qs.q: Identify the underlined clause: 'The man who came here yesterday is a famous surgeon.'
qs.e: 'Who came here yesterday' modifies the noun 'man', making it an adjectival (relative) clause.

qs.q: Choose the correct active voice form of: 'The stadium was damaged by the raging storm.'
o: The stadium damages the raging storm.
The raging storm was damaging the stadium.
The storm has damaged the stadium.
The raging storm damaged the stadium.
qs.e: In active voice, the agent ('The raging storm') becomes the subject performing the simple past action ('damaged').

qs.q: The manager appreciated _____ taking the initiative to resolve the customer's complaint.
qs.e: A possessive pronoun ('his') is required before a gerund ('taking').

qs.q: Of the two candidates, Musa is clearly the _____ qualified for the position.
qs.e: When comparing exactly two entities, the comparative degree ('more qualified') must be used.

qs.q: You haven't submitted your quarterly report yet, _____?
qs.e: A negative statement takes a positive question tag ('have you').

qs.q: If I _____ in your shoes, I would decline the offer immediately.
qs.e: Subjunctive mood expressing a hypothetical condition uses 'were' for all pronouns.

qs.q: The programmer's ingenious algorithm significantly reduced the application processing time.
qs.e: 'Ingenious' means clever, original, and inventive.

qs.q: The government launched a comprehensive campaign to eradicate cybercrime.
qs.e: 'Eradicate' means put an end to or destroy completely.

qs.q: The network administrator was praised for his diligent monitoring of system logs.
qs.e: 'Diligent' means having or showing care and conscientiousness in work, synonymous with 'assiduous'.

qs.q: The company's software update solved the persistent vulnerability in the system.
qs.e: 'Vulnerability' in computing refers to a flaw or weakness in security.

qs.q: Storing sensitive user passwords in plaintext makes them highly vulnerable to theft.
qs.e: 'Vulnerable' means exposed to the possibility of being attacked or harmed; its opposite is 'secure'.

qs.q: The server experienced a sudden surge in incoming user traffic during the product launch.
qs.e: 'Surge' means a sudden powerful forward or upward movement; its antonym is 'drop' or decline.

qs.q: The user interface design is remarkably intuitive, making it easy for beginners.
qs.e: 'Intuitive' means easy to use and understand without training; its antonym is 'counterintuitive' or complex.

qs.q: The online portal was rendered inaccessible due to a major network outage.
qs.e: 'Inaccessible' opposite is 'accessible'.

qs.q: Either the system analyst or the software engineers _____ responsible for fixing the bug.
qs.e: With 'either... or', the verb agrees with the closer plural subject ('engineers' -> 'are').

qs.q: The committee of IT experts _____ scheduled to meet with the minister tomorrow.
qs.e: Collective noun 'committee' acting as a single unit takes a singular verb ('is').

qs.q: Mathematics _____ an essential prerequisite for pursuing a degree in computer science.
qs.e: Academic disciplines ending in '-s' like 'Mathematics' take singular verbs ('is').

qs.q: Neither the software patch nor the hardware upgrades _____ resolved the network latency.
qs.e: With 'neither... nor', agreement is with closer plural noun 'upgrades' ('have').

qs.q: Five gigabytes of data _____ required to download the system operating software.
qs.e: Quantities of data or measurement take singular verbs ('is').

qs.q: By the time the technician arrived, the server _____ completely rebooted.
qs.e: Past perfect 'had' denotes an action completed before another past event ('arrived').

qs.q: If the network administrator _____ installed the firewall earlier, the cyber breach would have been averted.
qs.e: Third conditional requires 'had + past participle' in the if-clause.

qs.q: The cybersecurity firm _____ monitoring internet traffic for threats since last month.
qs.e: Present perfect continuous 'has been' indicates an action starting in past and continuing.

qs.q: It is essential that every user _____ their security credentials every ninety days.
qs.e: Subjunctive mood following 'essential that' takes the base verb ('update').

qs.q: To 'bite off more than one can chew' means to _____.
o: eat food too quickly without chewing properly
take on a task that is way beyond one's capability
qs.e: 'Bite off more than one can chew' means to commit to more work than one can manage.

qs.q: The phrase 'time is a thief' is an example of _____.
qs.e: Directly identifying time as a thief without using 'like' or 'as' is a metaphor.

qs.q: When an invention is described as 'cutting edge', it means it is _____.
qs.e: 'Cutting edge' refers to the most advanced stage in a field of technology.

qs.q: The expression 'an open secret' is an example of _____.
qs.e: Combining contradictory terms ('open' and 'secret') forms an oxymoron.

qs.q: In ICT, a security system designed to prevent unauthorized access to a private network is a _____.
qs.e: A firewall is a network security system that monitors and controls incoming and outgoing network traffic.

qs.q: The maximum rate of data transfer across a given network path is known as _____.
qs.e: Bandwidth is the maximum amount of data transmitted over an internet connection in a given amount of time.

qs.q: In aviation, the compartment in an aircraft where the pilot and flight crew sit is the _____.
qs.e: The cockpit is the compartment at the front of an aircraft from which the pilot controls the plane.

qs.q: The main body of an aircraft, excluding the wings and tail, is called the _____.
qs.e: The fuselage is the main body of an aircraft that holds passengers, crew, and cargo.

qs.q: In aviation, severe violent irregular movement of air encountered by an aircraft during flight is _____.
qs.e: Turbulence is violent or unsteady movement of air or water.

qs.q: The airline had to _____ several international flights owing to dense volcanic ash.
qs.e: 'Call off' means to cancel.

qs.q: The aircraft is scheduled to _____ at six o'clock tomorrow morning.
qs.e: 'Take off' means to leave the ground and begin flight.

qs.q: The computer system unexpectedly _____ during the high-volume data backup.
qs.e: 'Break down' means to cease functioning or fail.

qs.q: You should regularly _____ your important computer files to prevent loss of data.
qs.e: 'Back up' means to make a copy of computer data for safety.

qs.q: The pilot was praised for landing the plane safely in spite _____ severe crosswinds.
qs.e: 'In spite' collocates with 'of' ('in spite of').

qs.q: Users must comply _____ the security policies established by the IT department.
qs.e: The verb 'comply' takes the preposition 'with'.

qs.q: The new operating system is compatible _____ most existing hardware devices.
qs.e: 'Compatible' takes the preposition 'with'.

qs.q: Which of the following words contains the long vowel sound /uː/ as in 'too'?
qs.e: 'Shoe' (/ʃuː/) contains the long close back rounded vowel sound /uː/.

qs.q: Identify the word that features the short open-mid back unrounded vowel sound /ʌ/ as in 'sun'.
qs.e: 'Rough' (/rʌf/) features the vowel sound /ʌ/.

qs.q: Which word contains the diphthong /ɔɪ/ as in 'boy'?
qs.e: 'Voice' (/vɔɪs/) contains the diphthong /ɔɪ/.

qs.q: Which word features the diphthong /ɪə/ as in 'ear'?
qs.e: 'Tier' (/tɪər/) contains the diphthong /ɪə/.

qs.q: In which word is the consonant sound /tʃ/ present as in 'church'?
qs.e: 'Nature' (/ˈneɪ.tʃər/) contains the voiceless postalveolar affricate consonant sound /tʃ/.

qs.q: Which word contains the voiced labiodental fricative /v/?
qs.e: 'Nephew' (/ˈnev.juː/) in traditional British pronunciation contains the voiced fricative /v/.

qs.q: Identify the word that contains the voiceless alveolar fricative /s/.
qs.e: 'Rice' (/raɪs/) ends in the voiceless alveolar fricative /s/, unlike 'rise' (/raɪz/).

qs.q: In which word is the letter 'c' silent?
qs.e: The letter 'c' in 'muscle' (/ˈmʌs.əl/) is silent.

qs.q: Which word features a silent letter 'n'?
qs.e: The final letter 'n' in 'autumn' (/ˈɔː.təm/) is silent.

qs.q: In which word is the letter 'd' silent?
qs.e: The letter 'd' in 'handsome' (/ˈhæn.səm/) is silent.

qs.q: Select the word with primary stress on the third syllable.
qs.e: 'e-lec-TRIC-i-ty' (5 syllables) has primary stress on the third syllable.

qs.q: Which word has primary stress on the first syllable?
qs.e: 'IN-dus-try' has primary stress on the first syllable.

qs.q: Identify the sentence that matches emphatic stress on 'FIRST': 'The plane landed on the FIRST runway.'
o: Did the boat dock at the first runway?
Did the helicopter land on the first runway?
Did the plane take off from the first runway?
Did the plane land on the second runway?
qs.e: Emphatic stress on 'FIRST' contrasts the runway ordinal number.

qs.q: Which word rhymes with 'gauge'?
qs.e: 'Gauge' (/ɡeɪdʒ/) rhymes with 'cage' (/keɪdʒ/).

qs.q: Select the word that rhymes with 'stair'?
qs.e: 'Stair' (/steər/) rhymes with 'glare' (/ɡleər/).

qs.q: Identify the underlined clause in: 'I will call you when the aircraft touches down.'
qs.e: 'When the aircraft touches down' specifies time, making it an adverbial clause of time.

qs.q: Choose the passive voice form of: 'The ground crew inspected the Boeing aircraft.'
o: The ground crew was inspecting the aircraft.
The Boeing aircraft is inspected by the ground crew.
The Boeing aircraft had been inspected by ground crew.
The Boeing aircraft was inspected by the ground crew.
qs.e: Simple past active 'inspected' becomes 'was inspected' in passive voice.

qs.q: The agricultural extension officer advised farmers to practice crop rotation to enhance soil fertility.
qs.e: 'Enhance' means intensify, increase, or improve the quality, value, or extent of.

qs.q: The severe drought caused widespread famine across the arid region.
qs.e: 'Famine' refers to extreme scarcity of food, synonymous with 'starvation'.

qs.q: The community harvested a bountiful crop of cassava after the favorable rainy season.
qs.e: 'Bountiful' means large in quantity; abundant.

qs.q: Proper drainage is vital for preventing waterlogging in low-lying farmlands.
qs.e: 'Vital' means absolutely necessary or important; essential.

qs.q: The soil in the river basin is remarkably fertile, yielding rich harvests every year.
qs.e: 'Fertile' means producing or capable of producing abundant vegetation; its direct antonym is 'barren'.

qs.q: Organic farming methods promote sustainable agricultural practices for future generations.
qs.e: 'Sustainable' opposite is 'unsustainable'.

qs.q: The excessive application of chemical pesticides can contaminate local water sources.
qs.e: 'Contaminate' means make impure; its opposite is 'purify'.

qs.q: The sudden arrival of locust swarms caused catastrophic damage to the maize plantation.
qs.e: 'Catastrophic' means involving or causing sudden great damage; its opposite is 'beneficial' or advantageous.

qs.q: Neither the tractor nor the irrigation pumps _____ functioning properly during the dry season.
qs.e: Agreement with closer plural noun 'pumps' requires 'were'.

qs.q: The herd of cattle _____ grazing peacefully near the valley stream.
qs.e: Collective noun 'herd' as a single unit takes singular verb 'is'.

qs.q: Agricultural science _____ taught in all senior secondary schools across the state.
qs.e: 'Agricultural science' takes singular verb 'is'.

qs.q: Either the farm manager or his assistants _____ responsible for inspecting the granary daily.
qs.e: Agreement with closer plural noun 'assistants' ('are').

qs.q: Ten hectares of land _____ set aside for the establishment of a botanical garden.
qs.e: Land area treated as a single unit takes singular verb 'was'.

qs.q: By the time the harvesting season commenced, the grains _____ completely dried.
qs.e: Past perfect 'had' denotes completion prior to another past event.

qs.q: If the government _____ subsidized fertilizer prices, crop production would have doubled.
qs.e: Third conditional requires 'had + past participle'.

qs.q: The research team _____ conducting field trials on drought-resistant maize for three years.
qs.e: Present perfect continuous 'has been' indicates ongoing action from past.

qs.q: The ministry insisted that every farm owner _____ their cattle against anthrax.
qs.e: Subjunctive mood after 'insisted that' takes base verb 'vaccinate'.

qs.q: To 'reap what one sows' means to _____.
o: plant seeds carefully during the rainy season
face the natural consequences of one's past actions
buy agricultural produce at wholesale price
clear a piece of farmland before planting
qs.e: 'Reap what one sows' means to experience the results of one's own actions.

qs.q: The sentence 'The cornfields danced joyfully in the morning breeze' is an example of _____.
qs.e: Attributing dancing human movement to cornfields is personification.

qs.q: When a farmer is described as 'making hay while the sun shines', it means he is _____.
o: cutting grass during a severe rainstorm
taking immediate advantage of a good opportunity
drying corn in a dark storage room
sleeping late during the busy planting season
qs.e: 'Make hay while the sun shines' means to act while conditions are favorable.

qs.q: The phrase 'a sea of green crops' is an example of _____.
qs.e: Direct comparison equating crops to a sea is a metaphor.

qs.q: In agriculture, the artificial application of water to land or soil to assist in crop production is _____.
qs.e: Irrigation is the artificial supply of water to agricultural land.

qs.q: The science and practice of establishing, managing, and conserving forests and timberlands is _____.
qs.e: Silviculture is the practice of controlling the growth, composition/structure, and quality of forests.

qs.q: In soil science, the removal of topsoil by natural agents like water or wind is known as _____.
qs.e: Soil erosion is the wearing away of topsoil by water or wind.

qs.q: The agricultural practice of growing a series of different types of crops in the same area across sequential seasons is _____.
qs.e: Crop rotation involves growing different crops sequentially on the same land.

qs.q: A chemical substance used to destroy or control unwanted insects and agricultural pests is a _____.
qs.e: A pesticide is a chemical substance used to kill or control pests.

qs.q: The heavy rains caused the newly dug drainage channels to _____.
qs.e: 'Wash away' means carry off or destroy by water.

qs.q: The young farmer managed to _____ the difficult dry season with minimal livestock loss.
qs.e: 'Pull through' means survive or overcome a illness or hardship.

qs.q: The agricultural board decided to _____ the new cocoa farming policy next year.
qs.e: 'Bring in' means introduce a new law or system.

qs.q: We need to _____ all infected poultry birds to prevent the virus from spreading.
qs.e: 'Cull' means select and remove wild or domestic animals from a group.

qs.q: The success of crop yield is largely dependent _____ adequate rainfall.
qs.e: 'Dependent' takes the preposition 'on' ('dependent on').

qs.q: The farmlands were vulnerable _____ seasonal flooding from the nearby river.
qs.e: 'Vulnerable' takes the preposition 'to'.

qs.q: Farmers were advised to substitute organic manure _____ expensive inorganic fertilizers.
qs.e: One substitutes X 'for' Y.

qs.q: Which of the following words contains the vowel sound /ɑː/ as in 'barn'?
qs.e: 'Calf' (/kɑːf/) contains the long open back unrounded vowel sound /ɑː/.

qs.q: Identify the word that features the short front unrounded vowel sound /e/ as in 'bed'.
qs.e: 'Bread' (/bred/) features the short vowel sound /e/.

qs.q: Which word contains the diphthong /əʊ/ as in 'boat'?
qs.e: 'Sew' (/səʊ/) contains the diphthong /əʊ/.

qs.q: Which word features the diphthong /eə/ as in 'air'?
qs.e: 'Heir' (/eər/) contains the diphthong /eə/.

qs.q: In which word is the consonant sound /g/ present as in 'go'?
qs.e: 'Ghost' (/ɡəʊst/) begins with the voiced velar plosive sound /g/.

qs.q: Which word contains the voiceless labiodental fricative /f/?
qs.e: 'Laugh' (/lɑːf/) ends in the voiceless labiodental fricative /f/.

qs.q: Identify the word containing the palatal approximant /j/ as in 'yes'.
qs.e: 'Ewe' (/juː/) begins with the palatal approximant consonant sound /j/.

qs.q: In which word is the letter 'g' silent?
qs.e: The letter 'g' in 'reign' (/reɪn/) is completely silent.

qs.q: Which word features a silent letter 't'?
qs.e: The letter 't' in 'listen' (/ˈlɪs.ən/) is silent.

qs.q: In which word is the letter 'h' silent?
qs.e: The letter 'h' in 'vehicle' (/ˈvɪə.kəl/) is silent.

qs.q: Select the word with primary stress on the second syllable.
qs.e: 'ag-RON-o-my' has primary stress on the second syllable.

qs.q: Which word has primary stress on the third syllable?
qs.e: 'cul-ti-VA-tion' has primary stress on the third syllable (-tion rule).

qs.q: Identify the sentence that matches emphatic stress on 'MAIZE': 'The farmer planted MAIZE in his field.'
o: Did the farmer plant maize in his garden?
Did the teacher plant maize in his field?
Did the farmer harvest maize in his field?
Did the farmer plant rice in his field?
qs.e: Emphatic stress on 'MAIZE' contrasts the crop type.

qs.q: Which word rhymes with 'plough'?
qs.e: 'Plough' (/plaʊ/) rhymes with 'bough' (/baʊ/).

qs.q: Select the word that rhymes with 'corn'?
qs.e: 'Corn' (/kɔːn/) rhymes with 'born' (/bɔːn/).

qs.q: Identify the underlined clause in: 'Because the rain was heavy, the crop yield increased significantly.'
qs.e: 'Because the rain was heavy' gives the cause/reason, making it an adverbial clause of reason.

qs.q: Choose the active voice form of: 'Pesticides were applied by the agricultural officer.'
o: The agricultural officer has applied pesticides.
qs.e: Active voice subject 'The agricultural officer' performs simple past action 'applied'.

qs.q: The sovereign nation maintained its autonomy despite pressure from external powers.
qs.e: 'Autonomy' means the right or condition of self-government, synonymous with 'independence'.

qs.q: The electoral commission announced a stringent policy to prevent voting irregularities.
qs.e: 'Stringent' means strict, precise, and exacting.

qs.q: The diplomat negotiated a pragmatic compromise between the warring factions.
qs.e: 'Pragmatic' means dealing with things sensibly and realistically; practical.

qs.q: The constitution contains implicit guarantees regarding freedom of expression.
qs.e: 'Implicit' means implied though not plainly expressed.

qs.q: The government decided to ratify the international treaty on climate change.
qs.e: 'Ratify' means sign or give formal consent to; its opposite is 'reject' or repudiate.

qs.q: The minister's authoritarian leadership style alienated many parliamentary colleagues.
qs.e: 'Authoritarian' means favoring strict obedience to authority; its opposite is 'democratic'.

qs.q: The rebel group agreed to relinquish their weapons at the peace summit.
qs.e: 'Relinquish' means voluntarily cease to keep or claim; its antonym is 'retain' or keep.

qs.q: The newly elected governor demonstrated remarkable clemency toward political prisoners.
qs.e: 'Clemency' means mercy or leniency; its opposite is 'harshness' or severity.

qs.q: Neither the president nor his cabinet ministers _____ present at the press briefing.
qs.e: With 'neither... nor', agreement is with closer plural noun 'ministers' ('were').

qs.q: The National Assembly _____ passed the bill after three rigorous readings.
qs.e: 'National Assembly' acting as a single legislative body takes a singular verb ('has').

qs.q: Civics _____ an essential subject for fostering patriotism among young citizens.
qs.e: Subjects ending in '-s' like 'Civics' take singular verb ('is').

qs.q: Either the electoral officers or the security guard _____ held accountable for the missing ballot box.
qs.e: Agreement with closer singular noun 'guard' requires 'is'.

qs.q: A number of diplomatic envoys _____ arriving in the capital for the summit.
qs.e: 'A number of' takes a plural verb ('are').

qs.q: By the time the foreign minister delivered his address, the delegates _____ signed the accord.
qs.e: Past perfect 'had' denotes an action completed prior to another past event.

qs.q: If the opposition party _____ united earlier, they would have won the election.
qs.e: Third conditional requires 'had + past participle' in condition clause.

qs.q: The peacekeeping force _____ patrolling the border region since the ceasefire was announced.
qs.e: Present perfect continuous 'has been' indicates ongoing action from past.

qs.q: The supreme court ordered that the tribunal _____ the election petition without delay.
qs.e: Subjunctive mood after 'ordered that' takes base verb 'hear'.

qs.q: To 'pass the buck' means to _____.
o: spend money recklessly on luxury goods
shift responsibility or blame to another person
pay a bribe to a public official
win an election by a narrow margin
qs.e: 'Pass the buck' means to pass blame or responsibility to someone else.

qs.q: The statement 'The government machine moved at a snail's pace' contains _____.
qs.e: Comparing the government mechanism directly to a slow machine/snail's pace without 'like' is a metaphor.

qs.q: When a bill is 'pigeonholed' in parliament, it means it has been _____.
o: shelved or set aside indefinitely without action
sent to the president for immediate signing
published in the official government gazette
qs.e: 'Pigeonholed' means set aside or ignored indefinitely.

qs.q: The expression 'lame duck president' refers to an official who _____.
o: is nearing the end of term with diminished power
refuses to sign bills passed by parliament
was defeated in a primary election
qs.e: 'Lame duck' refers to an official in the final period of office, after the election of a successor.

qs.q: In political science, the right to vote in political elections is termed _____.
qs.e: Suffrage is the right to vote in political elections.

qs.q: A direct vote in which an entire electorate is invited to vote on a particular proposal is a _____.
qs.e: A referendum is a general vote by the electorate on a single political question.

qs.q: The practice of manipulating the boundaries of an electoral constituency to favor one party is _____.
qs.e: Gerrymandering is manipulating constituency boundaries for political advantage.

qs.q: A public declaration of policy and aims issued before an election by a political party is a _____.
qs.e: A manifesto is a published verbal declaration of the intentions, motives, or views of an issuer.

qs.q: In a legislature, prolonged speechmaking designed to delay or prevent a vote on a bill is a _____.
qs.e: A filibuster is an action such as a prolonged speech that obstructs progress in a legislative assembly.

qs.q: The parliament voted to _____ the outdated colonial legislation.
qs.e: 'Do away with' means abolish or eliminate.

qs.q: The diplomatic talks _____ when neither party agreed to compromise.
qs.e: 'Break down' means fail or collapse.

qs.q: The government plans to _____ a new tax framework for foreign investors.
qs.e: 'Bring in' means introduce.

qs.q: Protesters gathered at the capital to demand that the president _____.
qs.e: 'Step down' means resign from an office or position.

qs.q: The constitutional amendment was passed in accordance _____ established parliamentary rules.
qs.e: 'In accordance' collocates with 'with' ('in accordance with').

qs.q: The ambassador was exempted _____ paying local income taxes under diplomatic immunity.
qs.e: 'Exempted' takes the preposition 'from'.

qs.q: Citizens were warned against engaging in actions detrimental _____ national security.
qs.e: 'Detrimental' takes the preposition 'to'.

qs.q: Which of the following words contains the vowel sound /eɪ/ as in 'state'?
qs.e: 'Reign', 'rain', and 'veil' all contain the diphthong /eɪ/.

qs.q: Identify the word that features the short open back unrounded vowel sound /ɒ/ as in 'lot'.
qs.e: 'Was' (/wɒz/) features the short vowel sound /ɒ/.

qs.q: Which word contains the diphthong /aɪ/ as in 'vote'?
qs.e: 'Vice' (/vaɪs/) contains the diphthong /aɪ/.

qs.q: Which word features the diphthong /aʊ/ as in 'town'?
qs.e: 'Crown' (/kraʊn/) contains the diphthong /aʊ/.

qs.q: In which word is the consonant sound /z/ present as in 'zoo'?
qs.e: The verb 'close' (/kləʊz/) ends in the voiced alveolar fricative /z/.

qs.q: Which word contains the voiceless glottal fricative /h/?
qs.e: 'Who' (/huː/) begins with the sound /h/, whereas 'hour', 'honor', and 'heir' have silent 'h'.

qs.q: Identify the word containing the voiced velar plosive /g/.
qs.e: 'Guarantee' (/ˌɡær.ənˈtiː/) begins with the hard 'g' sound /g/.

qs.q: Which word features a silent letter 'p'?
qs.e: Initial 'p' in 'psalm' (/sɑːm/) before 's' is silent.

qs.q: Identify the sentence that matches emphatic stress on 'BILL': 'The senate passed the BILL yesterday.'
o: Did the senate pass the bill last week?
Did the house pass the bill yesterday?
Did the senate reject the bill yesterday?
Did the senate pass the motion yesterday?
qs.e: Emphatic stress on 'BILL' contrasts the legislative item.

qs.q: Which word rhymes with 'reign'?
qs.e: 'Reign' (/reɪn/) rhymes with 'plain' (/pleɪn/).

qs.q: Select the word that rhymes with 'law'?
qs.e: 'Law' (/lɔː/) rhymes with 'saw' (/sɔː/).

qs.q: Identify the underlined clause in: 'Although the candidate campaigned vigorously, he failed to secure the required majority.'
qs.e: 'Although the candidate campaigned vigorously' expresses concession.

qs.q: Choose the passive voice form of: 'The president signed the decree into law.'
o: The president signs the decree into law.
The decree is signed into law by the president.
The decree had been signed into law by president.
The decree was signed into law by the president.
qs.e: Simple past active 'signed' becomes 'was signed' in passive voice.

qs.q: Whom did the electorate select as _____ representative in parliament?
qs.e: Possessive adjective 'their' modifies 'representative'.

qs.q: The bill was _____ debated before being put to a final vote.
qs.e: Adverb 'intensely' modifies the verb 'debated'.

qs.q: The sovereign monarch rarely interferes in daily governance, _____?
qs.e: 'Rarely' gives a negative sense, so the tag is positive ('does he').

qs.q: It is essential that the returning officer _____ impartial throughout the voting process.
qs.e: Subjunctive mood after 'essential that' takes base verb 'remain'.

qs.q: The playwright's poignant drama left the theater audience visibly moved.
qs.e: 'Poignant' means evoking a keen sense of sadness or regret; touching.

qs.q: The editor made extensive revisions to refine the author's crude draft manuscript.
qs.e: 'Crude' means in a natural or raw state; unpolished.

qs.q: The novel portrays a vivid picture of life in pre-colonial West Africa.
qs.e: 'Vivid' means producing powerful feelings or strong, clear images in the mind; graphic.

qs.q: The critic gave a glowing review of the lead actor's exemplary performance.
qs.e: 'Exemplary' means serving as a desirable model; praiseworthy.

qs.q: The protagonist in the tragic play was portrayed as an exceptionally noble leader.
qs.e: The main character is the 'protagonist'; the principal opponent is the 'antagonist'.

qs.q: The theater director praised the actors for their spontaneous dialogue during rehearsals.
qs.e: 'Spontaneous' means performed as a result of sudden impulse; its opposite is 'rehearsed' or planned.

qs.q: The narrative style of the epic poem is intentionally intricate and multilayered.
qs.e: 'Intricate' means very complicated or detailed; its antonym is 'simple'.

qs.q: The drama performance reached a euphoric climax that thrilled the entire audience.
qs.e: The 'climax' is the most intense point; its opposite is an 'anticlimax'.

qs.q: Neither the director nor the lead actors _____ available for the press conference after the premiere.
qs.e: With 'neither... nor', agreement is with closer plural noun 'actors' ('were').

qs.q: The troupe of traveling actors _____ performing at the national theater tonight.
qs.e: Collective noun 'troupe' acting as a single entity takes singular verb 'is'.

qs.q: Dramatic literature _____ studied as a major branch of humanistic studies.
qs.e: 'Dramatic literature' takes singular verb 'is'.

qs.q: Either the scriptwriter or the prop managers _____ mistaken about the scene setting.
qs.e: Agreement with closer plural noun 'managers' requires 'are'.

qs.q: Two hours _____ the standard duration for a five-act theatrical play.
qs.e: Time durations taken as a single unit take singular verb 'is'.

qs.q: By the time the curtain rose, the auditorium _____ packed to full capacity.
qs.e: Past perfect 'had been' expresses state existing prior to another past event ('rose').

qs.q: If the novelist _____ published her autobiography earlier, she would have gained international acclaim.
qs.e: Third conditional pattern requires 'had + past participle'.

qs.q: The dramatic club _____ rehearsing the Shakespearean play for six consecutive weeks.
qs.e: Present perfect continuous 'has been' indicates ongoing action.

qs.q: The theater critic urged that the director _____ the controversial final scene.
qs.e: Subjunctive base verb 'modify' follows 'urged that the director...'.

qs.q: The literary device in 'The stars danced merrily in the night sky' is _____.
qs.e: Attributing dancing human behavior to stars is personification.

qs.q: When an actor is told to 'break a leg' before going on stage, it means _____.
qs.e: 'Break a leg' is a well-known theatrical idiom wishing good luck.

qs.q: The expression 'parting is such sweet sorrow' is an example of _____.
qs.e: Combining opposite feelings ('sweet' and 'sorrow') side-by-side forms an oxymoron.

qs.q: In drama, a long speech delivered by a character alone on stage expressing inner thoughts is a _____.
qs.e: A soliloquy is an act of speaking one's thoughts aloud when alone or regardless of any hearers.

qs.q: The introductory section or speech delivered at the beginning of a literary work or play is the _____.
qs.e: A prologue is a separate introductory section of a literary or musical work.

qs.q: A dramatic work marked by exaggerated emotion, stereotyped characters, and sensational plotlines is a _____.
qs.e: Melodrama features exaggerated characters and exciting events intended to appeal to emotions.

qs.q: In literary criticism, the use of humor, irony, exaggeration, or ridicule to expose human folly or vice is _____.
qs.e: Satire is the use of humor or irony to expose and criticize people's stupidity or vices.

qs.q: A story, poem, or picture that can be interpreted to reveal a hidden moral or political meaning is an _____.
qs.e: An allegory is a story with a hidden symbolic meaning.

qs.q: The lead actress decided to _____ from the production owing to creative differences.
qs.e: 'Pull out' means withdraw from an agreement or participation.

qs.q: The published biography failed to _____ to the expectations of literary critics.
qs.e: 'Live up to' means fulfill expectations.

qs.q: The theater director brought in an expert to _____ the stage lighting set.
qs.e: 'Set up' means assemble or configure equipment.

qs.q: The novel's intricate plot gradually _____ as the story progresses.
qs.e: 'Unfold' means reveal or develop gradually.

qs.q: The play was adapted _____ a famous historical novel written in the nineteenth century.
qs.e: 'Adapted' takes 'from' when referring to source material ('adapted from').

qs.q: The actor was commended _____ his flawless delivery of Shakespearean verse.
qs.e: 'Commended' takes the preposition 'for' ('commended for something').

qs.q: Her performance was superior _____ that of her co-stars in the tragic opera.
qs.e: Adjectives ending in '-ior' like 'superior' take 'to', not 'than'.

qs.q: Which of the following words contains the diphthong /aɪ/ as in 'light'?
qs.e: 'Sight', 'site', and 'cite' are homophones containing /aɪ/.

qs.q: Identify the word that features the short open-mid front unrounded vowel sound /e/ as in 'set'.
qs.e: 'Friend' (/frend/) features the short vowel sound /e/.

qs.q: Which word contains the diphthong /eə/ as in 'fair'?
qs.e: 'Stair' (/steər/) contains the diphthong /eə/.

qs.q: Which word features the long central vowel sound /ɜː/ as in 'furred'?
qs.e: 'Heard' (/hɜːd/) contains the long central vowel sound /ɜː/.

qs.q: In which word is the consonant sound /dʒ/ present as in 'gem'?
qs.e: 'Ginger' (/ˈdʒɪn.dʒər/) begins and ends its middle syllable with /dʒ/.

qs.q: Which word contains the voiceless postalveolar fricative /ʃ/?
qs.e: 'Precious' (/ˈpreʃ.əs/) contains the consonant sound /ʃ/.

qs.q: Identify the word containing the voiced dental fricative /ð/ as in 'this'.
qs.e: 'Smooth', 'soothe', and 'seethe' all end in the voiced dental fricative /ð/.

qs.q: Identify the sentence that matches emphatic stress on 'TRAGEDY': 'The play was a TRAGEDY, not a comedy.'
qs.e: Emphatic stress on 'TRAGEDY' contrasts the dramatic genre.

qs.q: Which word rhymes with 'rhyme'?
qs.e: 'Rhyme' (/raɪm/) rhymes with 'thyme' (/taɪm/).

qs.q: Select the word that rhymes with 'scene'?
qs.e: 'Scene' (/siːn/) rhymes with 'seen' (/siːn/) and 'lean' (/liːn/).

qs.q: Identify the underlined clause in: 'What surprised the critics was the young actor's emotional depth.'
qs.e: 'What surprised the critics' acts as subject of 'was', making it a noun clause.

qs.q: Choose the correct passive form of: 'The author wrote an outstanding trilogy.'
o: The author was writing an outstanding trilogy.
An outstanding trilogy is written by the author.
An outstanding trilogy had been written by author.
An outstanding trilogy was written by the author.
qs.e: Simple past active 'wrote' becomes 'was written' in passive voice.

qs.q: The award was presented to the playwright _____ script received unanimous praise.
qs.e: Possessive relative pronoun 'whose' modifies 'script'.

qs.q: The tragedy ended _____ with the downfall of the heroic protagonist.
qs.e: Adverb 'tragically' modifies the verb 'ended'.

qs.q: The audience barely moved throughout the tense theatrical performance, _____?
qs.e: 'Barely' provides a negative sense, requiring a positive tag ('did they').

qs.q: The director insisted that every actor _____ on stage thirty minutes before curtain call.
qs.e: Subjunctive base verb 'be' follows 'insisted that...'.

qs.q: The novel portrays the struggles of working-class families.
qs.e: 'Portrays' means depicts or represents.

qs.q: The dramatic production received overwhelming praise from national newspapers.
qs.e: Opposite of 'praise' is 'criticism' or 'condemnation'.

qs.q: The investigative journalist published an insightful article on environmental degradation.
qs.e: 'Insightful' means having or showing a accurate and deep understanding; perceptive.

qs.q: The editorial board issued a stern warning against yellow journalism.
qs.e: 'Stern' means serious and unrelenting; severe.

qs.q: The publisher agreed to subsidize the printing costs of the academic journal.
qs.e: 'Subsidize' means support financially; fund.

qs.q: The newspaper columnist delivered a trenchant critique of the new economic policy.
qs.e: 'Trenchant' means vigorous or incisive in expression or style.

qs.q: The press secretary tried to suppress the leaked memorandum before publication.
qs.e: 'Suppress' means prevent the development or publication of; its opposite is 'release' or publish.

qs.q: The magazine article contained several slanderous statements about the politician.
qs.e: 'Slanderous' means false and malicious; its opposite is 'laudatory' or complimentary.

qs.q: The author chose a pseudonymous identity to hide his real name from the public.
qs.e: 'Pseudonymous' means writing under a false name; its antonym is 'authentic' or real-named.

qs.q: The newspaper retracted its sensational front-page headline following public outcry.
qs.e: 'Retracted' means drew back or withdrew; its opposite is 'confirmed' or reaffirmed.

qs.q: Neither the chief editor nor the press reporters _____ present at the press conference.
qs.e: Agreement with closer plural subject 'reporters' requires 'were'.

qs.q: The board of publishers _____ meeting to approve the upcoming autumn catalog.
qs.e: Collective noun 'board' as a single entity takes singular verb 'is'.

qs.q: Journalism _____ considered the fourth estate in democratic societies.
qs.e: 'Journalism' takes singular verb 'is'.

qs.q: Either the chief editor or his assistants _____ responsible for proofreading the final page proofs.
qs.e: Agreement with closer plural noun 'assistants' ('are').

qs.q: Fifty thousand copies of the daily newspaper _____ printed every morning.
qs.e: Plural noun 'copies' takes plural verb 'are'.

qs.q: By the time the press conference commenced, the editor _____ verified the source.
qs.e: Past perfect 'had' expresses an action completed prior to another past event.

qs.q: If the newspaper _____ published the retracting statement earlier, libel charges would have been avoided.
qs.e: Third conditional requires 'had + past participle'.

qs.q: The publishing house _____ printing high school textbooks for over three decades.
qs.e: Present perfect continuous 'has been' indicates ongoing action.

qs.q: The editor-in-chief requested that every correspondent _____ their news story before noon.
qs.e: Subjunctive base verb 'submit' follows 'requested that...'.

qs.q: The statement 'The pen is mightier than the sword' is an example of _____.
qs.e: 'Pen' stands for written word and 'sword' for military force (metonymy).

qs.q: When news is described as 'hot off the press', it means it is _____.
o: printed using heated printing press plates
very recently printed and newly released
full of inaccurate and sensational claims
qs.e: 'Hot off the press' means newly printed or freshly published.

qs.q: The phrase 'a printed silence' is an example of _____.
qs.e: Combining contradictory terms side-by-side forms an oxymoron.

qs.q: In publishing, a written work submitted by an author to a publisher before printing is a _____.
qs.e: A manuscript is an author's text that has not yet been published.

qs.q: The trial impression of printed matter taken for making corrections before final printing is a _____.
qs.e: A proof is a trial print taken for correction or examination.

qs.q: The exclusive legal right given to an originator to print, publish, or record literary material is _____.
qs.e: Copyright is the exclusive legal right to reproduce, publish, sell, or distribute matter.

qs.q: In journalism, a published false statement that is damaging to a person's reputation is _____.
qs.e: Libel is a published false statement in written form that damages reputation.

qs.q: The style, arrangement, and appearance of printed matter on a page is known as _____.
qs.e: Typography is the art and technique of arranging type to make written language legible and appealing.

qs.q: The daily newspaper plans to _____ a special anniversary supplement next Sunday.
qs.e: 'Bring out' means publish or produce.

qs.q: The editor had to _____ several non-essential paragraphs to fit the page layout.
qs.e: 'Cut out' means remove or excise.

qs.q: The young author decided to _____ his manuscript after receiving critical feedback.
qs.e: 'Write over' / rewrite means revise or redraft.

qs.q: The publishing company refused to _____ to intimidation from corrupt politicians.
qs.e: 'Bow down' / yield means submit or surrender.

qs.q: The author held the copyright _____ all her published novels.
qs.e: 'Copyright' takes 'on' or 'to' ('copyright on/to something').

qs.q: The magazine reporter was charged _____ libel after publishing unverified allegations.
qs.e: Legal charge takes 'with' ('charged with libel').

qs.q: The editor insisted _____ verifying all quotes prior to publication.
qs.e: The verb 'insist' correctly collocates with the preposition 'on' ('insisted on verifying').

qs.q: Which of the following words contains the diphthong /əʊ/ as in 'quote'?
qs.e: 'Note' (/nəʊt/) contains the diphthong /əʊ/.

qs.q: Identify the word that features the short open front unrounded vowel sound /æ/ as in 'press'.
qs.e: 'Plait' (/plæt/) contains the short front unrounded vowel sound /æ/.

qs.q: Which word contains the diphthong /eɪ/ as in 'page'?
qs.e: 'Paper' (/ˈpeɪ.pər/) contains the diphthong /eɪ/.

qs.q: Which word features the short open-mid back rounded vowel sound /ɒ/ as in 'font'?
qs.e: 'Wash' (/wɒʃ/) contains the vowel sound /ɒ/.

qs.q: In which word is the consonant sound /f/ present as in 'proof'?
qs.e: 'Paragraph', 'phantom', and 'phase' all contain the consonant sound /f/.

qs.q: Which word contains the voiced velar plosive /g/?
qs.e: 'Galley' (/ˈɡæl.i/) begins with the hard sound /g/.

qs.q: Identify the word containing the voiceless dental fricative /θ/.
qs.e: 'Theme' (/θiːm/) begins with the voiceless dental fricative /θ/.

qs.q: Which word features a silent letter 'g'?
qs.e: The letter 'g' in 'campaign' (/kæmˈpeɪn/) is silent.

qs.q: Identify the sentence that matches emphatic stress on 'PROOF': 'The editor corrected the final PROOF.'
o: Did the editor correct the final manuscript?
Did the manager correct the final proof?
Did the editor discard the final proof?
Did the editor correct the first draft?
qs.e: Emphatic stress on 'PROOF' contrasts the document state.

qs.q: Which word rhymes with 'press'?
qs.e: 'Press' (/pres/) rhymes with 'dress' (/dres/).

qs.q: Select the word that rhymes with 'type'?
qs.e: 'Type' (/taɪp/) rhymes with 'ripe' (/raɪp/).

qs.q: Identify the underlined clause in: 'Whenever a major news story breaks, the press room becomes hyperactive.'
qs.e: 'Whenever a major news story breaks' specifies time, making it an adverbial clause of time.

qs.q: Choose the correct passive form of: 'The journalist interviewed the foreign ambassador.'
o: The journalist was interviewing the ambassador.
The foreign ambassador is interviewed by the journalist.
The foreign ambassador had been interviewed by journalist.
The foreign ambassador was interviewed by the journalist.
qs.e: Simple past active 'interviewed' becomes 'was interviewed' in passive voice.

qs.q: The editor commended both the lead columnist and _____ for excellent coverage.
qs.e: Preposition 'and' after verb 'commended' takes objective pronoun 'her'.

qs.q: The newspaper was printed _____ on eco-friendly recycled paper.
qs.e: Adverb 'entirely' modifies the past participle 'printed'.

qs.q: The press secretary rarely refuses to answer journalists' questions, _____?
qs.e: 'Rarely' gives a negative sense, requiring a positive tag ('does he').

qs.q: The ethics committee recommended that the reporter _____ suspended immediately.
qs.e: Subjunctive base verb 'be' follows 'recommended that...'.

qs.q: The investigative reporter uncovered substantial evidence of fraud.
qs.e: 'Uncovered' means revealed.

qs.q: The ship's captain maintained a tranquil demeanor during the stormy voyage across the Atlantic.
qs.e: 'Tranquil' means free from disturbance; calm.

qs.q: The coast guard launched a swift search-and-rescue operation for the missing vessel.
qs.e: 'Swift' means happening quickly or moving at high speed; rapid.

qs.q: The cargo vessel was anchored in a sheltered harbor during the tempest.
qs.e: 'Sheltered' means protected from bad weather; safe.

qs.q: The harbor master gave explicit instructions regarding port navigation.
qs.e: 'Explicit' means stated clearly and in detail.

qs.q: The ocean waters near the coral reef were remarkably tranquil during sunset.
qs.e: 'Tranquil' means calm; its antonym is 'turbulent' or stormy.

qs.q: The freighter was fully laden with containerized goods for export.
qs.e: 'Laden' means heavily loaded; its opposite is 'empty' or unladen.

qs.q: The coast guard issued a warning about treacherous sea currents along the coastline.
qs.e: 'Treacherous' means dangerous or unstable; its opposite is 'safe'.

qs.q: The ancient wooden sailboat was still buoyant despite taking on water.
qs.e: 'Buoyant' means able to stay afloat; its opposite is 'sinking' or submerged.

qs.q: Neither the ship's captain nor the crew members _____ aware of the approaching storm.
qs.e: Agreement with closer plural noun 'members' requires 'were'.

qs.q: The fleet of naval vessels _____ anchored off the coast of Lagos.
qs.e: Collective noun 'fleet' as a single entity takes singular verb 'is'.

qs.q: Maritime navigation _____ a complex discipline requiring rigorous training.
qs.e: 'Maritime navigation' takes singular verb 'is'.

qs.q: Either the harbor pilot or the dockworkers _____ responsible for securing the vessel.
qs.e: Agreement with closer plural noun 'dockworkers' ('are').

qs.q: Ten nautical miles _____ considered a short distance for modern container ships.
qs.e: Distances treated as a single unit take singular verb 'is'.

qs.q: By the time the tugboat arrived, the stranded vessel _____ taken on water.
qs.e: Past perfect 'had' expresses action completed prior to another past event.

qs.q: If the lighthouse operator _____ signaled the distress warning earlier, the shipwreck would have been avoided.
qs.e: Third conditional requires 'had + past participle'.

qs.q: The shipping line _____ operating cargo vessels along the West African coast for fifty years.
qs.e: Present perfect continuous 'has been' indicates ongoing action.

qs.q: The maritime authority insisted that every vessel _____ safety lifeboats.
qs.e: Subjunctive base verb 'carry' follows 'insisted that...'.

qs.q: To 'stem the tide' means to _____.
o: measure the height of ocean sea waves
stop or slow down the progress of something undesirable
navigate a boat against strong river currents
build a stone barrier along a beach
qs.e: 'Stem the tide' means to stop or contain the increase of something negative.

qs.q: The expression 'in the same boat' means that people are _____.
o: traveling together on a passenger ferry
facing the same difficult circumstances or danger
working for the same shipping company
qs.e: 'In the same boat' means experiencing the same predicament or difficulty.

qs.q: When a ship is described as being 'plain sailing', it implies that the situation is _____.
o: slow and tedious owing to lack of wind
smooth, easy, and free from obstacles
dangerous due to shallow rocky waters
qs.e: 'Plain sailing' means smooth and straightforward progress.

qs.q: The literary device in 'The ocean roared like an angry beast' is a _____.
qs.e: Comparison using 'like' is a simile.

qs.q: In maritime navigation, the front structure or bow section of a ship is called the _____.
qs.e: The bow is the forward part of the hull of a ship or boat.

qs.q: The right-hand side of a vessel when facing forward toward the bow is termed _____.
qs.e: Starboard is the right side of a ship when facing forward.

qs.q: The left-hand side of a ship when facing forward toward the bow is called _____.
qs.e: Port is the left-hand side of a ship when facing forward.

qs.q: A heavy metal object attached to a cable and cast overboard to moor a vessel is an _____.
qs.e: An anchor is a heavy device dropped to the sea bed to restrict vessel motion.

qs.q: In shipping, heavy material placed low in a vessel to improve its stability is called _____.
qs.e: Ballast is heavy material used to provide stability to a vehicle or structure.

qs.q: The passenger ferry is scheduled to _____ at eight o'clock tomorrow.
qs.e: 'Set sail' means begin a sea voyage.

qs.q: The coast guard managed to _____ the damaged vessel safely into the harbor.
qs.e: 'Tow in' means pull a boat into harbor using a towline.

qs.q: Dense fog forced the captain to _____ the vessel outside the harbor entrance.
qs.e: 'Lay to' / lie to means stop a sailing vessel by heading into wind.

qs.q: The custom officers decided to _____ the cargo vessel for illegal contraband.
qs.e: 'Search through' means examine thoroughly.

qs.q: The vessel was anchored _____ the coast during the severe storm.
qs.e: 'Off the coast' is the correct prepositional collocation.

qs.q: The captain was charged _____ negligence following the collision at sea.
qs.e: Legal charge takes 'with'.

qs.q: Sailors must adhere _____ maritime safety regulations at all times.
qs.e: 'Adhere' takes 'to' ('adhere to rules').

qs.q: Which of the following words contains the vowel sound /ɔː/ as in 'port'?
qs.e: 'Shore' (/ʃɔːr/) contains the long open-mid back rounded vowel sound /ɔː/.

qs.q: Identify the word that features the short open back rounded vowel sound /ɒ/ as in 'dock'.
qs.e: 'Yacht' (/jɒt/) features the short vowel sound /ɒ/.

qs.q: Which word contains the diphthong /aʊ/ as in 'prow'?
qs.e: 'Prow' (/praʊ/) contains the diphthong /aʊ/.

qs.q: Which word features the long vowel sound /iː/ as in 'keel'?
qs.e: 'Quay' (/kiː/) contains the long vowel sound /iː/.

qs.q: In which word is the consonant sound /v/ present as in 'vessel'?
qs.e: 'Wave' (/weɪv/) ends in the voiced labiodental fricative /v/.

qs.q: Which word contains the voiceless alveolar plosive /t/?
qs.e: 'Yacht' (/jɒt/) ends in /t/, whereas 'doubt', 'debt', and 'subtle' have silent 'b' and audible /t/.

qs.q: Identify the word containing the velar nasal sound /ŋ/.
qs.e: 'Anchor' (/ˈæŋ.kər/) contains the velar nasal consonant sound /ŋ/.

qs.q: In which word is the letter 'l' silent?
qs.e: The letter 'l' in 'calm' (/kɑːm/) is silent.

qs.q: Which word features a silent letter 'w'?
qs.e: Initial 'w' before 'r' in 'wreck' (/rek/) is silent.

qs.q: Identify the sentence that matches emphatic stress on 'CAPTAIN': 'The CAPTAIN gave the order to drop anchor.'
o: Did the captain give the order to clear the deck?
Did the captain give the order to hoist sail?
Did the captain execute the order to drop anchor?
Did the sailor give the order to drop anchor?
qs.e: Emphatic stress on 'CAPTAIN' contrasts the person giving command.

qs.q: Which word rhymes with 'dock'?
qs.e: 'Dock' (/dɒk/) rhymes with 'lock', 'rock', and 'sock'.

qs.q: Select the word that rhymes with 'deck'?
qs.e: 'Deck' (/dek/) rhymes with 'wreck', 'check', and 'neck'.

qs.q: Identify the underlined clause in: 'Although the weather was severe, the ship reached the harbor safely.'
qs.e: 'Although the weather was severe' expresses concession.

qs.q: Choose the passive voice form of: 'The coast guard rescued the stranded sailors.'
o: The coast guard was rescuing the sailors.
The stranded sailors are rescued by the coast guard.
The stranded sailors had been rescued by coast guard.
The stranded sailors were rescued by the coast guard.
qs.e: Simple past active 'rescued' becomes 'were rescued' in passive voice.

qs.q: The captain assigned duty shifts to both the chief officer and _____.
qs.e: Preposition 'to' takes objective case pronoun 'me'.

qs.q: The container ship navigated _____ through the narrow maritime channel.
qs.e: Adverb 'cautiously' modifies verb 'navigated'.

qs.q: Ships rarely navigate through icebergs without modern sonar equipment, _____?
qs.e: 'Rarely' gives a negative sense, requiring positive tag 'do they'.

qs.q: The principal together with two vice-principals _____ just arrived.
qs.e: The verb agrees with the singular subject 'principal' after 'together with'.

qs.q: The judge described the witness's testimony as candid.
qs.e: 'Candid' means honest and straightforward; frank.

qs.q: The old man gave a lucid account of the events of 1960.
qs.e: 'Lucid' means easy to understand; clear.

qs.q: It is futile to argue with a man who has made up his mind.
qs.e: 'Futile' means producing no useful result; pointless.

qs.q: The principal urged the students to be prudent with their allowances.
qs.e: 'Prudent' means acting with care for the future.

qs.q: The medicine gave the patient instantaneous relief.
qs.e: 'Instantaneous' means happening at once; immediate.

qs.q: Her resolute refusal to cheat impressed everyone.
qs.e: 'Resolute' means admirably purposeful; firm.

qs.q: The students found the new topic abstruse.
qs.e: 'Abstruse' means hard to understand; difficult.

qs.q: The governor lauded the health workers for their dedication.
qs.e: 'Lauded' means praised highly.

qs.q: Rain is scarce in the northern savanna during the dry season.
qs.e: 'Scarce' means insufficient or rare.

qs.q: The chairman's remarks were pertinent to the agenda.
qs.e: 'Pertinent' means directly relating to the matter.

qs.q: The pupils were jubilant when the results were released.
qs.e: 'Jubilant' means showing great joy.

qs.q: A vigilant security man stopped the intruder at the gate.
qs.e: 'Vigilant' means keeping careful watch.

qs.q: The new manager was meticulous in checking the accounts.
qs.e: 'Meticulous' means showing great attention to detail.

qs.q: The narrow bush paths became impervious after the heavy rains.
qs.e: 'Impervious' here means impossible to pass through.

qs.q: The coach commended the team for its valiant effort.
qs.e: 'Valiant' means possessing courage; brave.

qs.q: Public speaking once filled her with trepidation.
qs.e: 'Trepidation' means anxiety or fear.

qs.q: The beggar looked forlorn at the market junction.
qs.e: 'Forlorn' means sad and abandoned.

qs.q: The scientist's explanation was succinct.
qs.e: 'Succinct' means briefly and clearly expressed; concise.

qs.q: Nigerian jollof rice is renowned across West Africa.
qs.e: 'Renowned' means widely known and admired.

qs.q: The two communities finally reached an amicable settlement.
qs.e: 'Amicable' means done in a spirit of friendliness.

qs.q: Soldiers must endure rigorous training.
qs.e: 'Rigorous' means extremely thorough and demanding.

qs.q: The sun was scorching at midday in the desert.
qs.e: 'Scorching' means intensely hot.

qs.q: Her smile was infectious, and soon everyone was laughing.
qs.e: 'Infectious' here means spreading quickly to others.

qs.q: The company's fortunes dwindled after the fire.
qs.e: 'Dwindled' means decreased gradually.

qs.q: The manager tried to placate the angry customer.
qs.e: 'Placate' means to make someone less angry; appease.

qs.q: The election results were annulled by the court.
qs.e: 'Annulled' means declared officially invalid; cancelled.

qs.q: He was elated when he won the scholarship.
qs.e: 'Elated' means extremely happy.

qs.q: The toddler was inseparable from her teddy bear.
qs.e: 'Inseparable' means unable to be separated from.

qs.q: The teacher found the noise intolerable.
qs.e: 'Intolerable' means impossible to endure.

qs.q: Wise investors are averse to unnecessary risks.
qs.e: 'Averse to' means having a strong dislike of.

qs.q: The diplomat was fluent in three languages.
qs.e: 'Fluent' means speaking smoothly and easily.

qs.q: Farmers welcomed the abundant rainfall this season.
qs.e: 'Abundant' means existing in large quantities.

qs.q: The chairman rebuked the clerk for lateness.
qs.e: 'Rebuked' means criticised sharply; reprimanded.

qs.q: The thief was caught in the act and handed over to the police.
qs.e: 'Caught' here means seized; detained.

qs.q: The essay contained several glaring errors.
qs.e: 'Glaring' means extremely obvious and bad.

qs.q: She was reluctant to leave the quiet village.
qs.e: 'Reluctant' means hesitant and unwilling.

qs.q: The king's decree was final.
qs.e: 'Decree' is an official order; proclamation.

qs.q: Measures were taken to curb examination malpractice.
qs.e: 'Curb' means to restrain; check.

qs.q: The accountant detected a discrepancy in the figures.
qs.e: 'Discrepancy' means a difference between things that should match.

qs.q: The volunteers received rudimentary training before deployment.
qs.e: 'Rudimentary' means elementary; basic.

qs.q: The late rain aggravated the farmers' plight.
qs.e: 'Aggravated' means made worse.

qs.q: The decision was taken unanimously by the council.
qs.e: 'Unanimously' means agreed by everyone.

qs.q: The report gave a comprehensive review of the project.
qs.e: 'Comprehensive' means covering all aspects.

qs.q: Astride his bicycle, the messenger rode swiftly to the palace.
qs.e: 'Swiftly' means at high speed; quickly.

qs.q: The principal was jovial throughout the meeting.
qs.e: 'Jovial' means merry; its opposite is gloomy.

qs.q: The nurse was very gentle with the newborn.
qs.e: 'Gentle' means mild; its opposite is rough.

qs.q: The examination questions were straightforward.
qs.e: 'Straightforward' means easy; its opposite is complicated.

qs.q: The room was bright and airy.
qs.e: The opposite of 'bright' is 'dark'.

qs.q: He is notorious for breaking promises.
qs.e: 'Notorious' means famous for bad deeds; its opposite is reputable.

qs.q: The soldiers advanced toward the enemy camp.
qs.e: 'Advanced' means moved forward; its opposite is retreated.

qs.q: The fruit was sweet and juicy.
qs.e: The opposite of 'sweet' is 'bitter'.

qs.q: The herdsman was generous with his milk.
