qs.e: Area of a square = side² = 8² = 64 cm².

qs.q: A square has sides of 9 cm. Find its area.
qs.e: Area of a square = side² = 9² = 81 cm².

qs.q: A square has sides of 10 cm. Find its area.
qs.e: Area of a square = side² = 10² = 100 cm².

qs.q: A square has sides of 11 cm. Find its area.
qs.e: Area of a square = side² = 11² = 121 cm².

qs.q: Which of the following physical quantities is a vector quantity?
qs.e: Velocity has both magnitude and direction, making it a vector quantity, whereas mass, speed, and time are scalar quantities.

qs.q: What is the standard SI unit of acceleration?
qs.e: Acceleration is defined as the rate of change of velocity per unit time, measured in meters per second squared (m/s2).

qs.q: A car travels a distance of 150 meters in 10 seconds at uniform speed. What is its speed?
qs.e: Speed is distance divided by time: 150 m / 10 s = 15 m/s.

qs.q: What physical quantity is represented by the slope of a distance-time graph?
qs.e: The gradient or slope of a distance against time graph represents the speed of the moving body.

qs.q: An object falls freely from rest near the surface of the Earth. Neglecting air resistance, what is its acceleration?
qs.e: Under free fall in a vacuum near Earth's surface, all objects accelerate downward at approximately 9.8 m/s2 (acceleration due to gravity).

qs.q: What is the angular speed of a body rotating at 60 revolutions per minute?
qs.e: 60 rpm = 1 revolution per second. One revolution corresponds to 2 pi radians, so angular speed omega = 2 pi rad/s.

qs.q: A runner completes one full lap of a 400-meter circular track and returns to the starting line. What is the displacement?
qs.e: Displacement is the straight-line distance between initial and final position. Returning to the starting line gives a net displacement of 0 m.

qs.q: A car accelerates uniformly from rest to a speed of 20 m/s in 5 seconds. Calculate its acceleration.
qs.e: Acceleration a = (v - u) / t = (20 - 0) / 5 = 4 m/s2.

qs.q: A vehicle moving at 30 m/s decelerates uniformly to rest in 6 seconds. What is the magnitude of the deceleration?
qs.e: Deceleration magnitude a = (u - v) / t = (30 - 0) / 6 = 5 m/s2.

qs.q: What is the area under a velocity-time graph for a given time interval equal to?
qs.e: The area enclosed under a velocity-time graph represents the distance or displacement covered by the moving object.

qs.q: A particle moves along a straight line with initial velocity 4 m/s and constant acceleration 3 m/s2. Find its speed after 4 seconds.
A stone is dropped from the top of a tower and takes 3 seconds to reach the ground. Assuming g = 10 m/s2, calculate the height of the tower.
qs.e: Using height h = ut + 0.5 g t2: u = 0, so h = 0.5 * 10 * 3^2 = 5 * 9 = 45 m.

qs.q: A ball is thrown vertically upwards with a speed of 25 m/s. Taking g = 10 m/s2, how long does it take to reach maximum height?
qs.e: At maximum height, final velocity v = 0. Using v = u - gt: 0 = 25 - 10t, so t = 2.5 s.

qs.q: A wheel of radius 0.5 meters rotates with a constant linear speed of 10 m/s at its rim. What is its centripetal acceleration?
qs.e: Centripetal acceleration a = v2 / r = (10)^2 / 0.5 = 100 / 0.5 = 200 m/s2.

qs.q: A projectile is fired at an angle of 30 deg to the horizontal. Which component of its velocity remains constant throughout flight (ignoring air resistance)?
qs.e: In projectile motion without air resistance, no horizontal force acts, so the horizontal velocity component u cos(theta) remains constant.

qs.q: At what angle of projection to the horizontal is the maximum horizontal range achieved for a given launch speed?
qs.e: Horizontal range R = (u2 sin 2 theta) / g. Range is maximum when sin(2 theta) = 1, which occurs at 2 theta = 90 deg, so theta = 45 degrees.

qs.q: A cyclist covers 60 km in 2 hours and then 40 km in the next 3 hours. What is the average speed for the entire journey?
qs.e: Average speed = Total distance / Total time = (60 + 40) / (2 + 3) = 100 / 5 = 20 km/h.

qs.q: A bullet decelerates uniformly from 400 m/s to 100 m/s over a distance of 0.5 meters in a block of wood. Determine its deceleration magnitude.
A toy car moves around a circular track of radius 2 meters in 4 seconds at uniform speed. What is its linear speed?
qs.e: Linear speed v = 2 pi r / T = 2 * 3.1416 * 2 / 4 = 3.1416 m/s approx 3.14 m/s.

qs.q: A body starts from rest and moves with uniform acceleration of 2 m/s2 for 8 seconds. Calculate the distance covered.
A train starting from rest accelerates uniformly at 1.5 m/s2 until it reaches a velocity of 30 m/s. How far does it travel during this acceleration?
An object is thrown vertically upward with an initial velocity of 40 m/s. Taking g = 10 m/s2, calculate the maximum height reached.
qs.e: At maximum height v = 0. Using v2 = u2 - 2gh: 0 = 40^2 - 2(10)h => 20h = 1600 => h = 80 m.

qs.q: A projectile is launched with a speed of 50 m/s at an angle of 30 deg above the horizontal. Taking g = 10 m/s2, find its total time of flight.
qs.e: Time of flight T = (2 u sin theta) / g = (2 * 50 * sin 30 deg) / 10 = (100 * 0.5) / 10 = 5.0 s.

qs.q: A ball projected horizontally from the edge of a cliff 20 meters high lands 40 meters from the base of the cliff. Taking g = 10 m/s2, find the initial launch speed.
qs.e: Vertical height h = 0.5 g t2 => 20 = 5 t2 => t = 2 s. Horizontal speed u_x = range / t = 40 / 2 = 20 m/s.

qs.q: A body moving along a straight line accelerates uniformly from 10 m/s to 30 m/s while covering a distance of 100 meters. Find its acceleration.
A stone thrown vertically upwards returns to the ground after 6 seconds. Taking g = 10 m/s2, what was its initial launch speed?
qs.e: Total flight time T = 2u / g => 6 = 2u / 10 => 2u = 60 => u = 30 m/s.

qs.q: An aircraft flies in a horizontal circle of radius 500 meters at a constant speed of 100 m/s. What centripetal acceleration does it experience?
qs.e: Centripetal acceleration a = v2 / r = (100)^2 / 500 = 10000 / 500 = 20 m/s2.

qs.q: A car accelerating uniformly from rest covers 20 meters in the first 2 seconds. What distance will it cover in the next 2 seconds?
qs.e: s1 = 0.5 a (2)^2 => 20 = 2a => a = 10 m/s2. Total distance in 4 s: s_total = 0.5 * 10 * 4^2 = 80 m. Distance in next 2 s = 80 - 20 = 60 m.

qs.q: A projectile launched at 40 m/s at 45 deg to the horizontal reaches its apex. Taking g = 10 m/s2, what is the magnitude of its velocity at the apex?
qs.e: At the apex, vertical velocity component is zero, so velocity equals horizontal component: u cos 45 deg = 40 * (sqrt(2)/2) approx 28.28 m/s.

qs.q: A marble rolls off a horizontal table of height 1.25 meters with speed 4 m/s. Taking g = 10 m/s2, how far horizontally from the table edge does it land?
qs.e: Time to fall: h = 0.5 g t2 => 1.25 = 5 t2 => t2 = 0.25 => t = 0.5 s. Horizontal range = u * t = 4 * 0.5 = 2 m.

qs.q: A car moving at 20 m/s applies brakes and comes to rest after travelling 40 meters. What was the average deceleration during braking?
A body rotates in a circle of radius 4 meters with a constant period of 2 seconds. Determine its angular velocity.
qs.e: Angular velocity omega = 2 pi / T = 2 * 3.1416 / 2 = 3.1416 rad/s approx 3.14 rad/s.

qs.q: A speed boat accelerates uniformly from 5 m/s to 25 m/s in 10 seconds. Calculate the distance travelled in this time interval.
A stone dropped from a bridge hits the water after 4 seconds. Taking g = 9.8 m/s2, calculate the height of the bridge above water.
A projectile is launched with velocity 60 m/s at an angle of 60 deg above the horizontal. Taking g = 10 m/s2, calculate its maximum height.
qs.e: u_y = u sin 60 deg = 60 * (sqrt(3)/2) = 30 sqrt(3) approx 51.96 m/s. Max height H = u_y^2 / (2g) = (30 sqrt(3))^2 / 20 = 2700 / 20 = 135 m.

qs.q: A missile is fired with initial velocity 100 m/s at 30 deg to the horizontal over level ground. Taking g = 10 m/s2, find its horizontal range.
qs.e: Range R = (u2 sin 2 theta) / g = (10000 * sin 60 deg) / 10 = 1000 * 0.866025 approx 866 m.

qs.q: A body covers 12 meters in the 3rd second of its motion and 20 meters in the 5th second under uniform acceleration from rest. Find its acceleration.
qs.e: Distance in nth second s_n = u + a(n - 0.5). s5 - s3 = a(4.5 - 2.5) = 2a = 20 - 12 = 8 => a = 4 m/s2.

qs.q: A ball dropped from a height of 45 meters bounces off a hard floor, losing 20 percent of its kinetic energy upon impact. Taking g = 10 m/s2, to what height does it rebound?
qs.e: Rebound height is proportional to remaining energy: h_new = 0.80 * 45 = 36 m.

qs.q: A centrifuge drum of radius 0.2 meters accelerates from rest to 1200 revolutions per minute in 6 seconds. Calculate its angular acceleration.
qs.e: omega_final = 1200 * 2 pi / 60 = 40 pi approx 125.66 rad/s. Angular acceleration alpha = omega / t = 40 pi / 6 = 20.94 rad/s2.

qs.q: Two cars A and B move along parallel tracks in the same direction. Car A moves at a constant speed of 25 m/s while Car B accelerates from rest at 2 m/s2. How long does it take B to overtake A?
qs.e: Displacement of A = 25t. Displacement of B = 0.5(2)t2 = t2. Overtaking when t2 = 25t => t = 25 s.

qs.q: A stone thrown horizontally at 15 m/s from top of a cliff hits the ground at an angle of 45 deg to the horizontal. Taking g = 10 m/s2, what is the height of the cliff?
qs.e: Impact angle 45 deg implies vertical speed v_y = v_x = 15 m/s. Since v_y = gt, t = 15/10 = 1.5 s. Height h = 0.5 g t2 = 5 * (1.5)^2 = 11.25 m.

qs.q: An elevator ascends from rest with acceleration 2 m/s2 for 4 s, moves at constant speed for 8 s, and decelerates to rest at 4 m/s2. Total distance covered is:
A particle moves in a circle of radius 5 meters such that its linear speed increases at a constant rate of 3 m/s2. At the moment its speed is 10 m/s, what is the magnitude of total acceleration?
qs.e: Tangential accel a_t = 3 m/s2. Centripetal accel a_c = v2/r = 100/5 = 20 m/s2. Total a = sqrt(3^2 + 20^2) = sqrt(9 + 400) = sqrt(409) approx 20.22 m/s2.

qs.q: A cannonball is fired at 200 m/s at an angle of 30 deg above horizontal from a 120 m high cliff. Taking g = 10 m/s2, find its total time of flight.
A train decelerates uniformly from 36 m/s to 12 m/s while covering a distance of 360 meters. How much further will it travel before coming to complete rest?
A projectile fired from ground level at angle theta has horizontal range R and max height H. If R = 4H, what is the angle of projection theta?
qs.e: Range R = 4H / tan theta => tan theta = 4H/R. Since R = 4H, tan theta = 1, so theta = 45 degrees.

qs.q: A stone is dropped into a deep well, and the sound of the splash is heard 3.31 seconds later. Taking g = 10 m/s2 and speed of sound = 340 m/s, find the depth of the well.
qs.e: For h = 50 m: fall time t1 = sqrt(2*50/10) = sqrt(10) approx 3.162 s. Sound travel time t2 = 50 / 340 approx 0.147 s. Total time = 3.162 + 0.147 = 3.309 approx 3.31 s.

qs.q: A vehicle accelerates from rest at constant rate alpha for time t1, then decelerates at constant rate beta to rest in time t2. If total distance covered is S, total time T is given by:
qs.e: Max velocity V = alpha t1 = beta t2. Total time T = t1 + t2 = V(1/alpha + 1/beta). Total distance S = 0.5 V T => V = 2S/T. Substituting V gives T = sqrt(2S(alpha + beta) / (alpha * beta)).

qs.q: A particle moves in a plane with position coordinates x(t) = 3 t2 + 2 and y(t) = 4 t2 - 5. What is the magnitude of its velocity at t = 2 seconds?
qs.e: v_x = dx/dt = 6t. At t=2, v_x = 12 m/s. v_y = dy/dt = 8t. At t=2, v_y = 16 m/s. Speed v = sqrt(12^2 + 16^2) = sqrt(144 + 256) = sqrt(400) = 20 m/s.

qs.q: A banking angle theta for a curved road of radius 80 meters allows a car to negotiate the turn at 20 m/s without relying on friction. Taking g = 10 m/s2, find tan theta.
qs.e: For ideal banking without friction, tan theta = v2 / (r * g) = 20^2 / (80 * 10) = 400 / 800 = 0.50.

qs.q: Which of the following physical quantities is classified as a scalar quantity?
qs.e: Electric potential has magnitude only (measured in volts) and no directional component, making it a scalar quantity.

qs.q: What is the SI unit of angular velocity?
qs.e: Angular velocity is defined as the rate of change of angular displacement per unit time, measured in rad/s.

qs.q: Which instrument is most suitable for measuring the internal diameter of a small test tube accurately?
qs.e: Vernier calipers are equipped with internal jaws designed specifically to measure internal diameters of tubes.

qs.q: A car accelerates uniformly from rest at a rate of 2.5 m/s2. What is its speed after 8 seconds?
qs.e: Using v = u + at, with u = 0, a = 2.5 m/s2, and t = 8 s: v = 0 + 2.5 * 8 = 20 m/s.

qs.q: The slope of a velocity-time graph represents which physical quantity?
qs.e: The gradient or slope of a velocity against time graph gives the rate of change of velocity, which is acceleration.

qs.q: An object dropped freely from a high cliff falls under gravity. What is its acceleration assuming air resistance is negligible?
qs.e: In free fall near Earth surface with negligible air resistance, all objects accelerate downward at g = 9.8 m/s2.

qs.q: What trajectory does a projectile follow when launched horizontally near the surface of the Earth?
qs.e: Under constant downward gravitational acceleration and zero horizontal acceleration, a projectile describes a parabolic path.

qs.q: A body is thrown vertically upward with an initial speed of 30 m/s. Calculate the maximum height reached. (Take g = 10 m/s2)
qs.e: At maximum height v = 0. Using v2 = u2 - 2gh: 0 = 302 - 2(10)h => 20h = 900 => h = 45 m.

qs.q: A particle undergoes uniform circular motion in a circle of radius 4 m at a constant speed of 12 m/s. What is its centripetal acceleration?
qs.e: Centripetal acceleration a = v2 / r = (12)2 / 4 = 144 / 4 = 36 m/s2.

qs.q: A projectile is launched with an initial velocity of 40 m/s at an angle of 30 degrees to the horizontal. Find its time of flight. (Take g = 10 m/s2)
qs.e: Time of flight T = (2 * u * sin theta) / g = (2 * 40 * sin 30) / 10 = (80 * 0.5) / 10 = 4.0 s.

qs.q: A stone released from rest at the top of a tower takes 5 seconds to reach the ground. Calculate the height of the tower. (Take g = 10 m/s2)
A flywheel rotates at 120 revolutions per minute (rpm). What is its angular speed in radians per second?
qs.e: Angular speed omega = 2 * pi * f. Here f = 120 / 60 = 2 Hz. So omega = 2 * pi * 2 = 4 pi rad/s.

qs.q: Two force vectors of magnitude 6 N and 8 N act at right angles to each other. Calculate the magnitude of their resultant force.
qs.e: For perpendicular vectors, resultant R = sqrt(F1^2 + F2^2) = sqrt(6^2 + 8^2) = sqrt(36 + 64) = 10 N.

qs.q: A car accelerates uniformly from 10 m/s to 30 m/s while covering a distance of 100 m. Determine its acceleration.
An athlete runs around a circular track of radius 70 m in 44 seconds at constant speed. Find the speed of the athlete. (Take pi = 22/7)
qs.e: Distance = circumference = 2 * pi * r = 2 * (22/7) * 70 = 440 m. Speed v = distance / time = 440 / 44 = 10 m/s.

qs.q: What angle of projection yields the maximum horizontal range for a projectile launched on flat ground with a given initial speed?
qs.e: Horizontal range R = (u2 * sin 2 theta) / g. Range is maximum when sin 2 theta = 1, so 2 theta = 90 degrees and theta = 45 degrees.

qs.q: A micrometer screw gauge has a pitch of 0.5 mm and 50 divisions on its circular scale. What is its least count?
qs.e: Least count = pitch / number of circular scale divisions = 0.5 mm / 50 = 0.01 mm.

qs.q: A body moves along a straight path such that its distance s in meters at time t in seconds is given by s = 3t2 + 4t + 2. Find its velocity at t = 3 seconds.
qs.e: Velocity v = ds/dt = 6t + 4. At t = 3 s, v = 6(3) + 4 = 18 + 4 = 22 m/s.

qs.q: Calculate the magnitude of the horizontal component of a vector of magnitude 50 N inclined at an angle of 60 degrees to the horizontal.
qs.e: Horizontal component Fx = F * cos theta = 50 * cos 60 = 50 * 0.5 = 25.0 N.

qs.q: A ball is projected horizontally with a speed of 15 m/s from the top of a building 20 m high. Calculate its horizontal distance from the base when it hits the ground. (Take g = 10 m/s2)
qs.e: Vertical motion: h = 0.5 * g * t2 => 20 = 5 * t2 => t = 2 s. Horizontal distance = u_x * t = 15 * 2 = 30 m.

qs.q: A projectile launched at speed u at 60 degrees to the horizontal has a maximum height of 15 m. Calculate its initial speed u. (Take g = 10 m/s2)
A racing car accelerates uniformly from rest to 36 m/s in 6 seconds, then maintains this velocity for 10 seconds. What total distance did it cover?
qs.e: Distance in phase 1: s1 = 0.5 * v * t1 = 0.5 * 36 * 6 = 108 m. Phase 2: s2 = 36 * 10 = 360 m. Total distance = 108 + 360 = 468 m.

qs.q: An object in uniform circular motion completes 5 revolutions per second in a circle of radius 0.7 m. Calculate its linear speed. (Take pi = 22/7)
qs.e: Linear speed v = 2 * pi * r * f = 2 * (22/7) * 0.7 * 5 = 22 m/s.

qs.q: A particle released from rest falls freely under gravity. Find the ratio of the distance fallen during the 1st second to the distance fallen during the 3rd second.
qs.e: Distance in nth second: sn = 0.5 * g * (2n - 1). For n=1: s1 = 0.5g. For n=3: s3 = 2.5g. Ratio s1 : s3 = 0.5g : 2.5g = 1 : 5.

qs.q: Two velocity vectors V1 = 12 m/s due East and V2 = 5 m/s due North act on a particle. What is the direction of their resultant relative to East?
qs.e: tan theta = V_North / V_East = 5 / 12 = 0.4167. theta = arctan(0.4167) = 22.6 degrees North of East.

qs.q: A satellite orbits the Earth at a constant altitude where centripetal acceleration is 8.0 m/s2 and orbital speed is 8,000 m/s. Determine its orbital radius.
qs.e: Centripetal acceleration a = v2 / r => r = v2 / a = (8000)^2 / 8 = 8,000,000 m = 8.0 x 10^6 m.

qs.q: A gun fires a bullet vertically upward at 100 m/s. How long after firing will the bullet return to the point of projection? (Take g = 10 m/s2)
qs.e: Time to top t = u / g = 100 / 10 = 10 s. Total time of flight T = 2t = 20 s.

qs.q: A train slows down uniformly from 72 km/h to 36 km/h over a distance of 150 m. Find its deceleration.
A car accelerates from rest at 2 m/s2 for 10 s, then decelerates to rest at 4 m/s2. Calculate the total time of motion.
qs.e: Maximum speed v = 2*10 = 20 m/s. Deceleration time t2 = 20 / 4 = 5 s. Total time = 10 + 5 = 15 s.

qs.q: A cannonball is launched with speed 50 m/s at angle theta = 37 degrees (sin 37 = 0.6, cos 37 = 0.8). Calculate its horizontal range. (Take g = 10 m/s2)
qs.e: u_x = 50 * cos 37 = 40 m/s. u_y = 50 * sin 37 = 30 m/s. Time of flight T = 2 * 30 / 10 = 6 s. Range R = 40 * 6 = 240 m.

qs.q: A stone is thrown vertically upward with initial speed u. If it reaches half of its maximum height at velocity v1, what is the ratio v1 / u?
qs.e: Maximum height H = u2 / (2g). At h = H/2 = u2 / (4g), v1^2 = u2 - 2g(H/2) = u2/2 => v1 / u = 1 / sqrt(2).

qs.q: Three displacement vectors are represented by A = 3i + 4j, B = -i + 2j, and C = 2i - 6j. Find the magnitude of their resultant displacement.
qs.e: Resultant R = (3 - 1 + 2)i + (4 + 2 - 6)j = 4i + 0j. Magnitude |R| = sqrt(4^2 + 0^2) = 4 m.

qs.q: A centrifuge rotor accelerates from rest to 600 rad/s with a constant angular acceleration of 30 rad/s2. Through what angle does it rotate during this acceleration?
qs.e: Using omega^2 = omega_0^2 + 2 * alpha * theta: 600^2 = 0 + 2 * 30 * theta => 360,000 = 60 * theta => theta = 6,000 rad.

qs.q: An elevator descends with an acceleration of 2.0 m/s2. A small object inside is released from rest relative to the elevator 1.6 m above its floor. How long does it take to strike the floor? (Take g = 9.8 m/s2)
qs.e: Relative acceleration a_rel = g - a_ele = 9.8 - 2.0 = 7.8 m/s2. Using h = 0.5 * a_rel * t2: 1.6 = 3.9 * t2 => t = 0.64 s.

qs.q: A projectile is launched from ground level with speed 25 m/s at angle theta = 53 degrees (sin 53 = 0.8, cos 53 = 0.6). Calculate its velocity vector magnitude 1 second after launch. (Take g = 10 m/s2)
A car travelling at 20 m/s applies brakes and comes to rest after travelling 40 m. Assuming uniform deceleration, what distance was covered in the final second of motion?
qs.e: Deceleration a = 5 m/s2. Stopping time t = 4 s. Distance covered from t=3 to t=4 s is 40 - (20*3 - 0.5*5*9) = 40 - 37.5 = 2.5 m.

qs.q: A body is projected vertically upwards with speed u. At what fraction of its maximum height is its kinetic energy equal to its potential energy?
qs.e: Total mechanical energy E = mgH. When KE = PE, mgH = 2 mgh => h = H / 2.

qs.q: A river flows East at 3 m/s. A motorboat heads North across the river at 4 m/s relative to the water. Find the magnitude of the boat velocity relative to the river bank.
qs.e: Vectors are perpendicular: v = sqrt(4^2 + 3^2) = sqrt(25) = 5 m/s.

qs.q: A particle moves along a circular path of radius 2 m. Its speed increases at a constant rate of 3 m/s2. What is the magnitude of total acceleration when its speed is 4 m/s?
Two bodies A and B are projected simultaneously from the ground with speeds 30 m/s at 30 degrees and 20 m/s at 60 degrees respectively. Find the ratio of maximum height reached by A to that of B.
A wheel starting from rest accelerates with constant angular acceleration alpha = 4 rad/s2. How many complete revolutions does it make in the first 10 seconds?
qs.e: theta = 0.5 * 4 * 102 = 200 rad. Revolutions = 200 / (2 pi) = 31.83, which is 31 complete revolutions.

qs.q: A stone is dropped into a deep well, and the sound of impact with water is heard 3.2 seconds later. If the speed of sound is 340 m/s, calculate the depth of the well. (Take g = 10 m/s2)
qs.e: t1 = sqrt(2d/10) and t2 = d/340. For d = 46.2 m: t1 = sqrt(9.24) = 3.04 s and t2 = 0.136 s. Total = 3.176 s approx 3.2 s.

qs.q: A projectile is launched from ground level with speed u at angle theta. Show the relation between its horizontal range R and maximum height H.
qs.e: R / H = (2 u2 sin theta cos theta / g) / (u2 sin2 theta / 2g) = 4 cos theta / sin theta = 4 cot theta.

qs.q: A particle moves in a straight line with position x(t) = t3 - 6t2 + 9t + 2 (in meters). At what time t (t > 0) is the particle instantaneously at rest?
A hunter aims a rifle directly at a monkey hanging from a tree branch. The instant the bullet leaves the muzzle, the monkey drops. Assuming no obstacles, what happens?
o: The bullet passes above the monkey
The bullet passes below the monkey
The outcome depends entirely on muzzle velocity
The bullet hits the monkey regardless of launch speed
qs.e: Both bullet and monkey drop by 0.5 g t2 in time t, so the bullet hits the monkey.

qs.q: A aircraft flies horizontally at height H = 500 m with speed V = 100 m/s and releases a supply package. Calculate the angle of sight theta from the target on ground to the aircraft at the moment of release. (Take g = 10 m/s2)
qs.e: Time to fall t = 10 s. Horizontal distance X = 100 * 10 = 1000 m. tan theta = 500 / 1000 = 0.5 => theta = 26.6 degrees.

qs.q: A particle moves along a curved path x(t) = 4 t2 and y(t) = 3 t3. Determine the magnitude of its acceleration at t = 2 seconds.
qs.e: ax = 8, ay = 18t = 36. Magnitude a = sqrt(8^2 + 36^2) = sqrt(1360) = 36.88 m/s2.

qs.q: A stone is thrown from the top of an inclined plane at an angle alpha to the horizontal. If the inclination of the hill is beta, derive the maximum range down the inclined plane when initial velocity is u.
qs.e: Maximum range down an inclined plane sloping downward at angle beta is R_max = u2 / [g (1 - sin beta)].

qs.q: Two particles are projected simultaneously from the same origin with equal speeds u at angles alpha and beta to the horizontal (alpha != beta). If both have the same horizontal range R, what is the relation between alpha and beta?
qs.e: sin 2 alpha = sin 2 beta => 2 alpha = 180 - 2 beta => alpha + beta = 90 degrees.

qs.q: A particle undergoes simple harmonic motion with amplitude A and angular frequency omega. At what displacement x from equilibrium is its acceleration magnitude equal to half its maximum acceleration?
qs.e: In SHM, acceleration a = omega2 * x. For a = 0.5 * a_max: omega2 * x = 0.5 * omega2 * A => x = A / 2.

qs.q: A current of 1.0 A flows through a resistor of resistance 30 Ω. Determine the potential difference across it.
qs.e: According to Ohm's law, potential difference V = I × R = 1.0 A × 30 Ω = 30.0 V.

qs.q: A trolley of mass 1.5 kg moving at 9 m/s collides with a second trolley of mass 3.0 kg moving in the same direction at 2 m/s. If they coalesce upon collision, find their common velocity.
qs.e: By conservation of linear momentum: m₁u₁ + m₂u₂ = (m₁ + m₂)v ⇒ v = (1.5×9 + 3.0×2) / (1.5 + 3.0) = 4.33 m/s.

qs.q: A trolley of mass 0.5 kg moving at 19 m/s collides with a second trolley of mass 4.0 kg moving in the same direction at 2 m/s. If they coalesce upon collision, find their common velocity.
qs.e: By conservation of linear momentum: m₁u₁ + m₂u₂ = (m₁ + m₂)v ⇒ v = (0.5×19 + 4.0×2) / (0.5 + 4.0) = 3.89 m/s.

qs.q: An object of mass 4.0 kg moves with a constant velocity of 34 m/s. What is its kinetic energy?
qs.e: Kinetic energy K = ½ m v² = 0.5 × 4.0 kg × (34 m/s)² = 2312 J.

qs.q: A body of mass 8.0 kg moves in a circular path of radius 2.0 m at a constant speed of 5 m/s. Calculate the centripetal force acting on the body.
qs.e: Centripetal force F = m v² / r = (8.0 × 5²) / 2.0 = 100 N.

qs.q: A body of mass 1.0 kg moves in a circular path of radius 1.2 m at a constant speed of 25 m/s. Calculate the centripetal force acting on the body.
qs.e: Centripetal force F = m v² / r = (1.0 × 25²) / 1.2 = 521 N.

qs.q: A mass of 1.5 kg attached to a string of length 1.2 m revolves as a conical pendulum at an angle of 45° to the vertical. Calculate its period of revolution.

qs.q: A trolley of mass 0.5 kg moving at 9 m/s collides with a second trolley of mass 4.0 kg moving in the same direction at 2 m/s. If they coalesce upon collision, find their common velocity.

qs.q: A motor car traveling at an initial speed of 14 m/s decelerates uniformly at 3.0 m/s² until coming to rest. Find the stopping distance.
qs.e: Stopping distance s = u² / (2a) = (14)² / (2 × 3.0) = 32.7 m.

qs.q: A wire of length 2.0 m and diameter 1.2 mm is stretched by a force of 500 N. If Young's modulus for the wire material is 120 GPa, calculate the extension in mm.
A projectile is launched from ground level with an initial velocity of 39 m/s at an angle of 30° to the horizontal. Calculate its horizontal range, taking g = 10 m/s².
qs.e: Horizontal range R = u² sin(2θ) / g = (39² × sin(60°)) / 10 = 132 m.

qs.q: A sound wave has a frequency of 300 Hz and a wavelength of 1.2 m. Calculate its speed in the medium.
qs.e: Wave speed v = f × λ = 300 Hz × 1.2 m = 360.0 m/s.

qs.q: A wire of length 0.5 m and diameter 1.0 mm is stretched by a force of 400 N. If Young's modulus for the wire material is 70 GPa, calculate the extension in mm.
A wire of length 1.0 m and diameter 2.5 mm is stretched by a force of 800 N. If Young's modulus for the wire material is 150 GPa, calculate the extension in mm.
A force of 125 N is applied to a spring of force constant 500 N/m. Determine the extension produced in the spring.
qs.e: From Hooke's law F = k e, extension e = F / k = 125 N / 500 N/m = 0.25 m.

qs.q: A body of mass 1.0 kg moves in a circular path of radius 1.2 m at a constant speed of 20 m/s. Calculate the centripetal force acting on the body.
qs.e: Centripetal force F = m v² / r = (1.0 × 20²) / 1.2 = 333 N.

qs.q: A sound wave has a frequency of 400 Hz and a wavelength of 0.75 m. Calculate its speed in the medium.
qs.e: Wave speed v = f × λ = 400 Hz × 0.75 m = 300.0 m/s.

qs.q: A sound wave has a frequency of 900 Hz and a wavelength of 0.2 m. Calculate its speed in the medium.
qs.e: Wave speed v = f × λ = 900 Hz × 0.2 m = 180.0 m/s.

qs.q: A capacitor of capacitance 100.0 μF is charged to a potential difference of 500 V. Calculate the electrostatic energy stored in the capacitor in millijoules (mJ).
qs.e: Energy stored W = ½ C V² = 0.5 × (100.0×10⁻⁶ F) × (500 V)² = 12.5 J = 12500 mJ.

qs.q: A wire of length 1.0 m and diameter 1.5 mm is stretched by a force of 100 N. If Young's modulus for the wire material is 200 GPa, calculate the extension in mm.
A trolley of mass 5.0 kg moving at 19 m/s collides with a second trolley of mass 2.0 kg moving in the same direction at 1 m/s. If they coalesce upon collision, find their common velocity.
qs.e: By conservation of linear momentum: m₁u₁ + m₂u₂ = (m₁ + m₂)v ⇒ v = (5.0×19 + 2.0×1) / (5.0 + 2.0) = 13.9 m/s.

qs.q: A trolley of mass 5.0 kg moving at 15 m/s collides with a second trolley of mass 4.0 kg moving in the same direction at 4 m/s. If they coalesce upon collision, find their common velocity.
qs.e: By conservation of linear momentum: m₁u₁ + m₂u₂ = (m₁ + m₂)v ⇒ v = (5.0×15 + 4.0×4) / (5.0 + 4.0) = 10.1 m/s.

qs.q: A body of mass 3.0 kg moves in a circular path of radius 1.5 m at a constant speed of 15 m/s. Calculate the centripetal force acting on the body.
qs.e: Centripetal force F = m v² / r = (3.0 × 15²) / 1.5 = 450 N.

qs.q: Calculate the separation distance between the objective lens of focal length 90 cm and eyepiece of focal length 10 cm in an astronomical telescope set for normal adjustment.
qs.e: Length of telescope tube in normal adjustment L = f_o + f_e = 90 + 10 = 100 cm.

qs.q: A motor car traveling at an initial speed of 8 m/s decelerates uniformly at 2.5 m/s² until coming to rest. Find the stopping distance.
qs.e: Stopping distance s = u² / (2a) = (8)² / (2 × 2.5) = 12.8 m.

qs.q: A trolley of mass 2.5 kg moving at 11 m/s collides with a second trolley of mass 5.0 kg moving in the same direction at 3 m/s. If they coalesce upon collision, find their common velocity.
qs.e: By conservation of linear momentum: m₁u₁ + m₂u₂ = (m₁ + m₂)v ⇒ v = (2.5×11 + 5.0×3) / (2.5 + 5.0) = 5.67 m/s.

qs.q: A capacitor of capacitance 20.0 μF is charged to a potential difference of 200 V. Calculate the electrostatic energy stored in the capacitor in millijoules (mJ).
qs.e: Energy stored W = ½ C V² = 0.5 × (20.0×10⁻⁶ F) × (200 V)² = 0.4 J = 400 mJ.

qs.q: A body of mass 6.0 kg moves in a circular path of radius 4.0 m at a constant speed of 3 m/s. Calculate the centripetal force acting on the body.
qs.e: Centripetal force F = m v² / r = (6.0 × 3²) / 4.0 = 13.5 N.

qs.q: A body of mass 8.0 kg moves in a circular path of radius 0.8 m at a constant speed of 20 m/s. Calculate the centripetal force acting on the body.
qs.e: Centripetal force F = m v² / r = (8.0 × 20²) / 0.8 = 4000 N.

qs.q: A trolley of mass 1.5 kg moving at 3 m/s collides with a second trolley of mass 0.5 kg moving in the same direction at 4 m/s. If they coalesce upon collision, find their common velocity.
qs.e: By conservation of linear momentum: m₁u₁ + m₂u₂ = (m₁ + m₂)v ⇒ v = (1.5×3 + 0.5×4) / (1.5 + 0.5) = 3.25 m/s.

qs.q: A capacitor of capacitance 1.0 μF is charged to a potential difference of 500 V. Calculate the electrostatic energy stored in the capacitor in millijoules (mJ).
qs.e: Energy stored W = ½ C V² = 0.5 × (1.0×10⁻⁶ F) × (500 V)² = 0.125 J = 125 mJ.

qs.q: A trolley of mass 2.0 kg moving at 9 m/s collides with a second trolley of mass 5.0 kg moving in the same direction at 4 m/s. If they coalesce upon collision, find their common velocity.
qs.e: By conservation of linear momentum: m₁u₁ + m₂u₂ = (m₁ + m₂)v ⇒ v = (2.0×9 + 5.0×4) / (2.0 + 5.0) = 5.43 m/s.

qs.q: A wire of length 4.0 m and diameter 1.2 mm is stretched by a force of 1000 N. If Young's modulus for the wire material is 200 GPa, calculate the extension in mm.
Which subatomic particle carries a negative electric charge and orbits the atomic nucleus?
qs.e: Electrons are negatively charged subatomic particles that revolve around the atomic nucleus in defined energy levels or orbitals.

qs.q: What is the total number of protons present in the nucleus of a neutral carbon atom?
qs.e: Carbon has an atomic number of 6, which means every carbon atom contains exactly 6 protons in its nucleus.

qs.q: The atomic number of an element is defined as the total number of which particle in an atom?
qs.e: The atomic number (Z) represents the number of protons contained within the nucleus of an atom.

qs.q: Atoms of the same element that possess the same atomic number but different mass numbers are termed as what?
qs.e: Isotopes are atoms of the same chemical element having identical numbers of protons but differing numbers of neutrons.

qs.q: Which quantum subshell has a maximum capacity to hold up to six electrons?
qs.e: The p subshell contains 3 orbitals, each holding up to 2 electrons, giving a maximum capacity of 6 electrons.

qs.q: How many neutrons are contained in an atom of chlorine with mass number 35 and atomic number 17?
qs.e: Number of neutrons = Mass number (A) - Atomic number (Z) = 35 - 17 = 18 neutrons.

qs.q: What type of radioactive emission consists of high-energy electromagnetic radiation without mass or charge?
qs.e: Gamma rays are high-frequency electromagnetic photons emitted from an unstable nucleus and carry neither mass nor charge.

qs.q: An atom has 19 protons, 20 neutrons, and 19 electrons. What is its mass number?
qs.e: Mass number = Protons + Neutrons = 19 + 20 = 39.

qs.q: Which electron configuration correctly describes a neutral sodium atom in its ground state (Z = 11)?
qs.e: Sodium has 11 electrons: 1s2 2s2 2p6 fill the first two shells, and the 11th electron enters the 3s orbital.

qs.q: What is the total maximum electron capacity of the principal energy shell with principal quantum number n = 3?
qs.e: The maximum capacity of shell n is given by 2n^2. For n = 3, capacity = 2*(3^2) = 18 electrons (3s2, 3p6, 3d10).

qs.q: An ion M2+ has 10 electrons and 12 neutrons. What is the atomic number of element M?
qs.e: M2+ lost 2 electrons to leave 10 electrons, so neutral atom M has 12 electrons, meaning atomic number Z = 12.

qs.q: Which principal subshell contains orbitals that are spherical in shape?
qs.e: s orbitals are spherically symmetrical around the atomic nucleus.

qs.q: How many valence electrons are present in an atom of phosphorus with atomic number 15?
qs.e: Phosphorus electron configuration is 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p3. The outermost shell (n=3) contains 2 + 3 = 5 valence electrons.

qs.q: What particle is emitted when a nucleus undergoes beta-minus decay?
qs.e: In beta-minus decay, a neutron transforms into a proton and emits a high-speed electron (beta particle).

qs.q: Which rule states that orbitals of equal energy are each occupied by one electron before any orbital is doubly occupied?
qs.e: Hund's rule dictates that electrons occupy degenerate orbitals singly with parallel spins before pairing up.

qs.q: A naturally occurring sample of chlorine is composed of 75 percent Cl-35 and 25 percent Cl-37 isotopes. Calculate the relative atomic mass of chlorine.
How many d-orbitals exist in any given d-subshell?
qs.e: A d-subshell consists of 5 degenerate d-orbitals (dxy, dyz, dxz, dx2-y2, dz2).

qs.q: When an electron moves from a higher energy level to a lower energy level, what happens?
qs.e: De-excitation of an electron from a higher shell to a lower shell releases energy in the form of electromagnetic radiation (a photon).

qs.q: Which species is isoelectronic with a fluoride ion (F-)?
qs.e: F- has 9 + 1 = 10 electrons. Neon (Ne) has atomic number 10, so it also has 10 electrons, making them isoelectronic.

qs.q: What is the ground state electron configuration of a neutral chromium atom (Z = 24)?
qs.e: Chromium exhibits an anomalous configuration [Ar] 3d5 4s1 because half-filled 3d subshells provide extra thermodynamic stability.

qs.q: An element X has two isotopes, X-63 and X-65, with relative abundances of 70 percent and 30 percent respectively. Determine the relative atomic mass of X.
Which set of quantum numbers (n, l, ml, ms) is forbidden according to quantum mechanics principles?
qs.e: The azimuthal quantum number l must strictly be less than n. For n = 2, l can only be 0 or 1. Thus l = 2 is forbidden.

qs.q: A sample of a radioactive isotope decays from 80 grams to 10 grams in a time period of 24 minutes. What is the half-life of this isotope?
qs.e: 80g -> 40g -> 20g -> 10g represents 3 half-lives. Total time = 24 minutes. 1 half-life = 24 / 3 = 8 minutes.

qs.q: What is the electron configuration of the iron(III) ion, Fe3+ (Z of Fe = 26)?
qs.e: Fe atom is [Ar] 3d6 4s2. Ionization removes two 4s electrons first, then one 3d electron, giving [Ar] 3d5.

qs.q: In Rutherford's gold foil experiment, why did a tiny fraction of alpha particles bounce straight backward?
o: They hit the concentrated, positively charged nucleus
They were absorbed by empty space
They interacted with outer shell orbital fields
qs.e: Large-angle deflection occurred when positively charged alpha particles directly approached the dense, positively charged nucleus.

qs.q: Which line spectrum series in atomic hydrogen emission occurs in the ultraviolet region of the spectrum?
qs.e: The Lyman series involves electron transitions down to the n = 1 shell and emits high-energy photons in the ultraviolet region.

qs.q: An atom has an atomic number of 20 and a mass number of 42. How many neutrons and electrons are in its divalent cation (M2+)?
qs.e: Neutrons = 42 - 20 = 22. For divalent cation M2+, electrons = 20 - 2 = 18.

qs.q: Copper has two naturally occurring isotopes with masses 62.93 amu and 64.93 amu. If the average atomic mass is 63.55 amu, what is the approximate percentage abundance of the lighter isotope?
Which statement correctly describes the Pauli Exclusion Principle?
o: Electrons fill lowest available energy levels first
Orbitals of equal energy fill singly before pairing
No two electrons in the same atom can have identical values for all four quantum numbers
Energy is emitted in discrete quanta
qs.e: The Pauli Exclusion Principle states that an orbital can hold at most two electrons, and they must have opposite spins (+1/2 and -1/2).

qs.q: When Uranium-238 (atomic number 92) undergoes alpha decay followed by beta-minus decay, what is the mass number and atomic number of the resulting daughter nucleus?
qs.e: Alpha decay: 238U -> 234Th (Z=90) + 4He. Beta decay: 234Th -> 234Pa (Z=91) + e-. Result: Mass = 234, Atomic number = 91.

qs.q: How many unpaired electrons are present in a gaseous nitrogen atom in its ground state (Z = 7)?
qs.e: Nitrogen configuration is 1s2 2s2 2px1 2py1 2pz1. The three 2p orbitals each hold 1 unpaired electron.

qs.q: What is the total number of orbitals contained within the principal energy level n = 4?
qs.e: Total orbitals in shell n is n^2. For n = 4, total orbitals = 4^2 = 16 (1 s-orbital, 3 p-orbitals, 5 d-orbitals, 7 f-orbitals).

qs.q: Which species contains the greatest number of unpaired d-electrons?
qs.e: Fe2+ is 3d6 (4 unpaired d-electrons). Cu2+ is 3d9 (1 unpaired). Zn2+ is 3d10 (0 unpaired). Cr3+ is 3d3 (3 unpaired). Fe2+ has the most.

qs.q: If a radioactive nuclide has a half-life of 5 hours, what fraction of the original activity remains after a total time of 20 hours?
qs.e: Number of half-lives = 20 / 5 = 4. Remaining fraction = (1/2)^4 = 1/16.

qs.q: The mass spectrum of an element shows three isotopes: mass 24 (80%), mass 25 (10%), and mass 26 (10%). Calculate the relative atomic mass of this element.
Which quantum number specifies the orientation of an orbital in three-dimensional space relative to other orbitals?
qs.e: The magnetic quantum number ml describes the spatial orientation of the orbital in a magnetic field.

qs.q: In a nuclear reactor, heavy water or graphite is used as a moderator primarily to perform which function?
o: Control the chain reaction by capturing neutrons
qs.e: Moderators slow down energetic neutrons to thermal speeds so they can efficiently induce further fission in U-235.

qs.q: An atom has the ground state electron configuration [Ar] 3d10 4s1. To which group and period of the periodic table does this element belong?
qs.e: This is copper (Z = 29). It has 4 energy shells (Period 4) and 11 valence/d electrons (Group 11 transition metal).

qs.q: A sample contains 1.20 x 10^24 atoms of a radioactive substance. If its half-life is 10 days, how many atoms remain undecayed after 30 days?
qs.e: 30 days = 3 half-lives. Fraction remaining = (1/2)^3 = 1/8. Remaining atoms = (1.20 x 10^24) / 8 = 1.50 x 10^23 atoms.

qs.q: Which subshell filling order is predicted by the Aufbau principle for the subshells 4s, 3d, 4p, and 5s?
qs.e: According to the (n+l) rule, subshells fill in order of increasing energy: 4s (4+0=4) < 3d (3+2=5) < 4p (4+1=5) < 5s (5+0=5).

qs.q: How many angular nodes and radial nodes are present in a 3p atomic orbital?
qs.e: For a 3p orbital: l = 1 so angular nodes = 1. Radial nodes = n - l - 1 = 3 - 1 - 1 = 1.

qs.q: When Beta-plus (positron) emission occurs in an unstable atomic nucleus, how do the mass number and atomic number change?
o: Mass number decreases by 1, atomic number remains unchanged
Mass number decreases by 4, atomic number decreases by 2
Mass number remains unchanged, atomic number increases by 1
Mass number remains unchanged, atomic number decreases by 1
qs.e: Positron emission converts a proton into a neutron, releasing a positron (e+). Mass number stays constant while Z decreases by 1.

qs.q: What is the maximum number of electrons that can share the quantum numbers n = 3 and l = 1 in a single atom?
qs.e: n = 3 and l = 1 specifies the 3p subshell. A p-subshell contains 3 orbitals, holding a maximum of 6 electrons.

qs.q: If 75 percent of a radioactive sample decays in 40 hours, what is the half-life of the radioactive substance?
qs.e: 75% decayed leaves 25% (1/4) remaining. 1/4 = (1/2)^2, which means 2 half-lives elapsed in 40 hours. Half-life = 40 / 2 = 20 hours.

qs.q: Which pair of species are iso-electronic and have identical ground state electron configurations?
qs.e: S2- (16+2 = 18 electrons) and Argon (18 electrons) both have the electron configuration 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p6.

qs.q: Calculate the energy in Joules of a photon emitted when an electron drops between energy levels, given the frequency of light emitted is 6.0 x 10^14 Hz (Planck constant h = 6.63 x 10^-34 J s).

In a mass spectrometer, an ion with mass-to-charge ratio m/z = 56 is accelerated through a potential difference V and deflected in a magnetic field. If the magnetic field strength is doubled while keeping V constant, by what factor does the radius of curvature change?
qs.e: Radius of trajectory r = (1/B) * sqrt(2mV/q). Radius is inversely proportional to magnetic field strength B. Doubling B halves the radius.

qs.q: The binding energy per nucleon for a helium nucleus (4He, mass = 4.0015 amu) is calculated using proton mass 1.0073 amu and neutron mass 1.0087 amu (1 amu = 931.5 MeV). What is the total binding energy of 4He?

A radioactive mineral initially containing 100 mg of a parent nuclide currently contains 12.5 mg of the parent and 87.5 mg of its stable daughter product. If the half-life is 700 million years, what is the age of the mineral?
qs.e: 100 mg -> 50 mg -> 25 mg -> 12.5 mg represents 3 half-lives. Age = 3 * 700 million years = 2100 million years (2.1 billion years).

qs.q: What is the total number of degenerate quantum states (including spin) available in the n = 3 principal shell of a hydrogen atom?
qs.e: The total number of spatial orbitals in shell n is n^2 = 3^2 = 9. Since each orbital holds 2 spin states, total degenerate states = 2 * 9 = 18.

qs.q: Which vertical column in the modern periodic table contains elements with identical numbers of valence electrons?
qs.e: Elements arranged in the same vertical column belong to the same Group and share similar valence shell electronic configurations.

qs.q: How does the atomic radius generally change when moving from left to right across a period?
qs.e: Across a period, nuclear charge increases while inner electron shielding remains constant, pulling electrons closer and reducing atomic radius.

qs.q: Which group of elements in the periodic table is characterized by having full valence s and p subshells?
qs.e: Noble gases (Group 18) possess a stable octet (or duplet for He) with fully filled valence outer shells.

qs.q: What name is given to the elements belonging to Group 1 of the periodic table?
qs.e: Group 1 metals (Li, Na, K, Rb, Cs, Fr) are collectively known as alkali metals.

qs.q: Which property measures the ability of an atom in a covalent bond to attract shared bonding electrons?
qs.e: Electronegativity is the relative measure of an atom's attraction for shared electron pairs in a covalent bond.

qs.q: Which element among the halogens exhibits the highest electronegativity value on the Pauling scale?
qs.e: Fluorine is the most electronegative element with a Pauling electronegativity value of 4.0.

qs.q: Elements in which block of the periodic table fill their outer d-subshells?
qs.e: Transition elements belong to the d-block where progressive filling of the (n-1)d subshell occurs.

qs.q: Why does first ionization energy generally increase across a period from Group 1 to Group 18?
o: Increasing nuclear charge attracts outer electrons more strongly
Atomic radius increases across a period
Shielding by inner shell electrons increases drastically
Number of energy shells increases continuously
qs.e: Increased effective nuclear charge across a period holds outer electrons tighter, requiring higher energy to remove one electron.

qs.q: Comparing Na+ and Na, which species has the smaller radius and why?
o: Na+ is smaller because loss of an electron reduces electron-electron repulsion and shell count
Na is smaller because neutral atoms are always smaller than cations
Both have identical radii because proton number is unchanged
Na+ is larger due to expanded nuclear charge
qs.e: Na+ loses its 3s electron, dropping a entire energy shell and reducing electron repulsion, making Na+ much smaller than neutral Na.

qs.q: Which property is characteristic of transition metals but not typical of main group s-block metals?
o: Formation of colored ions in aqueous solution
qs.e: Transition metals form colored complexes due to d-d electronic transitions when d-orbitals split in a ligand field.

qs.q: How does metallic character change across Period 3 elements from Na to Cl?
qs.e: Period 3 moves from electropositive metals (Na, Mg, Al) through metalloid (Si) to electronegative non-metals (P, S, Cl).

qs.q: Which element in Period 3 forms an oxide that exhibits amphoteric behavior?
qs.e: Aluminum oxide (Al2O3) is amphoteric, reacting with both strong acids and strong bases to yield salts.

qs.q: Which halogen is a reddish-brown liquid at room temperature and standard atmospheric pressure?
qs.e: Bromine (Br2) is the only non-metallic element that exists as a dense reddish-brown liquid at STP.

qs.q: What general trend is observed for electron affinity values down Group 17 (Halogens)?
o: Increases to a maximum at Iodine
qs.e: As atomic radius increases down the group, incoming electrons experience weaker attraction to the nucleus, making electron affinity less exothermic overall.

qs.q: What neutral chemical element possesses the electronic ground state configuration 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p4?
qs.e: Total electrons = 2 + 2 + 6 + 2 + 4 = 16. Element 16 is sulfur (Group 16, Period 3).

qs.q: The hydride of which element reacts most violently with cold water to produce hydrogen gas and a alkaline solution?
qs.e: Potassium is a highly reactive Group 1 metal whose hydride/metal reacts vigorously with water releasing H2 gas.

qs.q: Beryllium and aluminum exhibit remarkably similar chemical behavior. What is the name of this relationship in the periodic table?
qs.e: Beryllium and aluminum exhibit similar chemical properties due to comparable charge density and electronegativity (diagonal relationship).

qs.q: What causes the anomalous lower first ionization energy of Oxygen compared to Nitrogen?
o: Nitrogen has a larger atomic radius than Oxygen
Paired electrons in Oxygen's 2p orbital experience mutual repulsion
Oxygen has fewer protons in its nucleus
Nitrogen outer electron is in a 3s orbital
qs.e: Oxygen has configuration 2p4 with 2 paired electrons in one orbital. Inter-electron repulsion makes this electron easier to remove than from Nitrogen's half-filled 2p3 subshell.

qs.q: Which oxide of Period 3 elements dissolves in water to form a strong dibasic acid?
qs.e: Sulfur trioxide (SO3) reacts with water to form sulfuric acid (H2SO4), which is a strong dibasic acid.

qs.q: Why does Magnesium have a higher first ionization energy than Aluminum, despite Aluminum having a greater nuclear charge?
o: Magnesium has a larger atomic radius than Aluminum
Aluminum's 3p electron is shielded by 3s electrons and higher in energy
Aluminum has a full d-subshell shielding its nucleus
Magnesium loses an electron from a 2p subshell
qs.e: Mg has filled 3s2 subshell. Al has configuration [Ne] 3s2 3p1. The 3p electron is higher in energy and shielded by 3s2 electrons, making it easier to remove.

qs.q: Arranging the ions Na+, Mg2+, F-, and O2- in order of increasing ionic radius yields which sequence?
qs.e: All 4 ions are isoelectronic (10 electrons). Higher nuclear charge pulls electrons closer: Mg2+ (Z=12) < Na+ (Z=11) < F- (Z=9) < O2- (Z=8).

qs.q: Which property of transition metals accounts for their ability to function as effective heterogeneous catalysts?
o: Presence of vacant d-orbitals and variable oxidation states
qs.e: Partially filled or vacant d-orbitals allow transition metals to adsorb reactant molecules on their surface and form reaction intermediates easily.

qs.q: Elements X and Y have atomic numbers 11 and 17 respectively. What is the nature of the bond formed between X and Y, and the formula of the resulting compound?
qs.e: X (Z=11, Na) is an alkali metal. Y (Z=17, Cl) is a halogen. Transfer of 1 electron yields ionic compound XY (NaCl).

qs.q: The successive ionization energies (in kJ/mol) for an element E are: 1st=578, 2nd=1817, 3rd=2745, 4th=11578, 5th=14830. To which group does element E belong?
qs.e: A huge jump occurs between the 3rd and 4th ionization energies (2745 to 11578 kJ/mol), indicating 3 valence electrons (Group 13, e.g. Al).

qs.q: Which oxide of Period 3 elements reacts with aqueous sodium hydroxide to form sodium silicate?
qs.e: Silicon dioxide (SiO2) is an acidic oxide that reacts with hot concentrated NaOH to form soluble sodium silicate (Na2SiO3).

qs.q: Why is the second ionization energy of Sodium significantly higher than its first ionization energy?
o: Sodium cation has fewer protons than neutral sodium
Nuclear charge decreases after first electron removal
The second electron is removed from a stable inner noble gas core (2p shell)
qs.e: First ionization removes 3s1. Second ionization requires removing an electron from the stable 2p6 octet close to the nucleus.

qs.q: Which element forms a chloride that hydrolyzes fumes heavily in moist air producing dense white acidic fumes of HCl?
qs.e: Covalent silicon tetrachloride (SiCl4) hydrolyzes readily in water/moist air: SiCl4 + 2H2O -> SiO2 + 4HCl(g).

qs.q: Comparing the boiling points of the hydrides NH3, PH3, AsH3, and SbH3, why does NH3 have an unexpectedly high boiling point?
o: NH3 has the highest molecular mass among the group
NH3 is a non-polar planar molecule
NH3 exhibits strong intermolecular hydrogen bonding
qs.e: Nitrogen's high electronegativity allows NH3 molecules to form strong hydrogen bonds, requiring extra thermal energy to separate.

qs.q: What trend in thermal stability is observed for Group 2 nitrates (Mg(NO3)2 to Ba(NO3)2) down the group?
o: Thermal stability decreases down the group
All Group 2 nitrates remain completely stable on heating
Thermal stability increases down the group as cation radius increases
Thermal stability peaks at Calcium nitrate
qs.e: Larger Group 2 cations down the group have lower charge density, exerting less polarizing power on the nitrate ion, increasing thermal stability.

qs.q: Which element exhibits the highest melting point among the Period 3 elements?
qs.e: Silicon forms a giant covalent macromolecular network structure (like diamond) requiring massive energy to break covalent bonds.

qs.q: Which complex ion of copper exhibits a characteristic deep blue color in aqueous solution?
qs.e: Adding excess aqueous ammonia to Cu2+ forms the tetraamminecopper(II) complex ion, [Cu(NH3)4]2+, which is deep blue.

qs.q: What is the reason for the decrease in atomic radius across a transition metal series (e.g. Sc to Zn) being much smaller than across Period 3?
o: Nuclear charge does not increase across transition series
d-electrons added to inner (n-1)d subshells effectively shield outer s-electrons from increased nuclear charge
qs.e: Electrons enter the inner (n-1)d subshell, providing screening that counteracts much of the increased nuclear charge.

qs.q: Which halide of Period 3 element forms a dimeric vapor molecule with the formula Al2Cl6 at moderate temperatures?
qs.e: Aluminum chloride exists as electron-deficient AlCl3 monomer at high temperatures but forms Al2Cl6 dimer via dative covalent bonds at moderate temperatures.

qs.q: What is the oxidation state of Chromium in the dichromate ion, Cr2O7(2-)?
The standard reduction potentials for metals A, B, and C are: A2+/A = -0.76 V, B2+/B = +0.34 V, C2+/C = -2.37 V. Which metal is the strongest reducing agent?
qs.e: The most negative electrode potential (-2.37 V for C) indicates the highest tendency to lose electrons, making Metal C the strongest reducing agent.

qs.q: Why does Chlorine have a more exothermic electron affinity (-349 kJ/mol) than Fluorine (-328 kJ/mol)?
o: Chlorine has a higher nuclear charge than Fluorine
Fluorine is a solid at room temperature
Fluorine's small 2p orbital experiences strong inter-electronic repulsion
Chlorine atomic radius is smaller than Fluorine
qs.e: Fluorine's tiny atomic radius leads to high electron density in its 2p subshell, causing severe electron-electron repulsion when an electron is added.

qs.q: An element Z forms a gaseous hydride ZH3 that dissolves in water to give a weak base. What is the group number of element Z?
qs.e: Element Z belongs to Group 15 (e.g., Nitrogen in NH3 or Phosphorus in PH3), forming hydrides with a lone pair capable of accepting protons.

qs.q: Which property decreases progressively down the alkali metal group (Group 1)?
qs.e: First ionization energy decreases down Group 1 as outer s-electrons get farther from the nucleus and experience greater shielding.

qs.q: Why are compounds of Zinc(II) and Scandium(III) diamagnetic and colorless in aqueous solution?
o: They contain high numbers of unpaired d-electrons
They contain completely filled or completely empty d-subshells (3d10 or 3d0)
qs.e: Zn2+ has 3d10 (filled, no unpaired electrons) and Sc3+ has 3d0 (empty). Without unpaired d-electrons, d-d transitions and paramagnetism cannot occur.

qs.q: When sodium hydroxide solution is added dropwise until in excess to aqueous aluminum chloride, what observations are made?
o: A white precipitate forms which remains insoluble in excess NaOH
A pungent ammonia gas is evolved
A white gelatinous precipitate forms which dissolves in excess NaOH
qs.e: Al3+ reacts with NaOH to form amphoteric Al(OH)3 white ppt, which redissolves in excess NaOH forming soluble aluminate complex [Al(OH)4]-.

qs.q: Which oxide of Period 3 element exhibits giant ionic giant lattice structure and highest lattice energy?
qs.e: MgO contains Mg2+ and O2- ions. The high product of ionic charges (2x2=4) yields an extremely high lattice enthalpy.

qs.q: Comparing Group 2 hydroxides Mg(OH)2 to Ba(OH)2, what trend in solubility in water is observed down the group?
o: All Group 2 hydroxides are completely insoluble
qs.e: Lattice enthalpy decreases faster down the group than hydration enthalpy, causing solubility of Group 2 hydroxides to increase down the group.

qs.q: What is the primary reason why transition elements form complex ions with neutral or anionic ligands?
o: Large ionic radii and low ionization energy
High electronegativity values comparable to fluorine
High positive charge density and low-energy vacant d-orbitals
qs.e: Small, highly charged transition metal cations offer vacant d-orbitals to accept electron pairs donated by ligands.

qs.q: An element with atomic number 35 is placed in which group and period of the periodic table?
qs.e: Z = 35 is Bromine ([Ar] 3d10 4s2 4p5). It has 4 energy shells (Period 4) and 7 valence electrons (Group 17 / Halogens).

qs.q: Which reaction represents the thermal decomposition of calcium nitrate when heated strongly?
qs.e: Group 2 nitrates decompose on heating to yield metal oxide, nitrogen dioxide gas (brown fumes), and oxygen gas.

qs.q: The first ionization energies of elements P, Q, R, S are 496, 738, 578, and 787 kJ/mol respectively. If these represent Period 3 elements Na, Mg, Al, Si in scrambled order, which value corresponds to Aluminum?
qs.e: IE1 trend in Period 3: Na (496) < Al (578) < Mg (738) < Si (787). Aluminum (578 kJ/mol) drops below Mg due to removal from 3p subshell.

qs.q: Calculate the effective nuclear charge (Zeff) experienced by a 3s electron in a neutral Sodium atom (Z = 11) using Slater's rules.
In the spectrochemical series, ligands are arranged by their ability to split d-orbitals. Which ligand produces the largest crystal field splitting energy (delta) in transition metal complexes?
qs.e: Cyanide (CN-) is a strong-field ligand that induces the greatest d-orbital crystal field splitting energy (delta).

qs.q: A element X has successive ionization energies (in eV) of 13.6, 35.1, 54.9, 77.4, 113.9, 138.1, 739.3, 871.1. How many valence electrons does X possess?
qs.e: A huge jump occurs between IE6 (138.1 eV) and IE7 (739.3 eV), demonstrating that 6 valence electrons were removed before breaking inner core shell.

qs.q: Which pair of Period 3 oxides, when mixed in stoichiometric quantities in water, produce a neutral aqueous solution?
qs.e: Na2O forms 2NaOH (strong base) and SO3 forms H2SO4 (strong acid). Equimolar reaction 2NaOH + H2SO4 -> Na2SO4 + 2H2O yields a neutral pH 7 salt solution.

qs.q: What type of chemical bond involves the complete transfer of electrons from a metal atom to a non-metal atom?
qs.e: Ionic (electrovalent) bonding results from the complete transfer of one or more valence electrons from a metal to a non-metal.

qs.q: Which type of bond is formed when two non-metal atoms share pairs of valence electrons?
qs.e: Covalent bonding involves the sharing of electron pairs between non-metal atoms.

qs.q: What predicted geometry is adopted by a methane molecule (CH4) according to VSEPR theory?
qs.e: Methane has 4 bonding pairs around central carbon with 0 lone pairs, giving a regular tetrahedral geometry with 109.5 degree bond angles.

qs.q: Which element forms giant covalent macromolecular structures present in diamond and graphite?
qs.e: Carbon forms allotropes like diamond and graphite which consist of giant covalent macromolecular structures.

qs.q: In a coordinate (dative covalent) bond, how are the bonding electrons supplied?
o: Both electrons are supplied by one atom
One electron is supplied by each atom
Electrons are donated from a free metal sea
qs.e: In a dative covalent bond, both shared electrons originate from a lone pair on a single donor atom.

qs.q: What type of attractive force holds positive metal cations together in a sea of delocalized electrons?
qs.e: Metallic bonding is the electrostatic attraction between metal cations and delocalized valence electrons.

qs.q: Which intermolecular force is strongest between water (H2O) molecules in liquid state?
qs.e: Water forms strong intermolecular hydrogen bonds between highly electronegative O atoms and H atoms.

qs.q: What is the bond angle in a water molecule (H2O) as predicted by VSEPR theory?
qs.e: Oxygen in water has 2 bonding pairs and 2 lone pairs. Lone pair repulsion compresses the tetrahedral angle from 109.5 to 104.5 degrees.

qs.q: Which molecule possesses a linear shape with a bond angle of 180 degrees?
qs.e: Carbon dioxide (O=C=O) has 2 double bond domains around carbon and no lone pairs, yielding a linear geometry.

qs.q: Why does graphite conduct electricity while diamond does not?
o: Graphite has delocalized pi electrons free to move along its layers
Diamond contains free ions while graphite does not
Graphite is ionic while diamond is covalent
Diamond is liquid at room temperature
qs.e: Each carbon in graphite is sp2 hybridized, leaving one unhybridized p-electron per carbon delocalized within hex planes.

qs.q: Which compound contains both ionic and covalent bonding within its crystal lattice?
qs.e: NaNO3 contains ionic bonds between Na+ and NO3- ions, and covalent bonds between N and O atoms within the NO3- nitrate anion.

qs.q: What orbital hybridization is adopted by the central carbon atom in an ethene molecule (C2H4)?
qs.e: In ethene (H2C=CH2), each carbon atom forms 3 sigma bonds (trigonal planar geometry, 120 degree angle) using sp2 hybrid orbitals.

qs.q: Which species contains a dative covalent (coordinate) bond?
qs.e: The ammonium ion (NH4+) is formed when an unshared lone pair on NH3 donates to an electron-deficient H+ ion.

qs.q: Why is the boiling point of HF significantly higher than that of HCl?
o: HF has a greater molar mass than HCl
HF molecules are held together by strong intermolecular hydrogen bonds
qs.e: Fluorine is extremely electronegative, enabling HF to form intermolecular hydrogen bonds, whereas HCl relies on weaker dipole-dipole forces.

qs.q: Which molecule is non-polar despite containing polar covalent bonds?
qs.e: CCl4 has a symmetrical tetrahedral shape where individual C-Cl bond dipoles cancel out completely, giving zero net dipole moment.

qs.q: How many sigma (s) and pi (p) bonds are present in an ethyne molecule (C2H2)?
qs.e: H-C≡C-H contains two C-H sigma bonds, one C-C sigma bond (total 3 sigma), and two C-C pi bonds.

qs.q: Which property is characteristic of simple molecular covalent compounds?
o: Low melting points and high volatility
qs.e: Simple molecular substances have weak intermolecular forces holding molecules together, resulting in low melting/boiling points.

qs.q: What geometry is adopted by boron trifluoride (BF3) central boron atom?
qs.e: BF3 has 3 bonding pairs around boron and 0 lone pairs, giving a trigonal planar shape with 120 degree bond angles.

qs.q: In which pair of substances are both members giant molecular structures?
qs.e: Both SiO2 (quartz) and graphite possess giant covalent macromolecular network structures.

qs.q: What molecular shape and bond angle are predicted for ammonia (NH3) by VSEPR theory?
qs.e: Ammonia has 3 bonding pairs and 1 lone pair. Lone pair-bonding pair repulsion reduces the bond angle to approximately 107 degrees (trigonal pyramidal).

qs.q: What is the hybridization state of carbon in carbon dioxide (CO2)?
qs.e: In CO2 (O=C=O), carbon forms two double bonds (2 sigma domains), requiring sp hybridization and linear geometry.

qs.q: Which factor primarily explains why calcium oxide (CaO) has a much higher lattice energy than sodium chloride (NaCl)?
o: Calcium has a larger atomic radius than Sodium
CaO contains divalent ions (Ca2+, O2-) whereas NaCl contains monovalent ions (Na+, Cl-)
NaCl is covalent whereas CaO is metallic
Oxygen is less electronegative than Chlorine
qs.e: Lattice energy is proportional to (q1 * q2). For CaO, charges are (+2)(-2) = 4, compared to (+1)(-1) = 1 for NaCl.

qs.q: Why does ice float on liquid water?
o: Hydrogen bonding creates an open 3D cage structure in ice with lower density than liquid water
Water molecules expand covalently upon freezing
qs.e: Below 4°C, water molecules form a rigid tetrahedral hydrogen-bonded network that traps open space, making ice less dense than water.

qs.q: Which shape is possessed by sulfur hexafluoride (SF6) according to VSEPR theory?
qs.e: SF6 has 6 electron pairs around sulfur and 0 lone pairs, giving a regular octahedral geometry with 90 degree bond angles.

qs.q: How many lone pairs of electrons are on the central iodine atom in triiodide ion (I3-)?
qs.e: I3- central iodine has 7 valence electrons + 2 bonding electrons + 1 negative charge = 10 electrons (5 pairs: 2 bonding, 3 lone pairs).

qs.q: Which substance possesses the highest electrical conductivity in solid state?
qs.e: Copper is a metal with mobile delocalized electrons in its lattice that conduct electricity in solid state.

qs.q: In phosphorus pentachloride (PCl5), what are the bond angles between equatorial and axial bonds?
qs.e: PCl5 has trigonal bipyramidal shape: equatorial-equatorial angles are 120 degrees, and axial-equatorial angles are 90 degrees.

qs.q: Which molecule contains the shortest carbon-carbon bond length?
qs.e: Ethyne contains a triple bond (C≡C), which is shorter and stronger than double (C=C) or single (C-C) bonds.

qs.q: What is the primary cause of London dispersion forces between non-polar molecules?
o: Temporary dipoles induced by instantaneous fluctuations in electron density
qs.e: Momentary asymmetric electron distribution creates instantaneous dipoles that induce temporary dipoles in adjacent non-polar molecules.

qs.q: Which shape is adopted by xenon tetrafluoride (XeF4)?
qs.e: XeF4 has 6 electron pairs around Xe (4 bonding, 2 lone pairs). The lone pairs occupy opposite axial positions, leaving a square planar molecular geometry.

qs.q: In ammonium chloride (NH4Cl), which types of bonding are present?
o: Ionic, covalent, and coordinate covalent bonds
qs.e: NH4Cl contains covalent N-H bonds, one coordinate covalent N-H bond in NH4+, and ionic attraction between NH4+ and Cl-.

qs.q: Why is aluminum chloride (AlCl3) soluble in organic non-polar solvents like benzene?
o: AlCl3 is a simple ionic salt
AlCl3 exhibits significant covalent character due to high polarizing power of Al3+
AlCl3 forms metallic bonds with benzene
qs.e: Small, highly charged Al3+ polarizes large Cl- electron clouds (Fajans' rules), giving AlCl3 high covalent character and organic solubility.

qs.q: Which molecule possesses a permanent electric dipole moment?
qs.e: SO2 has a bent shape due to a lone pair on sulfur, so S-O bond dipoles do not cancel out, yielding a net permanent dipole.

qs.q: What is the total number of valence electrons present in a carbonate ion (CO32-)?
qs.e: Valence electrons: C = 4, 3 * O = 3 * 6 = 18, 2- charge = 2. Total = 4 + 18 + 2 = 24 valence electrons.

qs.q: According to Fajans' rules, which combination of ionic properties promotes the highest degree of covalent character in an ionic compound?
o: Large cation, small anion, and low ionic charges
Large cation, large anion, and neutral charge
Small cation, large anion, and high ionic charges
Small cation, small anion, and low ionic charges
qs.e: High charge density on a small cation coupled with a large polarizable electron cloud on an anion maximizes covalent character.

qs.q: What molecular geometry is exhibited by chlorine trifluoride (ClF3)?
qs.e: ClF3 has 5 electron domains around Cl (3 bonding, 2 lone pairs). Equatorially placed lone pairs result in a T-shaped molecular geometry.

qs.q: Comparing the bond angles in CH4 (109.5°), NH3 (107°), and H2O (104.5°), what accounts for this progressive decrease?
o: Increasing atomic mass of central atom
Lone pair-lone pair > lone pair-bonding pair > bonding pair-bonding pair repulsion
qs.e: Lone pairs exert greater repulsive forces than bonding pairs, pushing adjacent bonding pairs closer together as lone pair count increases.

qs.q: In benzene (C6H6), how many delocalized pi electrons circulate above and below the planar carbon ring?
qs.e: Each of the 6 sp2 hybridized carbons contributes one unhybridized p-electron, forming a continuous delocalized system of 6 pi electrons.

qs.q: Which compound exhibits intramolecular hydrogen bonding rather than intermolecular hydrogen bonding?
qs.e: In 2-nitrophenol (ortho-nitrophenol), the -OH and -NO2 groups are adjacent, allowing a hydrogen bond to form within the same molecule.

qs.q: What hybridization is utilized by sulfur in sulfur hexafluoride (SF6)?
qs.e: SF6 expands its valence shell to accommodate 6 bonding pairs using six sp3d2 hybrid orbitals directed octahedrally.

qs.q: Why is the boiling point of ethanol (78°C) vastly higher than its isomer dimethyl ether (-24°C)?
o: Ethanol has a higher molar mass than dimethyl ether
Dimethyl ether is an ionic compound
Ethanol forms intermolecular hydrogen bonds while dimethyl ether cannot
qs.e: Ethanol possesses an -OH group capable of intermolecular hydrogen bonding. Dimethyl ether (CH3-O-CH3) lacks O-H bonds.

qs.q: Which ion is diamagnetic?
qs.e: Zn2+ has configuration 3d10 where all d-orbitals are completely filled with paired electrons, exhibiting diamagnetism.

qs.q: In the resonance structures of ozone (O3), what is the formal bond order of each oxygen-oxygen bond?
qs.e: Ozone resonates between O=O-O and O-O=O structures, giving an average bond order of 3/2 = 1.5.

qs.q: Which shape is adopted by phosphorus trifluoride (PF3)?
qs.e: PF3 has 3 bonding pairs and 1 lone pair on phosphorus, forming a trigonal pyramidal structure (isostructural with NH3).

qs.q: What type of solid crystal lattice is formed by solid argon at extremely low temperatures?
o: Molecular lattice held by London dispersion forces
qs.e: Solid argon consists of individual non-polar Ar atoms held together in a face-centered cubic molecular lattice by weak London dispersion forces.

qs.q: Calculate the formal charge on the central nitrogen atom in a nitrate ion (NO3-) with single resonance Lewis structure.
qs.e: FC = Valence - Nonbonding - 0.5(Bonding) = 5 - 0 - 0.5(8) = 5 - 4 = +1.

qs.q: What is the molecular geometry of bromine pentafluoride (BrF5)?
qs.e: BrF5 has 6 electron pairs around Br (5 bonding, 1 lone pair). One lone pair on an octahedral domain leaves a square pyramidal geometry.

qs.q: Using Born-Haber cycle principles, calculate the lattice enthalpy of NaCl if enthalpy of formation = -411 kJ/mol, atomization of Na = +107 kJ/mol, IE1 of Na = +496 kJ/mol, atomization of Cl = +122 kJ/mol, EA1 of Cl = -349 kJ/mol.
According to Molecular Orbital Theory, what is the bond order and magnetic property of oxygen molecule (O2)?
o: Bond order 2, diamagnetic with 0 unpaired electrons
Bond order 2, paramagnetic with 2 unpaired electrons
qs.e: MO configuration of O2 gives 8 bonding and 4 antibonding electrons: BO = (8-4)/2 = 2. Two degenerate pi* antibonding orbitals hold 1 electron each (paramagnetic).

qs.q: What is the bond angle in trioxygen / ozone (O3)?
qs.e: Ozone central oxygen has 2 bonding domains and 1 lone pair (sp2 hybridization). Lone pair repulsion compresses the 120° angle to 116.8°.

qs.q: What is the numerical value of Avogadro's constant representing the number of particles in one mole of a substance?
qs.e: Avogadro's number is 6.02 x 10^23 particles per mole.

qs.q: What volume does one mole of any ideal gas occupy at standard temperature and pressure (STP)?
qs.e: At STP (273 K, 1 atm), 1 mole of any ideal gas occupies a molar volume of 22.4 dm3.

qs.q: Calculate the molar mass of calcium carbonate, CaCO3 (Ca=40, C=12, O=16).
How many moles are present in 18 grams of pure water, H2O (H=1, O=16)?
qs.e: Molar mass of H2O = 2(1) + 16 = 18 g/mol. Moles = mass / molar mass = 18 / 18 = 1.0 mol.

qs.q: What is the percentage composition by mass of oxygen in sodium hydroxide, NaOH (Na=23, O=16, H=1)?
How many hydrogen atoms are contained in 1 mole of methane molecules, CH4?
qs.e: 1 mole of CH4 contains 4 moles of H atoms = 4 * 6.02 x 10^23 = 2.408 x 10^24 H atoms.

qs.q: What mass of carbon dioxide (CO2) is produced by complete combustion of 12 grams of carbon (C=12, O=16)?
qs.e: C + O2 -> CO2. 12 g (1 mol) of C produces 1 mol of CO2 = 12 + 2(16) = 44 g.

qs.q: What volume of oxygen gas at STP is required to completely react with 4.0 moles of hydrogen gas to form water?
qs.e: 2H2 + O2 -> 2H2O. 4 mol H2 requires 2 mol O2. Volume O2 = 2 mol * 22.4 dm3/mol = 44.8 dm3.

qs.q: Calculate the mass of hydrated copper(II) sulfate, CuSO4.5H2O, needed to prepare 250 cm3 of 0.1 mol/dm3 solution (Cu=64, S=32, O=16, H=1).
Determine the percentage of nitrogen by mass in ammonium nitrate, NH4NO3 (N=14, H=1, O=16).
qs.e: Molar mass NH4NO3 = 28 + 4 + 48 = 80 g/mol. Mass of N = 28 g. % N = (28 / 80) * 100 = 35.0%.

qs.q: If 5.0 grams of hydrogen gas react with 32.0 grams of oxygen gas to form water, which reagent is the limiting reactant (H=1, O=16)?
qs.e: 2H2 + O2 -> 2H2O. 5.0g H2 = 2.5 mol H2. 32.0g O2 = 1.0 mol O2. 1.0 mol O2 requires 2.0 mol H2. Oxygen is limited.

qs.q: What is the total mass of 0.25 moles of sulfuric acid, H2SO4 (H=1, S=32, O=16)?
When 10.0 grams of calcium carbonate are completely decomposed by heating, what volume of CO2 gas is collected at STP (Ca=40, C=12, O=16)?
qs.e: CaCO3 -> CaO + CO2. 10.0g CaCO3 = 10/100 = 0.1 mol. Yields 0.1 mol CO2 = 0.1 * 22.4 dm3 = 2.24 dm3.

qs.q: How many total ions are produced in solution when 1 mole of aluminum sulfate, Al2(SO4)3, completely dissociates in water?
qs.e: Al2(SO4)3 -> 2Al3+ + 3SO4(2-). 1 formula unit gives 2 + 3 = 5 ions. 1 mole gives 5 * 6.02 x 10^23 ions.

qs.q: What is the concentration in g/dm3 of a solution containing 11.7 grams of NaCl dissolved in 500 cm3 of solution (Na=23, Cl=35.5)?
qs.e: Volume = 500 cm3 = 0.5 dm3. Concentration = 11.7 g / 0.5 dm3 = 23.4 g/dm3.

qs.q: Calculate the mass of iron produced when 160 grams of iron(III) oxide (Fe2O3) are completely reduced by carbon monoxide (Fe=56, O=16, C=12)?
qs.e: Fe2O3 + 3CO -> 2Fe + 3CO2. Molar mass Fe2O3 = 2(56) + 48 = 160 g/mol. 160g = 1 mol Fe2O3 -> 2 mol Fe = 2 * 56 = 112 g.

qs.q: What volume of 0.50 mol/dm3 HCl solution is needed to react completely with 2.12 grams of anhydrous sodium carbonate, Na2CO3 (Na=23, C=12, O=16)?
qs.e: Na2CO3 + 2HCl -> 2NaCl + H2O + CO2. Molar mass Na2CO3 = 106 g/mol. 2.12g = 0.02 mol. Requires 0.04 mol HCl. Vol = 0.04 / 0.50 = 0.08 dm3 = 80 cm3.

qs.q: How many moles of oxygen atoms are present in 0.5 moles of hydrated magnesium sulfate, MgSO4.7H2O?
qs.e: 1 formula unit contains 4 + 7 = 11 oxygen atoms. In 0.5 moles, oxygen atoms = 0.5 * 11 = 5.5 moles.

qs.q: What mass of ammonia (NH3) gas occupies a volume of 5.6 dm3 at STP (N=14, H=1)?
qs.e: Moles = 5.6 / 22.4 = 0.25 mol. Molar mass NH3 = 17 g/mol. Mass = 0.25 * 17 = 4.25 g.

qs.q: A student reacted 6.5 grams of zinc metal with excess dilute hydrochloric acid and collected 2.0 dm3 of hydrogen gas at STP. What is the percentage yield of hydrogen gas (Zn=65)?
What mass of potassium chlorate (KClO3) must be heated to produce 6.72 dm3 of oxygen gas at STP (K=39, Cl=35.5, O=16)?
What is the molarity of a 98 percent w/w concentrated H2SO4 solution having a density of 1.84 g/cm3 (H=1, S=32, O=16)?
Calculate the mass of copper deposited at the cathode when a current of 2.0 A is passed through aqueous CuSO4 for 48 minutes 15 seconds (Cu=64, F=96,500 C/mol).

When 20 cm3 of a gaseous hydrocarbon CnHm were burnt in 100 cm3 of oxygen, 60 cm3 of oxygen remained and 40 cm3 of CO2 were produced (all volumes at STP). Determine the molecular formula of the hydrocarbon.
qs.e: Hydrocarbon = 20 cm3. Reacted O2 = 100 - 60 = 40 cm3. Produced CO2 = 40 cm3. CO2/HC = 40/20 = 2 -> n=2. CxHy + (x + y/4)O2 -> xCO2 + y/2 H2O. 2 + y/4 = 40/20 = 2 -> y=4. Formula C2H4.

qs.q: What volume of 0.20 mol/dm3 NaOH solution is required to neutralize 25.0 cm3 of 0.10 mol/dm3 H2SO4 acid?
A sample of 2.0 grams of impure limestone produced 0.384 grams of CO2 on treatment with excess acid. What is the percentage purity of CaCO3 in the limestone (Ca=40, C=12, O=16)?
How many water molecules are present in a single drop of water weighing 0.05 grams (H=1, O=16)?
What mass of sodium hydroxide is required to react completely with 0.1 moles of phosphoric acid, H3PO4, to form trisodium phosphate, Na3PO4?
qs.e: H3PO4 + 3NaOH -> Na3PO4 + 3H2O. 0.1 mol H3PO4 requires 0.3 mol NaOH. Mass NaOH = 0.3 * 40 = 12.0 g.

qs.q: What is the total mass of oxygen contained in 0.2 moles of aluminum nitrate, Al(NO3)3 (Al=27, N=14, O=16)?
qs.e: 1 mol Al(NO3)3 has 9 mol O atoms = 9 * 16 = 144 g O. 0.2 mol has 0.2 * 144 = 28.8 g oxygen.

qs.q: If 10.0 cm3 of 1.0 mol/dm3 HCl are diluted with distilled water to a final volume of 250 cm3, what is the concentration of the diluted acid?
How many moles of electrons are required to reduce 1 mole of dichromate ions (Cr2O72-) to chromium(III) ions (Cr3+) in acid solution?
qs.e: Cr2O7(2-) + 14H+ + 6e- -> 2Cr3+ + 7H2O. 1 mole of dichromate requires 6 moles of electrons.

qs.q: When 1.0 mole of hydrocarbon C3H8 undergoes complete combustion, what total volume of gaseous products is formed at STP?
qs.e: C3H8(g) + 5O2(g) -> 3CO2(g) + 4H2O(g). At STP, water is liquid, but assuming gaseous products total = 3 + 4 = 7 moles gas = 7 * 22.4 = 156.8 dm3.

qs.q: Calculate the volume of 0.05 mol/dm3 KMnO4 solution needed to react completely with 20.0 cm3 of 0.25 mol/dm3 FeSO4 solution in acidic medium.
What is the empirical mass of a compound with empirical formula CH2O (C=12, H=1, O=16)?
qs.e: Empirical formula CH2O mass = 12 + 2(1) + 16 = 30 g/mol.

qs.q: A mixture of 10 cm3 of methane (CH4) and 10 cm3 of ethane (C2H6) was exploded with excess oxygen. What total volume of carbon dioxide gas was produced (all volumes measured at same temperature and pressure)?
What mass of lead(II) nitrate, Pb(NO3)2, is required to react completely with sodium iodide to produce 6.915 grams of yellow lead(II) iodide precipitate (Pb=207, I=127, N=14, O=16)?
qs.e: Pb(NO3)2 + 2NaI -> PbI2(s) + 2NaNO3. Molar mass PbI2 = 207 + 2(127) = 461 g/mol. Moles PbI2 = 6.915 / 461 = 0.015 mol. Molar mass Pb(NO3)2 = 331 g/mol. Mass = 0.015 * 331 = 4.965 g.

qs.q: An organic compound contains 40.0% C, 6.7% H, and 53.3% O by mass. If its vapor density relative to hydrogen is 30, determine its molecular formula (C=12, H=1, O=16).
qs.e: Molar mass = 2 * vapor density = 2 * 30 = 60 g/mol. Empirical formula CH2O (mass 30). n = 60/30 = 2 -> Molecular formula C2H4O2.

qs.q: When 50 cm3 of 0.2 mol/dm3 BaCl2 is mixed with 50 cm3 of 0.3 mol/dm3 Na2SO4, what mass of BaSO4 precipitate is formed (Ba=137, S=32, O=16)?
What is the concentration of chloride ions in a solution made by mixing 100 cm3 of 0.1 mol/dm3 NaCl with 100 cm3 of 0.2 mol/dm3 CaCl2?
qs.e: From NaCl: 0.1 * 0.1 = 0.01 mol Cl-. From CaCl2: 0.1 * 0.2 * 2 = 0.04 mol Cl-. Total Cl- = 0.05 mol in 0.2 dm3 = 0.05 / 0.2 = 0.25 mol/dm3.

qs.q: In an experiment, 0.48 grams of magnesium ribbon reacted with excess N2 gas to form 0.666 grams of magnesium nitride. What is the empirical formula of magnesium nitride (Mg=24, N=14)?
What volume of SO2 gas at STP is produced when 12.8 grams of copper react completely with excess concentrated H2SO4 (Cu=64, S=32, O=16)?
Calculate the mass of anhydrous sodium carbonate present in 250 cm3 of a 0.05 mol/dm3 solution (Na=23, C=12, O=16).
qs.e: Molar mass Na2CO3 = 106 g/mol. Moles = 0.25 * 0.05 = 0.0125 mol. Mass = 0.0125 * 106 = 1.325 g.

qs.q: What mass of active oxygen is released when 0.2 moles of sodium peroxide (Na2O2) react completely with water according to 2Na2O2 + 2H2O -> 4NaOH + O2 (O=16)?
qs.e: 2 mol Na2O2 yields 1 mol O2 (32g). 0.2 mol Na2O2 yields 0.1 mol O2 = 0.1 * 32 = 3.2 g oxygen.

qs.q: If 0.50 moles of an ideal gas exert a pressure of 2.0 atm at 27°C, what volume does the gas occupy (R = 0.0821 L atm / mol K)?
How many total atoms are present in 0.1 moles of sucrose, C12H22O11?
qs.e: 1 formula unit contains 12 + 22 + 11 = 45 atoms. 0.1 mol contains 0.1 * 45 * 6.02 x 10^23 = 2.709 x 10^24 atoms.

qs.q: A hydrated salt MX.nH2O weighing 5.0 grams loses 1.8 grams of water when heated to constant mass. If the molar mass of anhydrous salt MX is 160 g/mol, determine the value of n (H=1, O=16).
When 100 cm3 of 0.5 mol/dm3 AgNO3 is added to 100 cm3 of 0.2 mol/dm3 K2CrO4, what is the mass of Ag2CrO4 precipitate formed (Ag=108, Cr=52, O=16)?
