qs.e: 2AgNO3 + K2CrO4 -> Ag2CrO4 + 2KNO3. Moles Ag+ = 0.1*0.5 = 0.05 mol. Moles CrO4 = 0.1*0.2 = 0.02 mol. Limiting = CrO4 (needs 0.04 Ag+). Moles Ag2CrO4 = 0.02 mol. Molar mass = 2(108)+52+64 = 332 g/mol. Mass = 0.02 * 332 = 6.64 g.

qs.q: A gaseous compound of nitrogen and oxygen contains 30.4% N and 69.6% O by mass. If 0.23 grams of this gas occupy 112 cm3 at STP, what is its molecular formula (N=14, O=16)?
qs.e: N: 30.4/14 = 2.17. O: 69.6/16 = 4.35 -> Empirical NO2 (mass 46). Moles gas = 0.112 / 22.4 = 0.005 mol. Molar mass = 0.23 / 0.005 = 46 g/mol, which is NO2.

qs.q: What volume of 0.1 mol/dm3 K2Cr2O7 in acidic medium is required to oxidize 50 cm3 of 0.3 mol/dm3 H2C2O4 (oxalic acid) solution according to Cr2O72- + 3C2O42- + 14H+ -> 2Cr3+ + 6CO2 + 7H2O?
qs.e: Moles oxalate = 0.05 * 0.3 = 0.015 mol. Ratio dichromate : oxalate = 1 : 3. Moles dichromate = 0.015 / 3 = 0.005 mol. Vol = 0.005 / 0.1 = 0.05 dm3 = 50 cm3.

qs.q: A sample of brass alloy weighing 2.0 grams was dissolved in nitric acid and treated with excess KI. The liberated iodine required 25.0 cm3 of 0.20 mol/dm3 Na2S2O3 for titration. What is the percentage of copper in the brass alloy (Cu=64, 2Cu2+ + 4I- -> 2CuI + I2; I2 + 2S2O32- -> 2I- + S4O62-)?
What term defines the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms of each element present in a chemical compound?
qs.e: The empirical formula represents the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms in a compound.

qs.q: What is the empirical formula of hydrogen peroxide, H2O2?
qs.e: Simplest whole-number ratio of H:O in H2O2 is 1:1, giving empirical formula HO.

qs.q: Which expression represents molar concentration (molarity, M) of a solute in solution?
o: Moles of solute / Volume of solution in dm3
Moles of solute / Mass of solvent in kg
Mass of solute in g / Volume of solution in dm3
Volume of solute / Volume of solution
qs.e: Molar concentration = moles of solute / volume of solution in cubic decimeters (dm3).

qs.q: What unit is standard for expressing molarity of an aqueous solution?
qs.e: Molarity is standardly measured in moles per cubic decimeter (mol/dm3 or M).

qs.q: What is the empirical formula of benzene, C6H6?
qs.e: Simplest whole-number ratio of 6:6 is 1:1, giving empirical formula CH.

qs.q: How many moles of solute are contained in 2.0 dm3 of a 0.5 mol/dm3 glucose solution?
qs.e: Moles = concentration * volume = 0.5 mol/dm3 * 2.0 dm3 = 1.0 mole.

qs.q: Which compound has the same empirical formula and molecular formula?
qs.e: H2O cannot be simplified further (ratio 2:1 is already lowest whole numbers), so empirical and molecular formulas are identical.

qs.q: A compound contains 85.7% Carbon and 14.3% Hydrogen by mass. What is its empirical formula (C=12, H=1)?
qs.e: Moles C = 85.7 / 12 = 7.14. Moles H = 14.3 / 1 = 14.3. Ratio H/C = 14.3 / 7.14 = 2. Empirical formula CH2.

qs.q: If the empirical formula of a hydrocarbon is CH2 and its relative molecular mass is 56, what is its molecular formula (C=12, H=1)?
qs.e: Empirical formula mass CH2 = 12 + 2 = 14. n = 56 / 14 = 4. Molecular formula = (CH2)4 = C4H8.

qs.q: What volume of 2.0 mol/dm3 stock H2SO4 is required to prepare 500 cm3 of 0.20 mol/dm3 dilute H2SO4?
Calculate the mass concentration in g/dm3 of a 0.25 mol/dm3 sodium hydroxide solution, NaOH (Na=23, O=16, H=1).
qs.e: Molar mass NaOH = 40 g/mol. Mass concentration = molarity * molar mass = 0.25 * 40 = 10.0 g/dm3.

qs.q: Chemical analysis of a phosphorus oxide sample reveals that it contains 43.6% Phosphorus and 56.4% Oxygen by mass. What is its empirical formula (P=31, O=16)?
qs.e: Moles P = 43.6 / 31 = 1.406. Moles O = 56.4 / 16 = 3.525. Ratio O/P = 3.525 / 1.406 = 2.5 = 5/2. Empirical formula P2O5.

qs.q: A salt solution is prepared by dissolving 14.2 grams of Na2SO4 in water to make 250 cm3 of solution. What is the sodium ion (Na+) concentration in mol/dm3 (Na=23, S=32, O=16)?
qs.e: Molar mass Na2SO4 = 142 g/mol. Moles Na2SO4 = 14.2 / 142 = 0.10 mol in 0.25 dm3 = 0.40 mol/dm3 Na2SO4. Each formula unit yields 2 Na+ ions, so [Na+] = 2 * 0.40 = 0.80 mol/dm3.

qs.q: Determining the empirical formula of an oxide of iron gave 70.0% Fe and 30.0% O by mass. What is the empirical formula (Fe=56, O=16)?
qs.e: Moles Fe = 70.0 / 56 = 1.25. Moles O = 30.0 / 16 = 1.875. Ratio O/Fe = 1.875 / 1.25 = 1.5 = 3/2. Empirical formula Fe2O3.

qs.q: How many grams of anhydrous copper(II) sulfate (CuSO4) remain when 24.95 grams of hydrated CuSO4.5H2O are heated to complete dryness (Cu=63.5, S=32, O=16, H=1)?
qs.e: Molar mass CuSO4.5H2O = 249.5 g/mol. 24.95g = 0.10 mol. Molar mass anhydrous CuSO4 = 159.5 g/mol. Mass remaining = 0.10 * 159.5 = 15.95 g.

qs.q: What volume of water must be added to 100 cm3 of 1.0 mol/dm3 HCl solution to dilute its concentration to 0.20 mol/dm3?
Analysis of a compound showed 52.2% C, 13.0% H, and 34.8% O. What is its empirical formula (C=12, H=1, O=16)?
A solution contains 5.85 g of NaCl in 250 cm3 solution. What is its molar concentration (Na=23, Cl=35.5)?
qs.e: Molar mass NaCl = 58.5 g/mol. Moles = 5.85 / 58.5 = 0.10 mol in 0.25 dm3. Concentration = 0.10 / 0.25 = 0.40 mol/dm3.

qs.q: What is the empirical formula of an organic acid containing 26.7% C, 2.2% H, and 71.1% O by mass (C=12, H=1, O=16)?
When 1.00 gram of a hydrocarbon was burned completely in oxygen, 3.14 grams of CO2 and 1.29 grams of H2O were formed. Determine the empirical formula of the hydrocarbon (C=12, H=1, O=16).
A hydrated salt of formula washing soda Na2CO3.nH2O weighing 2.86 grams lost 1.80 grams of water on strong heating. What is the value of n (Na=23, C=12, O=16, H=1)?
What is the concentration of nitrate ions (NO3-) when 50 cm3 of 0.2 mol/dm3 Mg(NO3)2 is mixed with 50 cm3 of 0.4 mol/dm3 Al(NO3)3?
qs.e: From Mg(NO3)2: 0.05 * 0.2 * 2 = 0.02 mol NO3-. From Al(NO3)3: 0.05 * 0.4 * 3 = 0.06 mol NO3-. Total NO3- = 0.08 mol in 0.10 dm3 = 0.80 mol/dm3.

qs.q: A volatile liquid compound contains 82.8% Carbon and 17.2% Hydrogen. If 0.58 grams of its vapor occupy 224 cm3 at STP, find its molecular formula (C=12, H=1).
qs.e: Moles C = 82.8/12 = 6.9. Moles H = 17.2/1 = 17.2 -> ratio H/C = 2.5 -> empirical C2H5 (mass 29). Moles vapor = 0.224 / 22.4 = 0.01 mol. Molar mass = 0.58 / 0.01 = 58 g/mol. n = 58/29 = 2 -> C4H10.

qs.q: How many cm3 of 0.5 mol/dm3 H2SO4 are required to completely react with 25 cm3 of 0.8 mol/dm3 KOH?
An organic substance contains C, H, and Cl. 0.20 grams of the compound gave 0.22 grams of CO2 and 0.09 grams of H2O. What is the empirical formula (C=12, H=1, Cl=35.5, O=16)?
What mass of sodium chloride is formed when 50 cm3 of 0.40 mol/dm3 HCl reacts with 50 cm3 of 0.50 mol/dm3 NaOH (Na=23, Cl=35.5)?
qs.e: Moles HCl = 0.05 * 0.4 = 0.02 mol. Moles NaOH = 0.05 * 0.5 = 0.025 mol. Limiting = HCl (0.02 mol). Moles NaCl = 0.02 mol. Mass = 0.02 * 58.5 = 1.17 g.

qs.q: A student dissolves 10.0 grams of impure KOH in water to make 500 cm3 solution. If 25.0 cm3 of this solution neutralizes 20.0 cm3 of 0.20 mol/dm3 HCl, what is the percentage purity of the KOH sample (K=39, O=16, H=1)?
qs.e: Moles HCl = 0.02 * 0.2 = 0.004 mol = Moles KOH in 25 cm3. In 500 cm3, moles KOH = 0.004 * 20 = 0.08 mol. Mass pure KOH = 0.08 * 56 = 4.48 g. % purity = (4.48 / 10.0) * 100 = 44.8%.

qs.q: An oxide of nitrogen contains 30.43% Nitrogen by mass. If its relative molecular mass is 92, what is its molecular formula (N=14, O=16)?
qs.e: Mass N = 0.3043 * 92 = 28 g -> 2 N atoms. Mass O = 92 - 28 = 64 g -> 4 O atoms. Molecular formula N2O4.

qs.q: What volume of 0.1 mol/dm3 Ba(OH)2 solution is needed to completely precipitate the sulfate ions in 30 cm3 of 0.2 mol/dm3 Fe2(SO4)3 solution?
qs.e: Fe2(SO4)3 + 3Ba(OH)2 -> 3BaSO4 + 2Fe(OH)3. Moles Fe2(SO4)3 = 0.03 * 0.2 = 0.006 mol. Moles Ba(OH)2 needed = 3 * 0.006 = 0.018 mol. Volume = 0.018 / 0.1 = 0.18 dm3 = 180 cm3.

qs.q: Determination of water of crystallization in Epsom salt, MgSO4.xH2O: 2.46 grams of hydrated salt yielded 1.20 grams of anhydrous MgSO4. Calculate x (Mg=24, S=32, O=16, H=1).
What is the concentration of H+ ions in a solution prepared by mixing 100 cm3 of 0.2 mol/dm3 HCl with 100 cm3 of 0.1 mol/dm3 NaOH?
qs.e: Moles H+ = 0.1 * 0.2 = 0.02 mol. Moles OH- = 0.1 * 0.1 = 0.01 mol. Remaining H+ = 0.01 mol in total volume 0.2 dm3. [H+] = 0.01 / 0.2 = 0.05 mol/dm3.

qs.q: A compound of sulfur and oxygen contains 50.0% S by mass. What is its empirical formula (S=32, O=16)?
qs.e: Moles S = 50/32 = 1.5625. Moles O = 50/16 = 3.125. Ratio O/S = 2. Empirical formula SO2.

qs.q: What volume of 0.02 mol/dm3 K2Cr2O7 is required to oxidize 25 cm3 of 0.10 mol/dm3 FeSO4 in acidic solution (Cr2O72- + 6Fe2+ + 14H+ -> 2Cr3+ + 6Fe3+ + 7H2O)?
Calculate the mass of crystalline oxalic acid, (COOH)2.2H2O, required to prepare 250 cm3 of 0.05 mol/dm3 standard solution (C=12, O=16, H=1).
qs.e: Molar mass (COOH)2.2H2O = 2(45) + 36 = 126 g/mol. Moles needed = 0.25 * 0.05 = 0.0125 mol. Mass = 0.0125 * 126 = 1.575 g.

qs.q: A 1.50 gram sample of an organic compound containing C, H, and O was burnt in excess oxygen producing 2.20 grams of CO2 and 0.90 grams of H2O. What is the empirical formula of the compound (C=12, H=1, O=16)?

What volume of 0.10 mol/dm3 Na2S2O3 solution is needed to titrate the iodine liberated when excess KI is added to 25.0 cm3 of 0.02 mol/dm3 KIO3 in acid solution (IO3- + 5I- + 6H+ -> 3I2 + 3H2O; I2 + 2S2O32- -> 2I- + S4O62-)?
Complete combustion of 0.20 moles of a gaseous alkane produced 17.92 dm3 of CO2 at STP. What is the molecular formula of the alkane?
qs.e: Moles CO2 = 17.92 / 22.4 = 0.80 mol CO2. Carbon atoms per alkane molecule = 0.80 / 0.20 = 4. Alkane C4H10.

qs.q: A sample of 2.50 grams of hydrated copper(II) sulfate was heated to constant mass. The residue weighed 1.60 grams. What is the percentage of water of crystallization in the crystal (Cu=64, S=32, O=16, H=1)?
What is the molarity of pure water at 4°C with a density of 1.00 g/cm3 (H=1, O=16)?
qs.e: 1 dm3 water = 1000 grams. Moles water = 1000 / 18 = 55.55 mol. Concentration = 55.5 mol/dm3.

qs.q: When 20 cm3 of a gaseous oxide of nitrogen decompose completely, 20 cm3 of N2 gas and 10 cm3 of O2 gas are formed (all volumes at same temperature and pressure). What is the formula of the oxide?
qs.e: 20 cm3 oxide -> 20 cm3 N2 + 10 cm3 O2. Equation: 2 NxOy -> 2 N2 + 1 O2. 2x = 4 -> x=2; 2y = 2 -> y=1. Formula N2O.

qs.q: Calculate the mass of sodium hydroxide contained in 250 cm3 of 0.50 mol/dm3 solution (Na=23, O=16, H=1).
An organic compound has an empirical formula of C2H4O and a relative vapor density of 44. What is its molecular formula (C=12, H=1, O=16)?
qs.e: Molar mass = 2 * 44 = 88 g/mol. Empirical mass C2H4O = 2(12) + 4 + 16 = 44. n = 88 / 44 = 2. Molecular formula C4H8O2.

qs.q: What volume of 0.2 mol/dm3 HCl is needed to completely react with 0.106 grams of anhydrous Na2CO3 (Na=23, C=12, O=16)?
qs.e: Na2CO3 + 2HCl -> 2NaCl + H2O + CO2. 0.106g Na2CO3 = 0.106 / 106 = 0.001 mol. Requires 0.002 mol HCl. Vol = 0.002 / 0.2 = 0.010 dm3 = 10 cm3.

qs.q: A solution contains 10.0% by mass of NaCl and has a density of 1.07 g/cm3. Calculate its molarity (Na=23, Cl=35.5).
qs.e: 1 dm3 solution = 1070 g. Mass NaCl = 0.10 * 1070 = 107 g. Moles = 107 / 58.5 = 1.829 mol/dm3.

qs.q: What mass of Fe3O4 is produced when 11.2 grams of iron wire react completely with excess steam according to 3Fe + 4H2O -> Fe3O4 + 4H2 (Fe=56, O=16)?

A 0.500 gram sample of an organic nitrogenous compound was analyzed by Kjeldahl's method. The ammonia evolved was absorbed in 50.0 cm3 of 0.100 mol/dm3 H2SO4. The excess acid required 28.0 cm3 of 0.100 mol/dm3 NaOH for complete neutralization. Calculate the percentage of Nitrogen in the sample (N=14).

A mixture of Na2CO3 and NaHCO3 weighing 2.00 grams required 22.0 cm3 of 1.00 mol/dm3 HCl for neutralization using methyl orange indicator. Calculate the percentage of Na2CO3 in the mixture (Na=23, C=12, O=16, H=1).

When 1.00 gram of a metal M was burnt in oxygen, 1.25 grams of its oxide were obtained. If the specific heat capacity of metal M is 0.214 J/g K, determine the exact atomic mass of M (Dulong and Petit law: Atomic mass x Specific heat ~ 25 J/mol K).
qs.e: Approx atomic mass ~ 25 / 0.214 = 116.8 g/mol. Mass M = 1.00g, Mass O = 0.25g. Equivalent mass M = (1.00/0.25)*8 = 32 g. Valence = 116.8 / 32 = 3.65 -> 4. Exact atomic mass = 4 * 32 = 128 or 3.5 * 32 = 112 g/mol.

qs.q: An aqueous solution of a non-volatile non-electrolyte solute boils at 100.26°C. If the ebullioscopic constant (Kb) for water is 0.52 K kg/mol, what is the molality of the solution?
What is the molar solubility of silver chromate, Ag2CrO4, in pure water if its solubility product constant Ksp is 1.1 x 10^-12 at 25°C?
Which law states that the volume of a fixed mass of gas is inversely proportional to its pressure at constant temperature?
qs.e: Boyle's Law states that P1V1 = P2V2 for a fixed mass of gas at constant temperature.

qs.q: Which law states that the volume of a fixed mass of gas is directly proportional to its absolute temperature at constant pressure?
qs.e: Charles's Law states that V1/T1 = V2/T2 at constant pressure when temperature is measured in Kelvin.

qs.q: What temperature on the Celsius scale corresponds to absolute zero (0 Kelvin)?
qs.e: Absolute zero is 0 K, which equals -273.15°C (commonly taken as -273°C).

qs.q: According to the kinetic theory of gases, what happens to the average kinetic energy of gas molecules when temperature increases?
qs.e: The absolute temperature of a gas is directly proportional to the average kinetic energy of its constituent molecules.

qs.q: Which gas law relates the rate of diffusion of a gas to its molar mass?
qs.e: Graham's Law of diffusion states that the rate of diffusion of a gas is inversely proportional to the square root of its molar mass.

qs.q: What is the total pressure of a mixture of non-reacting gases equal to according to Dalton's law?
qs.e: Dalton's Law states that total pressure P_total = P1 + P2 + P3 + ... for non-reacting gases.

qs.q: What conversion factor is used to convert temperature from Celsius (°C) to Kelvin (K)?
qs.e: To convert temperature from Celsius degrees to Kelvin units, add 273 (or 273.15) to the Celsius value.

qs.q: A sample of gas occupies a volume of 500 cm3 at a pressure of 1.0 atm. What volume will it occupy if the pressure is increased to 2.5 atm at constant temperature?
A gas occupies 300 cm3 at 27°C. What will be its volume at 127°C if pressure remains constant?
Comparing the rates of diffusion of methane (CH4, molar mass 16) and sulfur dioxide (SO2, molar mass 64), how much faster does methane diffuse?
qs.e: r(CH4)/r(SO2) = sqrt(M(SO2)/M(CH4)) = sqrt(64/16) = sqrt(4) = 2. Methane diffuses twice as fast as SO2.

qs.q: A gas mixture contains 0.2 moles of nitrogen and 0.8 moles of oxygen at a total pressure of 5.0 atm. What is the partial pressure of nitrogen?
qs.e: Mole fraction N2 = 0.2 / (0.2 + 0.8) = 0.2. Partial pressure P(N2) = 0.2 * 5.0 atm = 1.0 atm.

qs.q: Under which conditions of temperature and pressure does a real gas behave most like an ideal gas?
qs.e: High temperature minimizes intermolecular forces and low pressure makes molecular volume negligible relative to container volume.

qs.q: If 100 cm3 of oxygen gas diffuses through a porous plug in 20 seconds, how long will it take for 100 cm3 of hydrogen gas to diffuse under identical conditions (O=16, H=1)?
What happens to the pressure exerted by a gas inside a rigid container when its temperature in Kelvin is doubled?
qs.e: According to Gay-Lussac's pressure law (P1/T1 = P2/T2), pressure is directly proportional to absolute temperature.

qs.q: Calculate the volume occupied by 0.1 moles of CO2 gas at 27°C and 1.0 atm pressure (R = 0.0821 dm3 atm / mol K).
A gas collected over water at 25°C has a total pressure of 755 mmHg. If the saturated vapor pressure of water at 25°C is 24 mmHg, what is the partial pressure of the dry gas?
qs.e: P_dry = P_total - P_water = 755 - 24 = 731 mmHg.

qs.q: What is the density of oxygen gas (O2) in g/dm3 at STP (molar mass O2 = 32 g/mol, molar volume at STP = 22.4 dm3/mol)?
qs.e: Density = molar mass / molar volume = 32 / 22.4 = 1.428 g/dm3.

qs.q: Which property of liquids causes them to form spherical droplets and resist external forces?
qs.e: Surface tension is the cohesive force among liquid molecules at the surface that minimizes surface area into spherical shapes.

qs.q: When a liquid reaches its boiling point, how does its equilibrium vapor pressure compare to atmospheric pressure?
o: Vapor pressure exceeds atmospheric pressure by 2 atm
Vapor pressure is half atmospheric pressure
qs.e: Boiling occurs when the equilibrium vapor pressure of a liquid equals the prevailing external atmospheric pressure.

qs.q: A balloon filled with helium occupies 4.0 dm3 at 27°C and 1.0 atm. What volume will it occupy at an altitude where temperature is -23°C and pressure is 0.50 atm?

It takes 50 seconds for 200 cm3 of oxygen to diffuse through a porous membrane. How long will it take for 200 cm3 of an unknown gas X to diffuse under identical conditions if gas X has a molar mass of 64 g/mol (O2=32)?
A gas cylinder contains 0.64 grams of O2 and 0.56 grams of N2. Calculate the mole fraction of N2 in the cylinder (O=16, N=14).
A 2.0 L flask contains neon gas at 300 K and 1.5 atm. If the gas is transferred to a 5.0 L flask and heated to 450 K, what is the final pressure?
Determining the relative molecular mass of a volatile liquid: 0.29 grams of vapor occupied 112 cm3 at STP. What is its molar mass?
If gas A diffuses 1.5 times faster than gas B, what is the ratio of the molar mass of gas B to gas A (MB / MA)?
What is the molar volume of an ideal gas at 27°C and 1.0 atm pressure (R = 0.0821 dm3 atm / mol K)?
A gas mixture contains 4.0 g of He and 16.0 g of O2. If the total pressure is 3.0 atm, what is the partial pressure of Helium (He=4, O=16)?
qs.e: Moles He = 4/4 = 1.0 mol. Moles O2 = 16/32 = 0.5 mol. Total moles = 1.5. Mole fraction He = 1.0/1.5 = 2/3. Partial pressure He = (2/3) * 3.0 = 2.0 atm.

qs.q: Why do real gases deviate from ideal gas behavior at extremely high pressures?
o: Intermolecular attractive forces become significant and molecular volume is no longer negligible
qs.e: At high pressure, gas molecules are forced close together, making finite molecular volume and attractive forces non-negligible.

qs.q: Equal volumes of CO2 and SO2 gases under identical temperature and pressure conditions contain equal numbers of what?
qs.e: Avogadro's Law states that equal volumes of all gases under identical conditions contain equal numbers of molecules.

qs.q: What volume of dry hydrogen gas at STP is collected when 250 cm3 of wet H2 gas is collected over water at 27°C and 765 mmHg (SVP of water at 27°C = 25 mmHg)?
If the rate of diffusion of gas X is 4 times that of gas Y, what is the relative vapor density ratio (VD_Y / VD_X)?
qs.e: rX/rY = sqrt(VD_Y / VD_X) = 4 => VD_Y / VD_X = 4^2 = 16.

qs.q: What pressure is exerted by 32.0 grams of oxygen gas contained in a 10.0 dm3 vessel at 27°C (R = 0.0821 dm3 atm / mol K, O=16)?
Which gas diffuses fastest at room temperature among NH3, HCl, CO2, and SO2 (N=14, H=1, Cl=35.5, C=12, O=16, S=32)?
qs.e: Molar masses: NH3=17, HCl=36.5, CO2=44, SO2=64. Lowest molar mass (NH3) diffuses fastest.

qs.q: How does increasing the external atmospheric pressure affect the boiling point of liquid water?
o: Has no effect on boiling point
qs.e: Higher external pressure requires water vapor pressure to reach a higher value before boiling occurs, raising the boiling point (e.g. in pressure cookers).

qs.q: In van der Waals equation for real gases (P + a/V2)(V - b) = RT, what do parameters 'a' and 'b' account for?
o: 'a' accounts for molecular volume; 'b' accounts for intermolecular forces
'a' accounts for kinetic energy; 'b' accounts for mass
'a' accounts for intermolecular forces; 'b' accounts for molecular volume
'a' accounts for pressure; 'b' accounts for temperature
qs.e: Parameter 'a' corrects for attractive forces between gas molecules; 'b' corrects for finite volume occupied by gas molecules.

qs.q: A 5.0 dm3 container holds 2.0 mol of N2 and 3.0 mol of H2 at 400 K. Calculate the total pressure in atm (R = 0.0821 dm3 atm / mol K).
Calculate the root-mean-square speed (v_rms) of nitrogen molecules (N2, molar mass 0.028 kg/mol) at 300 K (R = 8.314 J/mol K).
If 50 cm3 of carbon monoxide diffuses through an orifice in 14.14 seconds, how long will it take for 50 cm3 of carbon dioxide to diffuse under the same conditions (C=12, O=16)?
At what temperature in Kelvin will the average kinetic energy of gas molecules be exactly double its value at 27°C?
qs.e: T1 = 27 + 273 = 300 K. Kinetic energy is proportional to T. Doubling KE requires T2 = 2 * 300 K = 600 K.

qs.q: A gas occupies 1000 cm3 at STP. To what temperature in °C must it be heated to double its volume if pressure is tripled?
Calculate the density of propane gas (C3H8, molar mass 44 g/mol) at 1.5 atm pressure and 27°C (R = 0.0821 dm3 atm / mol K).

A mixture of 2.0 moles of H2 and 1.0 mole of O2 is sparked in a closed vessel to form water. What is the total pressure remaining in the 10 dm3 vessel at 100°C if water is completely in gas state (R = 0.0821 dm3 atm / mol K)?
What is the ratio of rates of diffusion of Hydrogen gas (H2) to Deuterium gas (D2) at the same temperature (H=1, D=2)?
Why does liquid water have an abnormally high surface tension compared to ethanol?
o: Water forms an extensive 3D network of strong hydrogen bonds
qs.e: Multiple hydrogen bonds per water molecule create powerful inward cohesive forces at the liquid surface.

qs.q: What volume is occupied by 14.0 grams of nitrogen gas (N2) at 27°C and 750 mmHg pressure (N=14, R = 0.0821 dm3 atm / mol K, 760 mmHg = 1 atm)?
The mean free path (lambda) of gas molecules in kinetic theory is inversely proportional to which quantity?
o: Number density of molecules and square of molecular diameter
qs.e: Mean free path lambda = 1 / (sqrt(2) * pi * d^2 * n_V), where d is molecular diameter and n_V is number density.

qs.q: Calculate the Joule-Thomson inversion temperature (T_inv) for a gas in terms of van der Waals constants 'a' and 'b' (R = gas constant).
qs.e: The inversion temperature above which a gas warms upon expansion is T_inv = 2a / (R b).

qs.q: A mixture of 0.50 mol of CH4 and 0.50 mol of C2H6 exerts a total pressure of 2.0 atm in a closed vessel. If 10% of CH4 diffuses out through a pinhole, what is the new mole fraction of C2H6 in the remaining gas inside?
qs.e: Remaining CH4 = 0.50 * 0.90 = 0.45 mol. C2H6 = 0.50 mol. Total remaining = 0.95 mol. Mole fraction C2H6 = 0.50 / 0.95 = 0.526.

qs.q: Using the Clausius-Clapeyron equation ln(P2/P1) = (ΔH_vap/R)(1/T1 - 1/T2), calculate the enthalpy of vaporization of water if vapor pressure is 24 mmHg at 25°C (298 K) and 760 mmHg at 100°C (373 K) (R = 8.314 J/mol K).
What is the critical compressibility factor (Z_c = P_c V_c / R T_c) predicted for a gas obeying the van der Waals equation of state?
According to the Brønsted-Lowry theory, an acid is defined as what type of species?
qs.e: Brønsted-Lowry theory defines an acid as a proton (H+) donor.

qs.q: What is the pH value of pure neutral water at 25°C?
qs.e: At 25°C, pure neutral water has [H+] = 10^-7 M, giving a pH of 7.0.

qs.q: Which indicator changes color from yellow in basic solution to pink/red in acidic solution?
qs.e: Methyl orange turns red/pink in acidic solution (pH < 3.1) and yellow in alkaline solution (pH > 4.4).

qs.q: What is the product of the hydrogen ion concentration [H+] and hydroxide ion concentration [OH-] in pure water at 25°C?
qs.e: The ionic product of water Kw = [H+][OH-] = 1.0 x 10^-14 mol2/dm6 at 25°C.

qs.q: Which acid is classified as a strong dibasic mineral acid?
qs.e: H2SO4 completely ionizes in dilute solution releasing two protons per molecule, making it a strong dibasic acid.

qs.q: What name is given to a solution that resists changes in pH when small amounts of acid or base are added?
qs.e: A buffer solution maintains a nearly constant pH upon addition of small amounts of acid or alkali.

qs.q: Which base is commonly used in laboratory titrations as a primary standard base after standardization or anhydrous Na2CO3?
qs.e: Anhydrous sodium carbonate (Na2CO3) is a stable primary standard base used to standardize acid solutions.

qs.q: Determine the pH value of a dilute hydrochloric acid solution having a hydronium ion concentration of 0.001 mol/dm3.
What is the pH of a 0.01 mol/dm3 sodium hydroxide (NaOH) solution at 25°C?
In the reaction NH3 + H2O <-> NH4+ + OH-, which species acts as the conjugate acid of ammonia (NH3)?
qs.e: NH3 accepts a proton to form NH4+. Thus NH4+ is the conjugate acid of the base NH3.

qs.q: Which indicator is most suitable for titrating a weak acid (e.g. ethanoic acid) against a strong base (e.g. NaOH)?
qs.e: Weak acid vs strong base titration has an equivalence point in the alkaline region (pH 8-10), matching phenolphthalein (pH 8.3-10.0).

qs.q: What is the conjugate base of the hydrogen sulfate ion, HSO4-?
qs.e: HSO4- loses a proton (H+) to form its conjugate base, the sulfate ion SO4(2-).

qs.q: What volume of 0.10 mol/dm3 H2SO4 is required to completely neutralize 20.0 cm3 of 0.20 mol/dm3 NaOH solution?
A solution has a hydrogen ion concentration of 2.0 x 10^-5 mol/dm3. Calculate its pH (log 2 = 0.301).
Which definition classifies a Lewis acid as an electron pair acceptor?
qs.e: Lewis theory defines an acid as an electron-pair acceptor and a base as an electron-pair donor.

qs.q: Why does a solution of aluminum chloride (AlCl3) in water test acidic to litmus paper?
o: Al3+ undergoes hydrolysis yielding free H3O+ ions
qs.e: Small highly charged Al3+ polarizes water ligands: [Al(H2O)6]3+ + H2O <-> [Al(H2O)5(OH)]2+ + H3O+.

qs.q: What is the concentration of H+ ions in a solution with a pH of 2.0?
Which gas is evolved when dilute hydrochloric acid reacts with copper(II) carbonate?
qs.e: CuCO3 + 2HCl -> CuCl2 + H2O + CO2(g). Carbon dioxide gas effervesces.

qs.q: What happens to the pH of an acidic solution when it is diluted with a large excess of distilled water?
qs.e: Diluting an acid decreases [H+], causing pH to increase toward neutral pH 7.

qs.q: Calculate the pH of a 0.05 mol/dm3 sulfuric acid solution (H2SO4), assuming complete ionization of both protons.
A weak acid HA has an acid dissociation constant Ka = 1.0 x 10^-5. Calculate the pH of a 0.10 mol/dm3 solution of HA.
What volume of 0.50 mol/dm3 KOH is required to completely neutralize 25.0 cm3 of 0.20 mol/dm3 H3PO4 (phosphoric acid)?
Which salt undergoes hydrolysis in water to produce an alkaline solution (pH > 7)?
qs.e: Sodium ethanoate (CH3COONa) is a salt of a weak acid and strong base. CH3COO- hydrolyzes forming OH- ions.

qs.q: What is the pOH of a solution obtained by mixing 50 cm3 of 0.1 mol/dm3 HCl with 50 cm3 of 0.3 mol/dm3 NaOH?
qs.e: Moles H+ = 0.005. Moles OH- = 0.015. Excess OH- = 0.010 mol in 0.10 dm3 => [OH-] = 0.10 M => pOH = -log(0.10) = 1.0.

qs.q: In the reaction BF3 + NH3 -> F3B-NH3, which species acts as a Lewis acid and why?
o: NH3 because nitrogen donates a proton
BF3 because central boron accepts an electron pair
BF3 because it donates a lone pair
qs.e: BF3 has an incomplete octet (6 valence electrons around boron) and accepts an electron pair from NH3, acting as a Lewis acid.

qs.q: Calculate the pH of a buffer solution containing 0.10 M ethanoic acid and 0.20 M sodium ethanoate (Ka of CH3COOH = 1.8 x 10^-5, pKa = 4.74).
What is the pH of a 0.005 mol/dm3 solution of barium hydroxide, Ba(OH)2, assuming complete dissociation?
What is the normality (N) of a 0.20 mol/dm3 H2SO4 solution when used in an acid-base neutralization reaction?
qs.e: Normality = Molarity x Basicity = 0.20 x 2 = 0.40 N.

qs.q: What is the standard heat of neutralization when a strong monoprotic acid reacts completely with a strong monobasic alkali in dilute aqueous solution?
qs.e: The reaction H+(aq) + OH-(aq) -> H2O(l) has a constant enthalpy of neutralization of -57.3 kJ/mol.

qs.q: Which oxide is classified as an acidic oxide because it dissolves in water to form sulfurous acid?
qs.e: SO2 dissolves in water according to SO2 + H2O -> H2SO3 (sulfurous acid).

qs.q: Which oxide acts as a basic anhydride by reacting with water to form sodium hydroxide?
qs.e: Na2O + H2O -> 2NaOH. Metal oxides that dissolve in water to form alkalis are basic anhydrides.

qs.q: Which hydroxide displays amphoteric behavior by dissolving in both hydrochloric acid and excess sodium hydroxide solution?
qs.e: Zn(OH)2 reacts with HCl to give ZnCl2 and with excess NaOH to give sodium tetrahydroxozincate(II), [Zn(OH)4]2-.

qs.q: In volumetric acid-base analysis, what is a standard solution?
o: A solution that contains exactly one mole of solute per liter
A solution saturated at standard temperature and pressure
A solution whose exact concentration is accurately known
A solution with pH equal to 7.00
qs.e: A standard solution is one of accurately known concentration used to determine concentrations of other solutions.

qs.q: How does the equivalence point differ from the end point in an acid-base titration?
o: Equivalence point occurs at pH 7, end point occurs at pH 14
End point is theoretical while equivalence point is experimental
Equivalence point is theoretical stoichiometric neutrality, while end point is observed indicator color change
There is no distinction between them
qs.e: Equivalence point is where stoichometric amounts of acid and base have reacted; end point is when the indicator changes color.

qs.q: Calculate the mass of pure sodium hydroxide (NaOH) needed to prepare 250 cm3 of a 0.10 mol/dm3 standard solution (Na = 23, O = 16, H = 1).
qs.e: Molar mass NaOH = 40 g/mol. Moles needed = 0.10 * (250/1000) = 0.025 mol. Mass = 0.025 * 40 = 1.00 g.

qs.q: Determine the concentration in mol/dm3 of a calcium hydroxide solution, Ca(OH)2, that has a pH of 12.30 at 25°C (log 2 = 0.301).
Calculate the degree of ionization (alpha) of a 0.10 mol/dm3 ethanoic acid solution with dissociation constant Ka = 1.8 x 10^-5.

A sample of hydrated sodium carbonate Na2CO3.xH2O weighing 2.86 g is dissolved in water to make 1.0 dm3. If 25.0 cm3 of this solution neutralizes 20.0 cm3 of 0.050 mol/dm3 HCl, find x (Na=23, C=12, O=16, H=1).
How does the self-ionization constant of water (Kw) change when temperature is increased from 25°C to 50°C, and why?
o: Kw decreases because ion recombination accelerates
Kw remains constant because water is neutral
Kw becomes zero at elevated temperatures
Kw increases because self-ionization of water is an endothermic process
qs.e: H2O <-> H+ + OH- is endothermic (ΔH > 0). According to Le Chatelier's principle, raising temperature shifts equilibrium right, increasing Kw.

qs.q: Calculate the pH of an extremely dilute hydrochloric acid solution of concentration 1.0 x 10^-8 mol/dm3 at 25°C.
Under what condition is the buffer capacity of a weak acid and its conjugate base mixture at its maximum effectiveness?
o: When [weak acid] is ten times [conjugate base]
When [conjugate base] is ten times [weak acid]
When pH equals 7.0 regardless of pKa
When [weak acid] equals [conjugate base], making pH equal to pKa
qs.e: Buffer capacity is maximized when the ratio [base]/[acid] = 1, which occurs when pH = pKa.

qs.q: Why is ethanoic acid (CH3COOH) described as a monobasic acid despite containing four hydrogen atoms per molecule?
o: Three hydrogen atoms are covalently bonded to oxygen
It contains only one carbon atom in the chain
It neutralizes one mole of sulfuric acid
Only the carboxyl hydrogen atom ionizes in aqueous solution
qs.e: In CH3COOH, the three methyl hydrogens are bound to carbon and non-ionizable; only the carboxylic -COOH hydrogen dissociates.

qs.q: What color observation is made when universal indicator paper is dipped into a 1.0 mol/dm3 NaOH solution (pH ~ 14)?
qs.e: Universal indicator turns dark violet/purple in strongly alkaline solutions of pH 13-14.

qs.q: Washing soda crystals (Na2CO3.10H2O) turn into a white powder when exposed to dry air. What is this phenomenon called?
qs.e: Efflorescence is the loss of water of crystallization from a hydrated salt to the atmosphere upon exposure to dry air.

qs.q: Why is hydrochloric acid preferred over nitric acid as a standard acid in volumetric analysis of basic carbonates?
o: HCl is a dibasic acid while HNO3 is monobasic
HCl has a lower molecular mass
HCl is non-oxidizing whereas HNO3 can decompose or oxidize organic indicators
qs.e: HNO3 is a strong oxidizing agent that can destroy indicators or oxidize side species, whereas HCl is non-oxidizing under standard titration conditions.

qs.q: Calculate the pH of the resulting solution when 100 cm3 of 0.020 mol/dm3 H2SO4 is mixed with 100 cm3 of 0.030 mol/dm3 KOH.
What mass of hydrated oxalic acid (H2C2O4.2H2O, M = 126.07 g/mol) is required to prepare 500 cm3 of a 0.050 mol/dm3 standard solution?
A 0.500 g sample of impure calcium carbonate (CaCO3, M = 100.08 g/mol) neutralizes exactly 35.0 cm3 of 0.250 mol/dm3 HCl. Calculate the percentage purity of the CaCO3 sample.
Determine the pH of a 1.0 x 10^-3 mol/dm3 weak monobasic base BOH with dissociation constant Kb = 1.0 x 10^-5.
Calculate the volume of concentrated 12.0 mol/dm3 HCl solution required to prepare 1.50 dm3 of a 0.200 mol/dm3 dilute HCl solution.
What process involves the chemical decomposition of an electrolyte in molten or aqueous state by passing an electric current through it?
qs.e: Electrolysis is the breakdown of an ionic compound into its constituent elements by an electric current.

qs.q: During electrolysis, at which electrode does oxidation always take place?
qs.e: Oxidation (loss of electrons) always occurs at the anode in all electrochemical and electrolytic cells.

qs.q: At which electrode does reduction take place during an electrolytic reaction?
qs.e: Reduction (gain of electrons) always occurs at the cathode.

qs.q: What is the electric charge carried by one mole of electrons, known as Faraday's constant?
qs.e: 1 Faraday (1 F) = charge of 1 mole of electrons = 96,500 C/mol.

qs.q: What term describes a compound that conducts electricity in molten or aqueous form accompanied by chemical decomposition?
qs.e: An electrolyte is a liquid or solution containing free mobile ions that conducts electricity with decomposition.

qs.q: Which substance acts as a non-electrolyte in aqueous solution?
qs.e: Glucose is a covalent molecular compound that dissolves without forming ions, making it a non-electrolyte.

qs.q: During the electrolysis of dilute sodium chloride solution, which ion is preferentially discharged at the cathode?
qs.e: H+ ions lie lower than Na+ in the electrochemical series and are preferentially discharged to form H2 gas.

qs.q: Which mathematical equation expresses Faraday's First Law of electrolysis relating mass deposited (m) to current (I) and time (t)?
qs.e: Faraday's First Law states m is proportional to charge Q = I * t, so m = z * I * t, where z is the electrochemical equivalent.

qs.q: What electrode reaction occurs at the anode during the electrolysis of aqueous copper(II) sulfate using active copper electrodes?
qs.e: With copper electrodes, the copper anode oxidizes and dissolves: Cu(s) -> Cu2+(aq) + 2e-.

qs.q: What product is formed at the cathode during the electrolysis of molten sodium chloride?
qs.e: In molten NaCl, Na+ ions migrate to the cathode and gain electrons to form liquid sodium metal.

qs.q: What is the change in oxidation state of manganese when potassium permanganate (KMnO4) is reduced to manganese(II) sulfate (MnSO4)?
qs.e: In MnO4-, Mn is +7. In MnSO4, Mn is +2. Oxidation state changes from +7 to +2.

qs.q: What is the primary function of a salt bridge in a galvanic (voltaic) cell?
o: To maintain electrical neutrality by permitting ion migration between half-cells
To transfer electrons between two metallic electrodes
qs.e: The salt bridge completes the internal circuit and maintains charge neutrality by ion migration.

qs.q: What arbitrary standard electrode potential value is assigned to the Standard Hydrogen Electrode (SHE)?
qs.e: By international convention, the standard reduction potential of SHE is defined as exactly 0.00 V at 25°C.

qs.q: In the spontaneous redox reaction Zn(s) + Cu2+(aq) -> Zn2+(aq) + Cu(s), which species undergoes reduction?
qs.e: Cu2+ gains two electrons to form Cu(s), which is reduction.

qs.q: Which gas is evolved at the anode during the electrolysis of concentrated sodium chloride solution (brine) using inert carbon electrodes?
qs.e: In concentrated brine, high Cl- concentration causes preferential discharge of Cl- ions over OH- to yield Cl2 gas.

qs.q: What industrial application uses electrolysis to deposit a thin layer of a corrosion-resistant metal onto an object?
qs.e: Electroplating coats an object (cathode) with a metal (e.g. Cr, Ni, Ag) to resist corrosion or improve appearance.

qs.q: Why is dilute ethanoic acid classified as a weak electrolyte?
o: It ionizes only partially in aqueous solution
qs.e: Weak electrolytes dissociate only slightly into ions in solution, leading to low electrical conductivity.

qs.q: How does a primary electrochemical cell differ fundamentally from a secondary electrochemical cell?
o: Primary cell reactions are non-reversible, so it cannot be recharged
Primary cells use liquid electrolytes only
qs.e: Primary cells (e.g., Leclanché cell) cannot be recharged, whereas secondary cells (e.g., lead-acid battery) are rechargeable.

qs.q: Which two essential conditions are required simultaneously for the atmospheric rusting of iron to occur?
o: Presence of carbon dioxide and nitrogen
Presence of both oxygen and liquid water
Presence of pure hydrogen and light
Presence of sulfur dioxide and dry air
qs.e: Rusting of iron requires both oxygen and water/moisture simultaneously to form hydrated iron(III) oxide.

qs.q: Calculate the mass of copper deposited at the cathode when a constant electric current of 2.0 A flows through aqueous CuSO4 solution for 30 minutes (Cu = 63.5 g/mol, 1 F = 96,500 C).
What volume of oxygen gas at STP (molar volume = 22.4 dm3) is liberated when 0.20 Faraday of charge passes through dilute sulfuric acid?
qs.e: 4OH- -> O2 + 2H2O + 4e-. 4 F liberates 1 mol O2 = 22.4 dm3. 0.20 F liberates (0.20 / 4) * 22.4 = 1.12 dm3.

qs.q: Calculate the standard cell potential (E°cell) for Zn(s) | Zn2+(aq) || Cu2+(aq) | Cu(s) given E°(Zn2+/Zn) = -0.76 V and E°(Cu2+/Cu) = +0.34 V.
qs.e: E°cell = E°cathode - E°anode = +0.34 - (-0.76) = +1.10 V.

qs.q: How many Coulombs of electricity are required to deposit 10.8 g of silver from a silver nitrate solution (Ag = 108 g/mol, 1 F = 96,500 C)?
Identify the reducing agent in the redox reaction: 2FeCl2(aq) + Cl2(g) -> 2FeCl3(aq).
qs.e: Fe2+ in FeCl2 loses an electron to become Fe3+ in FeCl3; since it undergoes oxidation, FeCl2 is the reducing agent.

qs.q: Find the time in minutes required to deposit 0.60 g of aluminum metal from molten Al2O3 using a constant current of 5.0 A (Al = 27.0 g/mol, 1 F = 96,500 C).
Which metal among magnesium, iron, copper, and silver can spontaneously displace copper from aqueous copper(II) sulfate solution?
qs.e: Magnesium and iron lie above copper in the electrochemical series and can reduce Cu2+ ions to Cu metal.

qs.q: Why are magnesium blocks attached to the iron hulls of ocean-going ships?
o: Magnesium forms a waterproof paint layer on iron
Magnesium acts as a cathode to absorb oxygen
Magnesium oxidizes preferentially as a sacrificial anode, preventing iron corrosion
qs.e: Magnesium is more electropositive than iron; it corrodes sacrificially while keeping the iron hull intact.

qs.q: What are the electrode products formed at cathode and anode respectively during the electrolysis of molten lead(II) bromide using graphite electrodes?
o: Cathode: Bromine gas; Anode: Lead metal
Cathode: Hydrogen gas; Anode: Oxygen gas
Cathode: Lead metal; Anode: Bromine gas
Cathode: Lead metal; Anode: Oxygen gas
qs.e: Pb2+ ions accept electrons at cathode to form Pb metal; Br- ions lose electrons at anode to form Br2 gas.

qs.q: According to Faraday's Second Law of electrolysis, what relationship exists when the same quantity of electricity passes through different electrolyte solutions?
o: Masses liberated are inversely proportional to molar masses
Equal masses of all metals are deposited
Masses liberated are directly proportional to their chemical equivalent masses
Gas volumes liberated at cathodes are equal
qs.e: Faraday's Second Law states that m1/m2 = E1/E2, where E is chemical equivalent mass (molar mass / valency).

qs.q: What is the overall chemical cell reaction taking place in a standard Daniell galvanic cell?
qs.e: In a Daniell cell, zinc anode oxidizes (Zn -> Zn2+ + 2e-) and copper cathode reduces (Cu2+ + 2e- -> Cu).

qs.q: What is the oxidation number of sulfur in the thiosulfate ion, S2O3(2-)?
Why does molten sodium chloride conduct electricity whereas solid sodium chloride crystal does not?
o: Solid NaCl contains free electrons while liquid does not
Molten NaCl contains free water molecules
Molten state contains mobile Na+ and Cl- ions, while ions are fixed in solid crystal lattice
Melting converts ionic bond to metallic bond
qs.e: Electrical conduction in ionic liquids relies on mobile ions; solid ionic crystals hold ions rigidly in place.

qs.q: In a standard dry cell (Leclanché cell), what material serves as the anode container?
qs.e: The outer zinc container serves as the anode, undergoing oxidation: Zn(s) -> Zn2+(aq) + 2e-.

qs.q: What material is reduced at the positive cathode of a lead-acid storage accumulator during discharge?
qs.e: During discharge, lead dioxide (PbO2) cathode gains electrons and is reduced to PbSO4.

qs.q: Calculate the mass of nickel deposited at the cathode when a current of 3.0 A passes through a NiSO4 solution for 2.0 hours (Ni = 58.7 g/mol, 1 F = 96,500 C).
What volume of chlorine gas at STP (molar volume = 22.4 dm3) is liberated at the anode by electrolyzing brine with a 10.0 A current for 48.25 minutes?
Calculate E°cell for the reaction 2Al(s) + 3Fe2+(aq) -> 2Al3+(aq) + 3Fe(s) given E°(Al3+/Al) = -1.66 V and E°(Fe2+/Fe) = -0.44 V.
qs.e: E°cell = E°cathode - E°anode = -0.44 - (-1.66) = +1.22 V.

qs.q: During the electrolysis of dilute Na2SO4 solution using inert platinum electrodes, what gases are collected at the cathode and anode in volume ratio 2:1?
o: Cathode: Oxygen gas; Anode: Hydrogen gas
Cathode: Sodium gas; Anode: Sulfur dioxide
Cathode: Hydrogen gas; Anode: Chlorine gas
Cathode: Hydrogen gas; Anode: Oxygen gas
qs.e: Electrolysis of dilute Na2SO4 decomposes water: 2H2O -> 2H2(g) + O2(g). Cathode produces 2 vols H2, anode produces 1 vol O2.

qs.q: Calculate the electrochemical equivalent (z in g/C) of silver metal (Ag = 107.9 g/mol, 1 F = 96,485 C).
Determine the oxidation state of chromium in the dichromate salt formula K2Cr2O7.
During the electrolysis of aqueous CuSO4 solution using platinum inert electrodes, why does the characteristic blue color of the electrolyte gradually fade?
o: Cu2+ ions are converted into colorless SO4(2-) ions
Platinum electrodes react with sulfate ions
Cu2+ ions are progressively removed by deposition as Cu metal at the cathode
qs.e: The blue color is due to hydrated Cu2+(aq) ions; as Cu2+ is discharged at the cathode, its concentration decreases.

qs.q: Calculate the number of moles of electrons transferred when 1.204 x 10^23 copper atoms are deposited during electro-refining (Avogadro constant = 6.022 x 10^23).
qs.e: Moles Cu deposited = (1.204 x 10^23) / (6.022 x 10^23) = 0.20 mol. Cu2+ + 2e- -> Cu requires 2 * 0.20 = 0.40 mol electrons.

qs.q: Determine the standard cell potential (E°cell) for Cu(s) + 2Ag+(aq) -> Cu2+(aq) + 2Ag(s) given E°(Ag+/Ag) = +0.80 V and E°(Cu2+/Cu) = +0.34 V.
qs.e: E°cell = E°cathode - E°anode = +0.80 - (+0.34) = +0.46 V.

qs.q: What is the direction of electron flow in the external circuit wire connecting electrodes in a galvanic voltaic cell?
o: From cathode to anode (positive to negative electrode)
From salt bridge into the electrolyte solution
From anode to cathode (negative to positive electrode)
qs.e: Oxidation at the anode releases electrons, which flow through external wiring toward the cathode.

qs.q: Which half-cell reaction acts as the cathode when two half-cells with standard reduction potentials E°1 = +0.80 V and E°2 = -0.76 V are coupled?
o: Half-cell with E°2 = -0.76 V because it is negative
Neither, the cell potential becomes zero
Half-cell with E°1 = +0.80 V because it has the higher reduction potential
qs.e: The species with the more positive standard reduction potential undergoes reduction at the cathode.

qs.q: An electric current passes in series through two electrolytic cells containing AgNO3(aq) and M(NO3)2(aq). If 2.16 g of silver (Ag = 108 g/mol) is deposited in the first cell, calculate the mass of divalent metal M (M = 64.0 g/mol) deposited in the second cell.
Calculate the time in hours required for a current of 2.50 A to liberate 13.5 g of aluminum metal from molten alumina, Al2O3 (Al = 27.0 g/mol, 1 F = 96,500 C).
Estimate the equilibrium constant K at 25°C for the cell reaction Zn(s) + Cu2+(aq) <-> Zn2+(aq) + Cu(s) given E°cell = +1.10 V (use 2.303 RT/F = 0.0591 V).

Calculate the total volume of gas mixture (H2 and O2 combined) measured at STP (molar volume = 22.4 dm3) liberated during the electrolysis of dilute NaOH solution by passing a 2.00 A current for 9,650 seconds.
qs.e: Q = 2.00 * 9650 = 19,300 C = 0.20 F. 2H2O -> 2H2 + O2. H2 moles = 0.10 mol, O2 moles = 0.05 mol. Total gas moles = 0.15 mol. Vol = 0.15 * 22.4 = 3.36 dm3.

qs.q: Calculate the cathode current efficiency percentage if passing a 4.00 A current through aqueous CuSO4 for 30.0 minutes deposits 2.00 g of copper metal (Cu = 63.5 g/mol, 1 F = 96,500 C).
Which chemical element is present in all organic compounds without exception?
qs.e: Organic chemistry is defined as the study of carbon compounds.

qs.q: What is the general molecular formula for the homologous series of saturated hydrocarbons known as alkanes?
qs.e: Alkanes are saturated open-chain hydrocarbons with general formula CnH2n+2.

qs.q: What is the systematic IUPAC name for the straight-chain alkane with chemical structure CH3-CH2-CH3?
qs.e: A three-carbon alkane chain is named propane according to IUPAC nomenclature.

qs.q: Which functional group characterizes the class of organic compounds called alkanols (alcohols)?
qs.e: Alkanols contain the hydroxyl (-OH) functional group attached to an alkyl carbon.

qs.q: What name is given to a family of organic compounds sharing the same functional group and general formula?
qs.e: A homologous series consists of organic compounds with similar chemical properties differing by -CH2- units.

qs.q: How does a saturated hydrocarbon differ fundamentally from an unsaturated hydrocarbon?
o: Saturated hydrocarbons contain carbon-carbon single bonds only
Unsaturated hydrocarbons contain single bonds only
Saturated hydrocarbons dissolve readily in water
qs.e: Saturated hydrocarbons contain only C-C single bonds, whereas unsaturated ones contain C=C or C≡C multiple bonds.

qs.q: What phenomenon describes compounds having the same molecular formula but different structural arrangements of atoms?
qs.e: Isomerism is the occurrence of molecules with identical molecular formulae but distinct structural formulas.

qs.q: What is the systematic IUPAC name of the branched alkane CH3-CH(CH3)-CH2-CH3?
qs.e: The longest carbon chain contains 4 carbons (butane) with a methyl group at position 2.

qs.q: Which general molecular formula represents the aliphatic hydrocarbon family called alkenes?
qs.e: Alkenes are open-chain hydrocarbons containing one carbon-carbon double bond, formula CnH2n.

qs.q: Which reagent is used as a laboratory test to confirm unsaturation (double or triple bonds) in an organic compound?
o: Bromine water (or liquid bromine in CCl4)
qs.e: Unsaturated hydrocarbons decolorize reddish-brown bromine water rapidly via addition across double/triple bonds.

qs.q: Which characteristic functional group is present in all alkanoic (carboxylic) acids?
qs.e: Alkanoic acids contain the carboxyl group (-COOH) bonded to an alkyl group or hydrogen.

qs.q: What type of organic reaction occurs when an alkanol reacts with an alkanoic acid in the presence of concentrated H2SO4?
qs.e: Esterification is the reversible acid-catalyzed reaction between an alcohol and carboxylic acid to form an ester and water.

qs.q: Which functional group distinguishes alkanals (aldehydes) from alkanones (ketones)?
qs.e: Alkanals have a carbonyl carbon attached to at least one hydrogen atom at the end of the chain (-CHO).

qs.q: What structural feature characterizes alkanones (ketones)?
o: Carbonyl group bonded to two alkyl carbon atoms (>C=O)
qs.e: Alkanones contain a carbonyl group (>C=O) located within the carbon chain, flanked by two carbon atoms.

qs.q: What chemical product is formed when ethyne gas undergoes catalytic hydrogenation in the presence of nickel at 150°C?
qs.e: Ethyne (C2H2) adds two moles of H2 over Ni catalyst to form saturated ethane gas (C2H6).

qs.q: What are the ultimate products formed during the complete combustion of butane in excess oxygen gas?
qs.e: Complete combustion of any hydrocarbon yields carbon dioxide (CO2) and water (H2O).

qs.q: What is the empirical formula of the aromatic hydrocarbon benzene, C6H6?
qs.e: Empirical formula represents the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms: C6H6 simplifies to CH.

qs.q: What state of orbital hybridization is possessed by the carbon atoms in ethene, C2H4?
qs.e: Each carbon atom in ethene forms three sigma bonds (trigonal planar) and uses sp2 hybrid orbitals.

qs.q: What major natural resource serves as the primary raw material for obtaining aliphatic hydrocarbons industrially?
qs.e: Fractional distillation of petroleum yields various aliphatic hydrocarbon fractions (LPG, gasoline, kerosene, diesel).

qs.q: What is the systematic IUPAC name of the branched hydrocarbon CH3-CH2-C(CH3)2-CH3?
qs.e: The longest chain is 4 carbons (butane) numbered from right to give substituents lowest locants (2,2-dimethyl).

qs.q: Write the molecular formula of an open-chain alkane molecule containing exactly 5 carbon atoms.
qs.e: Alkane general formula CnH2n+2. For n=5, formula is C5H(2*5+2) = C5H12 (pentane).

qs.q: Calculate the mass of carbon present in 44.0 g of propane gas, C3H8 (C = 12.0 g/mol, H = 1.0 g/mol).
How many structural chain isomers exist for the molecular formula C5H12?
qs.e: C5H12 has three structural isomers: pentane, 2-methylbutane, and 2,2-dimethylpropane.

qs.q: What organic product is obtained when ethanol is oxidized by excess acidified potassium dichromate(VI) under reflux?
qs.e: Primary alcohols oxidize first to aldehydes and then fully under reflux to carboxylic acids (ethanoic acid).

qs.q: Which dehydrating agent converts ethanol to ethene when heated to 170°C in a laboratory preparation?
qs.e: Heating ethanol with excess conc. H2SO4 at 170°C removes water to yield ethene: C2H5OH -> C2H4 + H2O.

qs.q: What is the systematic IUPAC name for the ester compound CH3-CH2-COO-CH3?
qs.e: The alcohol part attached to oxygen is methyl (-CH3); the alkanoate part from propanoic acid is propanoate.

qs.q: What state of orbital hybridization and molecular geometry are found in ethyne (C2H2)?
qs.e: The triple-bonded carbon atoms in ethyne use sp hybrid orbitals forming linear molecules with 180° bond angles.

qs.q: What type of polymerization reaction converts ethene monomers into poly(ethene)?
qs.e: Addition polymerization joins unsaturated monomers together without eliminating any small molecules.

qs.q: What chemical process involves boiling vegetable oil or animal fat with concentrated sodium hydroxide solution to produce soap?
qs.e: Saponification is the alkaline hydrolysis of triglycerides yielding soap (sodium salts of fatty acids) and glycerol.

qs.q: What organic product and inorganic gas are formed when methane reacts with chlorine gas in diffuse sunlight?
qs.e: CH4 + Cl2 -> CH3Cl + HCl via a free radical substitution reaction in diffuse light.

qs.q: Which chemical reagent distinguishes propanal from propanone by forming a silver mirror on the test tube wall?
qs.e: Tollens' reagent oxidizes aldehydes (propanal) to carboxylates while reducing Ag+ to metallic silver (silver mirror test); ketones do not react.

qs.q: What structural condition must be met for an alkene to exhibit geometric (cis-trans) isomerism?
o: The alkene must contain at least six carbon atoms
The double bond must be at carbon position 1
Each double-bonded carbon atom must be attached to two different groups
The molecule must contain a benzene ring
qs.e: Restricted rotation about C=C requires that both carbons in the double bond have two non-identical groups attached.

qs.q: What monomer unit forms the natural polymer known as natural rubber (polyisoprene)?
qs.e: Natural rubber is a polymer of 2-methyl-1,3-butadiene (isoprene).

qs.q: What Industrial method produces ethanol directly from ethene and steam in the presence of a phosphoric acid catalyst?
qs.e: CH2=CH2 + H2O(g) -> CH3CH2OH at 300°C and 60 atm pressure over H3PO4 catalyst is catalytic hydration.

qs.q: An organic compound contains 85.7% carbon and 14.3% hydrogen by mass. Determine its empirical formula (C = 12.0, H = 1.0).
qs.e: Moles C = 85.7/12.0 = 7.14. Moles H = 14.3/1.0 = 14.3. Ratio H/C = 14.3/7.14 = 2. Empirical formula is CH2.

qs.q: If an organic hydrocarbon with empirical formula CH2 has a relative molecular mass of 56.0 g/mol, what is its molecular formula?
qs.e: Empirical formula mass CH2 = 12 + 2 = 14. n = 56 / 14 = 4. Molecular formula is (CH2)4 = C4H8.

qs.q: Calculate the volume of CO2 gas measured at STP (molar volume = 22.4 dm3) evolved by complete combustion of 5.8 g of butane gas, C4H10 (C = 12.0, H = 1.0).
qs.e: Molar mass C4H10 = 58 g/mol. Moles butane = 5.8 / 58 = 0.10 mol. 2C4H10 + 13O2 -> 8CO2 + 10H2O. Moles CO2 = 4 * 0.10 = 0.40 mol. Vol = 0.40 * 22.4 = 8.96 dm3.

qs.q: Calculate the theoretical mass of ethanol produced by complete yeast fermentation of 180 g of glucose, C6H12O6 (C = 12.0, H = 1.0, O = 16.0).
qs.e: C6H12O6 -> 2C2H5OH + 2CO2. 180 g glucose = 1.0 mol. Yields 2.0 mol ethanol = 2 * 46.0 g = 92.0 g.

qs.q: What carbonyl compound is produced exclusively when 2-butene undergoes ozonolysis followed by reductive cleavage with zinc and water?
qs.e: CH3-CH=CH-CH3 cleaves at double bond to yield two molecules of CH3CHO (ethanal).

qs.q: Calculate the total number of sigma (σ) and pi (π) bonds present in one molecule of prop-1-ene, CH2=CH-CH3.
qs.e: Propene has 6 C-H σ bonds + 2 C-C σ bonds = 8 σ bonds, and 1 C=C π bond.

qs.q: What is the systematic IUPAC name for the branched alkanol CH3-CH(OH)-CH(CH3)-CH3?
qs.e: Longest chain is 4 carbons (butanol). Numbering gives -OH lower locant (2): 3-methylbutan-2-ol.

qs.q: According to Markownikoff's rule, what major organic product is formed when hydrogen bromide (HBr) adds to propene (CH3-CH=CH2)?
qs.e: Markownikoff's rule states H adds to carbon with more H atoms (CH2), so Br adds to CH, forming 2-bromopropane.

qs.q: What structural feature is mandatory for an organic molecule to exhibit optical active enantiomerism?
o: A benzene ring with ortho substituents
At least one asymmetric chiral carbon atom bonded to four different groups
qs.e: Optical activity requires non-superimposable mirror image structures, caused by a chiral carbon atom.

qs.q: In the industrial fermentation of starch to ethanol, what sequence of enzymes acts progressively on starch?
qs.e: Diastase converts starch to maltose; Maltase hydrolyzes maltose to glucose; Zymase ferments glucose to ethanol.

qs.q: Which polymer is synthesized via a condensation polymerization reaction eliminating water molecules?
qs.e: Nylon-6,6 is formed by condensation of hexamethylenediamine and adipic acid with loss of H2O.

qs.q: Complete combustion of 0.20 mol of a gaseous hydrocarbon produces 17.92 dm3 of CO2 gas at STP and 18.0 g of water. Find its molecular formula.
An organic compound X containing C, H, O yielded 0.88 g CO2 and 0.36 g H2O on complete combustion of a 0.44 g sample. If its vapor density is 22.0, determine its molecular formula.
Calculate the volume of a 0.10 mol/dm3 bromine solution in CCl4 required to react completely with 1.12 g of 1-butene, C4H8 (C = 12.0, H = 1.0).
qs.e: Molar mass C4H8 = 56 g/mol. Moles C4H8 = 1.12 / 56 = 0.020 mol. C4H8 + Br2 -> C4H8Br2. Moles Br2 = 0.020 mol. Vol = 0.020 / 0.10 = 0.200 dm3 = 200 cm3.

qs.q: Calculate the mass of soap (sodium stearate, C17H35COONa, M = 306 g/mol) produced by complete alkaline saponification of 89.0 g of glyceryl tristearate (M = 890 g/mol) with excess NaOH.
qs.e: 1 mol fat yields 3 mol soap. Moles fat = 89.0 / 890 = 0.10 mol. Moles soap = 0.30 mol. Mass soap = 0.30 * 306 = 91.8 g.

qs.q: Calculate the percentage yield of ethanoic acid if oxidizing 23.0 g of ethanol (M = 46.0 g/mol) yields 24.0 g of pure ethanoic acid (M = 60.0 g/mol).
qs.e: Moles ethanol = 23.0 / 46.0 = 0.50 mol. Theoretical ethanoic acid = 0.50 * 60.0 = 30.0 g. Yield = (24.0 / 30.0) * 100 = 80.0%.

qs.q: Which term describes a chemical process in which heat energy is released to the surrounding environment?
qs.e: An exothermic reaction is one that proceeds with the liberation of heat energy to the surroundings, causing an increase in environmental temperature.

qs.q: For an endothermic chemical reaction taking place at constant pressure, what is the sign of the enthalpy change (ΔH)?
qs.e: Endothermic reactions absorb thermal energy from the surroundings, resulting in a positive enthalpy change (ΔH > 0).

qs.q: Which laboratory apparatus is specifically used to measure thermal energy changes accompanying chemical reactions?
qs.e: A calorimeter is an insulated vessel used to measure heat absorbed or released during physical processes or chemical reactions.

qs.q: What is the standard SI unit used to express molar enthalpy change in thermochemistry?
qs.e: Molar enthalpy change is measured in units of energy per amount of substance, which is Joules per mole (J/mol) or kilojoules per mole (kJ/mol).

qs.q: In a potential energy profile diagram for a chemical reaction, what state does the maximum peak of the energy curve represent?
qs.e: The highest energy state along the reaction coordinate corresponds to the short-lived, unstable species known as the activated complex or transition state.

qs.q: What are standard laboratory conditions defined as for thermochemical measurements?
qs.e: Standard thermochemical state conditions are defined at a temperature of 298.15 K (25 °C) and a standard pressure of 1 atm (101.3 kPa).

qs.q: What is the standard enthalpy of formation (ΔH°f) assigned to a pure element in its most stable physical state at 298 K?
qs.e: By international thermodynamic convention, the standard enthalpy of formation of an element in its standard state at 298 K is defined as zero.

qs.q: Given the thermochemical equation 2H2(g) + O2(g) -> 2H2O(l), ΔH = -572 kJ, how much heat is released when 2.0 moles of H2 gas react completely?
qs.e: The stoichiometric equation shows 2 moles of H2 reacting to release 572 kJ of heat energy.

qs.q: Which statement correctly describes the relative energy levels of reactants and products in an exothermic reaction?
o: Reactants have higher potential energy than products
Products have higher potential energy than reactants
Reactants and products have equal energy
Energy levels depend on atmospheric pressure
qs.e: In exothermic reactions, energy is liberated because the chemical potential energy of the reactants exceeds that of the products.

qs.q: If a 50.0 g sample of pure water absorbs 1050 J of heat energy, what is the resulting temperature rise? (Specific heat capacity of water = 4.2 J/g·°C)
How is the activation energy of a chemical reaction best defined?
o: Minimum energy colliding reactant particles must possess to undergo reaction
Total thermal energy stored inside all reactant bonds
Energy released when products form from transition state
Difference in enthalpy between solid and liquid phases
qs.e: Activation energy (Ea) is the minimum energy required by colliding reactant molecules to break existing bonds and form products.

qs.q: When solid ammonium nitrate dissolves in water, the reaction vessel cools significantly. What type of thermochemical process is this?
qs.e: A temperature drop indicates that the system absorbs heat energy from the surrounding water, making it an endothermic process.

qs.q: What effect does introducing a suitable positive catalyst have on the standard enthalpy change (ΔH) of a reaction?
o: It has no effect on ΔH
qs.e: A catalyst lowers the activation energy barrier for both forward and reverse paths but does not alter the enthalpy change (ΔH) between reactants and products.

qs.q: Which thermochemical quantity is always negative for the complete combustion of any organic fuel?
qs.e: Combustion reactions release energy as heat, so the standard enthalpy of combustion is always exothermic (negative value).

qs.q: Calculate the heat absorbed when 0.50 mol of calcium carbonate decomposes according to CaCO3(s) -> CaO(s) + CO2(g), ΔH = +178 kJ/mol.
qs.e: Decomposition of 1.0 mol requires +178 kJ. For 0.50 mol, heat absorbed = 0.50 * 178.0 = 89.0 kJ.

qs.q: What term defines the heat change when 1 mole of hydrogen ions reacts with 1 mole of hydroxide ions to produce 1 mole of water?
qs.e: The enthalpy of neutralization is the enthalpy change when an acid and base react to form one mole of water.

qs.q: For a chemical process to be thermodynamically spontaneous at all temperatures, what must be the signs of ΔH and ΔS?
qs.e: According to ΔG = ΔH - TΔS, when ΔH is negative and ΔS is positive, ΔG is always negative regardless of temperature T.

qs.q: Hess's Law of Constant Heat Summation is a direct logical consequence of which foundational physical law?
qs.e: Hess's Law states that total enthalpy change is independent of route, which reflects the first law of thermodynamics (conservation of energy).

qs.q: If a forward reaction has ΔH = +40 kJ/mol and an activation energy of 100 kJ/mol, what is the activation energy for the reverse reaction?
qs.e: Ea(reverse) = Ea(forward) - ΔH = 100 - 40 = 60 kJ/mol.

qs.q: Calculate the enthalpy of combustion of methane (CH4) using average bond energies: C-H = 413 kJ/mol, O=O = 498 kJ/mol, C=O = 805 kJ/mol, O-H = 463 kJ/mol for CH4 + 2O2 -> CO2 + 2H2O.

Determine ΔH for C(s) + 2H2(g) -> CH4(g) given thermochemical data: C(s) + O2(g) -> CO2(g) ΔH = -393.5 kJ; H2(g) + 0.5O2(g) -> H2O(l) ΔH = -285.8 kJ; CH4(g) + 2O2(g) -> CO2(g) + 2H2O(l) ΔH = -890.3 kJ.
Complete combustion of 0.80 g of ethanol (C2H5OH, molar mass = 46 g/mol) raised the temperature of 100 g of water by 54.0 °C. Calculate the molar enthalpy of combustion of ethanol (c = 4.2 J/g·°C).
qs.e: Heat absorbed by water q = 100 * 4.2 * 54.0 = 22680 J = 22.68 kJ. Moles of ethanol = 0.80 / 46 = 0.01739 mol. ΔHc = -22.68 / 0.01739 = -1304 kJ/mol.

qs.q: When 50.0 cm3 of 1.0 mol/dm3 HCl reacts with 50.0 cm3 of 1.0 mol/dm3 NaOH, the temperature rises by 6.8 °C. Assuming liquid density of 1.0 g/cm3 and c = 4.2 J/g·°C, calculate the molar enthalpy of neutralization.
What is the entropy change (ΔS) when 1.0 mole of liquid water vaporizes at its boiling point (373 K), given its enthalpy of vaporization ΔHvap = +40.7 kJ/mol?
qs.e: At phase equilibrium, ΔS = ΔH / T = 40700 J/mol / 373 K = +109.1 J/(mol·K).

qs.q: Calculate Gibbs free energy change (ΔG) at 300 K for a chemical process with ΔH = -50.0 kJ/mol and ΔS = -100 J/(mol·K).
Calculate the enthalpy change for N2(g) + 3H2(g) -> 2NH3(g) using bond energies: N≡N = 945 kJ/mol, H-H = 436 kJ/mol, N-H = 391 kJ/mol.
qs.e: Bonds broken = 945 + 3(436) = 2253 kJ. Bonds formed = 6(391) = 2346 kJ. ΔH = 2253 - 2346 = -93 kJ/mol.

qs.q: Calculate the lattice energy of sodium chloride (NaCl) using the Born-Haber cycle data: ΔHsub(Na) = +108 kJ/mol, IE1(Na) = +496 kJ/mol, 0.5*D(Cl2) = +122 kJ/mol, EA(Cl) = -349 kJ/mol, ΔHf(NaCl) = -411 kJ/mol.

In a calorimetry experiment, 2.0 g of NaOH is dissolved in 100 g of water, causing temperature to rise from 22.0 °C to 27.2 °C. Calculate heat of solution per mole of NaOH (molar mass = 40 g/mol, c = 4.2 J/g·°C).
Which of the following chemical reactions is associated with a net increase in disorder (positive ΔS)?
qs.e: Decomposition of solid CaCO3 produces a solid and a gas (CO2), significantly increasing the number of gas moles and disorder (ΔS > 0).

qs.q: Calculate the quantity of thermal energy required to heat 250 g of copper metal (specific heat capacity c = 0.385 J/g·°C) from 20 °C to 100 °C.
Given 2CO(g) + O2(g) -> 2CO2(g), ΔH = -566 kJ, calculate standard enthalpy of formation of CO(g) given ΔHf(CO2) = -393.5 kJ/mol.
Under what specific thermodynamic conditions will an endothermic reaction (ΔH > 0) with positive entropy change (ΔS > 0) be spontaneous?
o: Only at low temperatures near absolute zero
Only at high temperatures where TΔS exceeds ΔH
qs.e: For ΔG = ΔH - TΔS to be negative when ΔH > 0 and ΔS > 0, the temperature T must be sufficiently high so that TΔS > ΔH.

qs.q: What is the standard enthalpy of atomization per mole of gaseous bromine atoms produced from liquid Br2(l) if vaporization enthalpy is +31 kJ/mol and Br-Br bond energy is 193 kJ/mol?
Calculate thermal energy liberated when 10.0 g of liquid water freezes at 0 °C given molar enthalpy of fusion ΔHfus = 6.01 kJ/mol (molar mass H2O = 18 g/mol).
qs.e: Moles of water = 10.0 / 18 = 0.5556 mol. Heat released during freezing = 0.5556 * 6.01 = 3.34 kJ.

qs.q: Calculate the minimum temperature above which the decomposition reaction CaCO3(s) -> CaO(s) + CO2(g) becomes spontaneous at 1 atm, given ΔH = +178 kJ/mol and ΔS = +160 J/(mol·K).
qs.e: Setting ΔG = 0: T = ΔH / ΔS = 178000 J/mol / 160 J/(mol·K) = 1112.5 K.

qs.q: A bomb calorimeter with heat capacity 400 J/°C contains 200 g of water (c = 4.2 J/g·°C). Combustion of 0.16 g of methane (CH4, molar mass 16 g/mol) causes a 7.0 °C temperature rise. Calculate molar heat of combustion of methane.
For the reaction A + B -> C, forward activation energy Ea(f) is 75 kJ/mol and ΔH is -25 kJ/mol. What is the activation energy for reverse reaction C -> A + B?
qs.e: Ea(reverse) = Ea(forward) - ΔH = 75 - (-25) = 100 kJ/mol.

qs.q: Hydration enthalpy of K+ is -322 kJ/mol and Cl- is -364 kJ/mol. If lattice energy of KCl is -715 kJ/mol, calculate standard enthalpy of solution of KCl.
Determine enthalpy change for thermite reaction 2Al(s) + Fe2O3(s) -> Al2O3(s) + 2Fe(s) given ΔHf(Fe2O3) = -824.2 kJ/mol and ΔHf(Al2O3) = -1675.7 kJ/mol.
For a reaction with ΔH = -120 kJ/mol and ΔS = -200 J/(mol·K), at what temperature does ΔG equal zero?

A 50.0 g sample of an unknown metal at 100.0 °C is placed into 100.0 g of water at 20.0 °C in a calorimeter. Final temperature is 24.0 °C. Calculate specific heat capacity of metal (c_water = 4.2 J/g·°C).
Calculate enthalpy change for liquid hydrazine combustion N2H4(l) + O2(g) -> N2(g) + 2H2O(l) given ΔHf(N2H4(l)) = +50.6 kJ/mol and ΔHf(H2O(l)) = -285.8 kJ/mol.
For gas phase reaction 2NO2(g) -> N2O4(g), ΔH° = -57.2 kJ/mol and ΔS° = -175.8 J/(mol·K). Calculate standard free energy change ΔG° at 298 K.
Given H-H bond energy 436 kJ/mol, Cl-Cl bond energy 242 kJ/mol, and standard enthalpy of formation of HCl(g) ΔHf = -92.3 kJ/mol, calculate H-Cl bond energy.

Burning 1.00 g of benzoic acid (C7H6O2, molar mass 122 g/mol) in a bomb calorimeter increases temperature by 2.54 °C. Total calorimeter heat capacity is 10.4 kJ/°C. Calculate molar heat of combustion of benzoic acid.
Calculate theoretical enthalpy of hydrogenation of ethene (C2H4 + H2 -> C2H6) using bond energies: C=C = 614 kJ/mol, C-C = 348 kJ/mol, C-H = 413 kJ/mol, H-H = 436 kJ/mol.

A 0.500 g sample of magnesium ribbon is burned in excess oxygen inside a bomb calorimeter containing 1200 g of water (c = 4.184 J/g·°C, C_cal = 850 J/°C). Temp rises by 2.40 °C. Molar mass Mg = 24.31 g/mol. Calculate standard enthalpy of formation of MgO(s).
Using standard entropy values S°[SO2(g)] = 248 J/(mol·K), S°[O2(g)] = 205 J/(mol·K), S°[SO3(g)] = 257 J/(mol·K), calculate standard entropy change ΔS° for 2SO2(g) + O2(g) -> 2SO3(g).
For the gas phase equilibrium N2O4(g) -> 2NO2(g), ΔH° = +57.1 kJ/mol and ΔS° = +175.8 J/(mol·K). Calculate the thermodynamic equilibrium constant Kp at 298 K (R = 8.314 J/(mol·K)).

Dissolving 10.0 g of NH4Cl (molar mass 53.5 g/mol) in 150.0 g of water lowers temperature from 25.0 °C to 20.3 °C. Heat capacity of calorimeter is 50.0 J/°C and c_solution = 4.18 J/g·°C. Calculate molar enthalpy of solution of NH4Cl.
How is the rate of a chemical reaction generally defined in quantitative kinetics?
o: Change in concentration of reactant or product per unit time
Total time required for reaction to reach completion
Amount of catalyst consumed during the process
Total heat energy liberated per mole
qs.e: Reaction rate is defined as the change in concentration of a reactant or product per unit time.

qs.q: What happens to the frequency of collisions between reactant molecules when reactant concentration is increased?
qs.e: Higher concentration means more particles per unit volume, leading to more frequent collisions per unit time.

qs.q: What is the primary function of a positive catalyst added to a chemical reaction mixture?
o: Lowers activation energy by providing an alternative pathway
Increases total enthalpy change ΔH of reaction
Increases average kinetic energy of reactants
Shifts chemical equilibrium position to the right
qs.e: A catalyst provides an alternative reaction pathway with a lower activation energy, increasing reaction rate.

qs.q: Which unit is standard for expressing the rate of reaction in liquid solution phase kinetics?
qs.e: In solution phase, concentration change (mol dm^-3) per unit time (s) is expressed as mol dm^-3 s^-1.

qs.q: Why does crushing a solid reactant into a fine powder increase the rate of reaction with a solution?
o: Increases surface area exposed for collision
qs.e: Powdered solids offer a much greater surface area per unit mass, increasing contact area and collision frequency.

qs.q: What effect does increasing temperature have on the average kinetic energy of reacting gas molecules?
o: Has no effect on kinetic energy
Causes kinetic energy to fall to zero
qs.e: Temperature is a measure of average kinetic energy; raising temperature increases particle speed and kinetic energy.

qs.q: According to collision theory, what constitutes an effective collision between reactant particles?
o: Collision with energy ≥ Ea and correct orientation
Any collision regardless of energy or angle
Collision occurring in presence of noble gas
qs.e: Effective collisions require both sufficient kinetic energy (≥ activation energy Ea) and proper molecular orientation.

qs.q: For the reaction A + 2B -> C, if the rate of disappearance of reactant B is 0.040 mol dm^-3 s^-1, what is the rate of formation of product C?
qs.e: From stoichiometry, 2 moles of B yield 1 mole of C. Rate of C formation = 0.5 * (Rate of B loss) = 0.5 * 0.040 = 0.020 mol dm^-3 s^-1.

qs.q: What shift occurs in the Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution curve when temperature of a gas mixture is raised?
o: Peak shifts to right and flattens
Peak shifts to left and sharpens
qs.e: At higher temperatures, average molecular speed increases, shifting the peak to the right and broadening/flattening the curve.

qs.q: How is the overall order of a chemical reaction defined from its experimental rate equation?
o: Sum of powers of concentration terms in rate law
Sum of stoichiometric coefficients in balanced equation
Difference between reactant and product moles
Ratio of forward and reverse rate constants
qs.e: The overall order of reaction is the mathematical sum of the exponent powers in the experimental rate law equation.

qs.q: What term refers to the time required for half of the initial concentration of a reactant to be consumed?
qs.e: The half-life (t1/2) is the time required for reactant concentration to decrease to half of its initial value.

qs.q: What name is given to a catalyst that exists in a different physical state from the reactants in a system?
qs.e: A heterogeneous catalyst exists in a physical phase distinct from that of the reacting substances (e.g. solid platinum with gaseous reactants).

qs.q: If a chemical reaction rate doubles for every 10 °C temperature rise, by what factor does rate increase from 20 °C to 50 °C?
qs.e: Temperature rise ΔT = 50 - 20 = 30 °C, which is 3 increments of 10 °C. Rate factor = 2^3 = 8 times.

qs.q: For zero-order chemical kinetics, which explicit dimensions represent the rate constant k?
qs.e: For a zeroth-order reaction, Rate = k. Units of k equal units of rate, which is mol dm^-3 s^-1.

qs.q: In first-order chemical rate laws, what dimensions express the rate constant k?
qs.e: For first order, Rate = k[A]. Units: (mol dm^-3 s^-1) / (mol dm^-3) = s^-1.

qs.q: If the rate equation for a reaction is Rate = k[A][B]^2, what is the overall order of the reaction?
qs.e: Overall order is sum of exponents: 1 + 2 = 3 (third order).

qs.q: Which type of catalyst accelerates chemical reactions occurring inside living biological cells?
qs.e: Enzymes are specialized biological catalysts (globular proteins) that speed up metabolic reactions in organisms.

qs.q: In photochemical reactions such as silver chloride decomposition, what factor primarily dictates the reaction rate?
o: Intensity and wavelength of incident light
qs.e: Photochemical reaction rates depend directly on light intensity and photon energy (frequency/wavelength).

qs.q: Which method is suitable for monitoring the rate of reaction between marble chips (CaCO3) and dilute hydrochloric acid?
o: Measuring volume of carbon dioxide gas evolved over time
qs.e: CaCO3 + 2HCl -> CaCl2 + H2O + CO2(g). Evolved CO2 gas volume can be measured using a gas syringe vs time.

qs.q: For a first-order reaction with rate constant k = 0.0693 min^-1, calculate the half-life period t1/2 of the reaction.
A reaction follows the rate law Rate = k[A]^2. If the concentration of reactant A is tripled, by what factor does the reaction rate increase?
qs.e: Since rate is proportional to [A]^2, tripling [A] increases rate by 3^2 = 9 times.

qs.q: In the decomposition 2N2O5 -> 4NO2 + O2, [N2O5] drops from 1.20 mol dm^-3 to 0.80 mol dm^-3 in 20 seconds. Calculate average rate of N2O5 loss.
Initial rate data: when [A] = 0.10 M, Rate = 0.002 M/s; when [A] = 0.20 M, Rate = 0.008 M/s. Determine order of reaction with respect to A.
qs.e: Doubling [A] (0.20/0.10 = 2) quadruples rate (0.008/0.002 = 4 = 2^2), so reaction is second order wrt A.

qs.q: For a first-order decomposition with half-life t1/2 = 15.0 minutes, how long will it take for 75% of the original reactant to be consumed?
qs.e: After 1 half-life (15 min), 50% remains. After 2 half-lives (30 min), 25% remains (75% consumed). Total time = 30.0 min.

qs.q: In second-order reaction rate laws, which explicit units express the rate constant k in SI system?
qs.e: Rate = k[A]^2 => k units = (mol dm^-3 s^-1) / (mol dm^-3)^2 = dm^3 mol^-1 s^-1.

qs.q: In an Arrhenius plot of ln(k) against 1/T (in Kelvin), what physical parameter is represented by the slope of the straight line?
qs.e: Arrhenius equation ln(k) = ln(A) - Ea/(RT). A plot of ln(k) vs 1/T gives a straight line with slope = -Ea / R.

qs.q: For reaction 2A + B -> C with Rate = k[A][B], if reaction container volume is reduced to half at constant temperature, by what factor does rate increase?
qs.e: Halving volume doubles all gas concentrations: [A]' = 2[A], [B]' = 2[B]. New Rate = k(2[A])(2[B]) = 4 k[A][B] = 4 times.

qs.q: Radioactive Cobalt-60 undergoes first-order decay with half-life 5.27 years. If initial mass is 16.0 g, what mass remains after 15.81 years?
qs.e: Number of half-lives n = 15.81 / 5.27 = 3. Remaining mass = 16.0 / (2^3) = 16.0 / 8 = 2.0 g.

qs.q: What phenomenon occurs when trace impurities bind irreversibly to active catalyst sites, destroying catalytic activity?
qs.e: Catalyst poisoning occurs when impurities (e.g. arsenic or sulfur) strongly adsorb onto active surface sites, inactivating the catalyst.

qs.q: How does activation energy Ea affect the temperature sensitivity of the rate constant k of a reaction?
o: Reactions with lower Ea are more sensitive to temperature changes
Ea has no relationship with temperature sensitivity
Reactions with higher Ea are more sensitive to temperature changes
Ea makes rate independent of temperature
qs.e: By Arrhenius equation d(lnk)/dT = Ea/(RT^2), reactions with larger activation energy Ea exhibit greater fractional rate changes with temperature.

qs.q: If the rate law for a multi-step reaction is Rate = k[X]^0.5 [Y]^1.5, what is the overall order of the reaction?
qs.e: Overall order = sum of powers = 0.5 + 1.5 = 2.0 (second order).

qs.q: For a reaction with Ea = 50.0 kJ/mol at 300 K, a catalyst lowers Ea to 35.0 kJ/mol. Calculate ratio of catalyzed to uncatalyzed rate constant k_cat/k_uncat (R = 8.314 J/mol K).
In a multi-step reaction mechanism, which elementary step dictates the overall rate of product formation?
o: The step with zero activation energy
The step involving physical state change
qs.e: The slowest step in a multi-step mechanism acts as the bottleneck and determines the overall reaction rate.

qs.q: What term describes a reaction where one of the formed products acts as a catalyst for the ongoing reaction?
qs.e: Autocatalysis is a reaction in which a reaction product itself acts as a catalyst, accelerating the reaction as it proceeds.

qs.q: Initial rate data for A + B -> C: Exp 1 ([A]=0.1, [B]=0.1, Rate=0.005); Exp 2 ([A]=0.2, [B]=0.1, Rate=0.010); Exp 3 ([A]=0.1, [B]=0.2, Rate=0.020). Calculate rate constant k.
qs.e: Exp 1 vs 2: order wrt A = 1. Exp 1 vs 3: Rate quadruples when [B] doubles, order wrt B = 2. Rate = k[A][B]^2. 0.005 = k(0.1)(0.1)^2 => k = 0.005 / 0.0001 = 50 dm^6 mol^-2 s^-1.

qs.q: A first-order reaction is 50% complete in 20.0 minutes. Calculate the time required for 90% completion of the reactant.
An Arrhenius plot of ln(k) against 1/T yields a straight line with slope = -6000 K. Calculate activation energy Ea (R = 8.314 J/mol K).
For the gas reaction 3A -> 2B, the rate of loss of A is -d[A]/dt = 0.090 mol dm^-3 s^-1. What is the rate of formation of B (d[B]/dt)?
If the activation energy Ea of a chemical reaction is zero, how does the rate constant k depend on temperature T?
o: Rate constant k increases exponentially with T
Rate constant k decreases linearly with T
Rate constant k drops to zero
Rate constant k is independent of temperature
qs.e: If Ea = 0, k = A * e^(0) = A, so the rate constant is completely independent of temperature.

qs.q: The rate constant k for a first-order reaction is 2.0 x 10^-3 s^-1. Calculate the initial reaction rate when [A] = 0.50 mol dm^-3.
Calculate the half-life t1/2 of a second-order reaction with k = 0.50 dm^3 mol^-1 s^-1 when initial reactant concentration [A]0 = 0.20 mol dm^-3.
Decomposition 2H2O2 -> 2H2O + O2 is catalyzed by MnO2. If 0.10 mol H2O2 decomposes completely in 50 seconds, calculate average rate of O2 formation.
qs.e: Moles O2 formed = 0.10 / 2 = 0.050 mol. Average rate of O2 formation = 0.050 mol / 50 s = 0.0010 mol/s.

qs.q: Two reactions have activation energies Ea1 = 40 kJ/mol and Ea2 = 80 kJ/mol. Which reaction exhibits a larger percentage rate increase when temperature rises from 300 K to 310 K?
o: Reaction with lower activation energy (Ea1 = 40 kJ/mol)
Both reactions experience identical percentage increases
Reaction with higher activation energy (Ea2 = 80 kJ/mol)
