qs.q: When the price of computer printers increases by 25 percent, the demand for ink cartridges decreases by 25 percent. The cross elasticity of demand is
qs.e: Cross elasticity = % change in Q of cartridges / % change in P of printers = -25% / +25% = -1.0. The negative sign confirms they are complementary goods.

qs.q: The market demand and supply equations are Qd = 200 - 2P and Qs = 50 + 3P. If supply decreases by 25 units at every price, what is the new equilibrium price?
qs.e: Original equilibrium: 200 - 2P = 50 + 3P => 5P = 150 => P = 30. New Qs = 50 + 3P - 25 = 25 + 3P. Set Qd = new Qs: 200 - 2P = 25 + 3P => 5P = 175 => P = 35 naira.

qs.q: When the market price of palm oil increases from 100 naira to 120 naira per liter, local producers increase supply from 400 liters to 520 liters. What is the price elasticity of supply?
The net loss in total economic welfare (consumer plus producer surplus) resulting from an effective price ceiling in a competitive market is known as
qs.e: Deadweight loss represents the loss of economic efficiency and combined consumer/producer welfare when price controls prevent market equilibrium.

qs.q: A consumer with 12 naira consumes Good X (priced at 2 naira) and Good Y (priced at 3 naira). MUx sequence is 16, 14, 12, 10 while MUy sequence is 24, 21, 18, 15. To maximize utility, the consumer should purchase
o: 3 units of X and 2 units of Y
0 units of X and 4 units of Y
2 units of X and 3 units of Y
6 units of X and 0 units of Y
qs.e: MUx/Px for X: 16/2=8, 14/2=7, 12/2=6, 10/2=5. MUy/Py for Y: 24/3=8, 21/3=7, 18/3=6, 15/3=5. Equilibrium MU ratio = 6 at 3 units of X and 2 units of Y. Total expenditure = (3*2) + (2*3) = 6 + 6 = 12 naira.

qs.q: Given the demand function Qd = 150 - 5P, calculate the point price elasticity of demand when the market price is 10 naira.
The total quantity of a commodity that all producers in an industry are willing and able to offer for sale at various prices over a given period is known as
qs.e: Market supply is the horizontal summation of the supply schedules of all individual producers in a given market.

qs.q: A standard supply curve slopes upward from left to right, indicating that
o: production costs fall as output expands
consumers purchase more of a good at higher prices
producers supply more of a good at higher prices
price elasticity of supply is always less than one
qs.e: The upward slope of the supply curve reflects the direct relationship between market price and quantity supplied.

qs.q: The responsiveness of quantity supplied of a product to a change in its unit price is measured by the
qs.e: Price elasticity of supply measures how sensitive producers are to price changes.

qs.q: A movement along a single demand curve caused solely by a change in the price of the commodity is called a change in
qs.e: A change in price causes a movement along the existing demand curve (change in quantity demanded), whereas non-price factors shift the curve (change in demand).

qs.q: An economic good whose demand decreases as consumer real income increases is classified as an
qs.e: An inferior good has a negative income elasticity of demand, meaning consumers buy less of it as their income rises.

qs.q: When an increase in the price of commodity X leads to an increase in the demand for commodity Y, goods X and Y are
qs.e: Substitute goods can replace each other; an increase in the price of one causes consumers to buy more of the substitute.

qs.q: The price at which the quantity of a product demanded by buyers equals the quantity offered by sellers is called the
qs.e: Equilibrium price is the market-clearing price where demand and supply curves intersect.

qs.q: When the demand for a product is perfectly inelastic, the entire economic burden of an indirect tax falls on the
qs.e: With perfectly inelastic demand (vertical demand curve), consumers buy the same quantity regardless of price, so sellers pass 100% of the tax to buyers.

qs.q: If demand for a product is perfectly elastic, an indirect per-unit tax imposed on the product will be paid entirely by the
qs.e: With perfectly elastic demand (horizontal demand curve), sellers cannot raise the price at all without losing all sales, so producers bear the full tax incidence.

qs.q: A government production subsidy granted to agricultural farmers will cause the market supply curve to
qs.e: Subsidies reduce production costs per unit, encouraging farmers to supply more at every price level, shifting the supply curve rightward.

qs.q: Cross price elasticity of demand between two goods that are perfect complements is
qs.e: Complementary goods have negative cross elasticity because a price increase in one reduces demand for both.

qs.q: A normal good is defined as a commodity for which the income elasticity of demand is
qs.e: Normal goods have positive income elasticity of demand (YED > 0), meaning demand increases when consumer income rises.

qs.q: An increase in the cost of raw materials used in manufacturing shoes will cause the supply curve of shoes to
qs.e: Higher input costs decrease production profitability, causing manufacturers to reduce supply at every price level (leftward shift).

qs.q: Which of the following is an immediate consequence of enforcing an effective price ceiling below equilibrium?
o: Emergence of black markets and hoarding
qs.e: Effective price ceilings create shortages, leading to non-price rationing, long queues, hoarding, and unofficial black market trading.

qs.q: A government policy of buying surplus agricultural produce to maintain a price floor is known as a
qs.e: Buffer stock schemes buy surplus output during high-yield periods to maintain the minimum guaranteed floor price.

qs.q: The supply of mutton and wool obtained from sheep farming represents an example of
qs.e: Joint supply occurs when two or more goods are derived from a single production source or process.

qs.q: Using a piece of agricultural land to cultivate cassava instead of maize illustrates
qs.e: Competitive supply exists when factors of production can be switched between alternative competing outputs.

qs.q: The market demand curve for a commodity is derived by adding individual consumer demand curves
qs.e: Market demand curves are constructed by summing the quantities demanded by all individual buyers at each specific price (horizontal summation).

qs.q: Goods consumed primarily to demonstrate social status or wealth, where higher prices increase demand, are known as
qs.e: Veblen goods (conspicuous consumption items) have demand curves that slope upward because higher prices enhance their status appeal.

qs.q: Given Qd = 80 - 2P and Qs = 20 + 4P, what are the equilibrium price and equilibrium quantity?
qs.e: Equilibrium condition: 80 - 2P = 20 + 4P => 60 = 6P => P = 10 naira. Substituting P = 10 into Qd: 80 - 2(10) = 60 units.

qs.q: If the price elasticity of supply for cocoa is 2.0, a 15 percent increase in the market price of cocoa will cause quantity supplied to increase by
qs.e: PES = % change in Qs / % change in P => 2.0 = % change in Qs / 15% => % change in Qs = 2.0 * 15% = 30%.

qs.q: In a market where Qd = 80 - 2P and Qs = 20 + 4P, if government fixes a price ceiling at 5 naira, the market shortage will be
qs.e: At P = 5: Qd = 80 - 2(5) = 70 units. Qs = 20 + 4(5) = 40 units. Shortage = Qd - Qs = 70 - 40 = 30 units.

qs.q: In a market with Qd = 80 - 2P and Qs = 20 + 4P, setting a legal price floor at 15 naira results in a market surplus of
qs.e: At P = 15: Qs = 20 + 4(15) = 80 units. Qd = 80 - 2(15) = 50 units. Surplus = Qs - Qd = 80 - 50 = 30 units.

qs.q: A household's income increases from 4,000 naira to 5,000 naira per month, causing their demand for meat to rise from 80 kg to 120 kg. The income elasticity of demand is
Along a downward-sloping linear demand curve, price elasticity of demand is
o: constant at all points along the curve
zero at the top and infinite at the bottom
elastic above the midpoint and inelastic below the midpoint
inelastic above the midpoint and elastic below
qs.e: For a linear demand curve, elasticity varies continuously from infinity at the price intercept to zero at the quantity intercept, passing through unitary elasticity at the midpoint.

qs.q: On a standard supply and demand diagram, producer surplus is graphically represented as the area
o: below the demand curve and above the market price
below the supply curve down to the horizontal axis
between the demand curve and the vertical price axis
above the supply curve and below the market equilibrium price
qs.e: Producer surplus is the difference between total revenue received and minimum acceptable supply price, represented by the triangular area above the supply curve under the price line.

qs.q: Consumer surplus is graphically shown as the area
o: above the supply curve and below the market price
below the demand curve and above the market equilibrium price
underneath the supply curve to the origin
between the price ceiling and price floor
qs.e: Consumer surplus is the difference between maximum willingness to pay and market price, shown by the triangular area under the demand curve above the price level.

qs.q: An ad valorem tax of 10 percent placed on a retail commodity causes the supply curve to
o: pivot upward to the left with a steeper slope
shift downward to the right in a parallel manner
shift in a parallel direction upward to the left
qs.e: An ad valorem tax is a percentage tax; as price increases, the tax amount grows larger, causing the supply curve to pivot leftward rather than shift in parallel.

qs.q: A specific tax of 5 naira per unit imposed on manufacturers causes the supply curve to
o: pivot upward around the vertical axis intercept
shift upward to the left in a parallel movement
qs.e: A specific tax adds a fixed monetary amount per unit at every price, shifting the supply curve vertically upward in a parallel shift.

qs.q: The cobweb theory explains price fluctuations in agricultural markets primarily due to
o: constant changes in consumer taste and fashion
government intervention through price ceiling laws
time lags between production decisions and output realization
qs.e: The cobweb model demonstrates price volatility in markets (like agriculture) where supply decisions depend on past prices due to production lags.

qs.q: When an effective price ceiling causes a market shortage, non-price allocation mechanisms usually include
o: raising interest rates on commercial credit
granting export subsidies to domestic firms
rationing coupons and first-come first-served queueing
qs.e: Because price cannot adjust upward to clear shortages under a price ceiling, non-price rationing mechanisms like queues or rationing coupons emerge.

qs.q: If demand for a product is price elastic (PED > 1), a reduction in product price will cause the firm's total revenue to
qs.e: When demand is price elastic, the percentage increase in quantity demanded exceeds the percentage drop in price, resulting in higher total revenue.

qs.q: Which of the following is a major determinant of the price elasticity of supply for a manufactured product?
o: Degree of product durability in storage
qs.e: Spare capacity allows producers to quickly expand output when market price rises, making supply more price elastic.

qs.q: If a firm can easily substitute capital machinery for manual labor when wages rise, the demand for labor is
qs.e: High factor substitutability increases the elasticity of demand for a factor of production.

qs.q: Given the supply function Qs = -10 + 5P, determine the point price elasticity of supply at a market price of 10 naira.
qs.e: At P = 10, Qs = -10 + 5(10) = 40 units. Point elasticity of supply = (dQ/dP) * (P/Q) = 5 * (10/40) = 5/4 = 1.25.

qs.q: If a specific indirect tax of 4 naira per unit is levied on a market where demand and supply curves have equal linear slopes in absolute terms, how is the tax burden distributed?
o: 2 naira paid by consumers and 2 naira paid by producers
3 naira paid by consumers and 1 naira paid by producers
qs.e: When elasticities of demand and supply are equal (equal absolute slopes), the tax burden is split equally between buyers and sellers (50% each = 2 naira).

qs.q: Market demand is Qd = 100 - 2P and market supply is Qs = -20 + 3P. If a specific tax of 5 naira per unit is collected from sellers, what is the new equilibrium price paid by consumers?
qs.e: Original Qs = -20 + 3P. With a tax of 5 naira, sellers receive (P - 5), so new Qs = -20 + 3(P - 5) = -35 + 3P. Set Qd = new Qs: 100 - 2P = -35 + 3P => 5P = 135 => P = 27 naira.

qs.q: The price of coffee increases from 200 naira to 250 naira per tin, leading to an increase in monthly tea demand from 500 tins to 650 tins. The cross elasticity of demand is
Calculate the arc price elasticity of supply when price increases from 40 naira to 60 naira and quantity supplied expands from 100 units to 300 units.
A cobweb model exhibit continuous convergent price oscillations toward equilibrium when the supply curve is
o: flatter than the demand curve (supply more elastic than demand)
steeper than the demand curve (supply less elastic than demand)
identical in slope to the demand curve
qs.e: Convergence occurs in the cobweb model when supply is less elastic (steeper slope) than demand, dampening price fluctuations over successive periods.

qs.q: The implementation of a legal minimum wage rate above the market equilibrium wage rate for unskilled labor creates
o: a deficit of available unskilled workers
an immediate fall in worker productivity
an expansion in business profit margins
unemployment due to excess labor supply
qs.e: A minimum wage acts as a price floor in the labor market; when set above equilibrium, labor supplied exceeds labor demanded, causing unemployment.

qs.q: A significant depreciation of a nation's domestic currency causes the domestic market supply of exportable goods to
o: decrease due to reduced profit margins in national currency
remain unaffected because exchange rates do not alter supply
increase as foreign buyers demand more at cheaper relative prices
qs.e: Currency depreciation makes domestic exports cheaper in foreign currency terms, boosting export demand and incentivizing producers to expand export supply.

qs.q: Long-term price ceiling enforcement in the agricultural sector typically damages agricultural productivity because it
o: causes rapid hyperinflation in urban consumer centers
reduces farm income and discourages private capital investment
eliminates government expenditure on rural roads
forces farmers to double their annual harvest targets
qs.e: Artificially low ceiling prices suppress agricultural profitability, discouraging farmers from investing in modern machinery, fertilizers, and technology.

qs.q: The demand for necessity goods like salt and essential medicines is typically price inelastic because
o: their production processes exhibit decreasing returns to scale
they are consumed exclusively by high-income income earners
government taxes them at prohibitive ad valorem rates
they have very few close substitutes and represent a small fraction of budget
qs.e: Necessities have inelastic demand because consumers must purchase them regardless of minor price changes due to lack of viable substitutes.

qs.q: Deadweight loss resulting from a market distortion like a tax or price control represents the
o: loss of consumer and producer surplus not captured by anyone
total cost of production incurred by manufacturing firms
subsidy paid by government to distressed consumers
amount of tax revenue collected by the national treasury
qs.e: Deadweight loss measures uncaptured welfare reduction resulting from output falling below the socially optimal competitive equilibrium quantity.

qs.q: Suppose a market consists of 3 identical consumers, each having a demand function qi = 40 - 2P. If the market supply function is Qs = 20 + 4P, what is the equilibrium market price?
qs.e: Market Qd = 3 * (40 - 2P) = 120 - 6P. Set market Qd = Qs: 120 - 6P = 20 + 4P => 100 = 10P => P = 10 naira.

qs.q: A per-unit tax of 6 naira imposed on a commodity causes market output to fall from 1,000 units to 800 units. The deadweight loss to the economy is
qs.e: Deadweight loss triangle area = 0.5 * tax per unit * change in output = 0.5 * 6 * (1,000 - 800) = 0.5 * 6 * 200 = 600 naira.

qs.q: When the price of a good increases from 10 naira to 25 naira, total consumer expenditure on the good remains unchanged at 500 naira. The price elasticity of demand is
qs.e: When total expenditure stays constant following a price change, the percentage change in quantity demanded exactly offsets the percentage change in price, meaning PED = 1.0 (unitary elasticity).

qs.q: A firm seeking to maximize total sales revenue should adjust price until the price elasticity of demand equals
qs.e: Total revenue is maximized at the point on the demand curve where marginal revenue (MR) equals zero, which corresponds exactly to unitary elasticity (PED = 1.0).

qs.q: If a sudden weather shock reduces agricultural crop yields by 40 percent in an industry where price elasticity of demand is 0.5, total farm revenue will
qs.e: When demand is inelastic (PED = 0.5 < 1), a supply reduction causes price to rise by a larger percentage (+80%) than the output fall (-40%), increasing total revenue.

qs.q: The overall satisfaction derived by a consumer from consuming a specific total quantity of a commodity is known as
qs.e: Total utility refers to the cumulative satisfaction obtained from consuming a given number of units of a good.

qs.q: The additional satisfaction obtained from consuming one extra unit of a commodity is defined as
qs.e: Marginal utility measures the change in total utility resulting from consuming one additional unit of a product.

qs.q: The law of diminishing marginal utility states that as a consumer consumes successive units of a good, the marginal utility will eventually
qs.e: The law asserts that each additional unit consumed yields less extra satisfaction than the preceding unit.

qs.q: In cardinal utility analysis, a consumer maximizes total satisfaction when the marginal utility per naira spent is
o: greater for luxury goods than necessities
qs.e: Equilibrium occurs when MUx/Px = MUy/Py = ... = MUn/Pn, equalizing the marginal utility per unit of currency.

qs.q: Extractive economic activities such as agriculture, forestry, fishing, and mining are classified under
qs.e: Primary production involves extracting natural resources directly from the land, sea, or atmosphere.

qs.q: The economic reward or payment accruing to land as a factor of production is
qs.e: Rent is the return paid to owners of land and other natural resources for their use in production.

qs.q: The financial payment earned by human physical and mental effort contributed to production is
qs.e: Wages and salaries represent the reward for labor services rendered in the production process.

qs.q: Manufacturing and construction activities that transform raw materials into finished commodities belong to
qs.e: Secondary production converts raw materials from primary industries into consumer or capital goods.

qs.q: Activities that provide commercial, professional, and personal services like banking, transport, and teaching fall under
qs.e: Tertiary production comprises service industries that distribute goods or provide direct services.

qs.q: The income reward paid to owners of capital for lending their financial assets or machinery is
qs.e: Interest is the payment made for the use of capital assets or borrowed money over time.

qs.q: The residual economic return earned by the entrepreneur for organizing production and bearing business risks is
qs.e: Profit is the reward earned by the entrepreneur after all other factor rewards have been paid.

qs.q: A major advantage of division of labour and specialization in a manufacturing plant is that it
o: reduces the risk of industrial accidents to zero
eliminates the need for supervisory management staff
increases worker dexterity and overall operational efficiency
prevents worker boredom and job monotony
qs.e: Specialization allows workers to become highly skilled at specific tasks, increasing speed and efficiency.

qs.q: A significant disadvantage associated with extreme division of labour is that workers may experience
o: monotony and loss of job satisfaction
qs.e: Performing the same repetitive micro-task continuously leads to boredom and reduced job satisfaction.

qs.q: An indifference curve shows all combinations of two goods that provide the consumer with
o: an equal level of total satisfaction
qs.e: An indifference curve represents different combinations of two goods between which a consumer is indifferent.

qs.q: The rate at which a consumer is willing to give up good Y to obtain an additional unit of good X while maintaining constant total utility is the
qs.e: Marginal Rate of Substitution (MRSxy) measures the trade-off ratio along an indifference curve.

qs.q: An increase in a consumer's nominal income, with commodity prices remaining unchanged, will cause the budget line to
o: shift parallel inward to the left
pivot inward around the vertical axis
shift parallel outward to the right
slope upward from left to right
qs.e: Higher nominal income expands purchasing power, shifting the budget constraint parallel rightward.

qs.q: A decrease in the price of good X, holding consumer income and the price of good Y constant, will cause the budget line to
o: shift parallel outward to the right
qs.e: A lower price for good X allows more X to be bought, rotating the budget line outward on the X-axis intercept.

qs.q: The total change in quantity demanded resulting from a price change is decomposed into the
qs.e: Price effect = Substitution effect (relative price change) + Income effect (real purchasing power change).

qs.q: The law of diminishing returns sets in during short-run production because
o: all factor inputs expand at the same percentage rate
variable inputs are added to a fixed factor of production
qs.e: Combining increasing variable inputs with a fixed input eventually overcrowds the fixed input, diminishing marginal returns.

qs.q: If a consumer receives marginal utility of 20, 16, 12, and 8 utils from the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, and 4th cups of tea respectively, what is the total utility derived from consuming 4 cups?
qs.e: Total utility = sum of marginal utilities = 20 + 16 + 12 + 8 = 56 utils.

qs.q: A consumer's total utility is 70 utils after consuming 4 units of a commodity and 82 utils after consuming 5 units. The marginal utility of the 5th unit is
qs.e: Marginal utility = TU(5) - TU(4) = 82 - 70 = 12 utils.

qs.q: When 4 workers are employed in a bakery, total daily output of bread loaves is 120. What is the average product per worker?
qs.e: Average product AP = Total Product / Quantity of Labour = 120 / 4 = 30 loaves per worker.

qs.q: A farming enterprise produces 90 bags of maize using 3 farm hands and 110 bags using 4 farm hands. The marginal product of the 4th farm hand is
qs.e: Marginal product = TP(4) - TP(3) = 110 - 90 = 20 bags.

qs.q: A consumer buys Good X at 5 naira per unit and Good Y at 10 naira per unit. At utility equilibrium, if the marginal utility of Good Y is 40 utils, what is the marginal utility of Good X?
qs.e: Equilibrium condition: MUx / Px = MUy / Py => MUx / 5 = 40 / 10 => MUx / 5 = 4 => MUx = 20 utils.

qs.q: For a Giffen good, when its price falls, the negative income effect is
o: weaker than the substitution effect, causing quantity demanded to rise
equal to the substitution effect, keeping quantity demanded constant
stronger than the substitution effect, causing quantity demanded to fall
completely absent because real income is unaffected
qs.e: A Giffen good is an extreme inferior good where the negative income effect overwhelms the substitution effect, leading to a fall in quantity demanded when price drops.

qs.q: For a normal good, a decrease in price leads to an increase in quantity demanded because
o: both the substitution effect and income effect operate in the same direction
the substitution effect is negative while the income effect is zero
the income effect opposes the substitution effect but is weaker
the budget line shifts inward parallel
qs.e: For normal goods, lower prices make the good relatively cheaper (substitution effect) and increase real income (income effect); both act to increase demand.

qs.q: Reductions in long-run average production costs resulting from expansion of the firm's own internal scale of operation are called
qs.e: Internal economies of scale are cost advantages generated internally within a firm as its output scale expands.

qs.q: Cost reductions enjoyed by all firms in a specific geographic cluster due to industry-wide development are known as
qs.e: External economies of scale stem from external factors outside the firm, such as localized industry infrastructure and skilled labor pools.

qs.q: Internal diseconomies of scale occur in the long run when a firm becomes so large that
o: average costs increase due to communication breakdown and management complexity
average costs fall due to bulk purchasing discounts
qs.e: Diseconomies of scale happen when administrative complexity and communication lags cause long-run unit costs to rise as firm size grows.

qs.q: In the law of variable proportions, Stage II of production represents the range of output where
o: marginal product is positive but declining
qs.e: Stage II (the rational stage of production) begins where AP is maximized and ends where MP drops to zero.

qs.q: The slope of an indifference curve at any given point is equal to the ratio of the
o: total utilities of the two commodities
marginal utilities of the two commodities
qs.e: The slope of an indifference curve is -dY/dX = MRSxy = MUx / MUy.

qs.q: Optimal consumer choice under ordinal utility theory occurs at the tangency point where the slope of the indifference curve equals the slope of the
qs.e: Tangency occurs where MRSxy = Px / Py, maximizing consumer satisfaction within the budget constraint.

qs.q: Stage I of production ends at the specific input level where
o: average product reaches its maximum value and equals marginal product
total product reaches its absolute peak
qs.e: Stage I ends where Average Product (AP) reaches its maximum, which is also the point where AP intersects MP.

qs.q: In Stage III of short-run production, adding further units of the variable input causes total product to
o: decline because marginal product is negative
qs.e: Stage III is irrational because Marginal Product is negative, causing Total Product to fall with additional variable input.

qs.q: A producer minimizes cost by equating the marginal product per naira across inputs. If labor costs 10 naira per hour, capital costs 20 naira per hour, and MP of capital is 60 units, what must MP of labor be?
qs.e: Cost minimization condition: MPl / Pl = MPk / Pk => MPl / 10 = 60 / 20 => MPl / 10 = 3 => MPl = 30 units.

qs.q: Total Output for L = 1 to 5 is 15, 35, 60, 75, and 80 units respectively. At which unit of labor do diminishing marginal returns set in?
qs.e: MP sequence: L1=15, L2=20, L3=25, L4=15, L5=5. MP reaches its maximum of 25 at the 3rd unit, so diminishing marginal returns set in with the employment of the 4th unit.

qs.q: A firm's Total Product for 1 to 5 workers is 20, 48, 81, 108, and 125. At what level of employment is Average Product maximized?
qs.e: Calculate AP = TP/L: L=1 (20), L=2 (24), L=3 (27), L=4 (27), L=5 (25). Calculate MP: L1=20, L2=28, L3=33, L4=27, L5=17. AP is maximized at 4 workers where AP = MP = 27 units.

qs.q: A consumer has 18 naira to spend on X (priced at 4 naira) and Y (priced at 2 naira). MUx is 32, 28, 24, 20 while MUy is 16, 14, 12, 10, 8. What quantity combination maximizes utility?
o: 4 units of X and 1 unit of Y
2 units of X and 5 units of Y
3 units of X and 3 units of Y
1 unit of X and 7 units of Y
qs.e: MUx/Px sequence: 8, 7, 6, 5. MUy/Py sequence: 8, 7, 6, 5, 4. Match MU/P = 6 at 3 units of X and 3 units of Y. Total expenditure = (3*4) + (3*2) = 12 + 6 = 18 naira.

qs.q: An Engel curve that slopes upward with a decreasing gradient indicates that the good is a
qs.e: An Engel curve plots income against quantity demanded. For necessity goods, demand increases with income but at a diminishing rate as income rises.

qs.q: The substitution effect of a price reduction is always negative in the sense that the consumer
o: always purchases more of the good whose relative price has dropped
switches entirely to imported substitute goods
experiences a reduction in nominal monetary income
always reduces consumption of both commodities
qs.e: The substitution effect measures relative price change holding real utility constant; consumers always substitute toward the relatively cheaper commodity.

qs.q: If a production function Q = 5 * L^(0.4) * K^(0.8) represents a manufacturing firm, the returns to scale are
qs.e: For a Cobb-Douglas production function Q = A * L^a * K^b, sum of exponents = 0.4 + 0.8 = 1.2 > 1.0, which proves increasing returns to scale.

qs.q: Technical efficiency in production occurs when a firm produces a given output using
o: the lowest monetary cost of factor inputs
the highest ratio of variable to fixed capital
the maximum possible number of employees
the minimum physical quantity of input factors
qs.e: Technical efficiency means no inputs are wasted, achieving maximum physical output from a given set of physical inputs.

qs.q: Division of labour is primarily limited by the
o: extent of the market demand for the final product
number of public holidays declared by government
rate of inflation in the national economy
total land mass area of the manufacturing factory
qs.e: Adam Smith noted that division of labour is limited by the extent of the market; small demand cannot justify specialized high-volume production.

qs.q: The ease with which a worker can switch from being a carpenter to becoming a computer programmer is a measure of
qs.e: Occupational mobility refers to the capacity of workers to change their line of employment or trade.

qs.q: The process of creating capital goods like heavy machinery, bridges, and industrial plants through deferred consumption is called
qs.e: Capital formation (or investment) involves accumulating real physical assets by foregoing current consumption.

qs.q: A chemical processing firm has a production function Q = 10 * L^(0.3) * K^(0.5). If all inputs are increased by 100 percent, physical output will increase by
o: less than 100 percent (decreasing returns to scale)
more than 100 percent (increasing returns to scale)
qs.e: Sum of exponents = 0.3 + 0.5 = 0.8 < 1.0. A 100% increase in L and K results in output increasing by (2^0.8 - 1) = 74.1%, which is less than 100%.

qs.q: A consumer's marginal utility function for good X is MUx = 24 - 2X. If the market price is 4 naira per unit, what is the maximum total utility obtained at equilibrium?
qs.e: Equilibrium MUx = Px => 24 - 2X = 4 => 2X = 20 => X = 10 units. Total utility = integral of MUx from 0 to 10 = [24(10) - (10)^2] = 240 - 100 = 140 utils.

qs.q: A manufacturing firm has marginal product of labor MPl = 40 units and marginal product of capital MPk = 10 units. The Marginal Rate of Technical Substitution (MRTS) of labor for capital is
qs.e: MRTS (lk) = MPl / MPk = 40 / 10 = 4.0.

qs.q: If the prices of both Good X and Good Y double simultaneously while consumer nominal income remains constant, the budget line will
o: shift parallel outward to the right
shift parallel inward to the left
qs.e: Doubling both prices cuts the maximum purchase quantity of both goods in half, shifting both intercepts inward by 50% in a parallel shift.

qs.q: Cost minimization on a production isoquant map is achieved at the tangency point between an isoquant and an isocost line where the
o: Marginal Product of labor equals the price of capital
Total Product curve intersects the Average Cost curve
Average Product of labor is equal to zero
Marginal Rate of Technical Substitution equals the input price ratio (PL / PK)
qs.e: Equilibrium occurs where MRTSlk = -dK/dL = MPl / MPk = PL / PK.

qs.q: Production costs that do not vary with changes in the level of physical output are known as
qs.e: Fixed costs (e.g. factory rent, insurance) remain constant regardless of whether production is zero or high.

qs.q: Costs that change directly in proportion to alterations in output volume are classified as
qs.e: Variable costs (e.g. raw materials, direct labor) increase as output increases and fall to zero when production stops.

qs.q: In economic accounting, Total Cost (TC) is equal to the sum of
o: Total Fixed Cost and Total Variable Cost
qs.e: Total Cost equation: TC = Total Fixed Cost (TFC) + Total Variable Cost (TVC).

qs.q: The cost incurred per unit of physical output produced is calculated as
qs.e: Average Cost (AC) is calculated by dividing Total Cost by total output quantity (AC = TC / Q).

qs.q: Total revenue earned by a business firm from selling its product is calculated by multiplying
o: average cost by total fixed cost
unit price by total quantity sold
qs.e: Total Revenue equation: TR = Price (P) * Quantity (Q).

qs.q: The additional cost incurred by producing one additional unit of output is called
qs.e: Marginal Cost (MC) measures the change in Total Cost per unit change in output (MC = dTC / dQ).

qs.q: Average Revenue is defined as total revenue divided by quantity sold, which is always mathematically equal to the product's
qs.e: AR = TR / Q = (P * Q) / Q = Price (P).

qs.q: As a firm increases its volume of output, its Average Fixed Cost (AFC) will
o: remain completely constant at all output levels
continually decline toward the horizontal axis
qs.e: AFC = TFC / Q. Since TFC is constant, dividing by expanding Q causes AFC to fall continuously (spreading the overhead).

qs.q: The change in total revenue resulting from the sale of one extra unit of output is termed
qs.e: Marginal Revenue (MR) measures the additional revenue generated by selling an additional unit of output.

qs.q: Economic profit realized by an enterprise is determined by subtracting Total Cost from
qs.e: Economic Profit = Total Revenue (TR) - Total Cost (TC).

qs.q: A business firm reaches its break-even point when its total revenue is exactly equal to its
qs.e: At break-even, TR = TC, meaning economic profit is zero and the firm covers both explicit and implicit costs.

qs.q: Normal profit is formally defined in economic theory as the
o: windfall gain resulting from inflationary price shocks
excess of total revenue over total economic costs
minimum return required to keep the entrepreneur in business, included in total cost
qs.e: Normal profit is an opportunity cost of entrepreneurship and is treated as a component of total cost.

qs.q: Supernormal or economic profit occurs when a firm's total revenue
o: exceeds its total economic costs including normal profit
is less than its total variable costs
qs.e: Supernormal profit is any profit earned above normal profit (TR > TC).

qs.q: Short-run Average Cost (SAC) curves are generally U-shaped primarily because of the operation of the
qs.e: In the short run, fixed inputs cause initial falling average costs followed by rising average costs due to diminishing returns.

qs.q: The Long-Run Average Cost (LRAC) curve is U-shaped due to the influence of
o: the law of diminishing marginal returns
qs.e: In the long run, all inputs are variable; falling LRAC reflects economies of scale while rising LRAC reflects diseconomies of scale.

qs.q: On a standard cost diagram, the Marginal Cost (MC) curve intersects the Average Cost (AC) curve at the
o: maximum point of the AC curve
vertical axis intercept of the AC curve
minimum point of the AC curve
qs.e: When MC < AC, AC falls; when MC > AC, AC rises. Therefore, MC intersects AC at its minimum point.

qs.q: The Marginal Cost (MC) curve intersects the Average Variable Cost (AVC) curve at its
o: intercept with the vertical price axis
qs.e: Similarly, MC passes through the minimum point of the AVC curve.

qs.q: In the short run, a loss-making competitive firm should immediately shut down operations if product price falls below minimum
qs.e: If Price < AVC, total revenue fails to cover variable costs, so shutting down minimizes losses to just fixed costs.

qs.q: Expenditures on past business equipment that cannot be recovered or refunded are described as
qs.e: Sunk costs are historical unrecoverable expenditures that should not affect future operational decisions.

qs.q: A printing press incurs a Total Fixed Cost of 500 naira and a Total Variable Cost of 300 naira in producing 50 posters. What is the Total Cost?
qs.e: TC = TFC + TVC = 500 + 300 = 800 naira.

qs.q: If a tailor's monthly shop rent (TFC) is 1,000 naira and she sews 50 dresses per month, what is her Average Fixed Cost per dress?
qs.e: AFC = TFC / Q = 1,000 / 50 = 20 naira.

qs.q: A furniture maker pays 600 naira for timber and labor (TVC) to produce 30 wooden chairs. The Average Variable Cost per chair is
qs.e: AVC = TVC / Q = 600 / 30 = 20 naira.

qs.q: A shoe manufacturer records Total Cost of 200 naira for 4 pairs of shoes and 235 naira for 5 pairs. The Marginal Cost of the 5th pair is
qs.e: Marginal Cost = TC(5) - TC(4) = 235 - 200 = 35 naira.

qs.q: A poultry farmer sells 40 crates of eggs at a market price of 25 naira per crate. What is the Total Revenue earned?
qs.e: TR = Price * Quantity = 25 * 40 = 1,000 naira.

qs.q: A text book publisher generates 1,500 naira in Total Revenue while incurring 1,100 naira in Total Costs. The economic profit realized is
qs.e: Profit = TR - TC = 1,500 - 1,100 = 400 naira.

qs.q: Total Revenue generated by selling 3 radio sets is 120 naira, and for 4 radio sets is 150 naira. The Marginal Revenue of the 4th radio set is
qs.e: Marginal Revenue = TR(4) - TR(3) = 150 - 120 = 30 naira.

qs.q: Explicit costs differ from implicit costs in business accounting because explicit costs involve
o: foregone earnings from owner-supplied productive assets
direct out-of-pocket monetary payments to external parties
unrealized capital gains on real estate
qs.e: Explicit costs are actual cash payments made to buy factor inputs (e.g. wages, raw materials), whereas implicit costs represent opportunity costs of self-owned resources.

qs.q: Economic profit earned by an entrepreneur is equal to Total Revenue minus
o: both explicit costs and implicit opportunity costs
qs.e: Economic profit accounts for both explicit cash costs and implicit opportunity costs of owner capital and labor.

qs.q: To maximize total profit or minimize total loss, a business firm should expand production until
o: Marginal Revenue equals Marginal Cost (MR = MC)
Average Cost is at its absolute minimum
qs.e: The golden rule of profit maximization is MR = MC, provided MC cuts MR from below.

qs.q: In the short run, a firm experiencing economic losses will continue to operate if Total Revenue covers
qs.e: As long as TR >= TVC (or P >= AVC), operating generates a contribution margin that helps pay off a portion of fixed costs.

qs.q: The long-run period in production theory is defined as a time horizon in which
o: at least one factor input remains fixed
firms cannot enter or exit the industry
all factor inputs are variable and there are no fixed costs
qs.e: In the long run, all inputs can be adjusted, meaning all costs become variable.

qs.q: The Average Fixed Cost (AFC) curve is graphically represented as a
qs.e: Because TFC = AFC * Q is constant, the AFC curve forms a rectangular hyperbola asymptotic to both axes.

qs.q: On a graph plotting output on the horizontal axis and cost on the vertical axis, the Total Fixed Cost curve is a
o: vertical straight line parallel to the price axis
straight line sloping upward from the origin
horizontal straight line parallel to the quantity axis
U-shaped curve starting from the origin
qs.e: TFC does not change with output Q, so it appears as a flat horizontal line.

qs.q: A firm's optimum output scale is defined as the production level at which
o: Average Total Cost is minimized in the long run
Total Variable Cost equals Total Fixed Cost
qs.e: Optimum scale of production is achieved at the minimum point of the long-run average cost curve.

qs.q: A firm's total cost function is given by TC = 100 + 10Q + 2Q^2. What is the Marginal Cost when output Q is 5 units?
qs.e: MC is the derivative of TC with respect to Q: dTC/dQ = 10 + 4Q. At Q = 5: MC = 10 + 4(5) = 10 + 20 = 30 naira.

qs.q: If a total cost equation is TC = 100 + 4Q^2, at what output level Q is Average Cost (AC) minimized?
A sole proprietor generates 50,000 naira revenue. Explicit operating costs are 30,000 naira. If he gave up a salary of 12,000 naira to run the firm, his economic profit is
qs.e: Economic Profit = TR - Explicit Costs - Implicit Costs = 50,000 - 30,000 - 12,000 = 8,000 naira.

qs.q: A manufacturing company has fixed overheads of 200,000 naira. If selling price is 50 naira per unit and variable cost is 30 naira per unit, what is the break-even output quantity?
qs.e: Break-even Q = Fixed Cost / (Price - Variable Cost per unit) = 200,000 / (50 - 30) = 200,000 / 20 = 10,000 units.

qs.q: A firm's Total Cost schedule shows: Q=0 (TC=50), Q=1 (TC=80), Q=2 (TC=100), Q=3 (TC=130), Q=4 (TC=170). What is the Average Variable Cost at 4 units of output?
A competitive firm's short-run supply curve is represented by the segment of its
o: Average Total Cost curve above its Average Fixed Cost curve
Marginal Revenue curve above the horizontal price line
Marginal Cost curve that lies above its Average Variable Cost curve
Average Variable Cost curve sloping downward
qs.e: In pure competition, the firm produces where P = MC as long as P >= AVC; thus the MC curve above minimum AVC is its short-run supply curve.

qs.q: The Minimum Efficient Scale (MES) of a firm refers to the lowest level of output at which
o: total fixed cost drops to zero
long-run average cost reaches its absolute minimum
short-run average total cost exceeds price
marginal cost intersects average variable cost
qs.e: MES is the smallest output scale at which a firm can minimize long-run average cost, achieving full economies of scale.

qs.q: The mathematical relationship between the Total Cost curve and the Marginal Cost curve implies that MC is represented graphically by the
o: area under the Total Fixed Cost line
vertical distance between Total Cost and Total Variable Cost
ratio of Total Revenue to physical quantity
slope of the Total Cost curve at any given output level
qs.e: Marginal Cost is dTC/dQ, which corresponds to the instantaneous geometric slope of the Total Cost curve.

qs.q: Capacity utilization measures the extent to which a firm uses its installed productive capacity. Operating below optimum scale implies the presence of
qs.e: Excess capacity occurs when actual output is less than the output level that minimizes average total cost.

qs.q: Cost function duality in production theory demonstrates that Average Variable Cost is inversely related to
qs.e: AVC = Variable Wage Rate / Average Product of Labour (AVC = w / APL); when labor productivity APL rises, unit variable cost AVC falls.

qs.q: Similarly, Marginal Cost is inversely related to the
qs.e: MC = Variable Wage Rate / Marginal Product of Labour (MC = w / MPL); as productivity MPL increases, marginal cost MC decreases.

qs.q: A firm faces demand and cost functions TR = 100Q - 2Q^2 and TC = 200 + 20Q + 3Q^2. What output Q maximizes total economic profit?
qs.e: MR = dTR/dQ = 100 - 4Q. MC = dTC/dQ = 20 + 6Q. Set MR = MC: 100 - 4Q = 20 + 6Q => 10Q = 80 => Q = 8 units.

qs.q: Using the functions TR = 100Q - 2Q^2 and TC = 200 + 20Q + 3Q^2, calculate the maximum profit realized at the optimal output level of 8 units.
A firm's marginal cost function is MC = 6Q + 4. What is the Total Variable Cost incurred in producing 5 units of output?
qs.e: Total Variable Cost = integral of MC with respect to Q from 0 to 5 = [3Q^2 + 4Q] evaluated from 0 to 5 = 3(25) + 4(5) = 75 + 20 = 95 naira.

qs.q: Given TC = 50 + 10Q + 0.5Q^2, determine the minimum price at which the firm will continue short-run production rather than shut down.
qs.e: TVC = 10Q + 0.5Q^2 => AVC = TVC / Q = 10 + 0.5Q. The minimum of AVC occurs as Q approaches 0, where AVC = 10 naira. The shutdown price is 10 naira.

qs.q: The Long-Run Average Cost (LRAC) curve is described as an envelope curve because it is formed by
o: tangency points with a family of Short-Run Average Cost (SRAC) curves corresponding to different plant sizes
connecting the minimum points of all Short-Run Average Variable Cost curves
drawing a horizontal line at the lowest point of total fixed cost
summing the Short-Run Marginal Cost curves of all firms in the industry
qs.e: The LRAC curve envelopes all short-run plant options, being tangent to each SRAC curve at the lowest achievable unit cost for that plant capacity.

qs.q: A market structure characterized by a large number of buyers and sellers, homogeneous products, and free entry and exit is known as
qs.e: Perfect competition satisfies all key conditions including many buyers/sellers, standardized products, and no entry barriers.

qs.q: A market situation in which a single firm is the sole seller of a product with no close substitutes is defined as a
qs.e: A pure monopoly exists when one firm controls 100% of market supply for a unique product.

qs.q: A market structure with many competing sellers offering differentiated products is called
qs.e: Monopolistic competition combines features of competition (many firms) and monopoly (product differentiation).

qs.q: An industry dominated by a small number of large, interdependent producing firms is classified as an
qs.e: Oligopoly is characterized by market concentration among a few dominant firms whose decisions affect each other.

qs.q: Products that are identical in physical quality, appearance, and technical specifications across all sellers are described as
qs.e: Homogeneous products are perfect substitutes, making consumers indifferent about which seller they purchase from.

qs.q: In economic theory, a firm under pure competition is called a price taker because it
o: has complete authority to fix retail product prices
colludes with competitor firms to inflate prices
must accept the market price determined by industry supply and demand
qs.e: Competitive firms hold a negligible market share and face a horizontal demand curve at the market price.

qs.q: A firm that possesses significant market power to set product price by altering its supply volume is a
qs.e: A price maker (like a monopolist) faces a downward-sloping demand curve and can choose its price-quantity combination.

qs.q: Which of the following serves as a primary barrier to entry protecting a monopoly market position?
o: Legal patents and government exclusive franchises
Absence of advertising and promotion costs
Complete ease of factor input mobility
qs.e: Barriers to entry such as patents, copyrights, statutory monopolies, and resource control block potential competitors.

qs.q: The commercial practice of charging different prices to different buyers for identical goods based on demand elasticity is known as
qs.e: Price discrimination occurs when a firm sells the same product at different prices for reasons unrelated to cost differences.

qs.q: An industry where extreme economies of scale enable a single large firm to supply the entire market at lower unit costs than multiple firms is a
qs.e: Natural monopolies (e.g. municipal water, electricity grids) arise due to massive fixed capital infrastructure costs.

qs.q: The kinked demand curve model in oligopoly theory is primarily used to explain the phenomenon of
o: rapid price fluctuations during economic booms
complete freedom of entry into the industry
equal distribution of market share among firms
qs.e: The kinked demand curve assumes rivals match price reductions but ignore price increases, creating a kink at the current price where demand shifts from elastic to inelastic.

qs.q: A formal collusive agreement among independent oligopolistic producers to fix prices and restrict total output is called a
qs.e: A cartel (such as OPEC) coordinates production quotas among member firms to maximize collective monopoly profit.

qs.q: In the long run under monopolistic competition, excess capacity arises because firms produce at an output level where
o: Average Total Cost is above its absolute minimum point
qs.e: Monopolistically competitive firms operate on the downward-sloping portion of the LRAC curve, resulting in excess capacity.

qs.q: Under perfect competition in long-run equilibrium, freedom of market entry and exit ensures that firms earn only
qs.e: Entry of new firms eliminates short-run supernormal profits until P = AC and all firms earn normal profit.

qs.q: Unlike competitive firms, a pure monopolist can sustain supernormal economic profits in the long run due to the existence of
qs.e: Barriers to entry prevent competitor firms from entering the industry to compete away supernormal profits.

qs.q: A competitive firm achieves short-run profit maximization by setting output at the level where
o: Price equals Marginal Revenue and Marginal Cost (P = MR = MC)
Average Total Cost is at its absolute peak
Total Revenue equals Total Fixed Cost
qs.e: Since P = AR = MR under perfect competition, setting MR = MC implies P = MC.

qs.q: The demand curve faced by an individual firm operating in a perfectly competitive market is
qs.e: Because the firm is a price taker, it can sell any quantity at the market price, facing a horizontal demand curve.

qs.q: The demand curve facing a pure monopolist is identical to the
qs.e: Since the monopolist is the sole supplier, the firm's demand curve is the industry market demand curve, which slopes downward.

qs.q: Non-price strategies like distinct branding, special packaging, and post-sales servicing are examples of
qs.e: Product differentiation creates perceived or real differences between products, giving firms limited market power.

qs.q: A perfectly competitive firm sells product at 20 naira per unit. Its total cost is TC = 100 + 10Q + Q^2. What output Q maximizes profit?
qs.e: Under competition P = MR = 20. MC = dTC/dQ = 10 + 2Q. Set P = MC: 20 = 10 + 2Q => 2Q = 10 => Q = 5 units.

qs.q: A monopolist faces demand P = 50 - Q and constant marginal cost MC = 10 naira. What is the profit-maximizing output and price?
qs.e: TR = P * Q = 50Q - Q^2 => MR = 50 - 2Q. Set MR = MC: 50 - 2Q = 10 => 2Q = 40 => Q = 20 units. Price P = 50 - 20 = 30 naira.

qs.q: Using the monopoly equilibrium where Price is 30 naira and Quantity is 20 units, determine Total Revenue generated.
qs.e: Total Revenue = Price * Quantity = 30 * 20 = 600 naira.

qs.q: Monopoly results in economic inefficiency compared to perfect competition because the monopolist charges a
o: lower price and produces a larger output
higher price and produces a smaller output
price equal to minimum average cost
qs.e: Monopoly restricts output and inflates price above marginal cost, causing deadweight loss.

qs.q: Which of the following conditions is strictly required for a firm to successfully practice price discrimination?
o: Homogeneity of product across all sellers
Ability to separate market segments with different price elasticities of demand
qs.e: To discriminate prices, the firm must have market power, separate sub-markets, and prevent resale between low-price and high-price buyers.

qs.q: First-degree (or perfect) price discrimination occurs when a monopolist charges each buyer
o: a uniform bulk price based on quantity tiers
a price equal to marginal cost
different prices based on demographic age groups
the exact maximum price they are willing to pay, extracting all consumer surplus
qs.e: Perfect price discrimination captures 100% of consumer surplus by charging each buyer their maximum willingness to pay.

qs.q: Volume discounts offered by wholesale suppliers based on bulk quantity purchased represent an example of
qs.e: Second-degree price discrimination varies price per unit according to the block quantity or volume purchased.

qs.q: Charging lower airline ticket prices to students and senior citizens than to business travelers is an example of
qs.e: Third-degree price discrimination segregates buyers into distinct demographic groups based on price elasticity.

qs.q: In oligopolistic markets, firms often prefer non-price competition over price cutting because price wars tend to
o: reduce total profits for all competing firms in the industry
cause rapid inflation in consumer price indices
qs.e: Price wars lower profit margins for all oligopolists; hence firms compete through advertising and product design instead.

qs.q: A market structure consisting of exactly two competing manufacturing enterprises is technically defined as a
qs.e: A duopoly is a special case of oligopoly featuring exactly two sellers.

qs.q: A market structure featuring a single buyer facing many competitive sellers is known as a
qs.e: Monopsony is single-buyer market dominance (e.g. government buying military equipment).

qs.q: Allocative efficiency in resource allocation is attained when market price is equal to
qs.e: Allocative efficiency occurs where consumer marginal valuation (P) equals societal marginal cost of production (MC).

qs.q: Productive efficiency is achieved when a firm produces output at the point where
o: Total Revenue exceeds Total Cost by 100%
Average Total Cost is minimized in the long run
qs.e: Productive efficiency means producing goods at the lowest achievable unit cost.

qs.q: For a downward-sloping demand curve, Marginal Revenue is less than Price (MR < P) because
o: fixed costs continually fall as output expands
selling an additional unit requires reducing price on all preceding units sold
marginal cost rises exponentially with output
the firm operates as a price taker
qs.e: To sell one more unit, a price maker must lower the price on all units sold, so MR falls faster than P.

qs.q: A statutory monopoly is created through
o: government legislative decree or statutory license
natural ownership of rare raw material deposits
qs.e: Statutory monopolies are established by laws or government grants (e.g. public utilities).

qs.q: A competitive firm sells product at 15 naira. Its cost function is TC = 50 + 3Q + Q^2. At optimal output Q = 6 units, what is its profit or loss status?
o: Loss of 50 naira, should shut down immediately
Loss of 14 naira, but continues producing because Price exceeds AVC
qs.e: MC = 3 + 2Q = 15 => Q = 6. TR = 15 * 6 = 90 naira. TC = 50 + 3(6) + 36 = 104 naira. Loss = 104 - 90 = 14 naira. TVC = 3(6) + 36 = 54 => AVC = 9 naira. Since P = 15 > AVC = 9, the firm continues producing in short run.

qs.q: A discriminating monopolist operates in two isolated markets with MR1 = 100 - 2Q1 and MR2 = 80 - 4If MC = 20 naira, what prices will be charged in markets 1 and 2?
o: Market 1 Price = 40 naira, Market 2 Price = 15 naira
Market 1 Price = 80 naira, Market 2 Price = 60 naira
Market 1 Price = 50 naira, Market 2 Price = 50 naira
Market 1 Price = 60 naira, Market 2 Price = 50 naira

qs.q: If a profit-maximizing monopolist sets price at 50 naira where marginal cost is 20 naira, calculate the Lerner Index of Monopoly Power.
qs.e: Lerner Index L = (Price - Marginal Cost) / Price = (50 - 20) / 50 = 30 / 50 = 0.60.

qs.q: The kinked demand curve model exhibits two distinct demand segments: the demand segment above the kink price is highly
o: inelastic, while the segment below the kink is elastic
perfectly inelastic, while the segment below is unitary
unitary, while the segment below is infinite
elastic, while the segment below the kink is inelastic
qs.e: Above the kink, raising price causes customers to switch to rivals (elastic demand). Below the kink, cutting price leads rivals to follow (inelastic demand).

qs.q: The Prisoner's Dilemma framework in game theory demonstrates why oligopolistic firms often struggle to maintain cartels because of individual incentives to
o: voluntarily pay higher corporate income taxes
expand factory safety features beyond legal standards
cheat on production quotas and undercut agreed cartel prices
share proprietary technological secrets with rivals
qs.e: Cartels are inherently unstable because each individual firm can gain higher short-run profits by secretly cheating on output limits.

qs.q: If government regulates a natural monopoly by enforcing Marginal Cost Pricing (P = MC), the regulated firm will
o: incur short-run financial losses requiring state subsidy
break even with normal economic profit
qs.e: Because natural monopolies have declining average total costs, MC lies below ATC; enforcing P = MC sets price below unit cost, generating losses.

qs.q: Average Cost Pricing regulation (P = AC) forces a natural monopoly to
o: maximize total deadweight loss to consumers
produce where price equals unit cost, earning normal profit
double its research and development expenditure
charge zero price to low-income households
qs.e: Setting P = AC allows the natural monopoly to cover all costs including normal profit without requiring public subsidies.

qs.q: According to contestable market theory, potential threat of entry by new competitors causes incumbent monopolists to
o: raise prices to maximum short-run monopoly levels
merge immediately with foreign state corporations
keep prices low and operate efficiently near competitive levels
cease all advertising and promotional activities
qs.e: In a contestable market with zero sunk entry/exit costs, the threat of hit-and-run entry suppresses monopoly markups.

qs.q: In a dominant firm price leadership model, the dominant firm sets the market price while smaller fringe firms act as
o: price takers supplying the remaining residual demand
cartel managers fixing national output quotas
monopolists in their local geographical sub-markets
qs.e: The dominant firm sets price considering its marginal cost, and fringe firms take that price as given.

qs.q: Comparing output levels across market structures, total industry output under pure competition is
o: less than under monopoly, with competitive price being higher
equal to monopoly output, but at a higher price
greater than under monopoly, with competitive price being lower
qs.e: Pure competition maximizes output and minimizes price, whereas monopoly restricts output to raise price.

qs.q: The excess capacity theorem states that monopolistically competitive firms in long-run equilibrium produce an output level that is
o: greater than the output that minimizes long-run average cost
equal to the output of a pure monopoly
identical to the socially optimal competitive output
smaller than the output that minimizes long-run average cost
qs.e: Product differentiation creates a downward-sloping demand curve tangent to LRAC to the left of its minimum point, leaving excess capacity.

qs.q: A profit-maximizing monopolist operates at an output level where price elasticity of demand is -2.5. Calculate the firm's Lerner Index of Monopoly Power.
qs.e: Lerner Index condition: (P - MC) / P = 1 / |PED| = 1 / 2.5 = 0.40.

qs.q: A multi-plant monopolist operates Plant 1 (MC1 = 4 + 2Q1) and Plant 2 (MC2 = 2 + 4Q2). If optimal marginal cost across both plants is 10 naira, how much output should be produced in each plant?
qs.e: Equalize MC across plants to common MC = 10: Plant 1: 4 + 2Q1 = 10 => 2Q1 = 6 => Q1 = 3 units. Plant 2: 2 + 4Q2 = 10 => 4Q2 = 8 => Q2 = 2 units.

qs.q: Third-degree price discrimination increases a monopolist's total economic profit above single-price profit because it allows the firm to
o: extract additional consumer surplus from sub-markets with less elastic demand
eliminate variable production costs in all sub-markets
reduce total fixed overhead costs to zero
qs.e: By charging higher prices in inelastic sub-markets and lower prices in elastic sub-markets, total revenue and profit increase.

qs.q: The second-order condition for profit maximization by a competitive firm requires that the Marginal Cost curve must
o: cut the Marginal Revenue line from above (negative MC slope)
be completely horizontal and equal to Total Fixed Cost
cut the Marginal Revenue line from below (positive MC slope)
be tangent to the Average Fixed Cost curve
qs.e: For a maximum, d^2(Profit)/dQ^2 < 0 => dMR/dQ - dMC/dQ < 0 => dMC/dQ > 0 (MC must be rising).

qs.q: In short-run economic analysis, the excess of total revenue over total variable cost earned by fixed factor inputs is termed
qs.e: Quasi-rent is a temporary short-run return to fixed specialized inputs (like specialized machinery) that disappears in the long run.

qs.q: A business enterprise owned, financed, and managed by a single individual who bears all operational risks is a
qs.e: A sole proprietorship is a one-person business where the owner exercises full managerial control and assumes all financial risks.

qs.q: An association of two to twenty persons carrying on a business in common with a view to making profit is a
qs.e: Under standard commercial law, a general partnership comprises between 2 and 20 members pooling resources for profit.

qs.q: The financial condition in which a business owner's personal assets can be seized to pay company debts is known as
qs.e: Unlimited liability means the owner's liability is not restricted to invested capital; personal property can be attached to settle business debts.

qs.q: Limited liability protects company shareholders by restricting their maximum potential loss to the
o: total value of company fixed assets
total annual revenue generated by the firm
personal net worth of the board of directors
nominal value of the shares they subscribed for
qs.e: Limited liability ensures that a shareholder loses at most the amount invested or unpaid on their shares.

qs.q: A primary objective of a cooperative society is to
o: maximize financial dividends paid to external investors
promote the economic interest and welfare of its members
monopolize retail trade in urban markets
provide public infrastructure funded by taxation
qs.e: Cooperative societies are member-owned organizations formed to render services and improve member economic welfare.

qs.q: A public limited company (Plc) must have a minimum of how many shareholders at incorporation?
qs.e: Under company law, a public limited company requires a minimum of 7 shareholders and has no upper legal limit on membership.

qs.q: Shares of a public limited company differ from those of a private limited company because Plc shares can be
o: freely sold to the general public on the stock exchange
transferred only with unanimous consent of all directors
purchased exclusively by state government agencies
qs.e: Public limited companies can invite the general public to buy shares, which are freely traded on the stock exchange.

qs.q: State-owned business enterprises established by specific government statutes to provide essential public services are
qs.e: Public corporations (e.g. water boards, postal services) are created by parliamentary acts to provide public utilities.

qs.q: The written legal document governing the internal administration, voting rights, and appointment of directors in a limited company is the
qs.e: Articles of Association set out the internal rules and regulations for managing a company's internal affairs.

qs.q: The document outlining a company's external relationship with the outside world, including its name, registered office, and authorized capital, is the
qs.e: The Memorandum of Association defines the company's constitution, object clause, and external operating boundaries.

qs.q: An official document published by a public limited company inviting members of the public to subscribe for its shares or debentures is a
qs.e: A prospectus provides detailed financial information about a company to guide potential investors.

qs.q: A fixed-interest long-term loan certificate issued by a corporation to borrow funds from investors is a
qs.e: Debentures represent corporate debt capital; debenture holders are creditors receiving fixed interest regardless of profit.

qs.q: Ordinary shares are referred to as equity capital because ordinary shareholders
o: have priority claim on assets during company liquidation
are guaranteed a fixed interest rate every year
bear the ultimate financial risk and receive variable residual dividends
cannot vote at annual general meetings
qs.e: Ordinary shareholders are the real owners who bear business risk, holding voting rights and receiving dividends from remaining profits.

qs.q: Preference shareholders differ from ordinary shareholders because preference shareholders
o: possess full voting power at all board elections
receive a fixed dividend rate and have prior claim on profits
bear all residual business losses during insolvency
qs.e: Preference shares carry a fixed dividend rate paid before any dividend is distributed to ordinary shareholders.

qs.q: A partner whose liability is restricted to the specific capital amount contributed to the business is a
qs.e: A limited partner has limited liability provided there is at least one general partner with unlimited liability.

qs.q: A partner who contributes capital and shares in profits but takes no active part in daily business management is a
qs.e: Sleeping (dormant) partners provide financial capital but do not participate in active day-to-day operations.

qs.q: A retail cooperative society helps its members primarily by
o: extending high-interest commercial loans to foreign corporations
fixing minimum wage rates for industrial factory workers
buying goods in bulk directly from manufacturers to sell at lower prices to members
collecting direct customs duties at sea ports
qs.e: Retail cooperatives eliminate middleman markups by purchasing wholesale and reselling to members at near-cost prices.

qs.q: The transfer of state-owned public corporations to private investors through share sales is known as
qs.e: Privatization sells public state assets to private individuals or corporate investors to improve efficiency.

qs.q: Reorganizing a public enterprise to operate as a profit-making commercial business without government operating subsidies is called
qs.e: Commercialization retains government ownership but requires the enterprise to cover its operating costs and earn profit.

qs.q: Partners A and B share profits in the ratio 3:2. If the net profit for the trading year is 120,000 naira, what is Partner A's share?
qs.e: Total ratio parts = 3 + 2 = 5. Partner A's share = (3 / 5) * 120,000 = 72,000 naira.

qs.q: A company earns net profit of 500,000 naira. After paying 100,000 naira to preference shareholders, the remaining profit is distributed to 200,000 ordinary shares. What is the dividend per ordinary share?
qs.e: Residual profit = 500,000 - 100,000 = 400,000 naira. Dividend per share = 400,000 / 200,000 = 2.00 naira.

qs.q: A 8 percent debenture with a nominal value of 100 naira is currently trading on the stock exchange at 80 naira. What is the effective yield to an investor purchasing at this market price?
qs.e: Fixed annual interest = 8% of 100 = 8 naira. Effective yield = (Interest / Market Price) * 100 = (8 / 80) * 100 = 10.0%.

qs.q: A company issues 600,000 shares of 5 naira nominal value each. If directors call up 4 naira per share, what is the total uncalled capital?
qs.e: Uncalled amount per share = 5 - 4 = 1 naira. Total uncalled capital = 600,000 shares * 1 naira = 600,000 naira.

qs.q: A general partnership is legally dissolved upon the occurrence of
o: death or bankruptcy of any general partner
a temporary illness of an employee
a reduction in annual sales volume
an increase in federal corporate tax rates
qs.e: Unlike incorporated companies, a general partnership lacks perpetual succession; death or bankruptcy of a general partner dissolves the partnership.

qs.q: Perpetual succession is an important legal feature of an incorporated company, meaning that the company
o: is granted a monopoly by parliament for a hundred years
never pays interest on borrowed debenture capital
continues to exist legally regardless of changes in shareholder membership or death
is exempt from annual auditing by certified accountants
qs.e: Incorporation creates a separate legal entity distinct from its owners, allowing the company to endure indefinitely despite shareholder deaths.

qs.q: A major limitation of state-owned public corporations in developing nations is
o: excessive competition from foreign multinational monopolies
frequent political interference and operational inefficiency
inability to borrow capital from domestic commercial banks
strict regulation by international trade agencies
qs.e: Public corporations often suffer from political appointments, bureaucratic delays, corruption, and lack of profit incentive.

qs.q: A business alliance where two or more independent corporate entities pool resources to undertake a specific commercial project while maintaining separate legal identities is a
qs.e: A joint venture is a cooperative commercial agreement formed to execute a specific project or business activity.

qs.q: A company that owns more than 50 percent of the voting equity shares of another corporate enterprise is described as the
qs.e: A holding company owns controlling interest (over 50%) in another firm, known as its subsidiary.

qs.q: The legal document issued by the Registrar of Companies certifying that a company is legally incorporated as a body corporate is the
qs.e: The Certificate of Incorporation brings the company into existence as a distinct legal personality.

qs.q: A public limited company cannot commence business operations or exercise borrowing powers until it receives a
qs.e: Unlike private companies, a public limited company requires a Certificate of Trading before commencing business operations.

qs.q: A financial cooperative that pools members' regular savings to extend low-interest loans to its members is a
qs.e: Thrift and credit cooperatives encourage saving and provide affordable credit facilities to members.

qs.q: Multinational Corporations (MNCs) contribute positively to host developing economies primarily through
o: repatriation of all gross profits to parent country headquarters
eliminating domestic taxation on corporate income
foreign direct investment, technology transfer, and employment creation
qs.e: MNCs inject foreign capital, introduce advanced technology, create local employment, and expand industrial capacity.

qs.q: Indigenization policies implemented by governments aim to
o: nationalize all private agricultural farmland without compensation
transfer ownership and control of foreign enterprises to domestic citizens
prohibit domestic exports of crude oil and mineral resources
grant foreign firms 100 percent tax exemption status
qs.e: Indigenization laws ensure local participation and equity ownership in foreign-dominated sectors.

qs.q: The principal-agent problem in modern public limited companies arises because of the separation between
o: debt capital holders and preference shareholders
qs.e: Shareholders (principals) delegate management to directors (agents), who may pursue self-interest rather than shareholder wealth maximization.

qs.q: Partners A and B contribute 200,000 naira and 100,000 naira capital. Partnership deed allows 10 percent interest on capital and equal profit sharing. If net profit is 90,000 naira, Partner A receives
qs.e: Interest on capital: A = 10% of 200k = 20,000; B = 10% of 100k = 10,000. Total interest = 30,000 naira. Residual profit = 90,000 - 30,000 = 60,000 naira shared equally (30,000 each). Partner A total = 20,000 + 30,000 = 50,000 naira.

qs.q: A public limited company has 10 million ordinary shares listed on the stock exchange at a current market price of 25 naira per share. What is the company's total market capitalization?
qs.e: Market Capitalization = Total Issued Shares * Current Market Price = 10,000,000 * 25 = 250,000,000 naira.

qs.q: A corporation reports net earnings of 4 million naira available to 2 million ordinary shares. If market price per share is 20 naira, what is the Price-Earnings (P/E) ratio?
qs.e: Earnings Per Share (EPS) = Net Earnings / Number of Shares = 4,000,000 / 2,000,000 = 2 naira. P/E ratio = Market Price / EPS = 20 / 2 = 10.0.

qs.q: A company has 100,000 cumulative preference shares of 10 naira par value carrying a 5 percent dividend. If dividends were unpaid for 2 past years, what total preference dividend must be paid in Year 3 before ordinary dividends?
qs.e: Annual preference dividend = 5% of (100,000 * 10) = 5% of 1,000,000 = 50,000 naira per year. Cumulative arrears for 2 past years + current year = 3 * 50,000 = 150,000 naira.

qs.q: Corporate governance mechanisms in public limited companies aim to protect shareholder wealth through
o: independent board oversight, transparent financial auditing, and executive accountability
prohibiting institutional investors from voting at annual general meetings
fixing retail product prices above average operating costs
guaranteeing minimum annual dividend payments regardless of profit
qs.e: Corporate governance ensures that corporate managers act transparently in the long-term interest of shareholders.

qs.q: A horizontal merger occurs when two commercial enterprises combine operations if they are engaged in
o: different successive stages of the same industrial production chain
completely unrelated product markets and industrial sectors
the same stage of production within the same industry
importing and exporting agricultural raw materials
qs.e: Horizontal integration involves merging firms producing similar products at the same production stage to expand market share.

qs.q: A vertical backward merger takes place when a manufacturing company merges with its supplier of
qs.e: Vertical backward integration merges a firm with a supplier located at an earlier stage of the supply chain.

qs.q: A conglomerate merger is formed by the combination of business enterprises operating in
o: completely unrelated product lines and market sectors
successive processing stages of petroleum refining
qs.e: Conglomerate mergers combine firms in unrelated industries to diversify business risk.

qs.q: Corporate social responsibility (CSR) represents an enterprise's voluntary commitment to
o: address social and environmental impacts of its operations while contributing to community development
evade federal corporate tax obligations through offshore transfers
monopolize regional raw material supply chains
maximize short-run dividend payouts by reducing employee wage rates
qs.e: CSR emphasizes ethical conduct, environmental sustainability, and community welfare alongside profitability.

qs.q: A business franchise arrangement grants a franchisee the contractual right to operate using the franchisor's
o: factory machinery without paying any initial purchase price or fees
board of directors as legal general partners
brand name, trade mark, and proven business operating system in exchange for royalties
tax identification number for corporate exemption
qs.e: Franchising allows a business owner to replicate a established business concept in return for initial fees and ongoing royalties.

qs.q: Venture capital funds provide financial investment to young, high-risk start-up enterprises primarily in exchange for
o: guaranteed fixed interest payments backed by real estate collateral
equity ownership stakes and potential capital gains upon growth
qs.e: Venture capitalists provide high-risk equity capital to innovative early-stage firms expecting high equity returns.

qs.q: A corporation's capital structure consists of 60 percent equity (costing 15 percent) and 40 percent debt (costing 10 percent after tax). Calculate the Weighted Average Cost of Capital (WACC).
qs.e: WACC = (Weight of Equity * Cost of Equity) + (Weight of Debt * Cost of Debt) = (0.60 * 15%) + (0.40 * 10%) = 9.0% + 4.0% = 13.0%.

qs.q: A company offers a 1-for-4 rights issue at 20 naira per share when existing market price is 30 naira. Calculate the theoretical ex-rights price per share.
qs.e: Holder of 4 shares (value = 4 * 30 = 120 naira) buys 1 new share at 20 naira. Total 5 shares worth 120 + 20 = 140 naira. Theoretical ex-rights price = 140 / 5 = 28.00 naira.

qs.q: The landmark legal principle established in Salomon v. Salomon confirms that an incorporated company
o: possesses an independent legal personality separate from its individual shareholders and directors
dissolves automatically whenever its majority shareholder dies
is personally liable for the private debts of its board members
cannot enter into legal contracts in its own corporate name
qs.e: Salomon v Salomon established the separate corporate entity doctrine: a company is a distinct legal person.

qs.q: According to the trade-off theory of capital structure, an optimal debt-equity ratio balances the tax shield benefit of debt against the
o: dividend payout ratio demanded by preference shareholders
present value of financial distress and bankruptcy costs
level of ad valorem customs tariffs
qs.e: Trade-off theory balances the tax deductibility of interest against rising financial distress costs of heavy debt.

qs.q: Under a Build-Own-Operate-Transfer (BOOT) public-private partnership contract, a private company builds infrastructure, operates it to recover costs, and then
o: sells the asset to foreign multinational corporations on the stock exchange
liquidates the physical facility for scrap
converts the facility into a private military base
transfers ownership back to the state government at the end of the concession period
qs.e: BOOT contracts allow private capital to fund public infrastructure, transferring the facility back to government after a fixed operational term.

qs.q: Which branch of economics studies the economy as a whole, focusing on total national output, unemployment, and inflation?
qs.e: Macroeconomics is the study of aggregate economic behavior and national economic indicators like GDP, inflation, and employment.

qs.q: What name is given to the economic system in which both private enterprises and government participate in resource allocation?
qs.e: A mixed economy combines features of free market market mechanism and central government intervention.

qs.q: Which type of elasticity measures the responsiveness of quantity demanded of a good to a change in consumer income?
qs.e: Income elasticity of demand measures percentage change in quantity demanded divided by percentage change in consumer income.

qs.q: What is the primary motive for holding money according to Keynesian theory when money is kept for day-to-day routine expenditures?
qs.e: The transactions motive refers to holding cash to meet daily personal and business transactions.

qs.q: Which financial institution holds the exclusive right to issue legal tender currency notes and coins in a nation?
qs.e: The Central Bank has the sole legal authority and monopoly of currency note and coin issuance.

qs.q: Which canon or principle of taxation states that the amount of tax payable and the time of payment should be clear and plain to the taxpayer?
qs.e: Adam Smith's canon of certainty stipulates that the tax amount, payment method, and due date must be clear and non-arbitrary.

qs.q: A market structure characterized by a single seller offering a product with no close substitutes is known as a
qs.e: A monopoly exists when a single producer or supplier controls the entire market supply of a product with no close substitutes.

qs.q: If the price of petrol increases from N200 to N250 per litre and quantity demanded falls from 500 litres to 400 litres, what is the price elasticity of demand?
