qs.q: Which colonial constitution first formally divided Nigeria into three administrative regions: North, West, and East?
qs.e: The Richards Constitution introduced regionalism, establishing Regional Houses of Assembly for North, West, and East.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: Regional autonomy was formally established in Nigeria, creating a true federal system under the
qs.e: The Lyttelton Constitution established a federal structure with autonomous regions and specific legislative lists.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: The first political party formed in Nigeria following the introduction of the elective principle was the
o: National Council of Nigeria and the Cameroons
qs.e: Herbert Macaulay founded the NNDP to contest elective seats created in Lagos under the Clifford Constitution.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: Which colonial constitution provided for wide public consultation from village level to national level before its drafting?
qs.e: The Macpherson Constitution was drafted after extensive village, district, provincial, and regional conferences.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: Under the Lyttelton Constitution, the office of Regional Premier was created to head the executive in the
qs.e: The Lyttelton Constitution introduced regional premiers to lead regional executive councils.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: Which colonial constitution was criticized for excluding Northern Nigeria from the central Legislative Council?
qs.e: The Clifford Constitution created a Legislative Council whose jurisdiction was limited to Southern Nigeria.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: A major defect of the Richards Constitution was that it was introduced without prior consultation with the
o: British House of Commons in London
qs.e: Richards drafted and imposed his constitution without consulting Nigerian nationalist figures or public assemblies.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: Under the Macpherson Constitution, members of the central House of Representatives were elected through
o: indirect election from the Regional Houses of Assembly
direct adult suffrage across all federal constituencies
appointment by foreign commercial trading companies
qs.e: Regional Houses acted as electoral colleges to choose members for the central House of Representatives.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: The Lyttelton Constitution divided legislative powers between the federal government and regional governments using
o: Exclusive, Concurrent, and Residual legislative lists
unilateral executive decrees issued by regional governors
customary law codes administered by native courts
decrees enacted by the Privy Council
qs.e: Federal division of powers was defined through Exclusive (federal), Concurrent (shared), and Residual (regional) lists.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: Which constitutional arrangement under the Richards Constitution allowed non-official members to outnumber official British members in council?
o: Unofficial majority in the Legislative Council
Universal adult suffrage across all provinces
Creation of a supreme judicial court
qs.e: The Richards Constitution established an unofficial majority in the central Legislative Council, though members were largely nominated.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: The Willink Commission was appointed by the British colonial government primarily to investigate
o: fears of minority ethnic groups and suggest safeguards
financial corruption in native authority treasuries
boundary disputes between French and British colonies
qs.e: The Willink Commission investigated minority fears of domination by major ethnic groups prior to independence.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: Which colonial constitution established the Council of Ministers as the principal instrument of policy for the central government?
qs.e: The Macpherson Constitution created a Council of Ministers comprising British officials and Nigerian regional ministers.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: Under the Lyttelton Constitution, the Federal Capital Territory was established at
qs.e: Lagos was carved out of the Western Region to serve as a neutral Federal Capital Territory.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: The Ibadan Constitutional Conference was convened to review and harmonize proposals for the drafting of the
qs.e: The Ibadan Conference was the culmination of nationwide consultations that shaped the Macpherson Constitution.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: Which nationalist leader founded the Nigerian National Democratic Party (NNDP) to contest elections under the Clifford Constitution?
qs.e: Herbert Macaulay, known as the father of Nigerian nationalism, founded the NNDP.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: A key reason why the Macpherson Constitution collapsed within a few years of operation was the
o: total refusal of traditional emirs to participate in regional councils
crisis over the motion for self-government and central executive friction
outbreak of world war in European territories
imposition of military rule by British forces
qs.e: The 1953 self-government motion caused severe conflict between Northern and Southern politicians, collapsing the constitution.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: Under the Lyttelton Constitution, residual legislative powers were assigned exclusively to the
qs.e: Residual powers (matters not listed in Exclusive or Concurrent lists) were reserved for regional governments.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: Which legislative list under the Lyttelton Constitution contained subjects on which both federal and regional legislatures could pass laws?
qs.e: The Concurrent List included subjects (like higher education, industrial development) open to both levels, with federal law prevailing in conflict.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: The introduction of the Richards Constitution marked an important turning point in Nigerian political history because it
o: granted full national independence to Nigeria immediately
integrated Northern and Southern Nigeria into a single legislative framework for the first time
abolished all traditional chieftaincy institutions across the country
established a single-party socialist political state
qs.e: For the first time since amalgamation, representatives from Northern and Southern Nigeria sat in the same Legislative Council.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: Under the Clifford Constitution, the elective principle granted franchise exclusively to male adults in Lagos and Calabar who met a minimum
qs.e: Franchise was restricted to adult males residing in Lagos or Calabar with a gross annual income of at least 100 pounds sterling.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: The London Constitutional Conference resulted in agreements that led directly to the adoption of the
qs.e: The Constitutional Conferences agreed on replacing the unstable Macpherson structure with a federal system under Lyttelton.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: Which factor led to severe political friction under the Macpherson Constitution between regional leaders and central ministers?
o: Regional ministers lacked the power to collect local market taxes
Central ministers were accountable to regional party leaders rather than to the central legislature
British governors surrendered all veto powers to traditional rulers
Federal supreme court judges were appointed by regional premiers
qs.e: Ministers in the central council owed primary political loyalty to their regional parties, causing executive incohesion.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: The creation of the House of Chiefs in Northern and Western Regions under colonial constitutions was intended to give representation to
qs.e: Regional Houses of Chiefs provided a formal legislative chamber for traditional rulers alongside elected assemblies.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: Under the Lyttelton Constitution, if a regional law conflicted with a federal law on a matter on the Concurrent List, the
o: regional law automatically invalidated the federal statute
matter was referred to the Native Authority court for final decision
federal law prevailed to the extent of the inconsistency
Governor-General was required to dissolve parliament immediately
qs.e: Federal paramountcy applied in concurrent matters, ensuring federal law prevailed over conflicting regional law.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: The Kano Riots broke out primarily as a result of political tension following the
o: announcement of tax increases under the Richards Constitution
creation of the Federal Capital Territory at Lagos
booing of Northern delegates in Lagos over the self-government motion
imposition of Warrant Chiefs in Northern provinces
qs.e: Northern delegates were mocked in Lagos after opposing the self-government motion, sparking retaliatory riots in Kano.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: Under the Richards Constitution, the Regional Houses of Assembly functioned primarily as
o: sovereign parliaments with full power to enact regional constitutions
supreme judicial appeal courts for native law cases
electoral colleges and consultative bodies with limited legislative powers
executive boards managing foreign trade monopolies
qs.e: Regional assemblies under Richards acted largely as advisory bodies and electoral colleges to select central representatives.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: Which constitutional development conference was held to address the political crisis following the breakdown of the Macpherson Constitution?
qs.e: The London Conference brought Nigerian leaders together to negotiate a federal constitutional framework.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: The Willink Commission recommended that minority fears should be addressed primarily through
o: creating thirty new states immediately before independence
expelling majority ethnic populations from regional capitals
entrenching fundamental human rights and accelerating development in minority areas
abolishing all regional governments in favor of unitary rule
qs.e: The Willink Commission declined to create new states, recommending instead a bill of rights and special development boards.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: Under the Lyttelton Constitution, the judiciary was regionalized through the establishment of regional
o: Privy Council branches in each regional capital
High Courts alongside a Federal Supreme Court
qs.e: The judiciary was structured into Regional High Courts with a Federal Supreme Court acting as national appellate court.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: The Nigerian Youth Movement (NYM) emerged as a major nationalist organization that challenged the NNDP by advocating
o: permanent British colonial rule over Northern provinces
complete separation of Western Nigeria from the federation
genuine national unity and self-government for all Nigeria
adoption of French colonial administrative methods
qs.e: NYM was the first truly national movement bringing together young educated elites across ethnic divides.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: The office of Governor-General of Nigeria was established under the Lyttelton Constitution to serve as head of the
qs.e: The Governor-General headed the federal executive, while regional governors headed regional executive councils.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: Which colonial constitution first introduced a ministerial system of government at both central and regional levels?
qs.e: The Macpherson Constitution introduced ministers, though full portfolio responsibility was consolidated under Lyttelton.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: A key feature of the Clifford Constitution was that the Legislative Council consisted of official members, nominated unofficial members, and
o: thirty appointed emirs from Northern provinces
qs.e: The Clifford Council included four elected seats: three for Lagos and one for Calabar.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: The failure of the Richards Constitution to satisfy nationalist demands was largely due to its failure to grant
o: financial salaries to British colonial civil servants
customs tax exemption to foreign European shipping companies
real executive power or full elective representation to Nigerians
land ownership titles to traditional native authorities
qs.e: Nationalists rejected Richards Constitution because power remained vested in the Governor and nominated officials.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: Under the Lyttelton Constitution, civil service commissions were regionalized, meaning that each region gained control over the
o: command and deployment of regional military units
printing and issuance of regional legal tender currency
recruitment, promotion, and discipline of its civil servants
appointment of foreign ambassadors to international organizations
qs.e: Regionalization created separate regional civil services alongside the federal civil service.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: The self-government motion introduced in the House of Representatives demanded self-government for Nigeria in
o: the year nineteen hundred and fifty-six
qs.e: Anthony Enahoro moved the historic motion demanding self-government, which caused Northern-Southern political divergence.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: Which region attained internal self-government first alongside the Western Region?
qs.e: Western and Eastern Regions attained internal self-government, while Northern Region attained it later.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: The Lyttelton Constitution strengthened Nigerian federalism by making regional governments
o: completely subordinate to municipal local government councils
financially dependent on foreign loans from European commercial banks
subject to direct administration by traditional native treasuries
independent of the central government within their spheres of jurisdiction
qs.e: Regions gained autonomous legislative and executive powers within their constitutional jurisdictions.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: The minor status of Northern Nigeria in the early central Legislative Council established under the Clifford Constitution was due to the fact that Northern provinces were governed by the Governor through
o: executive decrees of the French Ministry of Colonies
judicial orders of the Federal Supreme Court
decisions of the Lagos Municipal Council
qs.e: Northern Nigeria was administered directly by executive proclamations of the Governor without Legislative Council oversight.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: The fundamental change brought about by the Constitutional Conference was the agreement to transform Nigeria from a quasi-federation into a
o: centralized unitary republic governed from London
confederation of totally independent sovereign nations
monarchical empire under a traditional paramount king
fully-fledged federal system with autonomous regions
qs.e: The conferences moved Nigeria from Macpherson's semi-unitary structure to Lyttelton's true federalism.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: Under the Macpherson Constitution, the central legislature was known as the
qs.e: The Macpherson Constitution renamed the central body the House of Representatives.

qs.q: A primary reason for the rapid growth of regional political parties in the 1950s was the regional structure established by the
qs.e: Regional legislative houses encouraged parties (AG in West, NPC in North, NCNC in East) to build regional bases.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: The Willink Commission recommended the entrenchment of fundamental human rights in the independence constitution to protect
o: foreign commercial companies against tax assessments
British colonial officers against recall by parliament
traditional chiefs against local council audits
minorities against potential abuse of power by regional majorities
qs.e: A bill of rights was seen as the most effective structural safeguard for ethnic minorities.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: Under the Lyttelton Constitution, revenue allocation was based predominantly on the principle of
qs.e: The Lyttelton Constitution prioritized derivation, giving regions revenue generated directly within their boundaries.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: The evolution of colonial constitutions in Nigeria demonstrated a progressive shift from
o: republican presidential governance to absolute monarchy
military dictatorship to direct French territorial assimilation
confederal sovereignty to municipal town council administration
unitary colonial autocracy to regional federalism and self-governance
qs.e: Constitutional development moved from autocratic Governor rule toward federal self-government.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: The structural fragility of the Macpherson Constitution stemmed from its hybrid nature, combining elements of
o: presidential executive power with absolute traditional monarchy
French assimilation laws with British military martial rule
direct democracy with hereditary aristocratic succession
unitary centralization with regional legislative structures
qs.e: It attempted to operate central executive power over regions that held distinct regional legislatures, causing deadlocks.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: The significance of the elective principle introduced under the Clifford Constitution was that it
o: granted universal voting rights to all rural peasant farmers immediately
abolished all foreign commercial trade monopolies across West Africa
transferred executive authority from the Governor to an elected Prime Minister
stimulated political awareness and paved the way for modern party formation in Nigeria
qs.e: Even with limited franchise, elective seats catalyzed press activity and party politics.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: Under the regional constitutions preceding independence, the Head of Executive in each region was the
o: Chief Justice of the Federal Supreme Court
Secretary of State for the Colonies in London
President of the Lagos Municipal Council
Regional Governor acting on the advice of the Premier
qs.e: The Regional Governor held formal executive authority, acting on the advice of the elected Premier.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: The Constitutional Conferences established the principle that national independence for Nigeria would be achieved within a framework of
o: a centralized unitary state controlled by a single party
a loose economic alliance without a central federal government
a military junta ruled by traditional native authorities
a federal republic respecting regional diversity
qs.e: Delegates agreed that federalism was the only viable structure for Nigeria's multi-ethnic nation state.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: Under the Independence Constitution of Nigeria, the formal Head of State was the
o: British Monarch represented by the Governor-General
qs.e: At independence, Nigeria retained the British monarch as constitutional Head of State, represented locally by a Governor-General.

qs.q: Which post-independence constitution transformed Nigeria into a republic and severed constitutional ties with the British Crown?
qs.e: The Republican Constitution established an indigenous Republic, replacing the Governor-General with an ceremonial President.

qs.q: The presidential system of government was first introduced in Nigeria under the
qs.e: The Second Republic Constitution replaced the Westminster parliamentary system with an executive presidential system.

qs.q: Under the Independence Constitution, executive government functions were headed by the
qs.e: The Prime Minister served as the head of government under the parliamentary structure at independence.

qs.q: Which constitution established the Supreme Court of Nigeria as the final court of appeal, replacing the Privy Council?
qs.e: The Republican Constitution abolished appeals to the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council in London.

qs.q: Under the Second Republic Constitution, the President exercised executive authority as both
o: Head of State and Head of Government
Head of State and Chief Justice
Speaker of the House and Senate President
qs.e: An executive presidential system combines the roles of Head of State and Head of Government in a single elected individual.

qs.q: The Midwestern Region was created through constitutional amendment during the tenure of the
qs.e: The Midwestern Region was carved out of the Western Region under the First Republic.

qs.q: A major difference between the Independence Constitution and the Republican Constitution was that under the Republican Constitution,
o: the President was elected by Nigerian parliamentarians rather than appointed by the British monarch
the Prime Minister was appointed directly by the British Privy Council
all regional governments were dissolved into a unitary state
military officers were appointed into the federal cabinet
qs.e: Under the Republican Constitution, the ceremonial President was chosen by a joint session of the Senate and House of Representatives.

qs.q: Under the Second Republic Constitution, the Federal Character principle was entrenched to ensure that
o: appointments to public offices reflect the geographical and ethnic diversity of Nigeria
only military officers can serve as ministers of state
regional premiers retain supreme veto power over federal laws
a single political party controls all state assemblies
qs.e: Federal Character promotes national unity and guards against ethnic or regional dominance in federal appointments.

qs.q: Which constitutional body was created under the Second Republic Constitution to enforce moral standards and integrity among public officers?
qs.e: The Code of Conduct Bureau and Tribunal were created to prevent corruption and conflict of interest among public officials.

qs.q: Under the Fourth Republic Constitution, the power to ratify treaties signed by the Executive is vested in the
qs.e: International treaties signed by the President must be enacted into law by the National Assembly before taking effect.

qs.q: The First Republic parliamentary system featured a bicameral federal legislature consisting of the
o: Senate and the House of Representatives
House of Chiefs and House of Assembly
Council of State and Executive Cabinet
National Judicial Council and Privy Council
qs.e: Federal parliament consisted of the elected House of Representatives and the nominated Senate.

qs.q: Under the Fourth Republic Constitution, a State House of Assembly consists of members elected to represent
o: state constituencies for a four-year term
qs.e: State legislators represent state constituencies and serve four-year renewable terms.

qs.q: Which post-independence constitution first explicitly incorporated a comprehensive list of Fundamental Human Rights?
qs.e: Following Willink Commission recommendations, the Independence Constitution entrenched a bill of rights.

qs.q: Under the Second Republic Constitution, if the office of the President becomes vacant, executive power assumes automatically to the
o: Speaker of the House of Representatives
qs.e: The Vice-President succeeds to the presidency for the unexpired term upon vacancy.

qs.q: The constitutional process of removing an Executive President or Governor for gross misconduct is termed
qs.e: Impeachment is the legislative procedure used to investigate and remove executive officers for misconduct.

qs.q: Under the Fourth Republic Constitution, legislative powers at the federal level are exercised by the
qs.e: The National Assembly (Senate and House of Representatives) holds federal legislative power.

qs.q: The National Judicial Council (NJC) established under the Fourth Republic Constitution is responsible for
o: enacting criminal laws for state governments
recommending the appointment and discipline of judicial officers
appointing ministers into the federal cabinet
qs.e: The NJC protects judicial independence by overseeing appointments, promotions, and disciplinary measures.

qs.q: Under the First Republic parliamentary system, a vote of no confidence passed by the House of Representatives against the executive resulted in the
o: impeachment of the Supreme Court judges
resignation of the Prime Minister and cabinet
dissolution of all regional traditional councils
qs.e: In a parliamentary system, losing a confidence vote forces the Prime Minister and cabinet to resign.

qs.q: Comparing the First Republic and Second Republic Constitutions, a major structural change in executive power was the transition from
o: a military junta to a colonial governor-general
a collective cabinet headed by a Prime Minister to a single executive President
a unitary central government to a confederal alliance
an absolute monarchy to a zero-party democracy
qs.e: The Second Republic abandoned parliamentary collective responsibility for single executive presidentialism.

qs.q: Under the Fourth Republic Constitution, a bill passed by the National Assembly becomes law when the President grants assent, or when the Assembly overrides a presidential veto by a
o: simple majority vote in the Senate only
two-thirds majority vote in both houses
unanimous vote of all state governors
three-fourths majority in the Supreme Court
qs.e: A two-thirds majority in both the Senate and House of Representatives can override a presidential veto.

qs.q: Which constitutional body advises the President on national economic planning, chieftaincy appointments, and prerogative of mercy?
o: Revenue Mobilization Allocation and Fiscal Commission
qs.e: The Council of State includes former heads of state, chief justices, state governors, and leadership of the National Assembly.

qs.q: The Fundamental Objectives and Directive Principles of State Policy in the Fourth Republic Constitution outline the
o: procedural rules for conducting military court martial trials
social, economic, and political goals of the government
qualifications for traditional chieftaincy title succession
customs tariffs applied to foreign commercial imports
qs.e: Directive principles guide government policy toward social justice, education, economic development, and democracy.

qs.q: Under the Fourth Republic Constitution, subjects listed in the Exclusive Legislative List are reserved solely for legislation by the
qs.e: Only the National Assembly can pass laws on Exclusive List subjects (defence, foreign affairs, currency, banking).

qs.q: The creation of the Revenue Mobilization Allocation and Fiscal Commission (RMAFC) under post-independence constitutions was designed to
o: collect direct personal income taxes from private citizens
audit the accounts of private commercial banks
monitor and review national revenue allocation principles and fiscal formula
manage external trade tariffs at international seaports
qs.e: RMAFC advises on equitable revenue allocation formulas among federal, state, and local governments.

qs.q: Under the Second Republic Constitution, the President required approval from which legislative body for ministerial appointments?
qs.e: Ministerial nominees presented by the President must be screened and confirmed by the Senate.

qs.q: A key reason for adopting the Federal Character principle in post-independence constitutions was to reduce
o: financial expenditure on federal civil service salaries
the number of states in the Nigerian federation
ethnic domination and regional imbalance in national governance
foreign diplomatic representation in European capitals
qs.e: Federal Character aims to ensure equitable distribution of public offices and resources among diverse groups.

qs.q: Under the Fourth Republic Constitution, local government councils derive their constitutional recognition and state revenue allocation through
o: direct foreign aid grants from international organizations
taxation imposed directly by regional traditional rulers
qs.e: The constitution established State Joint Local Government Accounts through which federal allocations flow to local councils.

qs.q: Which post-independence constitutional arrangement provided for a official bicameral legislature at the state level?
qs.e: First Republic regions had bicameral legislatures (House of Assembly and House of Chiefs); later constitutions made state legislatures unicameral.

qs.q: Under the Fourth Republic Constitution, an amendment to alter provisions of the constitution requires a two-thirds majority in the National Assembly and approval by
o: a simple majority of all traditional emirs and chiefs
the Federal Executive Council chaired by the President
at least two-thirds of the State Houses of Assembly
the Supreme Court of Nigeria in full bench session
qs.e: Constitutional amendment requires two-thirds majority in both national houses and endorsement by two-thirds (24 out of 36) state assemblies.

qs.q: The constitutional role of the Attorney-General of the Federation under post-independence constitutions is to serve as the
o: head of the federal civil service commission
presiding judge of the supreme court of appeal
chief law officer of the federal government
chairman of the national electoral commission
qs.e: The Attorney-General is the chief legal officer of the state and principal advisor on legal matters.

qs.q: Under the Fourth Republic Constitution, fundamental human rights provisions can be suspended legally only during a declared
o: state of emergency in accordance with constitutional procedures
qs.e: Rights may be restricted during a formally declared state of emergency approved by the legislature.

qs.q: A major criticism of the Directive Principles of State Policy in the Fourth Republic Constitution is that they are generally
o: binding only on local government councils
qs.e: Chapter II principles are non-justiciable, meaning citizens cannot easily sue government in court to enforce them.

qs.q: The First Republic parliamentary system produced executive instability primarily due to
o: total absence of a written constitutional document
veto exercised by the Federal Judicial Service Commission
coalition friction and lack of a single-party national majority
direct administration of ministries by colonial officers
qs.e: No single party secured a federal majority, leading to fragile coalition governments and intense inter-regional rivalry.

qs.q: Under the executive presidential system of the Fourth Republic, the principle of separation of powers is reflected in the complete independence of the
o: Military Council, Civil Service, and Trade Unions
Federal Cabinet, Regional Chieftaincy, and Local Councils
State Governors, Emirs, and Town Mayors
qs.e: Power is divided among three distinct branches, each exercising distinct constitutional functions and checks.

qs.q: The procedure for altering state boundaries or creating new states under the Fourth Republic Constitution requires
o: a unilateral executive order issued by the President
a decree published by the Federal Civil Service Commission
referendums and two-thirds majority approvals across federal and state legislative houses
an advisory opinion delivered by the Privy Council
qs.e: State creation involves rigorous referendum thresholds and legislative approvals at state and national levels.

qs.q: Under the Fourth Republic Constitution, the tenure of office for an Executive Governor is limited to
o: an indefinite period subject to legislative confidence
a maximum of two four-year terms
a maximum of three six-year terms
qs.e: Governors and Presidents can serve a maximum of two four-year terms (eight years total).

qs.q: Which post-independence constitutional document incorporated the Land Use Act, making land administration subject to state government control?
qs.e: The 1978 Land Use Decree was entrenched in the 1979 Second Republic Constitution, vesting urban land in state governors.

qs.q: In a presidential system, the President cabinet ministers are prohibited from simultaneously holding seats in the
qs.e: To maintain separation of powers, legislators appointed as ministers must resign their legislative seats.

qs.q: The supreme authority of the constitution over all other laws and authorities in Nigeria is expressed through the doctrine of
qs.e: Constitutional supremacy dictates that any law inconsistent with the constitution is null and void to the extent of the inconsistency.

qs.q: Under the Fourth Republic Constitution, the body responsible for conducting federal presidential and legislative elections is the
qs.e: INEC conducts presidential, national assembly, governorship, and state assembly elections.

qs.q: Which constitutional innovation under the Second Republic was aimed at ensuring that a presidentially elected candidate possessed broad national support?
o: Securing unanimous approval from all traditional emirs and chiefs
Obtaining two-thirds majority vote in the Federal Senate
Receiving endorsement from all state civil service unions
Winning a majority of votes plus at least one-quarter of votes in two-thirds of states
qs.e: The spatial spread requirement ensures the President enjoys cross-regional geographic support.

qs.q: The constitutional function of the Federal Civil Service Commission is to manage the
o: enactment of annual federal appropriation budgets
adjudication of disputes between state governors
command of military operations in international peacekeeping
recruitment, appointment, promotion, and discipline of federal civil servants
qs.e: The commission maintains merit and administrative discipline within the federal civil service.

qs.q: Under the Fourth Republic Constitution, the Exclusive Legislative List contains subjects such as
o: primary health care, local markets, and motor parks
agricultural extension, local chieftaincy, and chieftaincy disputes
secondary education, state roads, and local sanitation
defence, foreign affairs, currency, and customs duties
qs.e: Exclusive List subjects are reserved exclusively for the federal legislature.

qs.q: The Code of Conduct Tribunal possesses constitutional jurisdiction to try public officers for
o: breach of code of conduct guidelines and false declaration of assets
qs.e: The tribunal adjudicates cases involving asset non-declaration, illicit enrichment, and corruption by public officials.

qs.q: The fundamental shift from Westminster parliamentary governance to American-style presidential governance in post-independence Nigeria was driven by the desire to avoid
o: military coups organized by lower-ranking armed forces officers
the total abolition of state and local government administrative structures
financial expenditure on presidential election campaign advertising
executive instability and fragile cabinet coalitions inherent in parliamentary systems
qs.e: The constitution drafters sought a unified executive with a direct national mandate to foster stability.

qs.q: The constitutional doctrine of judicial review empowers Nigerian courts to
o: dismiss elected legislators without conducting public investigations
rewrite parliamentary appropriation bills to increase judicial funding
appoint ministers into the federal executive cabinet directly
declare unconstitutional any legislative law or executive action that violates constitutional provisions
qs.e: Judicial review allows courts to nullify laws or executive acts that conflict with the supreme constitution.

qs.q: Under post-independence federal constitutions, fiscal federalism has been a persistent source of controversy primarily because of
o: the total refusal of state governments to accept federal currency
conflicts over whether traditional chiefs should receive foreign pensions
mandates requiring local councils to fund national defence fleets
disagreements over revenue allocation formulas and state control over mineral resources
qs.e: Revenue allocation (derivation vs allocation based on population/need) remains a core federal friction point.

qs.q: The entrenchment of the Federal Character principle in the constitution reflects a institutional attempt to balance
o: military command hierarchies with civilian judicial appointments
private corporate commercial profits with public tax collection
traditional native customary law with international law treaties
meritocracy with equitable regional representation in public institutions
qs.e: Federal Character attempts to balance administrative merit with fair geographic and ethnic distribution.

qs.q: The supreme law of Nigeria dictates that if any statutory law passed by a State House of Assembly is inconsistent with federal legislation on a concurrent subject, the
o: federal law shall be nullified automatically by the state governor
matter shall be referred to the traditional council of chiefs for final resolution
state assembly shall dissolve the federal parliament immediately
state law shall be void to the extent of its inconsistency
qs.e: The doctrine of inconsistency invalidates state laws that conflict with valid federal legislation.

qs.q: A primary reason for adopting a federal system of government in Nigeria is the country's
o: vast geographic area and cultural diversity
desire for a single centralized traditional monarchy
total reliance on foreign administrative guidance
qs.e: Federalism accommodates cultural diversity, multi-ethnicity, and geographical expanse by dividing power.

qs.q: In the Nigerian federation, legislative powers are shared among levels of government using the
o: Exclusive, Concurrent, and Residual legislative lists
Directives published by trade union congresses
Judgments delivered by international maritime courts
qs.e: Constitutional lists allocate legislative competence between federal and state tiers.

qs.q: Subjects on which only the Federal National Assembly can pass laws are contained in the
qs.e: The Exclusive List is reserved solely for federal legislative jurisdiction.

qs.q: Which level of government in Nigeria is assigned responsibility for local markets, motor parks, and chieftaincy affairs under residual powers?
qs.e: Residual matters fall under state jurisdiction, with local matters managed by state and local authorities.

qs.q: The principle of derivation in Nigerian fiscal federalism dictates that a proportion of national revenue generated from natural resources should be allocated to
o: the specific states where the resources are extracted
states with the smallest population figures
landlocked states with no natural resource deposits
qs.e: Derivation returns a percentage of mineral revenue directly to resource-bearing states.

qs.q: Inter-governmental relations in a federal system refer to the political, financial, and administrative interactions between
o: different tiers and units of government within the federation
sovereign foreign nations through diplomatic embassies
private commercial banks and corporate shareholders
qs.e: Inter-governmental relations cover vertical (federal-state-local) and horizontal (state-state) linkages.

qs.q: The total number of constituent states that currently make up the Federal Republic of Nigeria is
qs.e: Nigeria comprises thirty-six states and the Federal Capital Territory, Abuja.

qs.q: Under Nigerian federalism, if a state law conflicts with a federal law on a subject on the Concurrent List, the
o: federal law prevails and the state law becomes void to the extent of the inconsistency
state law automatically overrides the federal statute
matter is submitted to traditional chiefs for binding arbitration
governor can dissolve the federal national assembly
qs.e: Federal supremacy applies in concurrent matters where conflict arises between federal and state law.

qs.q: Which statutory body is constitutionally mandated to review and recommend the revenue allocation formula in Nigeria?
o: Revenue Mobilization Allocation and Fiscal Commission
qs.e: RMAFC monitors revenue generation and proposes allocation formulas to the National Assembly.

qs.q: The major argument in favor of state creation in Nigeria has historically been to
o: bring government closer to the people and protect minority groups from domination
abolish all local government administration across the country
concentrate all financial resources in the federal capital
reduce the number of elected legislative representatives
qs.e: State creation responds to minority fears of ethnic domination and promotes grassroots development.

qs.q: Horizontal inter-governmental relations in Nigeria describe administrative interactions taking place between
o: governments at the same level, such as state-to-state or local-to-local
the federal executive and international diplomatic missions
the supreme court and regional native courts
the federal government and local council authorities
qs.e: Horizontal relations occur between units at the same level of authority (e.g. Governors Forum).

qs.q: Fiscal federalism in Nigeria deals primarily with the allocation of
o: financial resources and taxing powers among federal, state, and local tiers
military officer appointments among regional commands
judicial court cases among high court judges
qs.e: Fiscal federalism regulates resource distribution, tax jurisdiction, and revenue sharing across government tiers.

qs.q: Which body brings together the President, State Governors, and former Heads of State to deliberate on national policy and appointments?
qs.e: The Council of State provides high-level advisory consultation on major national issues.

qs.q: A key factor that led to the historical restructuring of Nigeria into twelve states was the need to
o: merge Nigeria with neighboring French-speaking West African territories
weaken regional secessionist threats and reassure minority ethnic groups
abolish all federal constitutional legislative lists
hand over administration to European trading companies
qs.e: Restructuring into twelve states broke regional hegemony and mobilized minority support for federal unity.

qs.q: Under the Concurrent Legislative List, both the Federal National Assembly and State Houses of Assembly can legislate on
o: defence, foreign policy, and legal tender currency
higher education, industrial development, and electricity generation
local chieftaincy titles and municipal motor parks
diplomatic immunity and foreign trade tariffs
qs.e: Concurrent subjects (education, health, electricity) allow both federal and state legislative involvement.

qs.q: The National Economic Council (NEC) is chaired constitutionally by the
qs.e: The Vice-President chairs NEC, which includes all state governors and the governor of the Central Bank.

qs.q: Which revenue allocation criterion allocates funds based on providing equal baseline funding to every state regardless of size or population?
qs.e: Equality of states divides a portion of the revenue pool equally among all states.

qs.q: The demand for resource control by oil-producing states in Nigeria centers on increasing the percentage of revenue allocated on the basis of
qs.e: Resource control advocates higher derivation returns to communities bearing environmental costs of extraction.

qs.q: State Joint Local Government Accounts were established under the constitution to manage the distribution of revenue to
o: private commercial contractors funding political campaigns
local government councils from federal and state allocations
foreign embassies operating in state capitals
qs.e: Federal statutory allocations to local governments pass through State Joint Local Government Accounts.

qs.q: The evolution of Nigerian federalism has been characterized by progressive centralization of fiscal authority, largely due to long periods of
o: direct parliamentary rule by the British House of Commons
military rule and total central control over oil revenue
judicial orders issued by the International Court of Justice
qs.e: Military command structure centralized financial and political power in the federal center.

qs.q: Which constitutional principle prevents any single ethnic group or state from dominating federal government institutions and agencies?
qs.e: Federal Character guarantees fair representation across states and geopolitical zones in federal appointments.

qs.q: In Nigerian inter-governmental relations, vertical relations refer specifically to interaction between
o: state assemblies and neighboring sovereign foreign nations
higher and lower tiers of government, such as Federal, State, and Local tiers
private commercial banks and local market associations
different departments within the same municipal ministry
qs.e: Vertical relations connect superior and subordinate tiers within the federal hierarchy.

qs.q: A persistent problem facing local government administration in Nigeria despite its recognition as a third tier is its
o: total exclusion from participating in national census counts
financial and administrative dependence on state governments
inability to employ staff possessing basic primary education
prohibition from collecting any form of local market fees
qs.e: State control over Joint Accounts and local elections often compromises local government autonomy.

qs.q: The Willink Commission report declined to recommend the creation of new states before independence because it believed state creation would
o: cause immediate bankruptcy of the British imperial treasury
delay the granting of national independence and create new minority problems
force all traditional rulers to resign from regional councils
trigger military invasion by neighboring West African territories
qs.e: The commission argued state creation would postpone independence and merely generate smaller minority groups.

qs.q: Under Nigerian fiscal federalism, customs duties, value added tax, and corporate income taxes are collected primarily by the
o: Local Government Councils exclusively for municipal development
Traditional Native Authorities in rural provinces
Federal Government and shared through the Federation Account
State Houses of Assembly through regional private banks
qs.e: Major federally collected taxes are pooled into the Federation Account for statutory distribution.

qs.q: The Joint Tax Board (JTB) functions in Nigerian inter-governmental fiscal relations to
o: determine the annual national defence budget
allocate crude oil production quotas to international companies
promote harmony and uniform administration of personal income tax laws across states
adjudicate boundary disputes between state governors
qs.e: JTB coordinates tax administration between federal and state tax authorities.

qs.q: Which historical exercise divided Nigeria into nineteen states, further decentralizing the regional structure?
o: Constitutional review under the Clifford framework
Regional merger under the First Republic parliament
State creation under the Murtala Mohammed regime
qs.e: The Murtala Mohammed administration expanded the federation from twelve to nineteen states.

qs.q: The main challenge posed by the proliferation of states and local governments in Nigeria is the
o: total collapse of foreign trade relations with neighboring West African countries
inability of the federal government to issue national currency notes
high cost of governance and overhead expenditure leaving fewer funds for capital development
complete elimination of all state judicial high courts
qs.e: Creating more states inflates administrative costs, diverting revenue from infrastructure and development.

qs.q: Under the constitution, boundary adjustment between adjacent states in Nigeria requires approval by the National Assembly and the
o: State Houses of Assembly of the affected states
Judicial Committee of the Privy Council
qs.e: Altering state boundaries involves legislative concurrence between the National Assembly and affected state assemblies.

qs.q: The Federation Account is a special account into which is paid all revenues collected by the Government of the Federation, except
o: petroleum profit tax from offshore oil operations
customs import duties collected at international seaports
personal income tax of armed forces personnel and capital territory residents
corporate tax paid by foreign manufacturing companies
qs.e: Certain personal taxes (military, police, FCT) are retained directly by the federal government rather than pooled.

qs.q: Inter-governmental fiscal transfers in Nigeria are intended to address fiscal imbalance, which occurs when lower tiers of government have
o: excess surplus funds deposited in private commercial banks
no legal authority to employ civil service personnel
expenditure responsibilities exceeding their independent revenue-generating capacities
total immunity from federal statutory financial audits
qs.e: Fiscal transfers bridge the gap between state/local spending needs and their limited tax bases.

qs.q: The Nigeria Governors' Forum (NGF) operates as an informal inter-governmental body primarily aimed at
o: enacting federal statutory legislation for the National Assembly
appointing judges into the Federal Supreme Court bench
promoting consensus, policy sharing, and collective bargaining among state executives
commanding regional military forces during national emergencies
qs.e: NGF provides a platform for state governors to align policy positions and negotiate with the federal executive.

qs.q: Which structural mechanism is utilized in Nigeria to resolve boundary disputes and inter-state land conflicts?
qs.e: The National Boundary Commission defines, negotiates, and resolves internal and international boundary issues.

qs.q: The term 'fiscal centralism' in Nigerian federalism describes a situation where
o: state governments collect all taxes and remit small grants to the federal center
local councils hold exclusive authority over national mineral deposits
the federal government controls the vast majority of national revenue generation and collection
private commercial banks determine national tax allocation formulas
qs.e: Centralization concentrates tax collection and resource distribution in federal hands.

qs.q: The major argument against using population as a major revenue allocation criterion in Nigeria is that it
o: prevents state governments from employing civil service staff
forces the federal government to borrow foreign capital
incentivizes the falsification and politicization of national census figures
abolishes all direct taxation in urban commercial cities
qs.e: Tieing revenue directly to population makes demographic censuses fiercely contested political battles.

qs.q: Under Nigerian federalism, residual powers belong to state governments because residual subjects are those
o: reserved exclusively for the President during wartime emergencies
administered directly by foreign diplomatic missions
neither listed in the Exclusive List nor the Concurrent List
governed by international maritime security treaties
qs.e: Residual powers encompass all unlisted matters, defaulting to state authority.

qs.q: The allocation of statutory revenue to local government councils directly from the Federation Account was designed to enhance
o: federal control over municipal market traders
the personal income of state assembly legislators
local government financial autonomy and grassroots development
military recruitment in rural agricultural villages
qs.e: Direct allocation aims to protect local councils from arbitrary financial retention by state governments.

qs.q: Which historical commission recommended the derivation formula that gave fifty percent of mineral revenue to regions of origin prior to centralization?
qs.e: The Raisman Commission (and earlier Chick Commission) shaped pre-independence revenue sharing emphasizing derivation.

qs.q: Inter-governmental conflict between the federal government and state governments in Nigeria is resolved through
o: executive decrees issued by the Federal Character Commission
arbitration by the Council of Traditional Emirs and Chiefs
resolutions passed by municipal local government councils
judicial adjudication by the Supreme Court of Nigeria
qs.e: The Supreme Court possesses original jurisdiction in disputes between the federal government and states.

qs.q: The principle of fiscal equalisation in federal systems is designed to ensure that
o: all states receive exactly equal amounts of foreign commercial investment
every citizen pays identical municipal water rates across the country
all local government councils build identical administrative headquarters
less wealthy states receive financial transfers to provide basic public services comparable to richer states
qs.e: Fiscal equalization reduces inter-regional disparities in public service provision.

qs.q: The Federal Character Commission was established to monitor and enforce compliance with the principles of proportional representation in
o: private commercial bank corporate board selections
judgments delivered in traditional customary courts
elections conducted for trade union leadership positions
public civil service appointments and bureaucratic distribution
qs.e: The commission enforces equitable distribution of federal civil service posts.

qs.q: In a true federal system, coordinate jurisdiction implies that federal and regional governments are
