qs.e: Igbo political organization was stateless and decentralized, relying on lineage heads, title holders, and age grades rather than kings.

qs.q: In the decentralized pre-colonial Igbo political structure, decision-making at the patrilineal lineage level was conducted by the
qs.e: The Umunna comprised male lineage members who assembled to deliberate on family and lineage affairs.

qs.q: In traditional Igbo society, age grades performed vital civic functions including
o: maintaining public security, executing communal labor, and enforcing laws
collecting royal tribute for the emperor
qs.e: Age grades maintained social order, provided public labor, defended communities, and enforced local council directives.

qs.q: In the pre-colonial Benin Kingdom, administrative and political authority was centralized under a divine monarch titled the
qs.e: The Oba of Benin exercised centralized political, judicial, and spiritual authority over the Benin Kingdom.

qs.q: Among the pre-colonial Efik people of Old Calabar, social order, law enforcement, and commercial disputes were regulated by the secret society known as
qs.e: The Ekpe secret society enforced laws, collected debts, and maintained social order in Efik society.

qs.q: The British colonial administrative policy of governing conquered African territories through traditional political institutions was known as
qs.e: Indirect Rule utilized existing indigenous political structures and native rulers to administer colonial territories.

qs.q: A primary economic and practical motivation for Britain's adoption of Indirect Rule in Nigeria was
o: strong desire to promote rapid African independence
severe shortage of British administrative personnel and limited financial funds
total absence of traditional rulers across the territory
military superiority of local traditional armies
qs.e: Shortage of European personnel and funds made Indirect Rule a cheap and feasible administrative solution for Britain.

qs.q: Indirect Rule achieved its greatest administrative success in Northern Nigeria primarily due to the existence of
o: a highly centralized administrative hierarchy and an established taxation system
direct intervention of French colonial troops
qs.e: The centralized Emirate structure, obedient subjects, and pre-existing tax system facilitated Indirect Rule in Northern Nigeria.

qs.q: Indirect Rule encountered severe operational resistance and failure in Eastern Nigeria largely because the region lacked
o: willingness to engage in international commerce
centralized monarchical institutions and formal taxation systems
agricultural land for cash crop cultivation
qs.e: The segmentary, non-centralized nature of Igbo society resisted appointed rulers and direct taxation.

qs.q: To implement Indirect Rule in Eastern Nigeria, British colonial authorities artificially created local rulers known as
qs.e: Warrant Chiefs were appointed by colonial warrants in acephalous communities, leading to widespread popular resentment.

qs.q: The Aba Women's revolt was triggered primarily by rumors regarding the direct imposition of colonial taxation on women by
o: Warrant Chiefs under British colonial administration
qs.e: Protests erupted in Aba and surrounding areas when Warrant Chiefs attempted to count women and livestock for taxation.

qs.q: The French colonial administrative doctrine aimed at transforming African subjects into culturally French citizens was the
qs.e: Assimilation aimed to absorb West Africans into French culture, legal systems, and citizenship.

qs.q: Under French colonial rule in West Africa, full French citizenship rights were initially granted to inhabitants of the Four Communes of
qs.e: Residents of the Four Communes in Senegal held full French political rights and parliamentary representation in Paris.

qs.q: The oppressive French colonial legal code that subjected non-citizen African subjects to summary punishment and forced labor was the
qs.e: The Indigénat legal code allowed French administrators to impose forced labor and summary penalties on non-citizens.

qs.q: France modified its colonial policy from Assimilation to the Policy of Association primarily because Assimilation
o: led to immediate political independence for all colonies
met strong African cultural resistance and proved expensive and impractical
was opposed by British colonial rulers
failed to expand French language instruction
qs.e: Association replaced Assimilation, respecting local customs while maintaining French political dominance.

qs.q: The colonial constitution that introduced the elective principle to Nigeria, permitting elected African representatives in Lagos and Calabar, was the
qs.e: The 1922 Clifford Constitution introduced the elective principle, establishing elected seats in the Legislative Council.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: Under the provisions of the Clifford Constitution, elected members in the Legislative Council represented which two coastal urban centers?
qs.e: Three elected members represented Lagos and one represented Calabar under the Clifford Constitution.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: A primary constitutional goal of the Richards Constitution was to
o: grant immediate independence to regional assemblies
create a presidential system of government
promote national unity and establish a framework covering both Northern and Southern provinces
qs.e: The Richards Constitution sought to integrate Northern and Southern Nigeria into a single legislative framework.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: Regional Houses of Assembly were first introduced in Northern, Western, and Eastern Nigeria under the provisions of the
qs.e: The Richards Constitution introduced regionalism by creating Regional Houses of Assembly in the North, West, and East.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: Nigerian nationalist leaders strongly condemned the Richards Constitution primarily because
o: it abolished the elective principle in Lagos
it was drafted and promulgated without consulting the Nigerian public or political leaders
it merged Nigeria with neighboring Francophone territories
qs.e: Nationalists rejected the Richards Constitution because Governor Richards enacted it without consulting Nigerian representatives.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: The Macpherson Constitution was unique among colonial constitutions because its provisions were formulated following
o: direct negotiations with United Nations representatives
a referendum conducted across West Africa
wide-ranging consultations from village and district levels to regional conferences
an executive decree issued by the British Monarch
qs.e: Sir John Macpherson instituted broad consultations at village, district, provincial, and regional levels before drafting.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: A semi-responsible ministerial system was created at the central level, assigning portfolios to Nigerian ministers, under the
qs.e: The Macpherson Constitution created central and regional executive councils with Nigerian ministers holding limited portfolios.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: The political rift between Northern and Southern legislators over the motion for self-government triggered the severe
o: Kano riots and subsequent constitutional revision conferences in London
dissolution of the national armed forces
qs.e: Tensions over the self-government motion led to the Kano riots and convinced colonial authorities to restructure federal governance.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: The historic parliamentary motion requesting self-government for Nigeria by nineteen fifty-six was moved in the House of Representatives by
qs.e: Chief Anthony Enahoro of the Action Group moved the self-government motion in the Central House of Representatives.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: A fully federal constitutional structure establishing distinct division of powers between central and regional governments was instituted under the
qs.e: The 1954 Lyttelton Constitution established a true federal structure with autonomous regions and specific legislative lists.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: Under the Lyttelton Constitution, regional governments were granted expanded autonomy, including their own premier, civil service, and
qs.e: Regions gained independent regional premiers, regional public civil services, and regional judicial structures under Lyttelton.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: Under the provisions of the Lyttelton Constitution, Lagos was constitutionally established as a
o: capital city of the Western Region
neutral federal capital territory independent of regional control
capital city of the Eastern Region
qs.e: Lagos was separated from the Western Region and made a Federal Capital Territory directly under the federal government.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: The Willink Commission was appointed by the British colonial authority primarily to investigate
o: financial corruption in regional public corporations
boundary disputes between Nigeria and Cameroon
the anxieties of ethnic minority groups regarding majority domination and propose safeguards
administrative reforms in the civil service
qs.e: The Willink Commission was established to inquire into minority fears of majority ethnic domination in the regions.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: The Willink Commission recommended against creating new states for minority groups before independence, advising instead
o: establishing a unitary system of government
inserting fundamental human rights clauses into the constitution
qs.e: The Willink Commission recommended constitutional human rights guarantees and special development boards rather than creating new states.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: The pioneer national political party co-founded by Herbert Macaulay and later led by Nnamdi Azikiwe was the
o: National Council of Nigeria and the Cameroons
qs.e: The NCNC was formed in 1944 as a broad national coalition uniting trade unions, professional associations, and cultural groups.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: The Action Group political party, which developed from the Egbe Omo Oduduwa cultural association, was led by
qs.e: Chief Obafemi Awolowo founded and led the Action Group, which became the dominant political party in Western Nigeria.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: The Northern People's Congress political party evolved directly from a Northern cultural organization named
qs.e: The NPC originated from Jam'iyyar Mutanen Arewa, transforming into a political party to represent Northern interests.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: The Nigerian Youth Movement marked a significant milestone in nationalist history as the first
o: political party to form a regional government
trade union to organize a nationwide strike
genuine multi-ethnic national political organization in Nigeria
qs.e: The NYM was Nigeria's first genuine pan-national political movement, uniting youth across ethnic lines.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: Nationalist press publications, notably the West African Pilot established by Nnamdi Azikiwe, contributed to anti-colonialism by
o: advocating the retention of colonial administration
mobilizing public opinion against colonial policies and fostering political consciousness
qs.e: The nationalist press served as a powerful instrument for criticizing colonial injustice and rallying public anti-colonial sentiment.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: The West African Students' Union established in London by Ladipo Solanke functioned as a key center for
o: training West African nationalist leaders and fostering anti-colonial political activism
qs.e: WASU mobilized West African students abroad, creating an influential forum for anti-colonial ideology and leadership.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: The return of West African soldiers who served in World War II accelerated anti-colonial nationalism because it
o: led to immediate military conquest of European nations
caused total collapse of agricultural cash crop exports
resulted in the abolition of traditional monarchies
demystified European superiority and heightened political rights consciousness
qs.e: Ex-servicemen returned with military skills, world experience, and heightened determination to challenge colonial rule.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: The Manchester Pan-African Congress was pivotal for African anti-colonial movements because it explicitly demanded
o: permanent integration of African colonies with European empires
expansion of colonial forced labor practices
creation of European settler colonies across West Africa
immediate political independence, self-determination, and end to colonial exploitation
qs.e: The 1945 Manchester Congress marked a militant turn, demanding complete independence and self-determination for African colonies.
qs.tp: Constitutional Development in Nigeria - Colonial Era

qs.q: In traditional Igbo political administration, sacred moral legitimacy and authority were represented by the ritual staff named
qs.e: The Ofo staff symbolized truth, justice, lineage authority, and sacred connection to ancestral spirits.

qs.q: In the pre-colonial Hausa-Fulani Emirate, the tax levied specifically on cattle owned by nomadic herdsmen was
qs.e: Jangali was the annual cattle tax collected from pastoral Fulani herdsmen in the Emirate.

qs.q: In the pre-colonial Hausa-Fulani Emirate, the compulsory Islamic tax levied on agricultural produce and wealth for charity was
qs.e: Zakat was the obligatory Islamic tax collected on crops and property for distribution to the needy.

qs.q: In the pre-colonial Oyo Kingdom, royal executive messages and administrative decrees were dispatched across provinces by emissaries known as
qs.e: The Ilaris were royal messengers and tax collectors who carried the Alaafin's executive authority to outlying districts.

qs.q: In the pre-colonial Kanem-Borno Empire, the sovereign ruler who exercised supreme religious and political authority held the title of
qs.e: The Mai was the hereditary monarch and supreme ruler of the Kanem-Borno Empire.

qs.q: In the pre-colonial Kanem-Borno political system, the official Queen Mother who wielded significant political influence was titled the
qs.e: The Magira was the Queen Mother in Kanem-Borno who held an influential official role in state affairs.

qs.q: Under the Independence Constitution, the representative of the British Monarch who functioned as symbolic Head of State in Nigeria was the
qs.e: The 1960 Independence Constitution retained the British Monarch as Head of State, represented locally by the Governor-General.

qs.q: The Republican Constitution severed constitutional links with the British Crown by replacing the Governor-General with a
o: ceremonial President as Head of State
Chief Justice as Head of Government
qs.e: The 1963 Republican Constitution created the office of ceremonial President, ending formal constitutional ties to the British Crown.

qs.q: Under the Republican Constitution, appeals from the Nigerian Federal Supreme Court to the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council in London were
o: abolished, establishing the Supreme Court of Nigeria as the final court of appeal
restricted exclusively to commercial law cases
replaced by appeals to the International Court of Justice
expanded to cover state high court judgments
qs.e: The 1963 Constitution abolished appeals to the Privy Council, making the Supreme Court of Nigeria the supreme judicial authority.

qs.q: The only region established in Nigeria through constitutional democratic procedures prior to military rule was the
qs.e: The Mid-Western Region was created in 1963 through constitutional referendum procedures, excised from the Western Region.

qs.q: An executive presidential system where the elected President functions as both Head of State and Head of Government was first introduced in Nigeria under the
qs.e: The 1979 Second Republic Constitution replaced the parliamentary system with an executive presidential model.

qs.q: Under the Second Republic Constitution, executive presidential appointments of federal ministers and ambassadors required formal confirmation by the
qs.e: The Senate was vested with constitutional power to screen and confirm presidential nominees for ministerial and diplomatic posts.

qs.q: The constitutional body established to enforce ethical standards, asset declarations, and curb corruption among public officers is the
qs.e: The Code of Conduct Bureau enforces transparency, asset declaration, and code of conduct compliance for public officers.

qs.q: The inaugural state creation exercise in Nigeria that restructured the four regions into twelve federal states was executed by the military regime of
qs.e: General Yakubu Gowon created twelve states on May twenty-seven to restructure the federation and defuse regional tensions.

qs.q: Restructuring Nigeria from twelve states into nineteen states, while establishing the Federal Capital Territory at Abuja, was enacted under the military administration of
qs.e: General Murtala Muhammed's regime created nineteen states and established Abuja as the new Federal Capital Territory.

qs.q: The revenue allocation principle assigning a specific percentage of federally collected revenue back to the state or region producing the resource is
qs.e: The derivation principle allocates a proportion of natural resource revenue directly to the region or state of origin.

qs.q: The revenue allocation principle that distributes a portion of the Federation Account equally among all states regardless of size or revenue capacity is
qs.e: Equality of states ensures that every state receives an equal share from a designated percentage of the central revenue pool.

qs.q: In Nigerian federalism, statutory allocations from the Federation Account destined for local government councils are disbursed through the
o: Revenue Mobilization Allocation and Fiscal Commission
qs.e: Section 162 of the constitution mandates that federal funds for local councils pass through the State Joint Local Government Account.

qs.q: The controversial military decree that abolished Nigeria's federal structure and introduced a centralized unitary system was
qs.e: Promulgated by General Aguiyi-Ironsi, Decree 34 abolished regions and established a unified civil service, sparking major backlash.
qs.tp: Military Rule in Nigeria and Political Transitions

qs.q: Under military administration in Nigeria, legislative enactments issued at the central national level were promulgated as
qs.e: Military regimes rule by executive power, issuing legislative laws at the federal level termed decrees.
qs.tp: Military Rule in Nigeria and Political Transitions

qs.q: Laws promulgated by state military governors during military regimes in Nigeria were officially classified as
qs.e: Military governors at the state level enacted state laws styled as edicts.
qs.tp: Military Rule in Nigeria and Political Transitions

qs.q: The supreme legislative and executive decision-making body during military governance in Nigeria was variously styled the
o: Supreme Military Council or Armed Forces Ruling Council
qs.e: The Supreme Military Council (later Armed Forces Ruling Council or Provisional Ruling Council) was the highest decision-making military organ.
qs.tp: Military Rule in Nigeria and Political Transitions

qs.q: Upon seizing political power, military regimes in Nigeria customarily suspend constitutional provisions governing
o: fundamental human rights in their entirety
legislative assemblies and political party activities
qs.e: Military coups suspend elected legislatures, ban political party activities, and rule through military decrees.
qs.tp: Military Rule in Nigeria and Political Transitions

qs.q: The transition program that successfully returned Nigeria to civilian democratic government in nineteen seventy-nine was completed under the military leadership of
qs.e: General Olusegun Obasanjo successfully handed over power to elected President Shehu Shagari on October one.
qs.tp: Military Rule in Nigeria and Political Transitions

qs.q: The civil service doctrine asserting that career public servants remain in office despite changes in political leadership is termed
qs.e: Permanence guarantees civil servants tenure security, ensuring institutional continuity across changing political administrations.

qs.q: The doctrine of civil service anonymity requires that public administrative officers must
o: withhold their true names from official government correspondence
work behind the scenes while political ministers take responsibility for policy outcomes
refuse to testify before legislative committees
refrain from signing official administrative documents
qs.e: Anonymity shields civil servants from public praise or blame, keeping accountability on elected political heads.

qs.q: The executive body charged with responsibility for recruiting, promoting, and disciplining career civil servants is the
qs.e: The Civil Service Commission oversees recruitment, promotion, discipline, and merit standards within the civil service.

qs.q: The major public service reform commission that harmonized unified salary structures and recommended modern management techniques in Nigeria was the
qs.e: The 1972-1974 Chief Jerome Udoji Commission introduced unified salary grading and modern management practices.

qs.q: The civil service reform that designated political ministers as chief executive and accounting officers of their ministries was the
qs.e: The 1988 Dotun Philips reform made ministers accounting officers and altered civil service designations to directors.

qs.q: A statutory enterprise established by an act of parliament to deliver essential utility services or commercial operations for public benefit is a
qs.e: Public corporations are semi-autonomous statutory bodies created by law to provide commercial or essential public services.

qs.q: The governing board appointed by government to provide overall policy direction and operational oversight for a public corporation is the
qs.e: The Board of Directors provides strategic policy guidelines and oversees executive management in public corporations.

qs.q: Legislative control over public corporations is exercised primarily through
o: scrutinizing annual financial reports, auditing accounts, and approving budget allocations
qs.e: Parliament holds public corporations accountable by reviewing annual financial audits, reports, and budgetary allocations.

qs.q: The policy of selling or transferring state-owned public corporations to private investors and enterprise management is
qs.e: Privatization transfers ownership, control, and management of state assets from the public sector to private investors.

qs.q: Restructuring state-owned enterprises to operate as self-sustaining, profit-making commercial entities without selling public ownership is
qs.e: Commercialization requires public enterprises to operate efficiently for profit without divesting state shareholding.

qs.q: The legislative policy implemented to transfer ownership and equity control of foreign-owned commercial firms to indigenous citizens is
qs.e: Indigenization policies, such as the Nigerian Enterprises Promotion Acts, reserved economic sectors for Nigerian citizens.

qs.q: The landmark reform that established local government administration across Nigeria as a uniform, distinct third tier of government was the
qs.e: The 1976 Reform introduced a uniform local government system with defined functions and statutory funding as a third tier.

qs.q: Statutory responsibilities constitutionally assigned to local government councils in Nigeria include the
o: establishment and maintenance of markets, motor parks, and public conveniences
qs.e: Fourth Schedule functions of local councils include managing markets, motor parks, slaughter houses, and local roads.

qs.q: Internal revenue generated directly by local government councils includes proceeds from
o: tenement rates, market stall fees, and motor park levies
personal income taxes of military personnel
qs.e: Local councils raise internal revenue through property tenement rates, market fees, licensing, and motor park charges.

qs.q: In Nigerian local government administration, the executive political head of the local government council is the
qs.e: The elected Local Government Chairman serves as chief executive officer directing local council administration.

qs.q: The independent statutory agency constitutionally mandated to organize, conduct, and supervise national and state elections in Nigeria is the
qs.e: INEC is the constitutional body responsible for organizing presidential, parliamentary, and governorship elections.

qs.q: The constitutional mandate requiring fair and equitable representation of all states and ethnic diversity in public appointments is the
qs.e: The Federal Character Principle ensures equitable distribution of government posts to promote national unity and prevent dominance.

qs.q: The constitutional body established to enforce equitable distribution of public appointments and social infrastructure across all states is the
qs.e: The Federal Character Commission enforces equitable sharing of bureaucratic, economic, and educational opportunities among federating units.

qs.q: The constitutional body responsible for reviewing revenue allocation formulas and fixing salaries for political office holders is the
o: Revenue Mobilization Allocation and Fiscal Commission
qs.e: RMAFC monitors revenue accruals, recommends revenue allocation formulas, and determines remuneration for political office holders.

qs.q: The constitutional commission mandated to conduct national demographic censuses and maintain continuous vital statistics registers in Nigeria is the
qs.e: The National Population Commission conducts national censuses and registers births, deaths, and demographic data.

qs.q: In contemporary Nigerian local government structures, traditional rulers function primarily as
o: executive chairmen of local government councils
judicial heads of state high courts
advisory custodians of indigenous culture and customary affairs in traditional councils
qs.e: Traditional rulers act as custodians of culture, communal peacemakers, and advisors to local council administrations.

qs.q: The Public Complaints Commission possesses statutory authority to investigate public grievances regarding administrative injustice against
o: judgments rendered by the Supreme Court
federal, state, and local government departments as well as private commercial firms
qs.e: The Ombudsman investigates administrative injustice, oppression, or red tape across public agencies and private companies.

qs.q: The codified body of administrative guidelines governing appointments, duties, discipline, and service conditions in the civil service is the
qs.e: Public Service Rules (formerly General Orders) set out operational standards, rights, and disciplinary procedures for public servants.

qs.q: The senior career civil servant who functions as administrative head and accounting officer of a government ministry is the
qs.e: The Permanent Secretary oversees administrative management, financial accounting, and policy execution within a ministry.

qs.q: The political head appointed by the chief executive to lead a government ministry and direct policy formulation is the
qs.e: Ministers are political appointees who formulate policy and exercise executive oversight over government ministries.

qs.q: The highest-ranking career civil servant who coordinates civil service administrative machinery and advises executive leadership is the
o: Chairman of the Civil Service Commission
Head of Civil Service of the Federation
qs.e: The Head of Civil Service of the Federation manages administrative leadership, civil service welfare, and bureaucratic efficiency.

qs.q: The political appointee responsible for coordinating cabinet secretariats, tracking executive decisions, and managing inter-ministerial affairs is the
o: Chief of Staff to the President
Secretary to the Government of the Federation
qs.e: The SGF serves as administrative secretary to the Federal Executive Council and coordinates overall government policy implementation.

qs.q: Under Nigeria's executive presidential constitution, the National Assembly can override a presidential veto on a bill by re-passing it with a
o: simple majority vote in both houses
three-quarters majority vote in the Senate alone
two-thirds majority vote in each legislative house
qs.e: Section 58 of the constitution empowers parliament to override a presidential veto through a two-thirds supermajority in both houses.

qs.q: The constitutional procedure through which the legislature can remove an executive President or Governor for gross misconduct is termed
qs.e: Impeachment is the formal constitutional process whereby the legislature investigates and removes an executive officer for gross misconduct.

qs.q: The constitutional mechanism permitting registered voters in a constituency to unseat an unsatisfactory legislator before the end of their term is
qs.e: Recall allows electors in a constituency to petition and vote to unseat an elected legislator prior to election cycles.

qs.q: A vote of no confidence is a legislative procedure used to dismiss the prime minister and executive cabinet in a
qs.e: In a parliamentary system, a vote of no confidence passed by the legislature forces the Prime Minister and cabinet to resign.

qs.q: A major administrative criticism of the State Joint Local Government Account system in Nigeria is that it allows state governments to
o: seize revenue collected by traditional councils
deduct, delay, or divert statutory funds constitutionally intended for local councils
qs.e: State control over Joint Local Government Accounts has frequently resulted in state interference and underfunding of local councils.

qs.q: When a novel employs frame story, the reader experiences the story through
o: a single linear timeline without subplots
a short poem with four lines
a dramatic script written for radio
a narrative structure containing a story within another overarching story
qs.e: A frame story embeds one or more secondary narratives within a primary story framework.

qs.q: How does flashback enhance dramatic effectiveness?
o: By providing a scene inserted to portray events that occurred prior to the present timeline
By ending the play abruptly without resolution
qs.e: Flashback depicts past occurrences to clarify present motivations and circumstances.

qs.q: Identify the sound device illustrated by repetition of internal vowel sounds in non-rhyming words.
qs.e: The sound device defined as repetition of internal vowel sounds in non-rhyming words is assonance.

qs.q: Which genre is characterized by a serious drama depicting the downfall of a noble protagonist?
qs.e: The genre characterized by a serious drama depicting the downfall of a noble protagonist is tragedy.

qs.q: In dramatic literature, soliloquy refers to
o: a speech given by the chorus to open the play
a speech delivered by a character alone on stage revealing inner thoughts
a conversation between two main actors
a brief whisper unheard by anyone on stage
qs.e: A soliloquy allows the audience to hear a character's unspoken thoughts while alone on stage.

qs.q: The protagonist's journey in Alex Agyei-Agyiri's Unexpected Joy at Dawn highlights the issue of
o: the conflict between traditional chiefs and British rulers
the hardship of deportation and xenophobic expulsion orders
the establishment of cocoa plantations in Ivory Coast
the discovery of diamond mines in Sierra Leone
qs.e: The narrative arc in Alex Agyei-Agyiri's Unexpected Joy at Dawn underscores the hardship of deportation and xenophobic expulsion orders.

qs.q: What literary effect is produced by employing synecdoche in a line?
o: It enhances meaning through figure of speech where a part of something represents the whole, or vice versa
It destroys the rhyme scheme completely
It changes the author's legal name
qs.e: Synecdoche uses a part to stand for the whole, such as using 'all hands on deck' to mean sailors.

qs.q: In literary analysis, setting in Alex Agyei-Agyiri's Unexpected Joy at Dawn refers to
o: Ghana and Nigeria during periods of economic crisis and alien compliance deportations
qs.e: The dual setting in Ghana and Nigeria highlights cross-border migrations, expulsions, and shared history.

qs.q: How does run-on line (line continuation) contribute to the overall rhythm or meaning of a poem?
o: By building meaning via the continuation of a sentence without a pause beyond the end of a line
By changing the language of the poem
qs.e: Run-on line carries a thought over line boundaries without terminal punctuation.

qs.q: How does setting in Bayo Adebowale's Lonely Days influence character actions?
o: By creating atmospheric pressure via rural Kufi village, reflecting traditional customs and widowhood expectations
qs.e: Kufi village provides the traditional social backdrop against which Yaremi asserts her independence.

qs.q: How does stanza contribute to the overall rhythm or meaning of a poem?
o: By changing the language of the poem
By building meaning via a grouped set of lines within a poem, set off by a space
qs.e: Stanzas structure poems into organized poetic units analogous to paragraphs.

qs.q: When a playwright uses aside, the intended effect on the audience is to
o: a formal song sung by a masked chorus
a lengthy speech delivered alone on stage
an actor's movement toward the back of the stage
words spoken by an actor directly to the audience, unheard by other characters on stage
qs.e: An aside is a dramatic convention where speech is shared with the audience while remaining unheard by onstage characters.

qs.q: What is the primary function of a round character in a narrative structure?
o: a nameless background extra in a play
a simple character defined by a single static trait
a complex, multi-dimensional character who undergoes psychological development
a stock character based entirely on popular stereotype
qs.e: The primary function of a round character is to act as a complex, multi-dimensional character who undergoes psychological development.

qs.q: Identify the narrative method described as an all-knowing narrator who knows the thoughts and feelings of all characters.
qs.e: The narrative method defined by an all-knowing narrator who knows the thoughts and feelings of all characters is third-person omniscient.

qs.q: The poetic effect of the line 'Parting is such sweet sorrow / That I shall say good night till it be morrow' relies on
qs.e: Juxtaposing contradictory words 'sweet' and 'sorrow' creates an oxymoron.

qs.q: A key distinction of pastoral poem compared to other poetic forms is its
o: a formal elegy written for a monarch
a poem describing urban industrial decay
a poem about sea voyages and naval battles
a poem idealizing rural life, nature, and the peaceful existence of shepherds
qs.e: Pastoral verse romanticizes rural tranquility and natural beauty.

qs.q: A writer chooses synecdoche over literal description in order to
o: create vivid mental impact via figure of speech where a part of something represents the whole, or vice versa
qs.e: Synecdoche uses a part to stand for the whole, such as using 'all hands on deck' to mean sailors.

qs.q: Which of the following best captures the core message of Birago Diop's 'Vanity'?
o: desire for youthful beauty and fame
struggle for political power in modern cities
folly of ignoring ancestral wisdom and cultural tradition
qs.e: The core message of Birago Diop's 'Vanity' centers on the folly of ignoring ancestral wisdom and cultural tradition.

qs.q: What structural feature defines a free verse?
o: poetry written in strict iambic pentameter
a 14-line poem ending in a rhyming couplet
a five-line poem with AABBA rhyme
poetry that does not follow a fixed meter, rhyme scheme, or line length
qs.e: Free verse relies on natural speech rhythms rather than fixed metrical patterns.

qs.q: In the context of African literature, Agostinho Neto's 'The Grieved Lands' is widely recognized for illustrating
o: enduring resilience of African people despite colonial suffering
triumph of royal dynasties in Central Africa
rapid industrial expansion across urban towns
qs.e: Literary analysis of Agostinho Neto's 'The Grieved Lands' demonstrates the enduring resilience of African people despite colonial suffering.

qs.q: The imagery in Niyi Osundare's 'The Leader and the Led' primarily serves to emphasize the
o: quest for an ideal leader possessing balanced qualities
qs.e: Through vivid imagery, Niyi Osundare's 'The Leader and the Led' highlights the quest for an ideal leader possessing balanced qualities.

qs.q: When a literary text establishes a theme of betrayal and loyalty, the reader perceives
o: the discovery of new agricultural methods
the moral dilemma between personal allegiance and deceitful self-interest
the mechanical maintenance of steam engines
qs.e: This theme contrasts steadfast devotion with deceptive backstabbing in human relationships.

qs.q: The sound device known as meter is defined as
o: the visual spacing of lines on paper
the moral message of an epic
the choice of vocabulary by a prose writer
the structured pattern of stressed and unstressed syllables in a line of poetry
qs.e: Meter measures the poetic feet and accents that structure verse cadence.

qs.q: The protagonist's journey in Elechi Amadi's The Concubine highlights the issue of
o: the political governance of pre-colonial chieftains
the educational advancement of rural children
the economic impact of palm produce trade
the supernatural tragic fate surrounding Ihuoma and her suitors
qs.e: The narrative arc in Elechi Amadi's The Concubine underscores the supernatural tragic fate surrounding Ihuoma and her suitors.

qs.e: The work exhibits theme of oppression and resilience through enduring human fortitude in the face of brutal tyranny or injustice.

qs.q: Identify the sound device illustrated by use of harmonious, pleasing, and melodious sound combinations.
qs.e: The sound device defined as use of harmonious, pleasing, and melodious sound combinations is euphony.

qs.q: When a literary text establishes a nostalgic mood, the reader perceives
o: a bitter cynical mockery of societal values
an aggressive call to immediate war
a wistful, longing affection for the past or lost childhood days
a fearful dread of future events
qs.e: Nostalgic mood reflects fond longing for past memories and lost times.

qs.q: In plot analysis, inciting incident is defined as
o: the specific event that initiates the main conflict of the plot
the final closing line of a novel
the comedic interlude in act three
qs.e: The inciting incident disrupts the initial status quo and sets the main action in motion.

qs.q: How does setting in Amma Darko's Faceless influence character actions?
o: By creating atmospheric pressure via the impoverished, dangerous Agbogbloshie slums of Accra
qs.e: The harsh street environment of Agbogbloshie drives the vulnerability and suffering of street youth.

qs.q: When an author emphasizes setting in Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie's Purple Hibiscus, the story highlights
o: rural Omokachi village during harvest time
Enugu and Nsukka, representing rigid oppression versus liberating academic freedom
Lagos and London during the dock workers strike
qs.e: Enugu represents Eugene's tyrannical domestic rule while Nsukka represents Aunty Ifeoma's open, free environment.

qs.q: In poetic analysis, volta refers to
o: a dramatic turn or shift in thought, tone, or emotion in a poem
the introductory stanza of an epic
a foot of two unstressed syllables
the repeating refrain of a ballad
qs.e: Volta marks a crucial thematic turn, famously occurring between octave and sestet in sonnets.

qs.q: What role does setting in Chinua Achebe's Things Fall Apart play in shaping narrative events?
o: It forces the narrative to end abruptly
It establishes context through Umuofia and Mbanta during the onset of British colonial penetration
It removes all conflict from the plot
It changes the author's narrative point of view
qs.e: The traditional Igbo villages of Umuofia and Mbanta frame the collision between native culture and British colonialism.

qs.q: When a poet utilizes synecdoche, the line relies primarily on
o: figure of speech where a part of something represents the whole, or vice versa
substitution of an attribute for the thing meant
qs.e: Synecdoche uses a part to stand for the whole, such as using 'all hands on deck' to mean sailors.

qs.q: What musical effect does a poet create by employing cacophony?
o: It forces lines to end without punctuation
It changes the meaning of all nouns
It enhances auditory resonance through use of harsh, jarring, and discordant sound combinations
qs.e: Cacophony uses harsh, clashing consonants to evoke disorder or violence.

qs.q: When a literary text establishes a theme of religious extremism, the reader perceives
o: destructive impact of fanatical religious zealotry on family and society
qs.e: This theme depicts how rigid, abusive religious dogmatism destroys interpersonal relationships.

qs.q: In literary analysis, a deuteragonist is best defined as
o: the least significant extra on stage
the second most important character in a narrative after the protagonist
the comedic actor delivering ending lines
the main author writing the literary text
qs.e: The deuteragonist holds the position of secondary importance in the dramatic hierarchy.

qs.q: The poetic form known as Petrarchan (Italian) sonnet is characterized by
o: a 14-line poem divided into an octave (ABBAABBA) and a sestet (CDECDE/CDCDCD)
a short poem of three lines with 5-7-5 syllables
a 19-line poem with two repeating refrains
a 14-line poem consisting of three quatrains and a couplet
qs.e: The Petrarchan sonnet splits into an 8-line octave presenting a problem and a 6-line sestet offering resolution.

qs.q: The narrative technique known as dual narrative is characterized by
o: a play performed by one actor
a poem written in rhyming couplets
a story told from two distinct alternating perspectives or voices
a narrative told by a single narrator
qs.e: Dual narrative alternates between two point-of-view characters to offer contrasting viewpoints.

qs.q: In dramatic literature, fourth wall refers to
o: the decorative curtain hanging above the stage
the imaginary invisible barrier separating actors on stage from the audience
the back wall of a physical theater stage
the script written by the playwright
qs.e: Breaking the fourth wall occurs when actors directly address or acknowledge the audience.

qs.q: Identify the poetic genre described by a traditional three-line poem with a syllable count of 5-7-5, often focusing on nature.
qs.e: The poetic genre defined by a traditional three-line poem with a syllable count of 5-7-5, often focusing on nature is haiku.

qs.q: What is the significance of parallel plot in organizing a story?
o: It organizes the plot by a narrative structure featuring two simultaneous storylines of equal importance
It changes the author's narrative style
qs.e: Parallel plots run side by side, offering contrasting or complementary perspectives on central themes.

qs.q: Which narrative device involves narration from the perspective of a character using 'I' or 'we'?
qs.e: The device involving narration from the perspective of a character using 'I' or 'we' is first-person point of view.

qs.q: The thematic resolution of Chinua Achebe's Things Fall Apart reflects the impact of
o: the growth of international palm oil corporations
the downfall of Okonkwo and the collapse of traditional Umuofia society
the history of ancient Benin kingdom bronzes
the migration of nomadic herders across the savannah
qs.e: The conclusion of Chinua Achebe's Things Fall Apart reveals the consequences of the downfall of Okonkwo and the collapse of traditional Umuofia society.

qs.q: What is the primary purpose of employing dramatic irony in a play?
o: a situation where the audience knows critical information unknown to characters on stage
a comedic scene following a tragic event
an abrupt ending leaving the plot unresolved
a statement that contradicts itself logically
qs.e: Playwrights use dramatic irony primarily to achieve a situation where the audience knows critical information unknown to characters on stage.

qs.q: How does parallel plot affect reader engagement?
o: By enhancing suspense through a narrative structure featuring two simultaneous storylines of equal importance
qs.e: Parallel plots run side by side, offering contrasting or complementary perspectives on central themes.

qs.q: In literary analysis, setting in Elechi Amadi's The Concubine refers to
o: traditional rural Omokachi village dominated by deity worship and spiritual laws
urban Lagos marketplace in modern times
qs.e: Omokachi village provides an environment governed by customary law, divine forces, and ancestral shrines.

qs.q: When a character serves as a central character who lacks conventional heroic virtues such as idealism or nobility, they function as a
qs.e: Such a character is identified as a anti-hero.

qs.q: What dominant theme is explored in Birago Diop's 'Vanity'?
o: desire for youthful beauty and fame
struggle for political power in modern cities
folly of ignoring ancestral wisdom and cultural tradition
qs.e: The primary theme depicted in Birago Diop's 'Vanity' is the folly of ignoring ancestral wisdom and cultural tradition.

qs.q: The authorial message embedded in Buchi Emecheta's Second Class Citizen exposes the consequences of
o: Adah's struggle against racial discrimination and spousal abuse in London
the trade union strikes in Liverpool docks
the life of cocoa farmers in Western Nigeria
the political campaign for Nigerian independence
qs.e: The underlying message in Buchi Emecheta's Second Class Citizen deals with Adah's struggle against racial discrimination and spousal abuse in London.

qs.q: What musical effect does a poet create by employing meter?
o: It enhances auditory resonance through the structured pattern of stressed and unstressed syllables in a line of poetry
It forces lines to end without punctuation
It changes the meaning of all nouns
qs.e: Meter measures the poetic feet and accents that structure verse cadence.

qs.q: When a writer incorporates falling action, the narrative flow is shaped by
o: events occurring after the climax that lead toward the final resolution
qs.e: Falling action relaxes narrative tension as consequences of the climax unfold.

qs.q: Which of the following descriptions accurately characterizes a confidant?
o: a trusted friend to whom the protagonist reveals secret thoughts and intentions
a stage manager directing live actor movements
a supernatural spirit causing dramatic conflict
the main villain attempting to kill the hero
qs.e: A confidant provides a believable way for the protagonist's inner thoughts to be voiced.

qs.q: When a poet utilizes metaphor, the line relies primarily on
o: a statement that contradicts itself directly
an implicit comparison between two unlike things asserting one is the other
qs.e: A metaphor asserts an equivalence between two unalike items without using comparative conjunctions.

qs.q: In literary criticism, the nostalgic mood refers to
o: a wistful, longing affection for the past or lost childhood days
a bitter cynical mockery of societal values
an aggressive call to immediate war
a fearful dread of future events
qs.e: Nostalgic mood reflects fond longing for past memories and lost times.

qs.q: What is the primary purpose of employing foreshadowing in a play?
o: a direct reference to historical documents
the resolution of all dramatic conflicts at the end
the use of clues or hints to suggest events that will occur later in the plot
a comic monologue breaking dramatic tension
qs.e: Playwrights use foreshadowing primarily to achieve the use of clues or hints to suggest events that will occur later in the plot.

qs.q: When a novel employs third-person omniscient, the reader experiences the story through
o: an all-knowing narrator who knows the thoughts and feelings of all characters
a narrator using 'I' to tell personal events
a narrator restricted to one character's perspective
a narrator speaking directly to the audience
qs.e: Omniscient narration provides complete access to all character thoughts and events.

qs.q: In the structure of Elechi Amadi's The Concubine, a recurring source of tension is
o: the supernatural tragic fate surrounding Ihuoma and her suitors
the economic impact of palm produce trade
the political governance of pre-colonial chieftains
the educational advancement of rural children
qs.e: Tension throughout Elechi Amadi's The Concubine stems directly from the supernatural tragic fate surrounding Ihuoma and her suitors.

qs.q: Which term describes a character who experiences significant internal growth or change over time?
qs.e: The term for a character who experiences significant internal growth or change over time is dynamic character.

qs.q: How does comic relief enhance dramatic effectiveness?
o: By ending the play abruptly without resolution
By providing a humorous scene inserted into a serious drama to temporarily ease tension
qs.e: Comic relief offers the audience a brief respite from intense emotional tension.

qs.q: Writers adopt the genre of myth primarily to
o: explore themes through a traditional story explaining natural phenomena, origins, or cultural customs
reduce the length of their books
qs.e: Myths are ancestral narratives explaining sacred origins, gods, and natural forces.

qs.q: What role does 'plot' play in narrative analysis?
o: It provides the structured arrangement of incidents and events in a story
It changes the font style of the text
It eliminates the need for punctuation
qs.e: Plot refers to the sequence of events and causal connections driving narrative action.

qs.q: The narrative technique known as third-person limited is characterized by
o: a narrative told in reversed chronological order
an all-seeing narrator knowing everyone's inner thoughts
a narrator who reports events from the focal perspective of a single character
a story narrated by an anonymous chorus
qs.e: Limited third-person focuses closely on the inner world of one character.

qs.q: Which choice best interprets the underlying meaning of 'Fair is foul, and foul is fair / Hover through the fog and filthy air'?
qs.e: The statement 'fair is foul, and foul is fair' presents a self-contradictory idea that holds symbolic truth.

qs.q: An analysis of social setting reveals its function in
o: building atmosphere and theme through the cultural beliefs, socio-economic context, and societal norms framing the plot
qs.e: Social setting reflects societal expectations, class structures, and cultural environment.

qs.q: How does assonance impact the reading experience?
o: By appealing to the ear via repetition of internal vowel sounds in non-rhyming words
qs.e: Assonance repeats vowel sounds within words, e.g. 'fleet feet sweep by sleep'.

qs.q: In literary studies, the term 'motif' refers to
o: a single punctuation mark used for emphasis
a recurring element, image, or idea that reinforces the main theme
the name of the principal villain
the first line of an epic poem
qs.e: A motif is a repeating motif, symbol, or structural detail that strengthens thematic meaning.

qs.q: The poetic form known as Shakespearean (English) sonnet is characterized by
o: a mournful lament for the dead
a narrative poem written in free verse
an octave and sestet with ABBAABBA rhyme
a 14-line poem composed of three quatrains (ABAB CDCD EFEF) and a concluding couplet (GG)
qs.e: The Shakespearean sonnet uses three quatrains to build an argument and a couplet to conclude.

qs.q: Which figure of speech is demonstrated when a writer uses giving human traits, feelings, or actions to non-human objects or abstractions?
qs.e: The device defined by giving human traits, feelings, or actions to non-human objects or abstractions is personification.

qs.q: In the extract 'Parting is such sweet sorrow / That I shall say good night till it be morrow', the speaker's tone is best described as
qs.e: The attitude of the speaker in 'Parting is such sweet sorrow / That I shall say good night till it be morrow' expresses a oxymoron perspective.

qs.q: In the context of African literature, Wole Soyinka's 'Abiku' is widely recognized for illustrating
o: stubborn refusal of the spirit child to remain bound to Earth
joy of parents raising a healthy child
peaceful harmony between humans and nature
success of native doctors in breaking spiritual curses
qs.e: Literary analysis of Wole Soyinka's 'Abiku' demonstrates the stubborn refusal of the spirit child to remain bound to Earth.

qs.q: In the context of African literature, Lenrie Peters's 'The Panic of Growing Older' is widely recognized for illustrating
o: unfulfilled dreams and the relentless march of time
excitement of acquiring material property in youth
qs.e: Literary analysis of Lenrie Peters's 'The Panic of Growing Older' demonstrates the unfulfilled dreams and the relentless march of time.

qs.q: When a poet writes a epic, the text adheres to
o: a long narrative poem on a grand scale depicting heroic deeds and national history
a short lyric poem expressing personal feelings
a comedic verse written for children
qs.e: Epics depict heroic achievements, divine intervention, and cultural values on an elevated scale.

qs.q: A key distinction of ode compared to other poetic forms is its
o: a narrative poem detailing military battles
a formal lyric poem written in praise of a person, object, abstract idea, or event
a poem commemorating a tragic funeral
a satirical poem ridiculing political leaders
qs.e: Odes express elevated emotions and praise for their subject.

qs.q: How does refrain contribute to the overall rhythm or meaning of a poem?
o: By building meaning via a repeated line, phrase, or group of lines recurring at regular intervals in a poem
By changing the language of the poem
qs.e: Refrain reinforces central themes through rhythmic repetition at fixed points in a poem.

qs.q: What literary element is highlighted in the passage: 'My love is like a red, red rose / That's newly sprung in June'?
qs.e: The passage 'My love is like a red, red rose / That's newly sprung in June' serves as an example of simile.

qs.q: In the context of African literature, Birago Diop's 'Vanity' is widely recognized for illustrating
o: struggle for political power in modern cities
folly of ignoring ancestral wisdom and cultural tradition
desire for youthful beauty and fame
qs.e: Literary analysis of Birago Diop's 'Vanity' demonstrates the folly of ignoring ancestral wisdom and cultural tradition.

qs.q: What effect does a poet achieve by using symbolism?
o: It enhances poetic expression through use of concrete objects or images to represent abstract concepts or ideas
It converts the poem into prose
It forces the poem to be sung aloud
qs.e: Symbolism connects physical items to deeper philosophical or emotional meanings.

qs.q: Which of the following descriptions accurately characterizes a round character?
o: a stock character based entirely on popular stereotype
a nameless background extra in a play
a simple character defined by a single static trait
a complex, multi-dimensional character who undergoes psychological development
qs.e: Round characters are realistic, dynamic, and possess complex personalities.

qs.q: In Bayo Adebowale's Lonely Days, the author uses the plot events to comment on
o: Yaremi's heroic resistance against humiliating widowhood rites
the rivalry between two royal dynasties
the conflict between traditional hunters and farmers
the construction of modern highways in rural areas
qs.e: Through key plot developments, Bayo Adebowale's Lonely Days comments on Yaremi's heroic resistance against humiliating widowhood rites.

qs.q: An author creates a solemn mood primarily to focus attention on
o: a deeply serious, formal, and dignified emotional atmosphere
qs.e: Solemn mood conveys formal gravity and serious reflection.

qs.q: What literary effect is produced by employing apostrophe in a line?
o: It enhances meaning through addressing an absent person, abstract quality, or inanimate object directly
It changes the author's legal name
It destroys the rhyme scheme completely
qs.e: Apostrophe occurs when a speaker addresses an absent entity as if it were present and capable of understanding.

qs.q: In literary analysis, setting in Wole Soyinka's The Lion and the Jewel refers to
o: the commercial port city of Lagos
Ilujinle village, serving as the battleground between traditional Yoruba culture and modern Western values
qs.e: Ilujinle provides the traditional setting where Baroka outwits Lakunle for Sidi's hand.

qs.q: A writer chooses paradox over literal description in order to
o: create vivid mental impact via a statement that appears self-contradictory but reveals an underlying truth
qs.e: A paradox seems logically impossible at first glance but holds deep philosophical truth.

qs.q: Writers adopt the genre of tragedy primarily to
o: reduce the length of their books
explore themes through a serious drama depicting the downfall of a noble protagonist
qs.e: Tragedy deals with serious themes and ends in catastrophe for the protagonist.

qs.q: How does dramatic irony enhance dramatic effectiveness?
o: By ending the play abruptly without resolution
By providing a situation where the audience knows critical information unknown to characters on stage
qs.e: Dramatic irony occurs when the audience understands events better than the unsuspecting characters.

qs.q: Which of the following literary works belongs to the genre of epistolary novel?
o: A text that presents a novel written in the form of letters, diary entries, or documents
qs.e: Epistolary fiction advances its narrative through written letters and personal correspondence.

qs.q: The emotional impact of a satirical mood is evident in its focus on
o: a mocking, critical atmosphere exposing human flaws through humor and irony
qs.e: Satirical mood uses irony and ridicule to critique foolishness or corruption.

qs.q: In poetic analysis, imagery refers to
o: the historical background of the poet
a mathematical pattern of rhyme sounds
vivid descriptive language appealing to one or more of the five senses
the formal title given to a poetic work
qs.e: Imagery creates vivid mental impressions through sensory details.

qs.q: When a writer incorporates rising action, the narrative flow is shaped by
o: the calm period after the climax
a series of events that build tension toward the central climax
the final moral lesson of a fable
qs.e: Rising action develops conflicts and escalates narrative suspense leading to the climax.

qs.q: The difference between 'motif' and other literary elements lies in its focus on
o: the first line of an epic poem
the name of the principal villain
a single punctuation mark used for emphasis
a recurring element, image, or idea that reinforces the main theme
qs.e: A motif is a repeating motif, symbol, or structural detail that strengthens thematic meaning.

qs.q: Which acoustic element in poetry is described as the measured flow of stressed and unstressed syllables in verse?
qs.e: The acoustic element defined by the measured flow of stressed and unstressed syllables in verse is rhythm.

qs.q: Identify the poetic element described as a pair of successive rhyming lines of verse, usually of the same length.
qs.e: The poetic element defined as a pair of successive rhyming lines of verse, usually of the same length is couplet.

qs.q: What advantage does a writer gain by using first-person point of view?
o: It makes the book impossible to translate
It allows narration from the perspective of a character using 'I' or 'we'
It eliminates the need for chapter divisions
It forces all characters to speak the same dialect
qs.e: First-person narration uses first-person pronouns to convey personal experiences.

qs.q: What dominant theme is explored in Wole Soyinka's 'Abiku'?
o: success of native doctors in breaking spiritual curses
joy of parents raising a healthy child
stubborn refusal of the spirit child to remain bound to Earth
peaceful harmony between humans and nature
qs.e: The primary theme depicted in Wole Soyinka's 'Abiku' is the stubborn refusal of the spirit child to remain bound to Earth.

qs.q: What is the primary function of a static character in a narrative structure?
o: a character who remains mentally and emotionally unchanged throughout the story
a character who undergoes radical moral transformation
a character who narrates the story from the future
the primary hero who resolves the main conflict
qs.e: The primary function of a static character is to act as a character who remains mentally and emotionally unchanged throughout the story.

qs.q: How does onomatopoeia impact the reading experience?
o: By appealing to the ear via use of words that imitate or echo the natural sound they describe
qs.e: Onomatopoeia includes sound-imitative words like 'buzz', 'hiss', 'clang', 'crash'.

qs.q: Which poetry form is defined as a formal lyric poem written in praise of a person, object, abstract idea, or event?
qs.e: The form defined as a formal lyric poem written in praise of a person, object, abstract idea, or event is ode.

qs.q: What structural feature defines a blank verse?
o: unrhymed poetry written in regular iambic pentameter
rhymed poetry written in free verse
a three-line stanza with interlocking rhyme
qs.e: Blank verse maintains regular iambic pentameter meter without end rhymes.

qs.q: The literary genre known as satire is best defined as
o: literary work using humor, irony, or ridicule to expose human folly and social vices
a tragic play focused on death
a factual biography of a monarch
qs.e: Satire aims to critique and reform societal shortcomings through mockery.

qs.q: Writers adopt the genre of comedy primarily to
o: reduce the length of their books
explore themes through a dramatic work designed to amuse and ending happily
qs.e: Comedy aims to entertain through humor and typically concludes with a joyful outcome.

qs.q: What is the significance of episodic structure in organizing a story?
o: It changes the author's narrative style
It organizes the plot by a narrative composed of a series of loosely linked independent episodes
qs.e: Episodic plots feature distinct scenes connected by a common central character or theme.

qs.q: Identify the figure of speech defined as deliberate and obvious exaggeration used for emphasis or effect.
qs.e: Hyperbole is defined as deliberate and obvious exaggeration used for emphasis or effect.

qs.q: In literary studies, the term 'plot' refers to
o: the structured arrangement of incidents and events in a story
the physical location where actors perform
the list of characters printed in a program
the rhyming scheme at the end of stanzas
qs.e: Plot refers to the sequence of events and causal connections driving narrative action.

qs.q: How does rhythm impact the reading experience?
o: By appealing to the ear via the measured flow of stressed and unstressed syllables in verse
qs.e: Rhythm establishes the musical movement and cadence of poetic lines.

qs.q: When a verse exhibits imagery, its structure relies on
o: the historical background of the poet
vivid descriptive language appealing to one or more of the five senses
the formal title given to a poetic work
a mathematical pattern of rhyme sounds
qs.e: Imagery creates vivid mental impressions through sensory details.

qs.q: Which poetic device is defined by a four-line stanza or poem, often with a distinct rhyme scheme?
qs.e: The device defined by a four-line stanza or poem, often with a distinct rhyme scheme is quatrain.

qs.q: Which structural stage of a narrative involves an abrupt ending at a moment of high tension, leaving outcomes unresolved?
qs.e: The stage involving an abrupt ending at a moment of high tension, leaving outcomes unresolved is cliffhanger.

qs.q: Which of the following literary works belongs to the genre of tragicomedy?
o: A text that presents a play combining elements of both tragedy and comedy
qs.e: Tragicomedy blends tragic themes with comedic scenes and often resolves happily.

qs.q: When a novel employs third-person limited, the reader experiences the story through
o: a narrative told in reversed chronological order
a story narrated by an anonymous chorus
an all-seeing narrator knowing everyone's inner thoughts
a narrator who reports events from the focal perspective of a single character
qs.e: Limited third-person focuses closely on the inner world of one character.

qs.q: An author creates a triumphant mood primarily to focus attention on
o: an exuberant, victorious emotional atmosphere celebrating success over adversity
a fearful anxiety about unknown dangers
qs.e: Triumphant mood expresses joy, victory, and overcoming hardship.

qs.q: The difference between 'conflict' and other literary elements lies in its focus on
o: the rhyming sound at line ends
the central struggle between opposing forces in a literary work
the price of a published novel
the speed of scene changes on stage
qs.e: Conflict provides tension and propels plot development in narrative works.

qs.q: The literary genre known as farce is best defined as
o: a solemn tragedy about royal downfall
a serious poem written in free verse
an extravagant comedy relying on absurd situations, physical humor, and improbability
qs.e: Farce uses crude humor, horseplay, and ridiculous situations to evoke laughter.

qs.q: What is the significance of rising action in organizing a story?
o: It changes the author's narrative style
It organizes the plot by a series of events that build tension toward the central climax
qs.e: Rising action develops conflicts and escalates narrative suspense leading to the climax.

qs.q: An example of foreshadowing in theatrical performance is
o: the use of clues or hints to suggest events that will occur later in the plot
a direct reference to historical documents
a comic monologue breaking dramatic tension
the resolution of all dramatic conflicts at the end
qs.e: Foreshadowing prepares the audience for future events by embedding subtle hints early in the narrative.

qs.q: An analysis of setting in Chinua Achebe's Things Fall Apart reveals its function in
o: building atmosphere and theme through Umuofia and Mbanta during the onset of British colonial penetration
qs.e: The traditional Igbo villages of Umuofia and Mbanta frame the collision between native culture and British colonialism.

qs.q: The imagery in Kofi Awoonor's 'The Weaver Bird' primarily serves to emphasize the
o: migration of wild birds during seasonal rains
colonial intrusion that displaced indigenous customs
peaceful arrival of foreign religious scholars
qs.e: Through vivid imagery, Kofi Awoonor's 'The Weaver Bird' highlights the colonial intrusion that displaced indigenous customs.

qs.q: Which structural stage of a narrative involves a narrative composed of a series of loosely linked independent episodes?
qs.e: The stage involving a narrative composed of a series of loosely linked independent episodes is episodic structure.

qs.q: In literary analysis, setting in Chinua Achebe's Things Fall Apart refers to
o: the city of Freetown during Sierra Leone mining conflict
urban Accra during modern political elections
Umuofia and Mbanta during the onset of British colonial penetration
qs.e: The traditional Igbo villages of Umuofia and Mbanta frame the collision between native culture and British colonialism.

qs.q: What is the primary function of a dynamic character in a narrative structure?
o: the author's voice speaking directly to readers
a static figure designed solely for background detail
a character who experiences significant internal growth or change over time
a minor stock character representing a social class
qs.e: The primary function of a dynamic character is to act as a character who experiences significant internal growth or change over time.

qs.q: The authorial message embedded in Bayo Adebowale's Lonely Days exposes the consequences of
o: the construction of modern highways in rural areas
the rivalry between two royal dynasties
the conflict between traditional hunters and farmers
Yaremi's heroic resistance against humiliating widowhood rites
qs.e: The underlying message in Bayo Adebowale's Lonely Days deals with Yaremi's heroic resistance against humiliating widowhood rites.

qs.q: In dramatic literature, hubris refers to
o: excessive pride or arrogance that leads to a character's tragic downfall
the introduction of comic relief in a play
a secret whisper to the audience
qs.e: Hubris is a common tragic flaw involving overwhelming pride that defies moral or divine boundaries.

qs.q: The authorial message embedded in Amma Darko's Faceless exposes the consequences of
o: the history of gold mining in Ghana
the academic achievements of university scholars
the vulnerability and exploitation of street children in Accra
the diplomatic relations between West African nations
qs.e: The underlying message in Amma Darko's Faceless deals with the vulnerability and exploitation of street children in Accra.

qs.q: The difference between 'diction' and other literary elements lies in its focus on
o: the metric rhythm of a poetic stanza
an author's choice and deliberate selection of words in a text
the speed at which an actor speaks
qs.e: Diction refers specifically to word choice and vocabulary employed by a writer.

qs.q: The thematic resolution of Buchi Emecheta's Second Class Citizen reflects the impact of
o: the political campaign for Nigerian independence
Adah's struggle against racial discrimination and spousal abuse in London
the life of cocoa farmers in Western Nigeria
the trade union strikes in Liverpool docks
qs.e: The conclusion of Buchi Emecheta's Second Class Citizen reveals the consequences of Adah's struggle against racial discrimination and spousal abuse in London.

qs.q: An analysis of the extract 'The thunder grumbled like an old man in pain' reveals that the author intends to convey
qs.e: Through 'The thunder grumbled like an old man in pain', the author conveys simile and personification.

qs.q: The imagery in Agostinho Neto's 'The Grieved Lands' primarily serves to emphasize the
o: triumph of royal dynasties in Central Africa
rapid industrial expansion across urban towns
enduring resilience of African people despite colonial suffering
qs.e: Through vivid imagery, Agostinho Neto's 'The Grieved Lands' highlights the enduring resilience of African people despite colonial suffering.

qs.q: What literary element is highlighted in the passage: 'The wind whispered secrets through the trembling leaves'?
qs.e: The passage 'The wind whispered secrets through the trembling leaves' serves as an example of personification.

qs.q: What literary element is highlighted in the passage: 'The sea is calm tonight / The tide is full, the moon lies fair'?
qs.e: The passage 'The sea is calm tonight / The tide is full, the moon lies fair' serves as an example of serene and contemplative.

qs.q: In literary analysis, a foil is best defined as
o: a character whose traits contrast sharply with another to highlight specific qualities
the main narrator of a dramatic performance
an identical twin character used for comedic confusion
a character who dies at the start of the play
qs.e: A foil serves to emphasize the distinct personality traits of another character through contrast.

qs.q: The difference between 'tone' and other literary elements lies in its focus on
o: the author's attitude toward the subject matter or audience
the emotional reaction felt by the reader
the physical volume of a speaker's voice
qs.e: Tone reflects the writer's perspective or mood toward their material.

qs.q: What is the primary purpose of employing fourth wall in a play?
o: the decorative curtain hanging above the stage
the imaginary invisible barrier separating actors on stage from the audience
the back wall of a physical theater stage
the script written by the playwright
qs.e: Playwrights use fourth wall primarily to achieve the imaginary invisible barrier separating actors on stage from the audience.

qs.q: Identify the figure of speech defined as direct comparison between two distinct things using 'like' or 'as'.
qs.e: Simile is defined as direct comparison between two distinct things using 'like' or 'as'.

qs.q: Which poetry form is defined as a poem idealizing rural life, nature, and the peaceful existence of shepherds?
qs.e: The form defined as a poem idealizing rural life, nature, and the peaceful existence of shepherds is pastoral poem.

qs.q: The narrative technique known as foreshadowing (prolepsis) is characterized by
o: narrative hints pointing toward events that will occur later in the story
the final resolution of a plot
qs.e: Prolepsis or foreshadowing anticipates future plot developments through subtle hints.

qs.q: What literary effect is produced by employing personification in a line?
o: It changes the author's legal name
It destroys the rhyme scheme completely
It enhances meaning through giving human traits, feelings, or actions to non-human objects or abstractions
qs.e: Personification endows inanimate objects or abstract concepts with human qualities.

qs.q: An author creates a theme of betrayal and loyalty primarily to focus attention on
o: the mechanical maintenance of steam engines
the moral dilemma between personal allegiance and deceitful self-interest
the discovery of new agricultural methods
qs.e: This theme contrasts steadfast devotion with deceptive backstabbing in human relationships.

qs.q: The narrative technique known as non-linear narrative is characterized by
o: a single act play set in real time
events narrated out of chronological order using flashbacks or jump cuts
qs.e: Non-linear stories disrupt chronological sequence to highlight thematic connections.

qs.q: How does setting in Chinua Achebe's Things Fall Apart influence character actions?
o: By creating atmospheric pressure via Umuofia and Mbanta during the onset of British colonial penetration
qs.e: The traditional Igbo villages of Umuofia and Mbanta frame the collision between native culture and British colonialism.

qs.q: What characterizes the theme of betrayal and loyalty in a narrative work?
o: the moral dilemma between personal allegiance and deceitful self-interest
the discovery of new agricultural methods
the mechanical maintenance of steam engines
qs.e: The work exhibits theme of betrayal and loyalty through the moral dilemma between personal allegiance and deceitful self-interest.

qs.q: The sound device known as assonance is defined as
o: repetition of internal vowel sounds in non-rhyming words
qs.e: Assonance repeats vowel sounds within words, e.g. 'fleet feet sweep by sleep'.

qs.q: In the extract 'The sun was a golden coin tossed into the azure sky', the speaker's tone is best described as
qs.e: The attitude of the speaker in 'The sun was a golden coin tossed into the azure sky' expresses a metaphor perspective.

qs.q: The poetic effect of the line 'The sun was a golden coin tossed into the azure sky' relies on
qs.e: Comparing the sun directly to a golden coin without using 'like' or 'as' is a metaphor.

qs.q: The literary genre known as epic is best defined as
o: a comedic play set in a village market
a long narrative poem celebrating the heroic deeds of a legendary figure
qs.e: An epic is a grand poetic narrative depicting heroic achievements and national identity.

qs.q: In literary analysis, a anti-hero is best defined as
o: a villain who completely destroys the protagonist
a divine deity introduced to solve plot complications
a chorus member who recites background information
a central character who lacks conventional heroic virtues such as idealism or nobility
qs.e: An anti-hero is a protagonist who exhibits non-traditional or morally ambiguous qualities.

qs.q: When an author emphasizes social setting, the story highlights
o: the rhyme scheme of a poem
the cultural beliefs, socio-economic context, and societal norms framing the plot
the physical climate of a desert island
qs.e: Social setting reflects societal expectations, class structures, and cultural environment.

qs.q: A writer includes a antagonist in a play primarily to
o: the main hero of the narrative
a background character with no influence on plot
the character or force that directly opposes the protagonist
the narrator telling the story in first person
qs.e: An antagonist creates conflict by working against the protagonist's goals.

qs.q: The emotional impact of a theme of betrayal and loyalty is evident in its focus on
o: the discovery of new agricultural methods
the mechanical maintenance of steam engines
the moral dilemma between personal allegiance and deceitful self-interest
qs.e: This theme contrasts steadfast devotion with deceptive backstabbing in human relationships.

qs.q: A critic analyzing 'conflict' in a novel is primarily examining
o: the price of a published novel
the rhyming sound at line ends
the speed of scene changes on stage
the central struggle between opposing forces in a literary work
qs.e: Conflict provides tension and propels plot development in narrative works.

qs.q: When a verse incorporates euphony, the line relies on
o: use of harsh, discordant, and unmusical sounds
use of harmonious, pleasing, and melodious sound combinations
qs.e: Euphony combines smooth, pleasing acoustic elements to create melodious verse.

qs.q: The literary genre known as melodrama is best defined as
o: a dramatic work with exaggerated characters and exciting events appealing to emotions
qs.e: Melodrama emphasizes sensational plot turns and sharp moral contrasts between good and evil.

qs.q: In dramatic literature, foreshadowing refers to
o: the resolution of all dramatic conflicts at the end
the use of clues or hints to suggest events that will occur later in the plot
a comic monologue breaking dramatic tension
a direct reference to historical documents
qs.e: Foreshadowing prepares the audience for future events by embedding subtle hints early in the narrative.

qs.q: A key distinction of blank verse compared to other poetic forms is its
o: a three-line stanza with interlocking rhyme
unrhymed poetry written in regular iambic pentameter
rhymed poetry written in free verse
qs.e: Blank verse maintains regular iambic pentameter meter without end rhymes.

qs.q: Which poetry form is defined as a long narrative poem on a grand scale depicting heroic deeds and national history?
qs.e: The form defined as a long narrative poem on a grand scale depicting heroic deeds and national history is epic.

qs.q: In literary classification, a story in which characters and events symbolize abstract moral or political ideas defines the category of
qs.e: This definition identifies the genre of allegory.

qs.q: The sound device known as slant rhyme (half rhyme) is defined as
o: words with similar but not exact matching sounds
words that do not share any sound
