qs.e: 2 Thessalonians 3:10 sets down the apostolic mandate that able-bodied believers who choose idleness should not receive community meals.

qs.q: What role did Prophetess Huldah play during King Josiah's religious reforms in Judah?
o: She authenticated the discovered Book of the Law and prophesied judgment on Jerusalem after Josiah's reign
She led the Temple choir during the Passover restoration
She personally destroyed the altar at Bethel with an iron rod
She anointed Josiah as king over Israel and Judah
qs.e: 2 Kings 22:14-20 states that King Josiah sent delegation to Prophetess Huldah, who confirmed the divine origin and warnings of the found scroll.

qs.q: In Paul's letter to Philemon, on what basis does Paul intercede for the runaway slave Onesimus?
o: He demands that Philemon pay monetary damages to the Roman authorities
He asks Philemon to receive Onesimus no longer as a slave, but as a beloved brother in Christ
He orders Philemon under apostolic threat to grant immediate civil freedom
He claims Onesimus was wrongfully accused of theft by Roman court
qs.e: Paul appeals to Philemon in love, asking him to welcome transformed Onesimus as a brother in the Lord (Philemon 1:15-16).

qs.q: What was Cain's profession before he murdered his brother Abel in Genesis chapter four?
qs.e: Genesis 4:2 states that Abel was a keeper of sheep, but Cain was a tiller of the ground.

qs.q: Which judge of Israel defeated the Midianites with an army reduced to three hundred men?
qs.e: God reduced Gideon's army from 32,000 down to 300 men who lapped water like dogs, ensuring the glory belonged to God.

qs.q: Which king of Israel built the glorious First Temple in Jerusalem?
qs.e: King Solomon constructed the First Temple in Jerusalem over seven years using cedar logs and skilled craftsmen from Hiram of Tyre.

qs.q: Which Roman governor presided over the trial of Jesus and handed Him over to be crucified?
qs.e: Pontius Pilate was the Roman procurator of Judea who condemned Jesus to death by crucifixion despite finding no fault in Him.
qs.tp: Trial, Death and Resurrection of Jesus

qs.q: In which city were believers in Jesus Christ first called Christians?
qs.e: Acts 11:26 records that the disciples were first called Christians in Syrian Antioch where Barnabas and Saul taught for a whole year.

qs.q: According to Paul in 1 Corinthians chapter 13, which virtue is described as the greatest of all?
qs.e: 1 Corinthians 13:13 concludes: 'And now abide faith, hope, love, these three; but the greatest of these is love.'

qs.q: What animal did Abraham discover caught in a thicket to substitute for Isaac on Mount Moriah?
qs.e: Genesis 22:13 states that Abraham looked up and saw a ram caught in a thicket by its horns, which he offered instead of Isaac.

qs.q: Why was the Tower of Babel built by humanity according to Genesis chapter eleven?
o: To protect themselves from another global flood
To make a name for themselves and prevent being scattered across the earth
To worship the sun, moon, and stars
To establish a sanctuary for the Levites
qs.e: The builders at Babel sought human fame and unity apart from God, prompting God to confuse their language and scatter them.

qs.q: How did God answer Elijah's prayer during the contest on Mount Carmel?
o: A violent earthquake split Mount Carmel into two parts
A heavy rainstorm extinguished the altar fires of Baal
An angel appeared and slew the 450 prophets of Baal directly
Fire fell from heaven and consumed the sacrifice, wood, stones, and water
qs.e: 1 Kings 18:38 describes God sending fire from heaven that consumed the sacrifice, wood, stones, dust, and licked up the water in the trench.

qs.q: What specific act caused King David to be rebuked by the prophet Nathan?
o: Refusing to build the Temple in Jerusalem
Forming a military covenant with the Philistines
Committing adultery with Bathsheba and arranging Uriah's death in battle
Offering sacrifices on foreign high places
qs.e: Nathan confronted David with the parable of the rich man who took a poor man's single ewe lamb, condemning David's sin against Uriah.

qs.q: What message did the prophet Hosea communicate through naming his daughter Lo-ruhamah?
o: God would make Israel the wealthiest nation in the region
Israel would immediately defeat the Assyrian army
The kingdom of Judah would merge with Northern Israel
God would no longer show pity or mercy to the house of Israel
qs.e: Hosea 1:6 explains that 'Lo-ruhamah' means 'Not Pitied', symbolizing God withholding mercy from Northern Israel due to persistent idolatry.

qs.q: Why did the prophet Jonah flee toward Tarshish instead of going to Nineveh?
o: He was terrified of being killed by Roman soldiers
He lacked the financial resources to travel overland
He believed Nineveh was an imaginary city
He did not want God to show mercy and spare the repentant Assyrians
qs.e: Jonah 4:2 reveals that Jonah fled because he knew God was gracious and merciful, and he desired judgment upon pagan Nineveh.

qs.q: In the Gospel of Luke, what sign was given to the shepherds by angels to recognize the newborn Savior?
o: A child wearing a royal golden crown in a palace
A baby wrapped in swaddling cloths and lying in a manger
A toddler reading the Torah in the Temple
A baby holding a wooden shepherd's staff
qs.e: Luke 2:12 records the angel stating: 'This will be the sign to you: You will find a Baby wrapped in swaddling cloths, lying in a manger.'
qs.tp: Birth, Infancy and Preparation of Jesus

qs.q: What did Jesus say when the Pharisees questioned Him about paying taxes to Caesar?
o: Never pay taxes to foreign pagan occupiers
Render to Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and to God the things that are God's
Pay double tribute to Caesar to demonstrate holiness
qs.e: Jesus examined a denarius bearing Caesar's image and taught that believers must fulfill both civil and spiritual obligations (Matthew 22:21).

qs.q: Which disciple doubted Jesus' resurrection until he placed his fingers into the nail marks?
qs.e: Thomas stated he would not believe unless he saw and touched Jesus' wounds, leading Jesus to appear and say 'Do not be unbelieving, but believing.'
qs.tp: Trial, Death and Resurrection of Jesus

qs.q: What deacon performed miracles in Samaria and explained the prophecy of Isaiah to an Ethiopian eunuch?
qs.e: Acts 8 describes Philip preaching Christ in Samaria and leading the Ethiopian official to faith and baptism on the road to Gaza.

qs.q: According to Paul in Galatians chapter five, what two forces are in constant conflict within a believer?
qs.e: Galatians 5:17 states: 'For the flesh lusts against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh; and these are contrary to one another.'

qs.q: How did Naaman the Syrian commander get healed of his leprosy through Elisha's instruction?
o: By offering gold and silver at the altar in Samaria
By washing in the Pool of Siloam in Jerusalem
By dipping seven times in the River Jordan
By wearing a consecrated linen robe for seven days
qs.e: 2 Kings 5 details Naaman obeying Elisha's command to wash seven times in the Jordan, resulting in his skin becoming restored like a child's.

qs.q: In the Parable of the Prodigal Son, why was the elder brother angry when his younger brother returned?
o: He wanted his younger brother thrown into prison for squandering family money
He was forced to clean the cattle stall for the banquet
The father refused to grant him any inheritance share
He felt his years of faithful service were overlooked while a feast was thrown for a rebellious son
qs.e: Luke 15:28-30 records the elder brother complaining that he had served faithfully without receiving even a young goat for a celebration.
qs.tp: Parables and Teaching on the Kingdom

qs.q: Why was the murder of Abel by Cain considered particularly grievous in biblical theology?
o: Abel was the King of Salem at the time
It was the first murder driven by envy over God's acceptance of righteous worship
It occurred inside the Tabernacle of the Lord
Cain used a sacred altar stone as a weapon
qs.e: Genesis 4 and 1 John 3:12 note that Cain killed Abel because his own works were evil while his brother's were righteous.

qs.q: How did Deborah and Barak achieve victory over Sisera's formidable army equipped with 900 iron chariots?
o: God threw the Canaanite army into panic near the River Kishon through a torrential flood
They bribed Sisera's lieutenants to abandon the battlefield
They used fire arrows to burn all 900 chariots at dawn
They made an alliance with the king of Moab
qs.e: Judges 4-5 explains that God swelled the Kishon River, miring Sisera's chariots in mud and allowing Barak's forces to rout them.

qs.q: How did Sisera meet his death after fleeing from the battlefield at Kishon?
o: He was captured by Barak and executed publicly in Kedesh
He drowned while attempting to cross the Jordan River
He fell upon his own sword inside his tent
Jael, wife of Heber the Kenite, drove a tent peg through his temple while he slept
qs.e: Judges 4:21 details Jael welcoming exhausted Sisera into her tent and driving a wooden tent peg through his temple into the ground.

qs.q: What judgment did the prophet Samuel announce against King Saul after Saul spared King Agag of Amalek?
o: Saul was condemned to die in captivity in Egypt
God rejected Saul from being king because to obey is better than sacrifice
Saul's lineage was exiled to the land of Moab
Saul was struck blind for forty days
qs.e: 1 Samuel 15:22-23 contains Samuel's famous declaration that obedience surpasses sacrifice, announcing God's rejection of Saul.

qs.q: How did David demonstrate restraint and reverence for God's anointed when hiding in the cave at En-gedi?
o: He refused to harm Saul, cutting off only a corner of Saul's robe secretly
He surrendered his weapons to Saul's guards
He fled into the desert of Paran without confronting Saul
He asked the High Priest to mediate between them
qs.e: 1 Samuel 24 records David sparing Saul's life in the cave, stating he would not stretch out his hand against the Lord's anointed.

qs.q: What tragedy struck Uzzah when King David was transporting the Ark of the Covenant to Jerusalem on a cart?
o: He was trampled by wild horses along the highway
He fell off a cliff while guiding the oxen
God struck him dead because he stretched out his hand to hold the Ark when the oxen stumbled
He was struck by lightning during a sudden thunderstorm
qs.e: 2 Samuel 6:6-7 records Uzzah touching the holy Ark directly contrary to divine law, resulting in immediate death at Nacon's threshing floor.

qs.q: What major mistake did King Solomon commit in his old age that caused God to divide his kingdom?
o: He sold the city of Jerusalem to the King of Egypt
He abolished the Aaronic priesthood in favor of foreign priests
He destroyed the Temple altar to build a military fortress
His foreign wives turned his heart away to worship pagan deities like Ashtoreth and Chemosh
qs.e: 1 Kings 11 explains that Solomon's 700 wives and 300 concubines led him into idolatry, prompting God to declare the kingdom would be torn away.

qs.q: In the Sermon on the Mount, how did Jesus reinterpretation the Old Testament law against murder?
o: He taught that unrighteous anger and insulting a brother make one liable to judgment
He abolished all civil court punishments for bodily harm
He required physical sacrifices for accidental harm
He restricted the commandment only to high priests
qs.e: Matthew 5:21-22 extends the prohibition of murder to internal anger, hatred, and abusive speech toward others.
qs.tp: Parables and Teaching on the Kingdom

qs.q: In the Parable of the Wheat and Tares, why did the master forbid his servants from pulling up the tares early?
o: Lest while gathering up the tares they root up the wheat along with them
Because the tares were valuable medical herbs
Because the servants lacked proper agricultural equipment
Because the tares would turn into wheat before harvest
qs.e: Matthew 13:28-30 records the master ordering both to grow together until harvest time to protect the good crop.
qs.tp: Parables and Teaching on the Kingdom

qs.q: What was the supernatural event that occurred at the exact moment Jesus died on the cross?
o: The curtain of the Temple was torn in two from top to bottom and an earthquake occurred
Fire fell from heaven and consumed the Roman soldiers
The sun turned red for three days and three nights
An angel descended and removed the cross from Golgotha
qs.e: Matthew 27:51 states that the Temple veil split in two, signifying open access to God's presence through Christ's death.
qs.tp: Trial, Death and Resurrection of Jesus

qs.q: How did Simon the Sorcerer react when he saw the Holy Spirit given through the laying on of the apostles' hands in Samaria?
o: He immediately challenged Peter to a public contest of magic
He reported the apostles to the Roman governor in Caesarea
He fled to Damascus to preach against the apostles
He offered money to buy the power to bestow the Holy Spirit
qs.e: Acts 8:18-19 details Simon offering money for apostolic authority, earning Peter's stern rebuke ('Your money perish with you!').

qs.q: What key issue caused a sharp disagreement between Paul and Barnabas before their second missionary journey?
o: Which city to choose as their administrative headquarters
Whether to take John Mark along after he had deserted them in Pamphylia
Whether Gentile believers should pay tithes to Antioch
Who should preach first in Jewish synagogues
qs.e: Acts 15:36-40 records that Barnabas wanted to take John Mark, but Paul resisted due to Mark's previous departure, leading them to separate.

qs.q: In Romans chapter three, how does Paul describe the universal spiritual condition of all humanity?
o: Jews are inherently sinless while Gentiles are entirely corrupted
Gentiles are justified by nature while Jews require circumcision
All have sinned and fall short of the glory of God
Humanity is divided into naturally good and naturally evil souls
qs.e: Romans 3:23 declares that both Jews and Greeks are under sin and rely entirely on divine grace for redemption.

qs.q: According to Paul in 1 Corinthians chapter 14, what is the primary purpose of exercising the gift of prophecy in church meetings?
o: Edification, exhortation, and comfort of believers
Predicting economic market trends in the city
Replacing the need for written scriptures
qs.e: 1 Corinthians 14:3 states: 'He who prophesies speaks edification and exhortation and comfort to men.'

qs.q: In James chapter five, what example from Old Testament history is used to illustrate the power of earnest prayer?
o: Moses dividing the waters of the Red Sea
Joshua commanding the sun to stand still at Gibeon
Daniel escaping unharmed from the lions' den
Elijah praying for rain to stop and then praying for it to rain again
qs.e: James 5:17-18 highlights Elijah as a man of like passions whose fervent prayer stopped rain for three and a half years.

qs.q: What was the core theological reason Jeroboam I set up golden calves at Dan and Bethel after the kingdom divided?
o: To fulfill a command given to him by Egyptian priests
To prevent northern Israelites from traveling to Jerusalem to worship and returning allegiance to Rehoboam
To celebrate the harvest festival of northern farmers
To honor the Ark of the Covenant which was lost in battle
qs.e: 1 Kings 12:26-28 records Jeroboam's political motive to retain royal power by establishing national shrines at Dan and Bethel.

qs.q: How did King Ahab obtain Naboth's vineyard after Naboth refused to sell his ancestral inheritance?
o: Ahab paid Naboth ten times the market price in gold
Ahab seized it using a decree issued by the King of Syria
Jezebel arranged false witnesses to accuse Naboth of blasphemy, leading to his stoning
Jezebel poisoned Naboth secretly in his home
qs.e: 1 Kings 21 relates Jezebel plotting Naboth's judicial murder through two worthless witnesses who falsely accused him of cursing God and the king.

qs.q: In 2 Kings chapter 19, how was Jerusalem saved when King Sennacherib of Assyria besieged the city?
o: King Hezekiah led a midnight cavalry charge that routed the Assyrians
The Egyptian army arrived and annihilated Sennacherib's forces
The angel of the Lord struck 185,000 Assyrian soldiers in their camp overnight
A massive flood swept away the Assyrian siege encampment
qs.e: 2 Kings 19:35 records that the angel of the Lord struck 185,000 in the camp of the Assyrians, forcing Sennacherib to retreat to Nineveh.

qs.q: What vision accompanied the call of the prophet Isaiah in Isaiah chapter six?
o: He saw a wheel within a wheel spinning in the clouds
He saw an almond branch and a boiling pot facing from the north
He saw the Lord high and lifted up in the Temple and a seraph touched his lips with a live coal
He saw four horsemen riding across the earth
qs.e: Isaiah 6 details Isaiah's vision of God's holiness, where a seraph purged his sin with a burning coal from the altar.

qs.q: What specific argument did the prophet Jeremiah use when he urged Judah to submit to Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon?
o: Babylonian pagan worship was superior to Judah's hypocritical rituals
Nebuchadnezzar was God's appointed instrument of judgment and resistance would bring destruction
Judah's army was larger than Babylon's and could easily conquer them
Egypt had secretly signed a treaty to defend Nebuchadnezzar
qs.e: Jeremiah 27 called Nebuchadnezzar 'God's servant', warning that nations refusing his yoke would face sword, famine, and pestilence.

qs.q: During Paul's trial before the Sanhedrin in Acts chapter 23, how did he strategically divide his accusers?
o: By declaring himself a Pharisee on trial regarding the hope of the resurrection of the dead
By accusing the High Priest of financial embezzlement of Temple funds
By demanding an immediate trial in the court of the governor of Syria
By claiming he was an official ambassador of the Roman Senate
qs.e: Acts 23:6-8 records Paul exploiting the doctrine of resurrection, causing a sharp debate between Pharisees (who believed) and Sadducees (who denied).

qs.q: In Paul's letter to the Ephesians chapter six, what spiritual weapon is identified as the Sword of the Spirit?
qs.e: Ephesians 6:17 explicitly states: 'And take the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God.'

qs.q: According to 1 Peter chapter two, what is the proper Christian attitude toward secular rulers and kings?
o: Organize underground political revolts against non-Christian rulers
Refuse to obey civil laws that are not written in the Torah
Submit for the Lord's sake, honor all men, fear God, and honor the king
Isolate completely from society to avoid civil involvement
qs.e: 1 Peter 2:13-17 instructs believers to submit to every human institution for the Lord's sake and honor civil rulers.

qs.q: In the Parable of the Unforgiving Servant, why did the master deliver the servant over to the torturers?
o: Because after being forgiven a massive debt of ten thousand talents, he refused to forgive his fellow servant a small debt
Because he stole gold from the royal treasury and fled to another country
Because he failed to double his master's money within one year
Because he refused to work during the vineyard harvest
qs.e: Matthew 18:23-35 teaches that God expects those who have received divine forgiveness to extend mercy to others.
qs.tp: Parables and Teaching on the Kingdom

qs.q: How did Daniel demonstrate unwavering faith when King Darius issued a decree prohibiting prayer to any god except the king?
o: He fled to the wilderness to pray in secret caves
He continued praying three times a day in his upper room with windows open toward Jerusalem
He organized a public protest outside the royal palace
He sent a letter of protest to the Medes and Persians court
qs.e: Daniel 6:10 records Daniel maintaining his daily prayer routine despite knowing the decree, leading to his placement in the lions' den.

qs.q: In the Parable of the Ten Virgins, what distinguished the five wise virgins from the five foolish ones?
o: The wise virgins took extra oil in flasks along with their lamps
The wise virgins remained awake all night without sleeping
The wise virgins wore expensive wedding garments
The wise virgins arrived at the banquet hall five hours early
qs.e: Matthew 25:1-13 notes that the wise brought reserve oil for their lamps, enabling them to meet the bridegroom when he arrived at midnight.
qs.tp: Parables and Teaching on the Kingdom

qs.q: In Ezekiel chapter 18, what key principle of divine justice does God establish regarding individual responsibility?
o: Children are automatically punished for four generations regardless of personal conduct
National repentance excuses individual persistent unrighteousness
The soul who sins shall die; a son shall not bear the guilt of his father nor a father the guilt of his son
Sacrifices offered by parents guarantee salvation for rebellious children
qs.e: Ezekiel 18:20 refutes the proverb about fathers eating sour grapes, asserting personal moral accountability before God.

qs.q: What theological truth does Paul articulate in Galatians chapter three regarding the purpose of the Mosaic Law?
o: The Law was intended to be the permanent path to eternal life for all nations
The Law was our tutor or guardian to lead us to Christ, so that we might be justified by faith
The Law was created by evil angels to enslave human conscience
The Law made justification by faith completely unnecessary
qs.e: Galatians 3:24 explains the historical and pedagogical role of the Law in exposing sin until Christ came.

qs.q: In 1 Peter chapter four, how are Christians instructed to view experiencing suffering for the name of Christ?
o: View it as proof that God has abandoned them to Satan
Retaliate with legal lawsuits against their persecutors
Hide their Christian identity to avoid all earthly friction
Rejoice in sharing Christ's sufferings, knowing that the Spirit of glory rests upon them
qs.e: 1 Peter 4:12-14 encourages believers not to be surprised by fiery trials but to rejoice as partakers in Christ's suffering.

qs.q: What prophecy in Micah chapter five verse two was cited by the chief priests when Herod inquired about Christ's birthplace?
o: A virgin would conceive in Nazareth and bear a son named Immanuel
Out of Bethlehem Ephrathah would come forth a Ruler who will shepherd Israel
A great light would shine upon the Galilee of the Gentiles
The Messiah would ride into Jerusalem on a donkey colt
qs.e: Matthew 2:5-6 quotes Micah 5:2 to identify Bethlehem as the prophesied birthplace of the messianic Ruler.
qs.tp: Birth, Infancy and Preparation of Jesus

qs.q: What did Paul preach at the Areopagus in Athens regarding the Unknown God?
o: The Greek gods Zeus and Apollo were manifestations of Yahweh
Philosophical debate in the Areopagus was superior to biblical faith
Idol worship was acceptable if practiced with sincere intent
God who made the world does not dwell in temples made with hands and now commands all men everywhere to repent
qs.e: Acts 17:22-31 records Paul's sermon on Mars Hill proclaiming the Creator God, the resurrection, and universal repentance.

qs.q: What covenant sign did God give to Noah after the Great Flood to promise He would never again destroy all flesh with a flood?
qs.e: Genesis 9:12-17 records God establishing the rainbow in the cloud as the perpetual sign of His covenant with Noah and earth.

qs.q: Which prophet was called by God while he was still a young boy ministering under Eli at Shiloh?
qs.e: 1 Samuel 3 records God calling Samuel three times during the night while he was serving in the Tabernacle under Eli.

qs.q: What giant Philistine champion did young David defeat with a sling and a stone?
qs.e: David confronted Goliath of Gath in the Valley of Elah, striking him in the forehead with a sling stone in the name of the Lord.

qs.q: Who was the mother of John the Baptist according to the Gospel of Luke?
qs.e: Luke 1 records that Elizabeth, wife of the priest Zechariah and cousin of Mary, gave birth to John the Baptist in her old age.
qs.tp: Birth, Infancy and Preparation of Jesus

qs.q: What miracle did Jesus perform at the wedding feast in Cana of Galilee?
qs.e: John 2:1-11 records Jesus turning water in six stone jars into choice wine, marking His first miraculous sign.

qs.q: In which city were Paul and Silas imprisoned when a sudden earthquake opened the prison doors?
qs.e: Acts 16 details Paul and Silas praying and singing hymns in prison at Philippi when an earthquake broke their chains.

qs.q: According to Paul in Ephesians chapter six, what piece of spiritual armor represents salvation?
qs.e: Ephesians 6:17 instructs believers to 'take the helmet of salvation and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God.'

qs.q: What request did young King Solomon make when God appeared to him in a dream at Gibeon?
o: Immense personal wealth and long life
An understanding heart and wisdom to govern God's people
Immediate destruction of all his political enemies
Territorial conquest over Egypt and Babylon
qs.e: 1 Kings 3:5-14 records Solomon asking for wisdom to discern between good and evil, pleasing God who also gave him riches and honor.

qs.q: How did Joseph's brothers react to his two dreams about their sheaves bowing down to his sheaf?
o: They immediately crowned him chief ruler of Hebron
They hated him even more and plotted against him
They repented of their anger and gave him gifts
They asked him to interpret their dreams as well
qs.e: Genesis 37:5-11 details Joseph sharing his dreams, which intensified his brothers' jealousy and hatred toward him.

qs.q: What sum of money did Joseph's brothers receive when they sold him to the Ishmaelite traders?
qs.e: Genesis 37:28 states that Joseph's brothers sold him to the Midianite/Ishmaelite merchants for twenty shekels of silver.

qs.q: How did God sustain Elijah at the Brook Cherith during the severe drought in Israel?
o: Manna fell around his tent every morning
Ravens brought him bread and meat morning and evening, and he drank from the brook
An angel brought him cooked meals twice daily
Widows from Samaria supplied him with oil and flour
qs.e: 1 Kings 17:2-6 describes ravens bringing Elijah bread and meat twice a day while he drank from Brook Cherith.

qs.q: What happened to the Egyptian army when they pursued the Israelites into the Red Sea?
o: An earthquake trapped them in desert canyons
The waters returned and covered Pharaoh's chariots and horsemen so that none survived
They lost their way in a sandstorm and returned to Memphis
They surrendered to Moses and joined the Israelite camp
qs.e: Exodus 14:26-28 records God causing the waters of the Red Sea to collapse upon Pharaoh's pursuing forces.

qs.q: In the Parable of the Good Samaritan, where was the wounded traveler journeying when he was attacked?
qs.e: Luke 10:30 specifies that the man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho when he fell among thieves.
qs.tp: Parables and Teaching on the Kingdom

qs.q: What miracle occurred when Peter stepped out of the boat onto the stormy Sea of Galilee toward Jesus?
o: He walked on water until he became afraid of the wind and began to sink
The storm immediately ceased before he touched the water
He was carried across the waves by two visible angels
The water instantly turned into solid ice beneath his feet
qs.e: Matthew 14:28-31 describes Peter walking on water toward Jesus, but sinking when his faith wavered before Jesus caught him.

qs.q: Who was released by Pontius Pilate instead of Jesus according to the custom at the Passover feast?
qs.e: Matthew 27:21 notes that the crowd, stirred by the chief priests, chose the notorious prisoner Barabbas to be released instead of Jesus.
qs.tp: Trial, Death and Resurrection of Jesus

qs.q: What message did the angel bring to Zechariah while he was burning incense in the Temple?
o: His wife Elizabeth would bear a son named John who would prepare the way for the Lord
The Roman Empire would be overthrown within one year
He would be appointed High Priest over all Judea
The Temple would be destroyed by foreign armies
qs.e: Luke 1:11-17 details the angel Gabriel appearing to Zechariah to announce the birth and mission of John the Baptist.
qs.tp: Birth, Infancy and Preparation of Jesus

qs.q: What condition did the Jerusalem Council impose on Gentile believers regarding food offered to idols?
o: They must eat only vegetables on holy days
They must abstain from things polluted by idols
They must purchase meat exclusively from Jewish merchants
They must burn all remaining food after sunset
qs.e: Acts 15:20, 29 lists abstaining from things offered to idols as one of the four essential requirements for Gentile believers.

qs.q: In Paul's letter to the Romans chapter six, what metaphor does he use to describe baptism into Christ?
o: Being cleansed with physical ceremonial water
Receiving royal citizenship in the Roman Empire
Being buried with Christ into death and raised to walk in newness of life
Putting on a physical linen priestly tunic
qs.e: Romans 6:3-4 teaches that baptism symbolizes burial with Christ and resurrection to a transformed moral life.

qs.q: According to James chapter one verse twenty-two, what does a person do who hears the word but does not act upon it?
o: He commits an unforgivable blasphemy against the Holy Spirit
He forfeits his civil right to vote in church assemblies
He brings immediate financial ruin upon his household
He deceives himself, like a man looking at his natural face in a mirror and immediately forgetting what he looks like
qs.e: James 1:22-24 compares a hearer who is not a doer to a man who glances in a mirror and forgets his appearance.

qs.q: How did God manifest His presence to Moses at Mount Horeb during his initial call?
o: In a quiet whisper inside a dark desert cave
As a pillar of cloud hovering over the Red Sea
Through an angel carrying golden tablets of law
In a flame of fire out of the midst of a bush that burned without being consumed
qs.e: Exodus 3:2-4 describes Moses seeing the bush burning with fire without being consumed, where God called him to deliver Israel.

qs.q: What plague finally compelled Pharaoh to release the Israelites from Egyptian bondage?
o: The death of all firstborn sons and livestock in Egypt
The plague of hail mixed with fire
The plague of dense darkness lasting three days
The turning of the Nile River into blood
qs.e: Exodus 12:29-32 records the fatal tenth plague striking all firstborn in Egypt, causing Pharaoh to command the Israelites to depart.

qs.q: What memorial was erected after the Israelites crossed the River Jordan under Joshua's leadership?
o: A golden altar constructed at Jericho
A high wooden tower built on Mount Ebal
A pillar of salt placed near the Dead Sea
Twelve stones taken from the middle of the Jordan set up at Gilgal
qs.e: Joshua 4:1-9 describes setting up twelve stones from the Jordan riverbed at Gilgal as a perpetual testimony of the miraculous crossing.

qs.q: Why was Achan executed along with his family after the battle of Jericho?
o: He refused to march around the city walls on the seventh day
He leaked battle plans to the king of Ai
He struck down a Gibeonite messenger
He stole devoted items including a Babylonian garment, silver, and gold from Jericho contrary to God's command
qs.e: Joshua 7 details Achan's sin of taking forbidden spoils from Jericho, causing Israel's initial defeat at Ai and leading to his judgment at Achor.

qs.q: How did Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego display extraordinary faith before King Nebuchadnezzar?
o: They refused to worship the golden image, affirming God could save them but even if He did not, they would not bow
They led a armed revolt inside the city of Babylon
They fled to Jerusalem under cover of darkness
They bribed the furnace guards to extinguish the flames
qs.e: Daniel 3:16-18 records their steadfast refusal to compromise worship, declaring God's power to deliver them from the fiery furnace.

qs.q: What specific sin of Israel did the prophet Amos condemn regarding the treatment of the poor in markets?
o: Refusing to build housing projects in Samaria
Selling the righteous for silver and the needy for a pair of sandals, using dishonest scales
Exporting grain to Egypt during regional famines
Forcing Levites to work in agricultural vineyards
qs.e: Amos 2:6 and 8:5 expose oppressive merchants who cheated the poor with rigged scales and bought needy debtors cheaply.

qs.q: What miracle occurred at the tomb of Lazarus in Bethany after he had been dead for four days?
o: An angel rolled away the stone and brought him out in white robes
Lazarus walked out silently while the mourners slept
A heavenly light consumed the tomb and restored his youth
Jesus called him by name and he came out bound in gravecloths
qs.e: John 11:43-44 records Jesus shouting 'Lazarus, come forth!', demonstrating His authority over death.

qs.q: In the Parable of the Talents, why was the servant who received one talent condemned by his master?
o: He hid his talent in the ground out of fear and slothfulness without putting it to work
He lost all the money in foolish business investments
He gave the money to foreign merchants in Tyre
He spent the talent on luxurious living and banquets
qs.e: Matthew 25:24-30 details the master rebuking the wicked and lazy servant for failing to trade or deposit the money for interest.
qs.tp: Parables and Teaching on the Kingdom

qs.q: What theological explanation did Peter give on Pentecost regarding Jesus' resurrection?
o: God raised Him up because it was impossible for death to hold Him, fulfilling David's Psalm
Jesus escaped the tomb through a secret underground tunnel
The Roman soldiers hid His body to prevent civil unrest
The resurrection was merely a spiritual vision seen by apostles
qs.e: Acts 2:24-31 cites Psalm 16 to prove that God raised Jesus, whose body did not see corruption in the grave.
qs.tp: The Early Church and Holy Spirit

qs.q: How did Cornelius the Roman centurion in Caesarea learn to send for Peter at Joppa?
o: He read a letter sent by the apostles in Jerusalem
Philip the evangelist told him during a dinner gathering
An angel of God appeared to him in a vision during prayer and instructed him
He received a dream while sleeping in his military barracks
qs.e: Acts 10:1-8 describes Cornelius, a devout God-fearing man, receiving an angelic visit commanding him to send men for Simon Peter.

qs.q: In 1 Corinthians chapter twelve, what does Paul teach about the distribution of spiritual gifts?
o: Gifts are earned strictly through senior church leadership rank
The same Spirit distributes individual gifts to each person as He wills for the common good
Every believer receives identical spiritual gifts upon baptism
Spiritual gifts are inherited through family bloodlines
qs.e: 1 Corinthians 12:11 emphasizes that spiritual gifts are imparted sovereignly by the Holy Spirit according to His divine wisdom.

qs.q: What contrast does Paul draw in Galatians chapter five between works of the flesh and fruit of the Spirit?
o: Works of the flesh are required for civil life, while fruit of the Spirit is only for private prayer
Works of the flesh lead to conflict and corruption, while fruit of the Spirit produces righteous communal life
Works of the flesh are practiced by Jewish believers, while fruit of the Spirit is for Gentiles
Works of the flesh are physical, while fruit of the Spirit is non-existent
qs.e: Galatians 5:19-23 contrasts destructive selfish behaviors (immorality, idolatry, outbursts of wrath) with godly virtues produced by the Spirit.

qs.q: In 2 Thessalonians chapter three, why did Paul remind believers of his own manual labor among them?
o: To prove that tentmaking was superior to apostolic preaching
To earn money to buy Roman citizenship for his companions
To set an example of hard work so as not to be a financial burden to anyone
To purchase real estate in Thessalonica for a church building
qs.e: 2 Thessalonians 3:7-9 explains that Paul worked night and day making tents to offer a model of self-sufficiency and diligence.

qs.q: According to James chapter two, how did Rahab the harlot demonstrate justification through works?
o: By receiving the Israelite spies with hospitality and sending them out another way
By offering animal sacrifices on the city wall of Jericho
By tearing down the pagan idols in her hometown
By fasting for forty days before the wall fell
qs.e: James 2:25 cites Rahab assisting the messengers as concrete evidence of her active, living faith.

qs.q: What assurance does Paul give in Romans chapter eight regarding the love of God in Christ Jesus?
o: Neither death, life, angels, principalities, nor any created thing can separate us from God's love
Believers will never experience physical sickness or economic poverty
God will immediately destroy all secular governments that oppose Christians
Salvation guarantees instant political power in Rome
qs.e: Romans 8:38-39 triumphantly declares that no circumstance or cosmic power can sever believers from the love of God in Christ.

qs.q: Why was the covenant between David and Jonathan considered extraordinary in Israelite history?
o: They agreed to divide the kingdom of Israel into two equal sovereign states
Jonathan betrayed his father Saul to lead David's army directly
Jonathan, as Saul's heir, unselfishly recognized David as God's chosen king and protected him from Saul's wrath
They built a joint sanctuary at Shiloh for all twelve tribes
qs.e: 1 Samuel 18-20 records Jonathan's deep covenant love and loyalty to David despite knowing David would succeed Saul on the throne.

qs.q: What specific event triggered the northern ten tribes to revolt against Rehoboam, leading to the schism of the kingdom?
o: Rehoboam ordered all northern altars torn down by force
Rehoboam appointed Egyptian priests over the tribe of Ephraim
Rehoboam moved the royal capital from Jerusalem to Hebron
Rehoboam rejected the elders' advice and vowed to make the people's taxation and labor heavier than Solomon's
qs.e: 1 Kings 12:1-16 details Rehoboam adopting the young men's harsh advice ('my little finger shall be thicker than my father's waist'), causing Jeroboam and the 10 tribes to rebel.

qs.q: What central theme did the prophet Ezekiel communicate through his allegory of the watchman in Ezekiel chapter 33?
o: Physical military walls are the only guaranteed defense for Jerusalem
A watchman must execute criminals on the spot without trial
Only ordained Levites are permitted to serve as city sentinels
The watchman is obligated to warn the wicked; if he fails, their blood is required at his hand
qs.e: Ezekiel 33:1-9 outlines the spiritual responsibility of the prophet to proclaim divine warnings faithfully to save lives.

qs.q: In the Gospel of John, what was the primary significance of Jesus washing the disciples' feet during the Last Supper?
o: He established a ceremonial washing required before eating Passover lamb
He fulfilled a Roman legal requirement for dining in upper rooms
He modeled servant leadership and radical humility, commanding His followers to serve one another
He demonstrated how to prepare bodies for immediate burial
qs.e: John 13:1-17 details Jesus performing the task of a slave to teach His disciples that greatness in His kingdom comes through humble service.

qs.q: What accusation did the Jewish leaders bring against Stephen before the Sanhedrin in Acts chapter six?
o: Organizing an armed insurrection against Roman garrisons in Judea
Stealing gold vessels from the Temple treasury
Practicing sorcery in the market of Jerusalem
Speaking blasphemous words against the Holy Place and the Law of Moses
qs.e: Acts 6:11-14 notes that false witnesses accused Stephen of speaking against the Temple and claiming Jesus would change Mosaic customs.

qs.q: How does Paul contrast the First Adam and the Last Adam (Christ) in 1 Corinthians chapter 15?
o: The first Adam brought sin and death to humanity, whereas Christ brings righteousness and resurrection life
The first Adam was a king in Babylon, while Christ was born in Nazareth
The first Adam created angels, while Christ created earthly animals
The first Adam abolished the Law, while Christ restored Mosaic sacrifices
qs.e: 1 Corinthians 15:21-22, 45 contrasts Adam as the head of fallen humanity with Christ as the giver of eternal life.

qs.q: In 1 Corinthians chapter eight, what rule does Paul give regarding eating meat previously offered to pagan idols?
o: Eating idol meat permanently revokes a person's salvation
All believers must inspect butcher shops daily under Levitical law
Believers have liberty, but should abstain if eating causes a weaker brother's conscience to stumble
Idol meat is holy and should be consumed in public feasts
qs.e: 1 Corinthians 8:9-13 establishes the principle of Christian love limiting personal liberty to prevent causing spiritually weaker believers to fall.

qs.q: In 2 Corinthians chapter nine, what spirit does Paul say God loves when believers contribute financial gifts?
o: God values only those who give their entire monthly income
God demands exact record-keeping presented at public altars
God loves a cheerful giver who gives not grudgingly or out of compulsion
God approves giving done solely to gain public honor
qs.e: 2 Corinthians 9:7 teaches: 'So let each one give as he purposes in his heart, not grudgingly or of necessity; for God loves a cheerful giver.'

qs.q: In the Sermon on the Mount, what did Jesus teach regarding retaliating against an evil person who slaps your right cheek?
o: Demand exact financial restitution under civil court law
Strike him back twice as hard to maintain personal honor
Turn to him the other cheek also, overcoming evil with good
Call down divine judgment and lightning upon his house
qs.e: Matthew 5:38-39 reinterprets 'an eye for an eye', advocating non-retaliation, radical patience, and love for enemies.
qs.tp: Parables and Teaching on the Kingdom

qs.q: What revelation did God give to the prophet Habakkuk regarding how the righteous shall live during times of national distress?
o: The righteous shall rely on military fortifications in Jerusalem
The righteous shall flee to Egypt for safety
The righteous shall offer double daily sacrifices
The righteous shall live by his faith and faithfulness
qs.e: Habakkuk 2:4 declares that while the proud soul is not upright, 'the just shall live by his faith', a key text quoted in Romans, Galatians, and Hebrews.

qs.q: How did King Saul meet his end during the disastrous battle against the Philistines on Mount Gilboa?
o: He was captured alive and executed in the temple of Dagon
He was struck down in single combat by the king of Gaza
Critically wounded by Philistine archers, he fell upon his own sword after his armor-bearer refused to kill him
He escaped to Ramah where he died of old age
qs.e: 1 Samuel 31:1-6 records Saul committing suicide on Mount Gilboa to avoid being captured and abused by the uncircumcised Philistines.

qs.q: What key messianic prophecy in Jeremiah chapter 31 verse 31 contrasts the Mosaic Covenant with the New Covenant?
o: The New Covenant will restore animal sacrifices in an expanded Jerusalem Temple
The New Covenant will enforce strict ceremonial laws exclusively upon Jews
The New Covenant will make the nation of Israel ruler over Rome
The New Covenant will be written directly on human hearts and minds, bringing complete forgiveness of sin
qs.e: Jeremiah 31:31-34 foretells an internal transformation where God writes His law upon hearts, forming the basis of Christian theology in Hebrews.

qs.q: In Paul's defense before King Agrippa II in Acts chapter 26, how did he summarize the core content of his gospel preaching?
o: Demanding that King Agrippa immediately abdicate his royal throne
Saying nothing beyond what the Prophets and Moses said would happen: that Christ would suffer and be first to rise from the dead
Announcing that Roman law was abolished throughout all provinces
Proclaiming that Gentiles must adopt Jewish dietary restrictions
qs.e: Acts 26:22-23 shows Paul asserting full continuity between his Christian gospel and the Old Testament Scriptures before Agrippa and Festus.

qs.q: In Romans chapter four, how does Paul demonstrate that Abraham was justified by faith before circumcision?
o: Abraham was circumcised in Egypt before God ever spoke to him
Circumcision was only introduced under King Solomon centuries later
Genesis recorded Abraham's faith credited as righteousness years before he received the sign of circumcision
Abraham refused circumcision throughout his entire lifetime
qs.e: Romans 4:9-12 points out the chronological timeline in Genesis 15 and 17, proving faith preceded circumcision, making Abraham father of all believers.

qs.q: What profound christological claim is made in Colossians chapter one regarding Christ's relation to creation?
o: He was the first created angel who later evolved into humanity
He is the image of the invisible God, and by Him all things in heaven and earth were created and held together
He created only spiritual beings while God created physical matter
He inherited creation as a reward after His resurrection
qs.e: Colossians 1:15-17 affirms Christ's pre-eminence, deity, and active role as Creator and Sustainer of the entire cosmos.

qs.q: In 1 Timothy chapter two, why does Paul urge that supplications and prayers be made for kings and all in authority?
o: To guarantee that Christian leaders are appointed as civil judges
To eliminate all civil taxation imposed on local churches
So that believers may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and reverence
To force rulers to convert to Christianity under threat of divine wrath
qs.e: 1 Timothy 2:1-2 instructs prayer for civil rulers to ensure social peace, stability, and freedom for gospel witness.

qs.q: Which son of Jacob was sold into Egypt by his brothers out of jealousy?
qs.e: Genesis 37 records Joseph's ten older brothers selling him to Midianite traders because of his dreams and their father's favoritism.

qs.q: What river did the Israelites cross on dry ground under Joshua's command to enter Canaan?
qs.e: Joshua 3 describes the waters of the Jordan River parting as soon as the priests carrying the Ark touched the river's edge.

qs.q: Who was the mother of King Solomon?
qs.e: Bathsheba, formerly the wife of Uriah the Hittite, became David's wife and bore him Solomon.

qs.q: What city was Jesus entering when crowds laid palm branches and garments on the road shouting Hosanna?
qs.e: Matthew 21 records Jesus' Triumphal Entry into Jerusalem riding on a donkey colt amidst joyful acclamations.
qs.tp: Trial, Death and Resurrection of Jesus

qs.q: Which apostle delivered the stirring sermon on Pentecost that resulted in about three thousand converts?
qs.e: Acts 2 details Peter explaining the outpouring of the Holy Spirit as the fulfillment of Joel's prophecy, resulting in 3,000 souls baptized.
qs.tp: The Early Church and Holy Spirit

qs.q: In which city did Paul deliver his speech regarding the Unknown God at the Areopagus?
qs.e: Acts 17 records Paul addressing the Greek philosophers at Mars Hill (Areopagus) in Athens after observing their altar to an unknown god.

qs.q: According to Paul in 1 Corinthians chapter thirteen, what happens if one speaks with tongues of men and angels but lacks love?
o: He becomes a noisy gong or a clanging cymbal
He is appointed chief apostle over Gentiles
qs.e: 1 Corinthians 13:1 emphasizes that spiritual eloquence without divine love is completely meaningless and hollow.

qs.q: How did Jacob obtain the birthright of his twin brother Esau in Genesis chapter twenty-five?
o: He defeated Esau in wrestling at Peniel
He paid Esau thirty shekels of silver
He forged a legal scroll approved by Isaac
He traded a bowl of red lentil stew for it when Esau was famished
qs.e: Genesis 25:29-34 details Esau despising his birthright by exchanging it for a meal of bread and lentil stew.

qs.q: What sign did God give to Gideon using a fleece of wool to confirm victory over Midian?
o: The fleece turned from white to purple overnight
Fire fell from heaven and consumed the fleece on a rock
First the fleece was wet with dew while the ground was dry, then the fleece was dry while the ground was wet
The fleece expanded to cover the entire threshing floor
qs.e: Judges 6:36-40 details Gideon requesting double dew signs on a woolen fleece to confirm God's promise to save Israel through him.

qs.q: How did young David react when Goliath cursed him by his pagan gods in the Valley of Elah?
o: He retreated to consult King Saul in his royal tent
He declared he came in the name of the Lord of hosts, whom Goliath had defied
He cursed Goliath back using pagan formulas
He asked the Philistines to send a different champion
qs.e: 1 Samuel 17:45 records David's courageous proclamation: 'You come to me with a sword... but I come to you in the name of the Lord of hosts.'

qs.q: Why was Queen Vashti deposed by King Ahasuerus in the Book of Esther?
o: She attempted to poison Haman during a royal feast
She secretly invited Jewish leaders into the royal palace
She stole royal jewels from the Persian treasury
She refused to obey the king's command to display her beauty before his banqueting guests
qs.e: Esther 1:10-19 records Vashti refusing the royal summons, prompting her removal so that other wives in Persia would respect their husbands.

qs.q: What vision did the prophet Ezekiel see beside the River Chebar in Ezekiel chapter one?
o: A throne chariot of God surrounded by four living creatures and wheels within wheels
A golden bowl overflowing with burning incense
A massive bronze altar destroyed by invading Babylonians
A valley of dry bones coming back to life
qs.e: Ezekiel 1 describes the prophet's majestic inaugural vision of God's glory above the living creatures and spinning wheels in exile.

qs.q: In the Gospel of Matthew, what gifts were brought by the Wise Men from the East to honor the young child Jesus?
o: Silver, fine linen, and olive oil
Diamonds, royal robes, and cedar wood
qs.e: Matthew 2:11 records the Magi opening their treasures and presenting Jesus with gold (royalty), frankincense (deity), and myrrh (death).
qs.tp: Birth, Infancy and Preparation of Jesus

qs.q: How did Jesus heal the blind man named Bartimaeus sitting by the road outside Jericho?
o: Jesus washed his eyes with water from the Jordan River seven times
Jesus said 'Go your way; your faith has made you well', and immediately he received sight
Jesus touched his eyes with consecrated oil from the Temple
Jesus commanded him to perform thirty days of ritual washings
qs.e: Mark 10:46-52 details Bartimaeus crying out 'Son of David, have mercy on me!', where Jesus commended his faith and restored his sight.

qs.q: In the Parable of the Rich Fool, why did God call the wealthy land owner a fool?
o: He accumulated physical wealth for himself while being spiritually bankrupt toward God, dying that very night
He built small barns that collapsed in a rainstorm
He refused to pay his farm laborers their daily wages
He sold his crops to foreign merchants at loss
qs.e: Luke 12:16-21 exposes the folly of hoarding earthly wealth while ignoring eternity ('Fool! This night your soul will be required of you').
qs.tp: Parables and Teaching on the Kingdom

qs.q: What took place during the Transfiguration of Jesus on the high mountain?
o: Fire fell from heaven and consumed the Roman garrison below
A choir of seraphim sang songs while Peter slept soundly
His face shone like the sun, His clothes became dazzling white, and Moses and Elijah appeared talking with Him
Jesus was crowned earthly King of Israel by twelve angels
qs.e: Matthew 17:1-8 records Jesus revealing His divine glory alongside Moses (the Law) and Elijah (the Prophets).

qs.q: How did the early Jerusalem church respond when Peter was arrested and imprisoned by King Herod Agrippa I?
o: They hired attorneys to argue his case in Roman court
They organized a riot to break open the prison gates
Earnest prayer was offered continuously to God by the church for him
They paid a large ransom to Herod's soldiers
qs.e: Acts 12:5 notes that while Peter was kept in prison, constant prayer was made to God by the church for his release.
qs.tp: The Early Church and Holy Spirit

qs.q: What work did Paul, Aquila, and Priscilla engage in to support themselves while preaching in Corinth?
qs.e: Acts 18:1-3 states that Paul lived and worked with Aquila and Priscilla in Corinth because they were tentmakers by trade.

qs.q: In Romans chapter twelve, how are believers instructed to respond to enemies who cause them harm?
o: Report them immediately to church elders for public cursing
If your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him a drink, overcoming evil with good
Sever all social and commercial communication
qs.e: Romans 12:19-21 commands believers never to avenge themselves but to conquer evil by extending kindness.

qs.q: Why did Jacob flee from his home in Canaan to his uncle Laban in Haran?
o: Because a severe famine struck the land of Canaan
Because Esau was plotting to kill him after Jacob stole Isaac's blessing
Because King Abimelech banished his family from Gerar
Because he wanted to study priesthood in Mesopotamia
qs.e: Genesis 27:41-45 records Rebekah advising Jacob to flee to Haran until Esau's murderous fury subsided.

qs.q: What dream did Jacob experience at Bethel while sleeping with his head on a stone?
o: Seven fat cows consumed by seven lean cows
A ladder set up on earth reaching to heaven with angels ascending and descending
The sun, moon, and eleven stars bowing down to him
A burning chariot carrying a glowing scroll
qs.e: Genesis 28:10-17 records Jacob's vision at Bethel where God reaffirmed the Abrahamic covenant with him.

qs.q: How did Moses react when he descended Mount Sinai and saw the Israelites worshiping the golden calf?
o: He fled back up the mountain to hide from the people
He joined Aaron in offering sacrifices on the golden altar
He commanded the Levites to build a wooden fence around the calf
In anger he threw down the two stone tablets breaking them, destroyed the calf, and made the people drink its powdered water
qs.e: Exodus 32:19-20 describes Moses breaking the stone tablets at the foot of Mount Sinai and grinding the idol to dust.

qs.q: Why did God prevent Moses from leading the Israelites across the Jordan into the Promised Land?
o: Because he refused to write the Book of Deuteronomy
Because he struck the rock twice at Meribah in anger instead of speaking to it as God commanded
Because he allowed Aaron to build the Tabernacle without permission
Because he was physically too weak to march into battle
qs.e: Numbers 20:7-12 details Moses disobeying God's explicit instruction by striking the rock in anger, failing to hallow God before the assembly.

qs.q: What strategy did Rahab the harlot use to protect the two Israelite spies sent by Joshua to Jericho?
o: She disguised them as Canaanite priests inside the city temple
She lowered them into a deep dry well in the city square
She hid them under stalks of flax on her roof and misled the king's pursuers
She helped them fight the king's guards with swords
qs.e: Joshua 2 details Rahab hiding the spies on her roof, securing an oath that her family would be spared when Jericho fell.

qs.q: How was Jericho captured by Joshua and the Israelite army according to Joshua chapter six?
o: They built siege mounds and battered down the gates with rams
They cut off the city's water supply until the citizens surrendered
They launched fire arrows over the walls at midnight
They marched around the city once a day for six days and seven times on the seventh day, blowing trumpets until the walls collapsed
qs.e: Joshua 6 describes the miraculous fall of Jericho's walls following divine instructions of marching, trumpet blowing, and shouting.

qs.q: What miraculous sign confirmed the appointment of Aaron's rod as High Priest during Korah's rebellion?
o: Aaron's wooden rod sprouted, budded, produced blossoms, and yielded ripe almonds overnight
Aaron's rod turned into a bronze serpent inside the Tabernacle
Aaron's rod caught fire without burning
Aaron's rod parted the waters of the Jordan River
qs.e: Numbers 17:1-11 records God vindicating Aaron's priesthood by causing his rod to blossom and bear almonds inside the Tent of Testimony.

qs.q: In the Parable of the Laborers in the Vineyard, why did the workers hired early in the morning complain against the landowner?
o: Because those hired at the eleventh hour received the same wage (a denarius) as those who worked all day
Because the master refused to pay them any wages at sunset
Because they were forced to work three extra hours past sunset
Because the master paid the evening workers double wages
qs.e: Matthew 20:1-16 illustrates God's sovereign grace, where the master paid everyone equally as agreed, exposing envy among earlier workers.
qs.tp: Parables and Teaching on the Kingdom

qs.q: What argument did Paul make in 1 Corinthians chapter fifteen to defend the reality of Christ's resurrection?
o: The resurrection was a figurative metaphor for personal moral improvement
If Christ is not risen, our preaching is empty, your faith is futile, and you are still in your sins
Only apostles needed to believe in the resurrection to hold office
Resurrection is impossible for human bodies but easy for angels
qs.e: 1 Corinthians 15:12-19 highlights that the physical resurrection of Christ is the indispensable foundation of Christian faith.
qs.tp: Trial, Death and Resurrection of Jesus

qs.q: How did an angel deliver Peter from prison on the night before King Herod Agrippa planned to execute him?
o: An angel shone in the cell, struck Peter's side, broke his chains, and guided him past guards through iron gates
An earthquake destroyed the prison wall allowing Peter to run
The angel struck all Roman guards blind for seven days
The angel transformed Peter into an invisible spirit
qs.e: Acts 12:6-11 details Peter's miraculous release, where his chains fell off and the prison iron gate opened automatically.
qs.tp: The Early Church and Holy Spirit

qs.q: In 1 Corinthians chapter ten, what warning does Paul give believers regarding Israel's wilderness history?
o: Israel's wilderness history applies only to ethnic Jewish Christians
Their experiences were written as examples for us so that we should not crave evil things or commit idolatry
Wilderness trials prove that God will never judge church members
Believers should physically reenact the forty-year desert journey
qs.e: 1 Corinthians 10:1-11 uses Israel's failures (idolatry, immorality, testing God) as solemn warnings against spiritual complacency.

qs.q: According to Paul in Galatians chapter two, why did he publicly confront Peter (Cephas) at Antioch?
o: Because Peter taught that animal sacrifices must be resumed in Jerusalem
Because Peter refused to preach to Jewish audiences in Syrian synagogues
Because Peter demanded financial tribute from Gentile churches
Because Peter withdrew from eating with Gentile believers out of fear of the circumcision group
qs.e: Galatians 2:11-14 records Paul rebuking Peter for hypocritical behavior that compromised gospel truth regarding Jew-Gentile unity.

qs.q: In James chapter three, how does the author describe the destructive power of the human tongue?
o: It is a small member that boasts great things, set on fire by hell, capable of defiling the whole body
It is an incurable physical disease that affects only older teachers
It is an organ that cannot be controlled even by divine grace
It is harmless in speech as long as physical actions are righteous
qs.e: James 3:1-12 compares the tongue to a horse's bit, a ship's rudder, and a small spark that sets a vast forest ablaze.

qs.q: What guidance does James chapter five give regarding a church member who is physically sick?
o: Isolate the sick person completely from the congregation for seven days
Send financial tribute to the Temple in Jerusalem for a blessing
Call for the elders of the church to pray over him and anoint him with oil in the name of the Lord
Require the sick person to fast for fourteen consecutive days
qs.e: James 5:14-15 promises that the prayer of faith will save the sick person and the Lord will raise him up.

qs.q: According to Paul in Romans chapter eight, what role does the Holy Spirit play during a believer's prayers?
o: The Spirit translates prayers into ancient Hebrew dialects
The Spirit helps our weakness and intercedes for us with groanings that cannot be expressed in words
The Spirit prevents believers from experiencing any emotional sorrow
The Spirit writes down all prayers on heavenly parchment scrolls
qs.e: Romans 8:26-27 teaches that when we do not know what to pray for as we ought, the Spirit intercedes according to God's will.

qs.q: What was the spiritual significance of God changing Abram's name to Abraham in Genesis chapter seventeen?
o: It marked his official coronation as King of the Canaanites
It indicated his total separation from his son Isaac
It signified his divine designation as the father of a multitude of nations under the covenant of circumcision
It rewarded him for building a fortress in Hebron
qs.e: Genesis 17:4-8 explains that 'Abraham' means 'father of a multitude', establishing circumcision as the perpetual covenant sign.

qs.q: How did Samson lose his supernatural physical strength according to Judges chapter sixteen?
o: He drank wine during a feast with Philistine rulers
He touched a human corpse contrary to Levite ritual law
He was struck by lightning on top of a mountain in Gaza
Delilah coaxed him into revealing his Nazirite vow, and she had his seven braids of hair shaved off while he slept
qs.e: Judges 16:15-20 records Delilah betraying Samson by shaving his hair, causing the Lord's power to depart from him.

qs.q: What dramatic event ended Elijah's earthly ministry before Elisha succeeded him?
o: He was struck down in battle against Hazael king of Syria
A chariot of fire with horses of fire appeared and Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven
He died of old age inside a cave on Mount Horeb
He was taken across the Red Sea in an angelic vessel
qs.e: 2 Kings 2:11 records Elijah being taken up into heaven in a whirlwind as Elisha watched and received his mantle.

qs.q: What central problem in Israelite society did the prophet Hosea address through his prophetic message?
o: Spiritual adultery characterized by idol worship of Baal and forsaking Yahweh's covenant love
Military cowardice during battles against the Philistines
Failure to rebuild the city walls of Samaria
Using incorrect currency denominations in local trade
qs.e: Hosea 2-4 depicts Israel's unfaithfulness to God as spiritual harlotry, calling the nation to return in repentance.

qs.q: In the Sermon on the Mount, how did Jesus contrast hypocritical almsgiving with true spiritual devotion?
o: Hypocrites sound trumpets in synagogues to be honored by men, whereas true giving must be done in secret so the Father rewards
Hypocrites give gold while true believers give only copper coins
Hypocrites give only to foreigners while true believers give to family
Hypocrites give on sabbaths while true believers give on weekdays
qs.e: Matthew 6:1-4 teaches that charitable giving must not be done for public display, but quietly before God.
qs.tp: Parables and Teaching on the Kingdom

qs.q: During Jesus' trial before Pontius Pilate, why did the chief priests insist on crucifying Him despite Pilate finding no crime?
o: They proved Jesus had led an armed revolt against the Roman garrison
They produced legal scrolls showing Jesus was born in Babylon
They claimed that anyone making himself a king speaks against Caesar, pressuring Pilate politically
They paid Pilate a large bribe in gold talents
qs.e: John 19:12-15 records the Jewish leaders manipulating Pilate by shouting: 'If you let this Man go, you are not Caesar's friend!'
qs.tp: Trial, Death and Resurrection of Jesus

qs.q: How did Philip the evangelist explain Isaiah chapter 53 verse seven to the Ethiopian eunuch on the road to Gaza?
o: He explained it was a historical account describing King David's military trials
He told him the passage applied strictly to the prophet Isaiah's personal life
He advised him to seek interpretation from priests in Jerusalem
He began at that Scripture and preached the good news about Jesus as the suffering lamb
qs.e: Acts 8:32-35 describes Philip using the prophecy of the led-to-slaughter sheep to present Christ to the official.

qs.q: In 1 Corinthians chapter six, why does Paul urge believers to flee sexual immorality?
o: Because the believer's body is a temple of the Holy Spirit who dwells within, bought with a price
Because sexual immorality was prohibited by Roman civil statues
Because physical sins affect only external reputation and not the soul
Because immorality reduces physical strength in church work
qs.e: 1 Corinthians 6:18-20 asserts that believers' bodies belong to God and ought to glorify Him in purity.

qs.q: In Ephesians chapter four, what primary purpose is given for Christ bestowing gifts of apostles, prophets, evangelists, pastors, and teachers?
o: For the equipping of the saints for the work of ministry, for the edifying of the body of Christ
To establish an earthly political government over all nations
To eliminate the need for personal Bible study among members
To replace civil magistrates in Roman courts
qs.e: Ephesians 4:11-13 explains that ministry leaders are gifted to train all believers toward spiritual maturity and unity.

qs.q: According to Paul in 1 Thessalonians chapter five, how will the Day of the Lord come upon the unsuspecting world?
o: Like a thief in the night, bringing sudden destruction like labor pains on a pregnant woman
With prior warning published in all major cities seven years ahead
Gradually over a period of ten thousand peaceful years
Only during a solar eclipse visible in Jerusalem
qs.e: 1 Thessalonians 5:1-3 warns that the Lord's return will be unexpected for those living in spiritual darkness.

qs.q: What fundamental principle regarding civil government is established in Romans chapter thirteen verse seven?
o: Christians are exempt from paying tariffs to non-Christian rulers
Civil taxes should be paid only when governments are completely sinless
Believers should pay taxes to local churches instead of secular authorities
Render to all their due: taxes to whom taxes are due, customs to whom customs, fear to whom fear, honor to whom honor
qs.e: Romans 13:7 instructs Christians to honor civic duties, including paying taxes and respecting lawful civil authorities.

qs.q: What theological significance attaches to God making coats of skins to clothe Adam and Eve in Genesis chapter three verse twenty-one?
o: It demonstrated human superiority over wild animals in Eden
It established the Levitical wool trade in ancient Canaan
It signaled that physical clothes were permanent punishment
It pointed to the necessity of animal blood sacrifice to cover human nakedness and sin
qs.e: Genesis 3:21 records God replacing frail fig leaves with skins, foreshadowing redemption through sacrificial blood.

qs.q: In Romans chapter seven, how does Paul use the law of marriage to illustrate a believer's freedom from the Mosaic Law?
o: Divorce is mandatory for anyone who converts to Christianity
Marriage vows are automatically voided upon Christian baptism
The Mosaic Law applies only to married citizens in Israel
A married woman is bound to her husband while he lives, but if he dies she is free to marry another; similarly, believers died to the Law through Christ
qs.e: Romans 7:1-6 uses the marital binding principle to demonstrate that death in Christ terminates legalistic bondage under the Law.

qs.q: What profound paradox regarding divine power is declared by Paul in 2 Corinthians chapter twelve verse nine?
o: Divine power is granted only to those who possess vast financial wealth
Human physical weakness is proof of unforgiven sin
My grace is sufficient for you, for My strength is made perfect in weakness
Miraculous power automatically eliminates all physical infirmities
qs.e: 2 Corinthians 12:9 records Christ's response to Paul's thorn in the flesh, revealing that divine power shines through human limitations.

qs.q: What was the core decision of the Jerusalem Council in Acts chapter fifteen regarding the law of circumcision for Gentile converts?
o: Gentiles are saved through the grace of the Lord Jesus exactly as Jews are, without needing circumcision
Gentiles must be circumcised within eight days of conversion
Gentile men must be circumcised, but women are exempt
Circumcision was made mandatory for all church officers only
qs.e: Acts 15:10-11 records Peter affirming salvation by grace alone through faith for both Jew and Gentile without legalistic burdens.

qs.q: In 1 Peter chapter five, how are elders instructed to shepherd the flock of God committed to their care?
o: Govern with absolute dictatorial authority over all church property
Charge mandatory consultation fees for spiritual advice
Shepherd willingly and eagerly, not for dishonest gain or lording it over others, but as examples to the flock
Enforce strict civil penalties on disobedient congregation members
qs.e: 1 Peter 5:1-4 outlines servant leadership guidelines for church elders under the Chief Shepherd.

qs.q: What body of water did Moses stretch out his hand over to allow the Israelites to escape from Egypt?
qs.e: Exodus 14 records God driving back the sea with a strong east wind after Moses stretched out his hand.

qs.q: Which young prophet was anointed by Samuel at Bethlehem to be king while Saul was still reigning?
qs.e: 1 Samuel 16 describes Samuel visiting Jesse's family in Bethlehem and anointing David, the youngest son who was tending sheep.

qs.q: What weapon did the boy David use to slay Goliath in battle?
o: A sling and a smooth stone
qs.e: 1 Samuel 17:49 records David embedding a sling stone into Goliath's forehead, bringing the giant down.

qs.q: What city was Jesus raised in after returning from Egypt with Joseph and Mary?
qs.e: Matthew 2:23 records that Joseph settled his family in Nazareth in Galilee, fulfilling that Jesus would be called a Nazarene.
qs.tp: Birth, Infancy and Preparation of Jesus

qs.q: Who was the Roman centurion in Caesarea whose family became the first Gentile converts to receive the Holy Spirit?
qs.e: Acts 10 details Cornelius, a God-fearing centurion, inviting Peter to preach to his household, where the Holy Spirit fell upon them.

qs.q: Which fruit of the Spirit listed in Galatians chapter five refers to self-restraint and discipline?
qs.e: Galatians 5:23 includes self-control (temperance) as the final virtue listed among the fruit of the Spirit.

qs.q: In which Old Testament book is the vision of the Valley of Dry Bones recorded?
qs.e: Ezekiel chapter 37 contains the famous vision of the valley filled with dry bones restored to life by God's Spirit.

qs.q: Why was Esau bitter toward Jacob when Isaac blessed Jacob in Genesis chapter twenty-seven?
o: Jacob disguised himself with goat skins and stole Esau's paternal blessing from blind Isaac
Jacob refused to share the family cattle in Gerar
Esau was forced to move to Egypt as a servant
qs.e: Genesis 27 describes Rebekah and Jacob deceiving Isaac into pronouncing the firstborn blessing upon Jacob.

qs.q: How did God sustain the Israelites with food during their forty years of desert wandering?
o: He rained down manna every morning and brought quail in the evening
He commanded surrounding nations to tribute wheat daily
He turned desert sand into edible bread crumbs
He caused fruit trees to grow instantly around their camp
qs.e: Exodus 16 records God sending manna from heaven and quails to feed the assembly throughout their journey.

qs.q: What punishment did God inflict upon the Israelites for believing the bad report of the ten faithless spies?
o: They were immediately sent back as slaves to Egypt
Their city of Shiloh was destroyed by a fire
They were condemned to wander forty years in the wilderness until that entire generation died
They were stripped of the Ark of the Covenant
qs.e: Numbers 14:26-35 details God decreeing one year of wandering for each day the spies searched the land (40 years total).

qs.q: How did Nehemiah respond when Tobiah and Sanballat ridiculed the rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls?
o: He abandoned the rebuilding project and fled to Susa
He prayed to God for protection, set up guards, and instructed workers to build with one hand while holding a weapon in the other
He paid a heavy tribute tax to Sanballat in gold
He challenged Sanballat to a sword duel on the wall
qs.e: Nehemiah 4:7-21 describes Nehemiah's vigilance, arming the builders with swords, spears, and bows to guard against surprise attacks.

qs.q: What symbolic act did the prophet Ahijah perform when announcing the division of Solomon's kingdom to Jeroboam?
o: He broke a clay flask in front of the elders at Shiloh
He tore his new garment into twelve pieces and gave ten pieces to Jeroboam
He poured sour wine over the altar at Bethel
He placed two wooden yokes upon Jeroboam's shoulders
qs.e: 1 Kings 11:29-39 details Ahijah tearing his cloak into twelve pieces, symbolizing the ten tribes Jeroboam would rule.

qs.q: In the Gospel of Luke, what was John the Baptist's advice to tax collectors who asked what they should do?
o: Quit your civil jobs immediately and join the Levites
Charge double taxes to wealthy foreign merchants
Surrender all personal wealth to the Jerusalem Temple
Collect no more money than what is appointed to you by law
qs.e: Luke 3:12-13 records John instructing tax collectors to practice honesty and avoid extortion in their official duties.

qs.q: What happened when Jesus was baptized by John in the Jordan River?
o: The river stopped flowing and turned into red wine
A bright star appeared directly over the Jordan River
The heavens opened, the Holy Spirit descended as a dove, and a voice from heaven said 'This is My beloved Son'
The temple veil in Jerusalem split in two
qs.e: Matthew 3:16-17 records the triune divine manifestation at Jesus' baptism in the Jordan.
qs.tp: Birth, Infancy and Preparation of Jesus

qs.q: In the Miracle of Calming the Storm, what did Jesus say to the wind and the waves on the Sea of Galilee?
qs.e: Mark 4:39 describes Jesus rebuking the wind and commanding the sea 'Peace, be still!', causing a great calm.

qs.q: What parable did Jesus tell to answer the lawyer's question 'And who is my neighbor?'
o: The Parable of the Good Samaritan
The Parable of the Prodigal Son
The Parable of the Lost Sheep
The Parable of the Unforgiving Servant
qs.e: Luke 10:25-37 records Jesus telling the story of the merciful Samaritan to define neighborly love across cultural boundaries.
qs.tp: Parables and Teaching on the Kingdom

qs.q: How was Apostle James the brother of John martyred in Jerusalem according to Acts chapter twelve?
o: He was stoned to death by the Sanhedrin outside the gate
He was executed with the sword by command of King Herod Agrippa I
He was crucified upside down in the market square
He was thrown off the Temple pinnacle by Roman guards
qs.e: Acts 12:1-2 records Herod Agrippa I laying violent hands on church members and killing James brother of John with a sword.

qs.q: In Romans chapter five, how does Paul contrast the consequence of Adam's sin with the gift of Jesus Christ?
o: Adam's sin affected only physical plants, while Christ restored animals
Adam's sin was forgiven instantly, while Christ brought a new law
Adam brought financial poverty, while Christ guarantees material gold
Adam's single transgression brought condemnation to all, but Christ's one righteous act brings justification and life
qs.e: Romans 5:12-19 contrasts death through Adam with abundant grace, righteousness, and eternal life through Jesus Christ.

qs.q: In 2 Corinthians chapter five, how does Paul define the ministry entrusted to all Christian believers?
o: The ministry of reconciliation, as ambassadors for Christ pleading with people to be reconciled to God
The ministry of civil governance over non-Christian nations
The ministry of mandatory Temple sacrificial worship
The ministry of collecting mandatory taxes for Jerusalem
qs.e: 2 Corinthians 5:18-20 states that God reconciled us to Himself through Christ and gave us the ministry of reconciliation.

qs.q: What tragic sin did Cain commit that brought a divine curse upon his agricultural labor in Genesis chapter four?
o: He built a pagan altar to worship the sun
He murdered his brother Abel out of jealousy because God favored Abel's sacrifice
He stole sheep from his neighbor's field
He refused to offer any firstfruits to the Lord
qs.e: Genesis 4:8-12 details Cain killing Abel, resulting in the ground no longer yielding its strength to his farming.

qs.q: How did God call Moses to lead Israel out of Egyptian bondage at Mount Horeb?
o: An angel handed Moses a golden scroll written in Egyptian hieroglyphs
God appeared in a thunderous storm over the Nile River
God spoke to him from a burning bush that was not consumed, revealing His holy name 'I AM WHO I AM'
Moses received a dream while serving in Pharaoh's palace
qs.e: Exodus 3:1-15 records Moses at the burning bush where God revealed His name Yahweh and commissioned Moses as deliverer.

qs.q: What lesson did God teach Elijah through the events at Mount Horeb in 1 Kings chapter nineteen?
o: God manifests His power exclusively through violent thunder and lightning
Elijah was the only faithful servant remaining in all of Israel
God was not in the strong wind, the earthquake, or the fire, but in a still small voice
God commanded Elijah to establish a military garrison in Damascus
qs.e: 1 Kings 19:11-13 records Elijah discovering God's presence in a gentle whisper ('a still small voice') on Horeb.

qs.q: Why was Prophet Amos expelled from the royal sanctuary at Bethel by High Priest Amaziah?
o: Because Amos refused to pay sanctuary entering fees
Because Amos was a foreigner from Egypt who lacked Levite credentials
Because Amos attempted to tear down the golden calf altar
Because Amos prophesied the death of King Jeroboam II and the exile of Israel due to social oppression
qs.e: Amos 7:10-17 records Amaziah telling Amos to flee back to Judah and stop prophesying against Bethel.

qs.q: What significant discovery did High Priest Hilkiah make during the Temple restoration under King Josiah?
o: The original golden Ark built by Bezaleel
A secret chest containing King Solomon's personal crown
The Book of the Law of the Lord given by Moses
A prophecy foretelling the destruction of Nineveh
qs.e: 2 Kings 22:8 records Hilkiah finding the Book of the Law in the Temple, which initiated Josiah's national reformation.

qs.q: What occurred when Jesus was tempted by the devil to turn stones into bread in the wilderness?
o: Jesus performed the miracle to demonstrate His power over physical hunger
Jesus called down angels to strike Satan with lightning
Jesus remained completely silent until Satan departed
Jesus answered 'It is written: Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds from the mouth of God'
qs.e: Matthew 4:3-4 records Jesus quoting Deuteronomy 8:3 to defeat the devil's temptation concerning physical appetite.
qs.tp: Birth, Infancy and Preparation of Jesus

qs.q: In the Miracle of Healing the Ten Lepers, what distinguished the one leper who returned to thank Jesus?
o: He was a wealthy Roman officer who gave silver to the disciples
He was a Levite priest who brought a lamb sacrifice
He was a Pharisee who publicly confessed his sins
