He was a Samaritan who fell on his face giving glory to God, while the other nine Jews went away
qs.e: Luke 17:11-19 notes that only the foreigner (a Samaritan) returned to give thanks, prompting Jesus to commend his faith.

qs.q: In the Parable of the Sower, what happens to seed sown among thorns?
o: Birds immediately swoop down and devour the seed
The worries of this world and the deceitfulness of wealth choke the word, making it unfruitful
The sun scorches the plants because they have no root
The seed grows rapidly and yields a hundredfold crop
qs.e: Matthew 13:22 explains that thorny ground represents hearts choked by material anxieties and riches.
qs.tp: Parables and Teaching on the Kingdom

qs.q: What statement did the Roman centurion make at the cross upon witnessing Jesus' death and the accompanying signs?
o: This man was guilty of treason against Caesar!
Truly this was the Son of God!
Let us build a sanctuary on Golgotha!
The Jewish leaders were completely justified in his sentence!
qs.e: Matthew 27:54 records the centurion and soldiers guarding Jesus being terrified by the earthquake and confessing His divine sonship.
qs.tp: Trial, Death and Resurrection of Jesus

qs.q: What charge led to the arrest and eventual martyrdom of Stephen in Acts chapter seven?
o: He delivered a speech accusing the Jewish council of resisting the Holy Spirit and betraying the Righteous One
He stole money from the widow distribution fund
He claimed to be the earthly King of Judea
He led a military revolt against the Roman garrison
qs.e: Acts 7:51-60 describes Stephen rebuking the Sanhedrin, leading to them dragging him outside the city and stoning him.

qs.q: In 1 Corinthians chapter six, why does Paul forbid Christians from bringing lawsuits against fellow believers before secular courts?
o: Because Roman judges charged exorbitant court entry fees
Because civil law prohibits religious members from testifying
Because believers should settle internal disputes within the church community rather than before unbelievers
Because secular courts automatically execute all plaintiffs
qs.e: 1 Corinthians 6:1-8 admonishes believers for going to court before unrighteous judges instead of seeking wise church arbitration.

qs.q: According to Paul in Ephesians chapter two, how are believers saved from sin and spiritual death?
o: By rigorous adherence to Mosaic ceremonial washings
By earning spiritual merit through public charitable donations
By grace through faith, and this not of yourselves; it is the gift of God, not of works
By virtue of physical descent from Abraham
qs.e: Ephesians 2:8-9 emphasizes that salvation is entirely a unmerited gift of divine grace received through faith.

qs.q: In 1 Thessalonians chapter four, what instruction does Paul give regarding Christian work and quiet living?
o: Aspire to lead a quiet life, mind your own business, and work with your hands so as to walk properly before outsiders
Depend entirely on financial support from secular authorities
Quit all daily jobs to wait on mountaintops for the Lord's return
Force non-believers to pay monthly tithes to church leaders
qs.e: 1 Thessalonians 4:11-12 advises believers to practice diligence, respectability, and personal responsibility in daily labor.

qs.q: According to James chapter one verse five, what should a believer do if he lacks wisdom?
o: Consult Greek secular philosophers in Athens
Perform forty days of ceremonial Temple washings
Purchase ancient wisdom scrolls from merchants
Ask of God, who gives to all liberally and without reproach, and it will be given to him
qs.e: James 1:5 promises that God generously grants wisdom to those who ask Him in faith without doubting.

qs.q: In 1 Peter chapter five, what metaphor is used to describe the devil's aggressive spiritual warfare against believers?
o: A subtle venomous viper hiding in desert rocks
A giant sea monster destroying fishing vessels
A roaring lion prowling around seeking someone to devour
A soaring eagle hunting weak prey in open fields
qs.e: 1 Peter 5:8 warns believers to be sober and vigilant because their adversary the devil walks about like a roaring lion.

qs.q: What spiritual lesson is conveyed by the account of Abraham offering Isaac in Genesis chapter twenty-two?
o: God requires human sacrifice as a regular practice for covenant faith
Supreme obedience and trust in God, who provides the ultimate sacrificial ram on His holy mountain
Isaac was disobedient and needed physical punishment
Pagan altars in Canaan were acceptable for worshiping Yahweh
qs.e: Genesis 22 demonstrates Abraham's unreserved trust in God, where Jehovah-Jireh ('The Lord Will Provide') provided a substitute ram.

qs.q: How did King Saul's jealousy toward David manifest after David's victory over Goliath?
o: Saul immediately banished David to the land of Moab
Women sang 'Saul has slain his thousands, and David his ten thousands', driving Saul to attempt killing David with a spear
Saul stripped David of his army position and made him a farmer
Saul handed David over to the Philistines in Gaza
qs.e: 1 Samuel 18:6-11 records Saul envying David's popular acclaim and trying twice to pin David to the wall with his spear.

qs.q: What key reform did King Hezekiah execute regarding the high places and sacred pillars in Judah?
o: He removed the high places, smashed the sacred stones, cut down the Asherah poles, and broke the bronze serpent Nehushtan
He built larger high places in every city of Judah to accommodate foreign merchants
He required all sacrifices to be offered strictly on Mount Carmel
He transferred the high places to the control of the Assyrians
qs.e: 2 Kings 18:4 details Hezekiah's thorough religious purge, restoring centralized worship at the Jerusalem Temple.

qs.q: In the Book of Daniel chapter six, why did the Persian officials plot against Daniel?
o: Daniel stole gold coins from King Darius' royal treasury
Daniel attempted to assassinate King Darius during a banquet
Daniel refused to pay civil taxes to the Persian government
They were jealous of his exceptional administrative success and could find no ground of corruption or fault in him
qs.e: Daniel 6:1-5 records the governors envying Daniel's promotion, realizing they could only trap him regarding his fidelity to God's law.

qs.q: What underlying message did the prophet Hosea proclaim regarding Israel's sacrifices and knowledge of God?
o: For I desire mercy and not sacrifice, and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings
Burnt offerings are superior to moral integrity in pleasing Yahweh
God prefers foreign Egyptian rituals over Levitical sacrifices
Sacrifices are only effective when offered on high places
qs.e: Hosea 6:6 contains God's declaration that heartfelt covenant loyalty and intimate knowledge of God supersede ritual sacrifices.

qs.q: In the Parable of the Sheep and the Goats, on what basis does the Son of Man separate humanity at the final judgment?
o: How much gold wealth they accumulated during their earthly life
How they treated the needy, hungry, stranger, naked, sick, and imprisoned ('the least of these My brethren')
Their exact genealogical lineage tracing back to Abraham
Their political influence and rank in the Roman Empire
qs.e: Matthew 25:31-46 shows that compassionate actions toward vulnerable people reflect genuine saving faith in the King.
qs.tp: Parables and Teaching on the Kingdom

qs.q: How did Jesus respond when the Pharisees caught a woman in adultery and demanded her stoning under Mosaic law?
o: He immediately ordered Roman soldiers to arrest the woman
He wrote on the ground and said 'He who is without sin among you, let him throw a stone at her first'
He commanded the crowd to stone her outside the city gate
He declared that adultery was no longer a sin in any circumstance
qs.e: John 8:1-11 details Jesus exposing the accusers' hypocrisy, leading them to leave one by one until only Jesus and the woman remained.
qs.tp: Parables and Teaching on the Kingdom

qs.q: What major breakthrough occurred in Peter's theology during his ministry at the house of Cornelius in Caesarea?
o: He realized that God shows no partiality, but accepts from every nation anyone who fears Him and works righteousness
He concluded that Gentile believers must adopt circumcision before baptism
He decided to move the apostolic headquarters permanently to Rome
He instituted mandatory animal sacrifices for Gentile converts
qs.e: Acts 10:34-35 records Peter's famous declaration acknowledging God's universal salvation offered to Gentiles.

qs.q: In Romans chapter eight verse twenty-eight, what enduring promise is given to believers in all circumstances?
o: Believers will never experience financial loss or physical trials
All human beings will eventually achieve temporal political power
All things work together for good to those who love God, to those who are called according to His purpose
God will eliminate all secular laws that govern society
qs.e: Romans 8:28 assures believers that divine providence arranges every circumstance for their ultimate spiritual good.

qs.q: In 1 Corinthians chapter three, how does Paul describe the work of Christian leaders like himself and Apollos?
o: I planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the increase; so neither he who plants nor he who waters is anything, but God
Paul is the supreme monarch over the church while Apollos is his servant
Apollos earned salvation through preaching while Paul earned it through writing
Leaders own the local churches as personal commercial property
qs.e: 1 Corinthians 3:6-7 corrects sectarian rivalry in Corinth by emphasizing that God alone causes spiritual growth.

qs.q: According to Paul in Galatians chapter six, what principle of divine retribution governs human choices?
o: Do not be deceived, God is not mocked; for whatever a man sows, that he will also reap
Human actions carry no spiritual or moral consequences in this life
Sowing to the flesh guarantees temporal earthly prosperity
Reaping is determined purely by physical strength and luck
qs.e: Galatians 6:7-8 warns that sowing to the flesh reaps corruption, while sowing to the Spirit reaps everlasting life.

qs.q: What theological doctrine does Paul explain in Romans chapter three verses twenty-one to twenty-six regarding Christ's death as a propitiation?
o: God presented Christ as a propitiatory sacrifice through faith in His blood to demonstrate God's justice in forgiving past sins
Christ died strictly to satisfy Roman political legal standards
Christ's blood abolished the moral requirement for holy living
Propitiation applies only to ethnic Jews who observe the Sabbath
qs.e: Romans 3:21-26 unfolds how Christ's sacrificial death satisfies divine justice while justifying believers by grace through faith.

qs.q: In 2 Corinthians chapter four, how does Paul describe the treasure of the gospel residing within human believers?
o: The gospel is a physical scroll hidden inside a golden box in Jerusalem
Believers become physically immortal vessels immune to persecution
We have this treasure in earthen vessels, that the excellence of the power may be of God and not of us
The gospel grants believers supernatural economic wealth
qs.e: 2 Corinthians 4:7 contrasts the glorious, immortal message of Christ with frail, mortal human ministers ('earthen vessels').

qs.q: In Philippians chapter three, what does Paul consider his impressive Jewish religious pedigree compared to knowing Christ?
o: He considers his Pharisaic credentials superior to apostolic ministry
He demands that all Gentile believers adopt his exact Pharisaic training
He regrets ever leaving his administrative post in the Sanhedrin
He counts all his former gains as loss and rubbish for the excellence of knowing Christ Jesus his Lord
qs.e: Philippians 3:7-9 details Paul renouncing self-righteous legalistic credentials to gain Christ's righteousness through faith.

qs.q: What key point does the author of James make in James chapter two verse nineteen regarding intellectual belief in God without saving faith?
o: Intellectual belief alone is completely sufficient for salvation
Demons are incapable of knowing basic facts about God
Belief without action is commended as the highest spiritual virtue
Even the demons believe that there is one God—and tremble!
qs.e: James 2:19 shows that mere mental assent to monotheism is insufficient, as even demons acknowledge God's existence with fear.

qs.q: In 1 Peter chapter two, how are believers described as a collective spiritual community?
o: A political faction formed to overthrow the Roman emperor
A chosen generation, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, God's own special people called out of darkness into marvelous light
A secret society reserved exclusively for wealthy landowners
A group of isolated individuals who hold no communal identity
qs.e: 1 Peter 2:9 applies Israel's ancient covenant titles (Exodus 19:6) to the church as God's redeemed people.

qs.q: Which prophet was thrown into a lions' den for praying to God in violation of King Darius' decree?
qs.e: Daniel chapter 6 records Daniel being thrown into the lions' den, where an angel shut the lions' mouths because he was innocent.

qs.q: Who was the High Priest who questioned Jesus during His trial before the Sanhedrin?
qs.e: Matthew 26:57 records Jesus being led to Caiaphas the High Priest, where the scribes and elders were assembled.
qs.tp: Trial, Death and Resurrection of Jesus

qs.q: What tax collector climbed a sycamore tree in Jericho to see Jesus passing by?
qs.e: Luke 19:1-10 details Zacchaeus, a wealthy chief tax collector who was short of stature, climbing a sycamore-fig tree to see Jesus.

qs.q: Which apostle was chosen by lot to replace Judas Iscariot among the Twelve?
qs.e: Acts 1:21-26 records the believers praying and casting lots between Joseph called Barsabbas and Matthias, and the lot fell on Matthias.
qs.tp: The Early Church and Holy Spirit

qs.q: What town was the hometown of Mary, Martha, and their brother Lazarus?
qs.e: John 11:1 specifies that Bethany was the village of Mary and her sister Martha, located near Jerusalem on the Mount of Olives.

qs.q: Who was the father of King David according to the Old Testament genealogies?
qs.e: 1 Samuel 16 records Samuel being sent to Jesse the Bethlehemite to anoint one of his sons as king over Israel.

qs.q: According to Paul in 1 Corinthians chapter thirteen, what quality never fails even when prophecies and knowledge cease?
qs.e: 1 Corinthians 13:8 declares: 'Love never fails. But whether there are prophecies, they will fail; whether there are tongues, they will cease.'

qs.q: Why was the widow of Zarephath blessed with an unfailing supply of flour and oil during Elijah's time?
o: She gave Elijah ten shekels of silver from her savings
She obeyed Elijah's request to feed him first from her meager remaining flour and oil
She built a wooden sanctuary for Yahweh in Zarephath
She hid Elijah from Ahab's guards inside a dry well
qs.e: 1 Kings 17:8-16 records the widow demonstrating faith by baking a small cake for Elijah first, after which her jar of flour and jug of oil did not run dry.

qs.q: What punishment did King Uzziah suffer when he entered the Temple to burn incense on the altar?
o: He was struck blind for forty days and forty nights
His royal crown melted on his head
He was struck with leprosy on his forehead directly before the priests
He fell dead immediately in front of the Holy Place
qs.e: 2 Chronicles 26:16-21 details Uzzah becoming proud and arrogating priestly duties, resulting in leprosy breaking out on his forehead.

qs.q: How did Queen Esther prepare her people and herself before approaching King Ahasuerus uninvited?
o: She hired a army of mercenary bodyguards to escort her
She asked Mordecai and all Jews in Susa to fast with her for three days and three nights
She sent royal gifts of gold and silver to Haman
She offered forty animal sacrifices on Mount Zion
qs.e: Esther 4:15-17 describes Esther instructing all Jews in Susa to fast neither eating nor drinking for three days before she went to the king.

qs.q: What lesson did Jesus teach His disciples when He placed a young child in their midst in Matthew chapter eighteen?
o: Children are incapable of understanding spiritual truth until adulthood
Only physical parents are eligible for leadership in the church
Unless you turn and become like little children, you will never enter the kingdom of heaven
Children must be taught to earn their salvation through fasting
qs.e: Matthew 18:1-4 uses a child's humility, trust, and dependence as the pattern for true greatness in the Kingdom.
qs.tp: Parables and Teaching on the Kingdom

qs.q: In the Miracle of Walking on the Sea, what did Jesus say to reassure His terrified disciples who thought they saw a ghost?
o: Row faster to the shore at Capernaum!
Be of good cheer! It is I; do not be afraid
Look at the stars to guide your course!
Pray to the angels for immediate deliverance!
qs.e: Matthew 14:27 records Jesus identifying Himself across the stormy waters to calm His frightened disciples.

qs.q: What happened to the prison guard at Philippi after the earthquake opened the doors and loosened the prisoners' chains?
o: He drew his sword to kill himself, but Paul stopped him, and he and his household believed and were baptized
He fled into the surrounding mountains to escape the Roman governor
He executed Paul and Silas immediately on the spot
He reported the apostles to the High Priest in Jerusalem
qs.e: Acts 16:27-34 records the jailer asking 'Sirs, what must I do to be saved?', resulting in his salvation and baptism.

qs.q: According to Paul in Romans chapter eight, what status do believers receive through the Spirit of adoption?
o: Servants bound under the Mosaic Law
Children of God and joint heirs with Christ
qs.e: Romans 8:14-17 teaches that believers are adopted as God's children, crying 'Abba, Father' and sharing Christ's inheritance.

qs.q: In 1 Corinthians chapter ten, what key promise does God give regarding temptation?
o: God eliminates all earthly temptations for baptized believers
God is faithful and will not allow you to be tempted beyond what you can bear, but will provide a way of escape
Temptation is proof that a believer has lost eternal salvation
Believers should seek out severe temptations to demonstrate moral strength
qs.e: 1 Corinthians 10:13 reassures believers that God limits trial intensity and provides victory and escape.

qs.q: What instruction does Paul give children in Ephesians chapter six regarding their parents?
o: Children should obey parents only if parents are sinless
Children, obey your parents in the Lord, for this is right, honoring father and mother
Children should support parents financially only after age fifty
Children must leave home immediately upon reaching age twelve
qs.e: Ephesians 6:1-3 cites the fifth commandment ('Honor your father and mother'), noting it is the first commandment with a promise.

qs.q: In the Book of James chapter four verse seven, how are Christians instructed to handle the devil?
o: Submit to God; resist the devil and he will flee from you
Negotiate terms of peace with the devil in prayer
Seek out demonic spirits in desert places to fight them
qs.e: James 4:7 links divine submission with victorious resistance: 'Submit to God. Resist the devil and he will flee from you.'

qs.q: What was the main purpose of the Nazirite vow in ancient Israel as illustrated by Samson and Samuel?
o: To train for military command in the royal palace
To qualify for priesthood in the tribe of Levi
To fast for forty consecutive days in the wilderness
To consecrate oneself specially to the Lord through total abstinence from wine, uncut hair, and avoiding dead bodies
qs.e: Numbers 6 outlines the Nazirite vow of special devotion, marked by uncut hair, abstaining from grape products, and ritual purity.

qs.q: What was the reaction of the disciples when Jesus predicted His upcoming passion and death in Matthew chapter sixteen?
o: They immediately abandoned Jesus and returned to Galilee
Peter took Him aside and began to rebuke Him, saying 'Far be it from You, Lord; this shall never happen to You!'
They threw a feast in Bethany to celebrate His royalty
They hired guards to protect Him from Roman soldiers
qs.e: Matthew 16:21-23 records Peter rejecting Christ's cross, earning Jesus' rebuke: 'Get behind Me, Satan!'
qs.tp: Trial, Death and Resurrection of Jesus

qs.q: How did Jacob prepare for his tense reunion with Esau after returning from Mesopotamia in Genesis chapter thirty-two?
o: He hired an Egyptian army to escort his family across the border
He challenged Esau to single combat before the elders of Edom
He hid his family in caves while he fled back to Haran
He divided his people and livestock into two camps, prayed earnestly to God, and sent generous gifts of livestock ahead in waves
qs.e: Genesis 32:7-21 describes Jacob's prudent preparation, humble prayer, and sending hundreds of animals as a peace offering to Esau.

qs.q: What sin caused Nadab and Abihu, sons of Aaron, to be consumed by fire from the Lord in Leviticus chapter ten?
o: They stole gold utensils from the Most Holy Place
They refused to undergo ceremonial washings before entering
They offered pagan sacrifices on Mount Sinai
They offered profane fire before the Lord, which He had not commanded them
qs.e: Leviticus 10:1-3 records Nadab and Abihu offering unauthorized fire, emphasizing God's absolute holiness in worship.

qs.q: Why was King Saul rejected by God after his victory over the Amalekites in 1 Samuel chapter fifteen?
o: He refused to share battle spoils with the tribe of Judah
He disobeyed God's explicit command by sparing King Agag and the best of the sheep and cattle
He lost the Ark of the Covenant to the Philistines during the battle
He built a golden altar to pagan gods in Gilgal
qs.e: 1 Samuel 15 details Saul's partial obedience, leading Samuel to declare that 'to obey is better than sacrifice'.

qs.q: What covenant promise did God make to David through the prophet Nathan in 2 Samuel chapter seven?
o: David's descendants would conquer all nations from Egypt to Rome within fifty years
David would live to be two hundred years old and see the Temple built
The Ark of the Covenant would never leave Mount Zion
God would establish David's house, throne, and kingdom forever through his descendant
qs.e: 2 Samuel 7:12-16 contains the foundational Davidic Covenant, promising an everlasting royal throne fulfilled in Jesus Messiah.

qs.q: In the Book of Amos, how did God view the luxurious lifestyle of the wealthy leaders in Samaria who ignored the poor?
o: He praised their economic success as proof of divine covenant favor
He commanded them to construct larger palaces to house refugees
He condemned their ease, ivory beds, and costly wines while they were unconcerned with the ruin of the nation
He instructed Levites to collect double tithes from their estates
qs.e: Amos 6:1-7 denounces those who lie on beds of ivory and drink wine from bowls while ignoring social injustice and impending judgment.

qs.q: What vision did the prophet Zechariah see regarding the High Priest Joshua in Zechariah chapter three?
o: Joshua was offered a golden crown by the king of Persia
Joshua was struck blind for offering unholy incense
Joshua stood before the angel of the Lord in filthy garments, Satan stood to accuse him, and God replaced his filthy clothes with rich robes
Joshua was carried away to Babylon in a chariot of fire
qs.e: Zechariah 3:1-5 portrays divine forgiveness and cleansing, replacing filthy garments (sin) with pure priestly vestments.

qs.q: What was the response of the people of Nineveh when Jonah proclaimed 'Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown!'?
o: They seized Jonah and executed him outside the city walls
They mocked Jonah and threw stone missiles at him
The people believed God, proclaimed a fast, and put on sackcloth from the greatest to the least, turning from their evil ways
They sent a military battalion to conquer Israel
qs.e: Jonah 3:5-10 records Nineveh's complete national repentance, prompting God to relent from destroying the city.

qs.q: What miracle took place when Jesus healed the woman with an issue of blood for twelve years?
o: She touched the fringe of His garment in faith, and immediately her bleeding stopped as Jesus felt power go out from Him
Jesus spat on the ground, made clay, and anointed her body
She washed seven times in the Jordan River at sunset
Jesus commanded her to fast for forty days in the Temple
qs.e: Mark 5:25-34 describes the woman's desperate faith touching Jesus' cloak, where Jesus declared 'Daughter, your faith has made you well.'

qs.q: In the Parable of the Workers in the Vineyard, what principle regarding God's kingdom does Jesus illustrate?
o: Early converts receive higher spiritual rank in heaven than late converts
Hard physical labor is the sole basis of salvation
Salvation depends strictly on human seniority and lineage
God's grace is sovereign and unearned, making the last first and the first last
qs.e: Matthew 20:1-16 refutes legalistic merit by showing that all who enter God's kingdom receive divine grace equally.
qs.tp: Parables and Teaching on the Kingdom

qs.q: What happened to Elymas the sorcerer when he opposed Paul and Barnabas in Cyprus before proconsul Sergius Paulus?
o: He was struck dead instantly like Ananias and Sapphira
He was transformed into a pillar of salt on the seashore
Paul rebuked him as a son of the devil, and mist and darkness fell upon him so that he went about seeking someone to lead him by the hand
He fled to Rome where he was imprisoned by Caesar
qs.e: Acts 13:6-12 details Elymas (Bar-Jesus) being struck with temporary blindness, causing Sergius Paulus to believe the gospel.

qs.q: What key defense did Paul give before Governor Felix at Caesarea in Acts chapter twenty-four?
o: He claimed he had never stepped foot inside the Jerusalem Temple
He argued that Mosaic Law was invented by pagan philosophers
He promised to pay Felix a large financial tribute
He worshiped the God of his fathers according to the Way, believing everything written in the Law and Prophets, having hope in the resurrection
qs.e: Acts 24:14-16 shows Paul affirming his continuity with Israel's faith and his clear conscience before God and men.

qs.q: In Romans chapter twelve, how does Paul describe a believer's proper spiritual worship (rational service)?
o: Offering physical animal sacrifices at the Jerusalem Temple daily
Presenting one's body as a living sacrifice, holy and acceptable to God, not conformed to this world but transformed by renewing the mind
Reciting liturgical prayers seven times every afternoon
Fleeing into desert monasteries to avoid all human contact
qs.e: Romans 12:1-2 calls for total personal dedication to God, transforming daily life through a renewed mind.

qs.q: According to Paul in 1 Corinthians chapter fourteen, why is speaking in understandable prophecy superior to uninterpreted tongues in public meetings?
o: Prophecy requires no divine spiritual inspiration
Prophecy edifies, exhorts, and comforts the whole church, whereas uninterpreted tongues edify only the speaker
Tongues are sinful in all circumstances both private and public
Prophecy grants physical earthly riches to church elders
qs.e: 1 Corinthians 14:1-5 emphasizes intelligible communication in public worship so that the entire assembly benefits.

qs.q: In Colossians chapter three, what practical household guidelines does Paul give husbands regarding their wives?
o: Husbands must force wives to earn all family income
Husbands, love your wives and do not be harsh with them
Husbands are immune from spiritual accountability in the home
Husbands must demand daily public vows of allegiance
qs.e: Colossians 3:19 commands Christian husbands to model Christ's self-giving love and avoid bitterness toward their wives.

qs.q: What guidance does 1 Peter chapter five give to young members of the congregation regarding their relationship with elders?
o: Be submissive to elders, and clothe yourselves with humility toward one another, for God resists the proud but gives grace to the humble
Young members should replace elders in governance immediately
Young members are exempt from church discipline
Young members must pay higher tithes than older members
qs.e: 1 Peter 5:5 quotes Proverbs 3:34, emphasizing mutual humility and respect for pastoral leadership.

qs.q: What profound truth did Jacob acknowledge when he wrestled with a divine visitor at Peniel in Genesis chapter thirty-two?
o: He realized he could conquer the Esau's army through military strategy
He learned that his father Isaac had cursed him in error
He discovered a secret valley filled with gold in Edom
I have seen God face to face, and my life is preserved, receiving the name Israel because he strived with God and prevailed
qs.e: Genesis 32:24-30 describes Jacob wrestling at Peniel, receiving the name 'Israel' ('struggles with God') and divine blessing.

qs.q: How did Solomon's heart turn away from wholehearted devotion to Yahweh in his later years?
o: His foreign wives inclined his heart after other gods, and he built high places for Chemosh, Molech, and Ashtoreth
He abandoned the administrative capital of Jerusalem to live in Egypt
He converted to the Samaritan worship system at Mount Gerizim
He was overthrown by his son Rehoboam in a military coup
qs.e: 1 Kings 11:1-8 records Solomon's idolatrous compromises through his foreign marriages, bringing divine judgment upon his dynasty.

qs.q: What symbolic action did Jeremiah perform with a linen waistcloth in Jeremiah chapter thirteen?
o: He tore it into twelve strips and burned them in the Temple courtyard
He hid it in a crevice of the rock at the Euphrates; when retrieved later, it was ruined, symbolizing how God would mar the pride of Judah
He wore it unwashed for three years as a sign against Egypt
He gave it to King Jehoiakim as a royal mantle
qs.e: Jeremiah 13:1-11 uses the ruined waistcloth to illustrate how Judah, created to cling to God, had become useless through idolatry.

qs.q: In the Book of Ezekiel chapter eighteen, how does God address the popular fatalistic proverb 'The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children's teeth are set on edge'?
o: He declares the proverb shall no longer be used in Israel, for every individual soul belongs to God and dies for its own sin
He confirms that children will suffer permanently for ancestral sins regardless of conduct
He orders sour grape vineyards throughout Judah destroyed
He restricts the proverb exclusively to Gentile nations
qs.e: Ezekiel 18:1-4 refutes generational fatalism, establishing personal moral responsibility before divine justice.

qs.q: How did Jesus explain the meaning of the Bread of Life discourse in John chapter six following the feeding of the five thousand?
o: He declared 'I am the bread of life; he who comes to Me shall never hunger, and he who believes in Me shall never thirst'
He commanded His followers to store physical grain in Jerusalem for future famines
He taught that physical manna in the wilderness was superior to eternal salvation
He required His disciples to fast from physical bread every Sabbath
qs.e: John 6:35 presents Jesus as the spiritual nourishment sent from heaven, giving eternal life to all who believe.

qs.q: During the trial of Paul before Governor Festus and King Agrippa in Acts chapter twenty-five, why did Paul appeal to Caesar?
o: To claim a monetary reward granted to Roman citizens in Italy
To escape execution for committing murder in Ephesus
To avoid being sent back to Jerusalem to be tried by the Jewish leaders who plotted to ambush and kill him
To challenge the authority of Roman law over Christian apostles
qs.e: Acts 25:9-12 details Paul exercising his right as a Roman citizen to appeal to Caesar's supreme court in Rome.

qs.q: In Galatians chapter three, how does Paul describe the status of all believers in Christ Jesus regarding social and ethnic divisions?
o: Jewish believers hold permanent spiritual superiority over Gentile members
There is neither Jew nor Greek, slave nor free, male nor female; for you are all one in Christ Jesus
Free citizens are exempt from local church leadership obligations
Men receive double grace while women receive single grace
qs.e: Galatians 3:28 proclaims radical spiritual equality and unity among all believers incorporated into Christ.

qs.q: In Ephesians chapter five, how does Paul describe the relationship between Christ and the Church as a pattern for Christian marriage?
o: Christ demands mechanical legal compliance without love
Husbands may abandon wives who do not earn income
Marriage is a temporary secular contract voided by physical sickness
Christ loved the church and gave Himself up for her to sanctify her, so husbands should love their wives as their own bodies
qs.e: Ephesians 5:25-33 presents Christ's sacrificial love for the church as the holy model for Christian husbands.

qs.q: In Philippians chapter four verse six, what divine remedy does Paul prescribe for anxiety and worry?
o: Be anxious for nothing, but in everything by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known to God
Accumulate financial savings to guard against uncertain economic times
Consult astrologers regarding future personal events
Isolate completely from church community meetings
qs.e: Philippians 4:6-7 promises that prayer with thanksgiving brings 'the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding'.

qs.q: According to 2 Timothy chapter three verse sixteen, what is the divine origin and utility of all Scripture?
o: Scripture is purely human historical literature subject to cultural errors
All Scripture is given by inspiration of God and is profitable for doctrine, reproof, correction, and instruction in righteousness
Only the Law of Moses is divinely inspired while the Prophets are human opinion
Scripture is useful exclusively for academic debate among scholars
qs.e: 2 Timothy 3:16 asserts divine inspiration (theopneustos) and practical authority of Holy Scripture for spiritual maturity.

qs.q: In 1 Peter chapter three, how does Peter instruct wives to win over unbelieving husbands?
o: By arguing theological doctrines forcefully at every meal
By withholding family meals until the husband converts
Through chaste and respectful conduct and a gentle, quiet spirit without relying on outward physical adornment
By filing for immediate divorce in Roman civil courts
qs.e: 1 1 Peter 3:1-4 emphasizes the silent witness of a godly, gentle character in winning non-Christian spouses.

qs.q: In Romans chapter eight verses nine to eleven, what role is attributed to the indwelling Spirit regarding the believer's future physical body?
o: The Spirit replaces physical bodies with immaterial spirit phantoms at death
The Spirit guarantees physical bodies will never experience aging or disease on earth
If the Spirit of Him who raised Jesus from the dead dwells in you, He will also give life to your mortal bodies
The Spirit resurrects only souls while physical bodies remain permanently corrupted
qs.e: Romans 8:11 grounds the future bodily resurrection of believers in the indwelling Holy Spirit who raised Christ.

qs.q: In 2 Corinthians chapter three, how does Paul contrast the ministry of the Old Covenant with the ministry of the New Covenant?
o: The Old Covenant was a ministry of condemnation written on stone, whereas the New Covenant is a ministry of the Spirit bringing righteousness and glory
The Old Covenant granted eternal life while the New Covenant brings physical death
The Old Covenant was for Gentiles while the New Covenant is strictly for Jews
The Old Covenant requires no mediator while the New Covenant requires angels
qs.e: 2 Corinthians 3:6-11 contrasts the fading glory of Mosaic stone tablets with the abiding glory of the Spirit writing on human hearts.

qs.q: What christological truth is articulated in Hebrews chapter four verses fourteen to sixteen regarding Jesus as High Priest?
o: We have a High Priest who sympathizes with our weaknesses, was tempted in all points as we are yet without sin, enabling us to approach the throne of grace boldly
Jesus as High Priest offers annual animal blood sacrifices in the heavenly sanctuary
Jesus is immune to understanding human trials because He never took real flesh
Jesus restricts access to God's presence only to ordained Levites
qs.e: Hebrews 4:14-16 emphasizes Christ's empathetic, sinless high priesthood opening direct access to divine mercy for all believers.

qs.q: In 1 John chapter one verses eight to nine, what critical truth regarding sin and confession is declared?
o: Believers become morally sinless immediately upon water baptism and never sin again
Confessing sin to human priests is mandatory to avoid eternal hellfire
God forgives sin without requiring personal confession or repentance
If we say we have no sin, we deceive ourselves; but if we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us and cleanse us from all unrighteousness
qs.e: 1 John 1:8-9 addresses ongoing Christian life, promising forgiveness and cleansing upon honest confession of sin.

qs.q: In Revelation chapter three verse twenty, what invitation does the exalted Christ extend to the lukewarm church in Laodicea?
o: He threatens to destroy their physical city with an earthquake within seven days
He demands they pay gold tribute to the church in Philadelphia
He commands them to rebuild the Temple in Jerusalem
Behold, I stand at the door and knock; if anyone hears My voice and opens the door, I will come in to him and dine with him
qs.e: Revelation 3:20 presents Christ graciously seeking restored fellowship with lukewarm believers who open their hearts to Him.

qs.q: Which prophet was swallowed by a great fish after fleeing from God's command to go to Nineveh?
qs.e: Jonah chapter 1 records Jonah fleeing toward Tarshish, where he was swallowed by a great fish prepared by God.

qs.q: Who was the High Priest at Shiloh who mentored young Samuel?
qs.e: 1 Samuel 1-3 details Samuel serving the Lord under the tutelage of Eli the priest at the sanctuary in Shiloh.

qs.q: What city was surrounded by the Israelites who marched around its walls for seven days until they collapsed?
qs.e: Joshua 6 describes the miraculous fall of Jericho after the Israelite army marched around the city for seven days.

qs.q: Which Gospel writer was a former tax collector called by Jesus from his booth in Capernaum?
qs.e: Matthew 9:9 records Jesus calling Matthew (Levi) while sitting at the tax office, prompting Matthew to follow Him.

qs.q: What deacon was Philip's companion who defended the faith before the Sanhedrin and became the first Christian martyr?
qs.e: Acts 6-7 records Stephen, full of faith and power, giving a brilliant historical defense before being stoned to death.

qs.q: According to Paul in Galatians chapter five, what virtue stands first among the fruit of the Spirit?
qs.e: Galatians 5:22 begins listing the fruit of the Spirit with love (agape) as the primary foundational virtue.

qs.q: What king of Judah repaired the Temple, found the Book of the Law, and led a great religious reform?
qs.e: 2 Kings 22-23 records King Josiah discovering the Book of the Law and abolishing idol worship throughout Judah.

qs.q: How did Jacob obtain the blessing of the firstborn from his father Isaac?
o: He paid Isaac fifty silver talents from his farming profits
He covered his hands and neck with goat skins to imitate Esau's hairy skin and wore Esau's clothes
He forced Esau to write a legal declaration before the elders
He brought Isaac wild venison that he personally hunted in Edom
qs.e: Genesis 27 describes Rebekah dressing Jacob in Esau's garments and goat skins to deceive blind Isaac into bestowing the blessing.

qs.q: What miracle did God perform through Elisha for the widow who was in danger of losing her sons to a creditor?
o: He caused gold coins to drop from heaven inside her house
He turned her barren field into an abundant wheat harvest overnight
He multiplied her single jar of oil to fill all borrowed empty vessels, enabling her to pay her debt
He struck the greedy creditor with sudden blindness
qs.e: 2 Kings 4:1-7 records Elisha multiplying the widow's oil until every vessel she borrowed from neighbors was filled.

qs.q: What happened to King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon when he boasted of his royal majesty in Daniel chapter four?
o: He was struck dead instantly on his golden throne
He was defeated in battle by King Cyrus of Persia
His royal palace collapsed in a sudden earthquake
He was driven from men to eat grass like oxen and lived in the wild until his hair grew like eagles' feathers
qs.e: Daniel 4:28-33 details Nebuchadnezzar's temporary madness (boanthropy) as punishment for pride, lasting seven times until he acknowledged God.

qs.q: How did Jesus respond when the Pharisees questioned why His disciples ate with unwashed hands?
o: He commanded His disciples to perform thirty days of ceremonial washings
He ordered the Pharisees to leave Galilee immediately
He taught that what goes into the mouth does not defile a person, but what comes out of the heart defiles him
He declared that bodily hygiene was completely forbidden for believers
qs.e: Matthew 15:1-20 clarifies that moral impurity originates in evil thoughts and desires of the heart, not unwashed hands.
qs.tp: Parables and Teaching on the Kingdom

qs.q: In the Miracle of Feeding the Four Thousand, how many baskets of leftover pieces were collected?
qs.e: Matthew 15:32-38 notes that after feeding four thousand men with seven loaves and a few small fish, seven large baskets of fragments remained.

qs.q: What vision led Paul to cross over into Macedonia during his second missionary journey?
o: A man of Macedonia stood begging him 'Come over to Macedonia and help us!'
A fiery chariot appearing over the Aegean Sea
An angel delivering a golden scroll written in Greek
A star shining brightly toward the city of Athens
qs.e: Acts 16:9-10 describes Paul's night vision at Troas prompting his team to preach the gospel in Europe.

qs.q: In Romans chapter eight, how does Paul describe the present sufferings of believers in comparison to future glory?
o: Present sufferings prove that God has rejected the church
Sufferings grant instant physical wealth on earth
Sufferings are experienced only by disobedient church members
The sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory that shall be revealed in us
qs.e: Romans 8:18 provides eternal perspective, declaring earthly trials insignificant compared to eternal weight of glory.

qs.q: According to Paul in 1 Corinthians chapter six, why should Christians avoid taking internal grievances before unrighteous civil judges?
o: Because Roman judges were corrupt and charged high entrance fees
Because civil courts execute all plaintiffs automatically
Because law courts are reserved exclusively for non-religious citizens
Because saints will judge the world and even angels, so church members should settle minor earthly disputes among themselves
qs.e: 1 Corinthians 6:1-3 highlights the high spiritual calling of believers who will participate in eschatological judgment.

qs.q: In Galatians chapter six, what instruction does Paul give regarding supporting those who teach the Word of God?
o: Let him who is taught the word share in all good things with him who teaches
Teachers must work in agriculture to support themselves entirely
Congregations should pay salaries using Roman government grants
Teachers are forbidden from accepting any material hospitality
qs.e: Galatians 6:6 instructs believers to share material blessings with spiritual leaders who instruct them in Scripture.

qs.q: What condition does James set for receiving answers to prayer in James chapter one?
o: Recite the prayer at least fifty times before sunset
Offer animal sacrifices at an altar before praying
Pray exclusively while standing inside a church sanctuary
Ask in faith, with no doubting, for he who doubts is like a wave of the sea driven and tossed by the wind
qs.e: James 1:6-7 warns that double-minded, doubting petitioners should not expect to receive anything from the Lord.

qs.q: Why was Zacharias, father of John the Baptist, struck mute until the day of John's birth?
o: Because he touched the incense altar with unwashed hands
Because he did not believe the angel Gabriel's words regarding Elizabeth bearing a child in her old age
Because he refused to offer sacrifices for the Roman governor
Because he revealed the secret name of the Messiah to the crowds
qs.e: Luke 1:18-20 records Gabriel muting Zechariah as a sign and consequence for doubting the divine birth announcement.
qs.tp: Birth, Infancy and Preparation of Jesus

qs.q: What warning did Jesus give regarding salt that loses its flavor in the Sermon on the Mount?
o: It should be used as fertilizer in wheat fields
It must be presented to the priests for purification
It is good for nothing except to be thrown out and trampled underfoot by men
It turns into poison if consumed by children
qs.e: Matthew 5:13 warns believers against losing their distinct spiritual influence and witness in the world.
qs.tp: Parables and Teaching on the Kingdom

qs.q: What tragedy occurred at Shiloh when news arrived that the Philistines had captured the Ark of the Covenant?
o: The Tabernacle caught fire and was burned to ashes
Samuel was taken captive by the Philistines to Gaza
Ninety-eight-year-old Eli fell backward off his seat, broke his neck, and died upon hearing that his sons were dead and the Ark taken
King Saul declared war on the Levites
qs.e: 1 Samuel 4:12-18 details Eli's shock at the loss of God's Ark, resulting in his tragic death.

qs.q: How did David handle the opportunity to kill King Saul in the Wilderness of Ziph?
o: He set fire to Saul's tent and fled into Philistine territory
He bound Saul in chains and delivered him to Samuel
He forced Saul to sign a treaty abdicating the throne
He entered Saul's camp while everyone slept, took Saul's spear and water jug, but spared his life
qs.e: 1 Samuel 26 describes David taking Saul's spear and jar to prove his loyalty while refusing to harm the Lord's anointed.

qs.q: What divine judgment fell upon King Belshazzar of Babylon during his lavish banquet in Daniel chapter five?
o: Fingers of a human hand wrote on the plaster wall 'MENE, MENE, TEKEL, UPHARSIN', predicting the fall of his kingdom that night
An earthquake destroyed the royal hall killing his lords
Fire fell from heaven and consumed his golden wine goblets
He was struck with sudden leprosy before his guests
qs.e: Daniel 5 records Daniel interpreting the handwriting on the wall, and Belshazzar was slain that very night by the Medes.

qs.q: In the Book of Isaiah, how does God describe the Servant who suffers for the sins of the people in Isaiah chapter 53?
o: He was a mighty earthly monarch who conquered Rome with iron weapons
He was a wealthy landowner who distributed grain to the poor
He was a priest who offered sacrifices on Mount Gerizim
He was wounded for our transgressions, bruised for our iniquities, led like a lamb to the slaughter without opening His mouth
qs.e: Isaiah 53 outlines the vicarious, substitutionary atonement of the Messiah who bears the sins of many.

qs.q: What occurred during the healing of the paralytic who was lowered through the roof in Capernaum?
o: Jesus first declared 'Son, your sins are forgiven you', provoking charges of blasphemy from the scribes before He healed him physically
The scribes applauded Jesus for His medical knowledge
The roof owners demanded payment before Jesus spoke
The paralytic refused to walk until given gold coins
qs.e: Mark 2:1-12 demonstrates Jesus' divine power to forgive sins, verified by restoring the paralytic's physical health.

qs.q: In the Parable of the Rich Man and Lazarus, what request did the rich man make from torment in Hades?
o: That Abraham grant him permission to return to earth as a king
That Abraham send Lazarus to dip his finger in water and cool his tongue, or send him to warn his five brothers
That his money be brought to Hades to buy his release
That his brothers be punished for squandering his estate
qs.e: Luke 16:19-31 exposes the permanence of the afterlife state and the sufficiency of the Scriptures ('Moses and the Prophets').
qs.tp: Parables and Teaching on the Kingdom

qs.q: What took place when Paul and Barnabas preached at Lystra during their first missionary journey?
o: The proconsul converted and proclaimed Christianity the state religion
The crowd built a Christian Temple in the city square
Paul was arrested by Roman soldiers and sent directly to Caesar
After Paul healed a man lame from birth, the crowd called them gods (Zeus and Hermes), but later stoned Paul and dragged him out of the city
qs.e: Acts 14:8-20 records Lystra's volatile reaction, attempting pagan sacrifice to the apostles before turning hostile under opposition.

qs.q: In Romans chapter twelve verse two, how are believers exhorted to be transformed rather than conforming to the world?
o: By the renewing of your mind, so that you may prove what is that good and acceptable and perfect will of God
By adopting strict ascetical vows of silence in monasteries
By acquiring higher degrees in Greek philosophy
By isolating from all civil governance and taxation
qs.e: Romans 12:2 calls for cognitive and spiritual renewal through God's Word to live out His righteous will.

qs.q: In 1 Corinthians chapter eleven, what warning does Paul issue regarding taking the Lord's Supper unworthily?
o: Unworthy participation causes instant physical blindness
Taking the Supper unworthily forfeits all civil voting rights
Unworthy participants must pay financial fines to church elders
He who eats and drinks in an unworthy manner eats and drinks judgment to himself, not discerning the Lord's body, causing sickness and death
qs.e: 1 Corinthians 11:27-30 mandates self-examination before partaking of the Holy Communion to honor Christ's sacrifice.

qs.q: According to Paul in Galatians chapter four, what does the sending of the Spirit of God's Son into our hearts enable us to cry?
qs.e: Galatians 4:6 highlights the intimate filial relationship believers enjoy as sons and daughters of God.

qs.q: In Ephesians chapter four, how does Paul describe the Christian duty regarding truthfulness in speech?
o: Truth should be spoken only to fellow church members
Lying is permissible if it prevents financial loss
Putting away lying, let each one speak truth with his neighbor, for we are members one of another
Speech should be limited to liturgical recitations
qs.e: Ephesians 4:25 commands absolute honesty, pointing out our corporate unity in the body of Christ.

qs.q: What guidance is given in 1 Peter chapter four regarding hospitality among believers?
o: Offer hospitality strictly to ordained church elders
Be hospitable to one another without grumbling, using whatever gift received to serve others
Charge reasonable room rates for traveling Christians
Limit hospitality to immediate family relatives
qs.e: 1 Peter 4:9-10 promotes ungrudging, cheerful hospitality and faithful stewardship of spiritual gifts.

qs.q: How did King Solomon demonstrate discernment when two women claimed the same surviving baby?
o: He ordered both women thrown into prison for thirty days
He called for a sword to divide the child, revealing the real mother when she pleaded to give the baby away to save its life
He cast sacred lots before the High Priest at the Temple
He gave the child to the royal palace nurses to raise
qs.e: 1 Kings 3:16-28 details Solomon's iconic judgment that revealed true maternal compassion.

qs.q: What consequence did King David face for taking an unauthorized census of Israel in 2 Samuel chapter twenty-four?
o: An invasion by Egypt captured Jerusalem
A pestilence sent by God killed 70,000 men of Israel in three days
David was deposed as king for ten years
The Temple treasury was emptied by foreign raiders
qs.e: 2 Samuel 24 records David choosing three days of plague as divine discipline for his proud military census.

qs.q: In the Parable of the Mustard Seed, what aspect of God's Kingdom is highlighted?
o: Its rapid destruction by hostile worldly powers
Its restriction exclusively to educated scholars
Its tiny, insignificant beginnings growing into a vast, dominant kingdom providing shelter for many
Its sudden disappearance after a few centuries
qs.e: Matthew 13:31-32 illustrates the expansive growth of the Kingdom from a tiny seed into a large tree.
qs.tp: Parables and Teaching on the Kingdom

qs.q: What key theological theme is emphasized in the Call of Jeremiah in Jeremiah chapter one?
o: Jeremiah was selected because of his vast political experience in Jerusalem
Jeremiah was appointed king over Judah and Babylon simultaneously
Jeremiah was called strictly to write historical chronicles
God foreordained him before his birth, setting him as a prophet to the nations to pluck up, pull down, build, and plant
qs.e: Jeremiah 1:4-10 reveals divine sovereign election before birth ('Before I formed you in the womb I knew you') and universal prophetic scope.

qs.q: How did Jesus answer the Sadducees when they tested Him regarding the resurrection of a woman married to seven brothers?
o: In the resurrection they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like angels of God in heaven, for God is God of the living
The woman will belong strictly to the first husband in the afterlife
The resurrection is impossible because physical bodies decompose
Marriage relationships continue unchanged throughout eternity
qs.e: Matthew 22:23-33 refutes the Sadducees' skepticism by clarifying the transformed nature of resurrected existence and citing God as God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
qs.tp: Trial, Death and Resurrection of Jesus

qs.q: What major lesson did Peter learn on the roof in Joppa before visiting Cornelius?
o: Dietary laws must be enforced strictly across all Roman provinces
What God has cleansed, no person must call common or unclean, breaking down Jew-Gentile ceremonial barriers
Apostles are forbidden from eating meals with Roman centurions
Visiting foreign coastal cities causes ritual defilement
qs.e: Acts 10:9-16 details Peter's vision of clean and unclean animals, preparing him to preach Christ freely to Gentiles.

qs.q: In 1 Corinthians chapter nine, how does Paul explain his personal willingness to adapt his lifestyle for the sake of the gospel?
o: He became all things to all men, that he might by all means save some, subordinating personal rights to gospel fruitfulness
He adopted pagan religious worship to gain Greek followers
He compromised core moral commandments to please civil rulers
He demanded financial salaries from every church he established
qs.e: 1 Corinthians 9:19-23 details Paul's apostolic flexibility in non-essential matters to reach Jews and Gentiles effectively.

qs.q: In 2 Corinthians chapter twelve, why did God permit a 'thorn in the flesh, a messenger of Satan' to harass Paul?
o: Lest he should be exalted above measure by the abundance of revelations he received
Because Paul committed unforgivable sin during his journey to Damascus
To force Paul to resign from his missionary office
To prevent Paul from writing additional epistles
qs.e: 2 Corinthians 12:7-10 explains that the thorn maintained Paul's spiritual humility, proving divine strength in human weakness.

qs.q: In Philippians chapter two, how are believers exhorted to conduct themselves within a corrupt generation?
o: Do all things without complaining and disputing, shining as lights in the world while holding fast the word of life
Retaliate with legal lawsuits against hostile neighbors
Isolate completely from all civil commerce and public schools
Conform outward behavior to current popular culture
qs.e: Philippians 2:14-16 calls for blameless, harmonious living so that Christians shine brightly amidst moral darkness.

qs.q: According to 1 Thessalonians chapter four, what is the clear will of God regarding a believer's personal sanctification?
o: That believers achieve immense material gold wealth on earth
That all church members hold high political positions in Rome
That Christians fast for thirty days every single month
That you should abstain from sexual immorality and know how to possess your own vessel in sanctification and honor
qs.e: 1 Thessalonians 4:3-5 defines God's will as moral purity, self-control, and freedom from lustful passions.

qs.q: In 1 Timothy chapter six verse ten, what key warning is issued regarding the love of money?
o: Possessing any money is inherently sinful for Christians
Money is the supreme virtue required for spiritual perfection
For the love of money is a root of all kinds of evil, for which some have strayed from the faith and pierced themselves with many griefs
Rich believers receive double reward in heaven automatically
qs.e: 1 Timothy 6:10 isolates the covetous desire for wealth ('love of money') as a dangerous source of moral and spiritual ruin.

qs.q: In Hebrews chapter eleven verse one, how is faith fundamentally defined?
o: Faith is a vague wishful feeling unsupported by divine revelation
Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen
Faith is intellectual agreement with historical ancient facts
Faith is a human emotion generated through physical rituals
qs.e: Hebrews 11:1 provides the classic biblical definition of faith as confident assurance and conviction in God's promises.

qs.q: In James chapter two, how does the author illustrate that faith without works is dead using the example of Abraham?
o: Abraham was saved because he built a physical temple in Haran
Abraham was justified by works when he offered Isaac his son on the altar, showing that faith was working together with his works
Abraham achieved perfection through strict dietary observances
Abraham's works replaced the need for divine covenant grace
qs.e: James 2:21-24 shows that Abraham's active obedience at Moriah brought his faith to complete, visible expression.

qs.q: What core command is given to Christian husbands in 1 Peter chapter three verse seven regarding honoring their wives?
o: Require wives to earn all household income without assistance
Treat wives as commercial property subject to disposal
Avoid communicating with wives regarding spiritual matters
Dwell with them with understanding, giving honor to the wife as to the weaker vessel and as joint heirs of the grace of life, so your prayers are not hindered
qs.e: 1 Peter 3:7 connects a husband's respectful, considerate treatment of his wife with the spiritual efficacy of his prayers.

qs.q: In Romans chapter eleven, what metaphor does Paul use to explain the inclusion of Gentile believers into God's covenant family?
o: Wild olive branches grafted into a cultivated olive tree, sharing in the root and fatness of the original olive tree
Wild wolves adopted into a flock of domestic sheep
Foreign vessels brought into a royal harbor
Bricks built into a temple fortress
qs.e: Romans 11:17-24 uses the olive tree metaphor to illustrate Gentile inclusion alongside Israel while warning against pride.

qs.q: In 2 Corinthians chapter five verse twenty-one, what central doctrine of substitutionary atonement is stated?
o: God overlooked human sin without requiring any sacrifice
For He made Him who knew no sin to be sin for us, that we might become the righteousness of God in Him
Christ became a sinful human who repented at baptism
Righteousness is earned through rigorous personal fasting
qs.e: 2 Corinthians 5:21 formulates the Great Exchange: sinless Christ bearing our sin so believers receive divine righteousness.

qs.q: What cosmic claim is made regarding Christ in Colossians chapter two verse nine?
o: In Him dwells a portion of divine wisdom alongside Greek philosophers
For in Him dwells all the fullness of the Godhead bodily
He was an earthly prophet who achieved divinity after resurrection
He is one of many equal spiritual mediators between God and men
qs.e: Colossians 2:9 asserts the complete, unabridged deity of Jesus Christ in His incarnate bodily existence.

qs.q: In Hebrews chapter nine, how does the author contrast the blood of animals with the blood of Christ?
o: Animal blood cleansed outward ceremonial impurity, but Christ offered Himself without spot to God to cleanse our conscience from dead works
Animal blood provides permanent salvation while Christ's blood is temporary
Animal blood and Christ's blood have identical spiritual
Neither animal blood nor Christ's blood can cleanse human conscience
qs.e: Hebrews 9:11-14 demonstrates the infinite superiority of Christ's eternal, voluntary sacrifice over Levitical animal offerings.

qs.q: In 1 John chapter four verse eight, what foundational statement defines the essential character of God?
o: God is strict vengeance without any mercy
God is an impersonal force governing physical nature
God is accessible exclusively through secret academic knowledge
He who does not love does not know God, for God is love
qs.e: 1 John 4:8 affirms that love is the essential nature of God, making love for others the proof of knowing Him.

qs.q: What land did God promise to give to Abraham and his descendants in Genesis chapter twelve?
qs.e: Genesis 12:5-7 records God calling Abram to travel to the land of Canaan, promising to give that land to his seed.

qs.q: Which prophet defeated the prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel?
qs.e: 1 Kings 18 details Elijah's dramatic contest on Mount Carmel where God answered by fire to consume the sacrifice.

qs.q: Who was the father of John the Baptist who served as a priest in the Temple?
qs.e: Luke 1:5 records Zechariah of the priestly division of Abijah as the father of John the Baptist.
qs.tp: Birth, Infancy and Preparation of Jesus

qs.q: What city was Jesus entering when He wept over it, foretelling its eventual destruction?
qs.e: Luke 19:41-44 records Jesus weeping over Jerusalem during His Triumphal Entry because it failed to recognize the time of its visitation.
qs.tp: Trial, Death and Resurrection of Jesus

qs.q: Which deacon preached the gospel in Samaria and baptized the Ethiopian eunuch?
qs.e: Acts 8 records Philip's effective ministry in Samaria and his guided encounter with the Ethiopian official on the Gaza road.

qs.q: According to Paul in Romans chapter three, how many people are righteous on their own merits before God?
qs.e: Romans 3:10 quotes the Old Testament stating: 'There is none righteous, no, not one.'

qs.q: What title is given to Jesus in the opening verse of the Gospel of John?
qs.e: John 1:1 declares: 'In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.'

qs.q: Why was the younger son in the Parable of the Prodigal Son forced to feed swine in a distant country?
o: He was captured by foreign soldiers and made a slave
He squandered his inheritance in wild living, and a severe famine struck the land
His elder brother drove him out of his home with weapons
He was punished by local judges for failing to pay taxes
qs.e: Luke 15:11-16 details the prodigal son wasting his wealth and sinking to feeding pigs—a humiliating job for a Jew.
qs.tp: Parables and Teaching on the Kingdom

qs.q: How did God speak to Moses at Mount Sinai when delivering the Ten Commandments?
o: In a quiet private whisper inside Moses' tent
Through a golden scroll handed to Aaron in secret
As a soft breeze over the Red Sea shore
In thunder, lightning, thick cloud, a loud trumpet blast, and a voice out of smoke
qs.e: Exodus 19:16-19 portrays the awe-inspiring divine majesty at Sinai as God spoke the Law in thunder and smoke.

qs.q: What punishment did God inflict on King Nebuchadnezzar's empire when Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego survived the furnace?
o: Nebuchadnezzar was immediately forced to relinquish his throne
Nebuchadnezzar decreed that anyone speaking against their God would be cut in pieces and their house destroyed
Babylon was destroyed by a sudden desert flood
The three young men were crowned joint kings over Babylon
qs.e: Daniel 3:28-29 records Nebuchadnezzar praising the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego and decreeing protection for their faith.

qs.q: What request did the mother of James and John make of Jesus in Matthew chapter twenty?
o: That her two sons sit one at His right hand and the other at His left in His Kingdom
That her sons be exempted from taking up their cross
That her family receive half the Temple treasury funds
That Jesus make her sons Roman governors in Judea
qs.e: Matthew 20:20-28 records her request, prompting Jesus to teach that true kingdom leadership comes through servant humility.

qs.q: In the Miracle of Raising Jairus' Daughter, what did Jesus say to the twelve-year-old girl when He took her by the hand?
o: Talitha, cumi! (which means 'Little girl, I say to you, arise!')
qs.e: Mark 5:41 records Jesus speaking the Aramaic phrase 'Talitha cumi!', immediately restoring the girl to life.

qs.q: What happened to the apostle Paul on the island of Malta (Melita) after his shipwreck in Acts chapter twenty-eight?
o: A viper bit his hand while he gathered firewood, but he suffered no harm, leading the islanders to think he was a god
He was arrested by local guards and thrown into a dungeon
He built a large ship to carry the passengers to Italy
He was crowned governor of the island by local citizens
qs.e: Acts 28:1-6 details Paul shaking off the poisonous viper into the fire unharmed, demonstrating divine protection.

qs.q: In Romans chapter twelve, how does Paul describe a Christian's duty toward civic order and peace?
o: If it is possible, as much as depends on you, live peaceably with all men
qs.e: Romans 12:18 instructs believers to pursue peaceable relationships with everyone to the extent humanly possible.

qs.q: According to Paul in 1 Corinthians chapter nine, why does an athlete exercise strict self-control in all things?
o: Athletes run to obtain a perishable crown, but Christians strive for an imperishable eternal crown
To win gold prize money from the Roman emperor
To prove personal physical superiority over non-athletes
To avoid paying civil entrance taxes at stadiums
qs.e: 1 Corinthians 9:24-27 uses athletic discipline as a metaphor for spiritual focus and self-mastery in Christian life.

qs.q: In Ephesians chapter four, what instruction is given regarding anger among believers?
o: Be angry and do not sin; do not let the sun go down on your wrath, nor give place to the devil
Suppress all emotional anger until public church meetings
Retaliate immediately before sunset against enemies
Anger is always a mortal sin in any circumstance
qs.e: Ephesians 4:26-27 warns against nursing grudgeful anger, which grants spiritual footholds to the adversary.

qs.q: What guidance does 1 Peter chapter two give regarding suffering unjustly as a Christian?
o: File immediate legal lawsuits against persecutors
Retaliate with physical violence against hostile masters
If you suffer when you do good and take it patiently, this is commendable before God, following Christ's example
Abandon Christian faith to avoid earthly pain
qs.e: 1 Peter 2:19-23 holds up Christ's patient, non-retaliatory suffering as the holy model for believers undergoing trial.

qs.q: What message did the prophet Haggai deliver to the returned Jewish exiles in Jerusalem?
o: Build a military fortress around Jerusalem before doing anything else
Return to Babylon where economic conditions are prosperous
Abolish the Aaronic priesthood in favor of foreign Levites
Rebuild the house of the Lord, for you dwell in panelled houses while God's house lies in ruins
qs.e: Haggai 1:1-11 challenged the exiles' misplaced priorities, urging them to complete rebuilding the Temple.

qs.q: What sign was given to King Ahaz in Isaiah chapter seven verse fourteen regarding divine deliverance?
o: Behold, the virgin shall conceive and bear a Son, and shall call His name Immanuel
The sun would stand still over Jerusalem for twelve hours
An army of angels would destroy the Syrian encampment
A golden altar would fall from heaven into the Temple
qs.e: Isaiah 7:14 records the famous messianic sign of Immanuel ('God with us'), cited in Matthew 1:23.
qs.tp: Birth, Infancy and Preparation of Jesus

qs.q: How did Joseph test his ten brothers when they came to Egypt to purchase grain during the famine?
o: He threw them all into prison for seven years
He demanded they pay ten thousand gold talents
He forced them to work as slave labor on Pharaoh's palace
He accused them of being spies, detained Simeon, and required them to bring their youngest brother Benjamin to prove their honesty
qs.e: Genesis 42 records Joseph testing his brothers' repentance and character without revealing his identity initially.

qs.q: What miraculous event occurred when Moses held up his hands during the battle against Amalek at Rephidim?
o: Fire fell from heaven and consumed the Amalekite army
An earthquake swallowed up the Amalekite soldiers
Whenever Moses held up his hand, Israel prevailed; whenever he let down his hand, Amalek prevailed
The sun stood still in the sky for three full days
qs.e: Exodus 17:8-13 describes Aaron and Hur holding up Moses' hands until sunset, securing victory for Joshua's army.

qs.q: Why were the Israelites defeated in their initial battle against the small city of Ai in Joshua chapter seven?
o: Because Achan had secretly taken devoted spoils from Jericho, bringing divine disfavor on the entire camp
Because Joshua failed to consult the High Priest Eleazar
Because the army was severely outnumbered by Canaanite chariots
Because the soldiers refused to march on the Sabbath
qs.e: Joshua 7 details how one man's hidden theft brought corporate guilt and military defeat at Ai until dealt with.

qs.q: What prophecy did Prophet Nathan deliver to King David following his sin with Bathsheba?
o: The sword would never depart from David's house, and the child born to Bathsheba would die
David would be overthrown immediately by the King of Egypt
David's royal throne would be transferred to the tribe of Benjamin
David would be struck with immediate physical leprosy
qs.e: 2 Samuel 12:10-14 details Nathan pronouncing divine judgment on David's household despite David's personal forgiveness.

qs.q: How did Elijah demonstrate the total powerlessness of Baal on Mount Carmel in 1 Kings chapter eighteen?
o: He ordered his servants to attack the prophets of Baal with swords
He let the 450 prophets of Baal pray all day without answer, then drenched his own altar with twelve water jars before praying for God's fire
He called down a hailstorm to destroy Baal's altar
He challenged Baal's priests to a chariot race across Kishon
qs.e: 1 Kings 18:20-39 contrasts Baal's silence with Yahweh's immediate answer by fire consuming sacrifice, wood, stone, and water.

qs.q: What vision did the prophet Jeremiah see during his call in Jeremiah chapter one that symbolized impending judgment from the north?
o: A golden bowl falling off the Temple altar
A boiling pot tilted away from the north, showing disaster breaking out from the north upon all inhabitants of the land
A basket of summer fruit rotting in the sun
Four horsemen riding across Jerusalem's streets
qs.e: Jeremiah 1:13-14 uses the boiling pot image to signify Babylonian invasion coming from the northern corridor.

qs.q: What occurred during Jesus' temptation in the wilderness when Satan asked Him to throw Himself down from the Temple pinnacle?
o: Jesus replied 'It is written again: You shall not test the Lord your God'
Jesus jumped down safely to prove His divinity to the crowds below
Jesus called down fire to consume the devil on the spot
Jesus remained completely silent until Satan departed
qs.e: Matthew 4:5-7 records Jesus quoting Deuteronomy 6:16 to refuse presumptuous testing of divine providence.
qs.tp: Birth, Infancy and Preparation of Jesus

qs.q: In the Parable of the Unforgiving Servant, how did the master punish the servant who strangled his fellow servant for a small debt?
o: The master banished him to the wilderness for forty years
The master was angry and delivered him to the torturers until he should pay all that was due to him
The master made him work as a field hand without wages
The master confiscated his home and gave it to the debtor
qs.e: Matthew 18:32-35 warns that God will treat unmerciful believers severely if they do not forgive others from their hearts.
qs.tp: Parables and Teaching on the Kingdom

qs.q: What sign accompanied the death of Jesus on Golgotha according to the Synoptic Gospels?
o: Fire fell from heaven and destroyed the Roman garrison
A bright star shone directly over Golgotha at noon
Darkness covered the whole land from the sixth to the ninth hour, and the Temple veil was torn in two
The River Jordan turned into blood
qs.e: Matthew 27:45, 51 records three hours of darkness and the splitting of the Temple veil as Jesus gave up His spirit.
qs.tp: Trial, Death and Resurrection of Jesus

qs.q: How did the early church at Jerusalem resolve the complaint of Hellenistic Jews regarding the daily distribution to widows in Acts chapter six?
o: They abolished the widow distribution fund completely
They required Gentile widows to return to their native cities
They selected seven spiritual, wise men (deacons) to oversee the serving of tables so apostles could focus on prayer and preaching
They appointed Roman guards to handle church finances
qs.e: Acts 6:1-6 describes the appointment of the Seven Deacons, maintaining harmony and enabling word ministry to expand.
qs.tp: The Early Church and Holy Spirit

qs.q: In 1 Corinthians chapter twelve, what point does Paul emphasize by asking 'Are all apostles? Are all prophets? Are all teachers?'?
o: Only ordained apostles are permitted to pray in public meetings
Every believer must manifest all nine spiritual gifts simultaneously
Spiritual gifts are reserved exclusively for Jewish church members
Spiritual gifts are diverse and not every believer holds the same office or manifests the same spiritual gift
qs.e: 1 Corinthians 12:28-30 refutes spiritual uniformity, affirming that the Spirit distributes different functions across the body.

qs.q: According to Paul in Galatians chapter five, how is the whole Mosaic Law fulfilled in a single command?
o: You shall offer sacrifices three times a year in Jerusalem
You shall abstain from all non-Kosher food items
You shall observe ceremonial washings on every Sabbath
You shall love your neighbor as yourself
qs.e: Galatians 5:14 summarizes the ethical core of the Law in love for neighbor (Leviticus 19:18).

qs.q: In Colossians chapter three, what does Paul instruct believers to do regarding their speech?
o: Speak only in ancient Hebrew or Greek during daily conversation
Put off all bitter speech, slander, and filthy language out of your mouth, speaking encouraging truth
Limit all speech to liturgical recitations in church meetings
Avoid speaking to non-Christian citizens entirely
qs.e: Colossians 3:8-9 urges believers to discard destructive verbal habits as part of putting on the new self.

qs.q: According to 1 John chapter three verse sixteen, how do we know what genuine love is?
o: By acquiring vast theological knowledge in Greek libraries
By this we know love, because He laid down His life for us; and we also ought to lay down our lives for the brethren
By performing spectacular public miracles in the market
By accumulating material gold wealth to distribute at death
qs.e: 1 John 3:16 points to Christ's self-sacrificial death as the ultimate definition and standard of divine love.

qs.q: In 1 Peter chapter one, how does Peter describe the incorruptible inheritance reserved in heaven for believers?
o: A physical earthly kingdom centered in Rome
A temporal gold supply granted during earthly life
An inheritance incorruptible and undefiled and that does not fade away, kept by God's power through faith
A secret sanctuary built on Mount Sinai
qs.e: 1 Peter 1:4-5 assures believers of their secure, imperishable heavenly inheritance kept by divine power.

qs.q: What significant role did Deborah play as a judge in Israel recorded in Judges chapter four?
o: She served as High Priest in Shiloh after Eli died
She built the city walls of Samaria with iron gates
She was a prophetess who judged Israel under a palm tree, instructed Barak to assemble troops, and accompanied him to battle against Sisera
She was queen of Edom who formed a treaty with Joshua
qs.e: Judges 4:4-9 details Deborah's prophetic authority, military encouragement to Barak, and spiritual leadership in Israel.

qs.q: How did King Hezekiah demonstrate profound faith when he received a threatening letter from Sennacherib of Assyria?
o: He surrendered the city of Jerusalem and paid 500 gold talents
He hired Egyptian mercenaries to attack Sennacherib's rear lines
He fled to Egypt under cover of night with the Temple gold
He went up to the house of the Lord, spread the letter before the Lord, and prayed for deliverance so all kingdoms would know Yahweh is God
qs.e: 2 Kings 19:14-19 describes Hezekiah spreading Rabshakeh's letter in the Temple and praying, resulting in the miraculous destruction of the Assyrian army.

qs.q: What allegory did the prophet Ezekiel present in Ezekiel chapter sixteen regarding Jerusalem's spiritual history?
o: A fruitful vine planted by waters that was uprooted by wild beasts
A towering cedar tree in Lebanon chopped down by Babylonian axes
A fortress built on high rocks that collapsed due to rotten stones
An abandoned, helpless infant rescued and raised by God into a beautiful queen who then committed egregious spiritual adultery with foreign idols
qs.e: Ezekiel 16 uses the vivid allegory of a rescued orphan bride turned adulteress to depict Jerusalem's gross covenant unfaithfulness.

qs.q: In the Sermon on the Mount, how did Jesus reinterpret the commandment regarding oaths and vows?
o: Swear only by the Jerusalem Temple altar stone
Do not swear at all, neither by heaven nor by earth, but let your 'Yes' be 'Yes' and your 'No' be 'No'
Take oaths only when testifying before Roman civil magistrates
Swear by your ancestors to prove truthfulness
qs.e: Matthew 5:33-37 demands absolute truthfulness without relying on elaborate oaths to guarantee integrity.
qs.tp: Parables and Teaching on the Kingdom

qs.q: What main conflict arose during Paul's ministry in Ephesus recorded in Acts chapter nineteen?
o: The Roman governor banned all Christian assemblies in Ephesus
Demetrius the silversmith stirred up a riot among craftsmen because Paul's preaching threatened the trade of Artemis (Diana) idols
Jewish leaders burned all Greek philosophy scrolls in the market
A severe famine forced Paul to move to Corinth immediately
qs.e: Acts 19:23-41 describes Demetrius organizing the silversmiths against Paul because widespread conversions reduced idol sales.

qs.q: In Romans chapter six, what does Paul teach regarding a believer's relationship to sin after baptism?
o: Consider yourselves dead indeed to sin, but alive to God in Christ Jesus; do not let sin reign in your mortal body
Believers may continue in sin freely because grace increases automatically
Physical baptism makes future moral choices completely irrelevant
Sin reigns over believers until they achieve physical death
qs.e: Romans 6:1-14 emphasizes that union with Christ in His death and resurrection breaks the mastery of sin.

qs.q: In 2 Corinthians chapter nine, what agricultural metaphor does Paul use to encourage generous giving?
o: He who sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and he who sows bountifully will also reap bountifully
He who plants wheat will harvest wild thorns
